# Catalyst Center NetAsCode parity

**Alpha; full parity remains incomplete.** The
[alpha checkpoint](catalyst-center-alpha.md) defines the current operating and
merge contract; the [roadmap](catalyst-center-roadmap.md) groups the remaining
work. The sections below retain incremental implementation history. Consult
the [resource ledger](catalyst-center-resource-parity.md) and dated evidence for
the scope of each completed operation.

CVK targets the upstream `catalyst_center` data model, with the same section
names and leaf semantics. Model recognition, schema validation, configuration
observation, planning and mutation are separate capabilities. Inventory reads
and a working SWIM upgrade do not establish configuration parity.

## Pinned upstream baseline

The baseline is `netascode/nac-catalystcenter/catalystcenter` **0.5.0**, tag commit
`a435555fe828f03cf3311d52fe1ab6572a247916`. This is the latest published tag
observed on 12 October 2026; CVK never resolves `latest` at runtime.

Sources:

- [Module and data model introduction](https://netascode.cisco.com/docs/start/catalystcenter/introduction/).
- [Terraform Registry module](https://registry.terraform.io/modules/netascode/nac-catalystcenter/catalystcenter/latest).
- [Immutable module source](https://github.com/netascode/terraform-catalystcenter-nac-catalystcenter/tree/a435555fe828f03cf3311d52fe1ab6572a247916).
- [Model merging and defaults](https://github.com/netascode/terraform-catalystcenter-nac-catalystcenter/blob/a435555fe828f03cf3311d52fe1ab6572a247916/merge.tf).

The module merges YAML into `local.model` and resolves defaults separately in
`local.defaults`; individual resources also perform fallbacks and filtering.
Consequently `terraform output -json model` is **not by itself proof of a fully
resolved model**. Template files, managed-site selection and global settings
also affect the effective desired state. An eventual CVK export must preserve
those semantics and record its immutable source revision, exporter version and
qualified schema provenance. A source commit is not a schema digest.

Offline [source composition](catalyst-center-model-merge.md) now implements the
pinned module's directory/file/final-model ordering and utils 2.0.0 core merge
semantics, preserving model/default components with ordered input provenance.
Strict input-language and resource execution limits remain separate; this does
not set any whole-section parity flag.

Opt-in [YAML source resolution](catalyst-center-model-merge.md#explicit-yaml-source-resolution)
now resolves qualified references/tags and explicit environment bindings offline,
with effective snapshot provenance. Runtime parsing and per-resource parity
flags remain unchanged.

## Current capability matrix

All eleven sections are recognized by the adapter descriptor and the offline
coverage tool. The module uses [93 distinct resource types](catalyst-center-resource-parity.md),
so section recognition is only the first boundary check.

The `NetworkControllerConfig` reconciler supports bounded native configuration
for sites, network settings, global authentication templates, template projects
and definitions, inventory tags, switching network profiles, and global L3 virtual
network definitions. These resources
reuse the existing worker, REST transport and durable ownership/operation journal.
Task completion is followed by independent resource readback. The detailed
coverage below distinguishes implemented operations from remaining fields,
scopes and lab qualification. Prune/delete support is resource specific and remains partial. Whole-section
parity flags remain false; the coverage tool reports bounded support separately.

| Section | Upstream constructs / work remaining |
| --- | --- |
| `sites` | Areas, buildings, floors; hierarchy, normalized paths and dependencies |
| `network_settings` | Credentials, DNS/NTP, AAA, address pools/reservations and telemetry; inheritance and secret references |
| `network_profiles` | Switching/wireless profiles and site/template assignments |
| `fabric` | Fabric sites/zones, transits, virtual networks, gateways and device roles |
| `templates` | Projects, templates, content/versioning, composite dependencies and deployments |
| `inventory` | Discovery, device settings/provisioning, PnP and RMA; operational inventory reads alone are insufficient |
| `wireless` | SSIDs, profiles, policies, AP configuration and provisioning |
| `lan_automation` | Discovery/provisioning and link operations with durable task recovery |
| `system_settings` | External authentication and policy servers, including secret handling |
| `authentication_templates` | Fabric authentication templates; previously missing from CVK's section list |
| `feature_templates` | Wireless feature templates; previously missing from CVK's section list |

The separate operational path supports managed SWIM within the
[documented live qualification limits](catalyst-center.md). It is not a twelfth
NetAsCode section and remains governed by the existing rollout/handoff machinery.

## Run the offline coverage check

```bash
go run ./tools/cvk-netascode-migrate controller-report \
  --model-version 0.5.0 \
  examples/configs/catalyst-center/parity/model.nac.yaml
```

Use a single YAML or JSON document with only the `catalyst_center` root. Input
may be piped through standard input with `-`. The tool identifies the presence
of sections and reports `configurationRead`, `plan`, `apply` and `prune`
independently. It prints no leaf values, makes no API calls, emits no CRs, and
never alters Terraform state or configuration ownership.

For a CI migration gate:

```bash
go run ./tools/cvk-netascode-migrate controller-report \
  --model-version 0.5.0 --require-config-parity model.nac.yaml
```

The compiled tool returns:

- `0`: section coverage report produced with no unknown sections. This is **not**
  schema validation, a resolved-model attestation or confirmation of parity.
- `1`: invalid/ambiguous input, unknown sections, input/output failure or size limit.
  Unknown sections are included in the report rather than silently discarded.
- `2`: invalid flags or unsupported/missing model version.
- `3`: `--require-config-parity` requested, but a supplied section lacks
  configuration read, plan or apply support. The report is still produced.

`go run` wraps a nonzero tool exit as its own failure; build a binary if a CI
script needs to distinguish these exit codes.

The parser rejects duplicate keys, multiple documents, YAML aliases/anchors,
merge keys, non-string keys, null/scalar sections and input over 1 MiB. Parsing
errors do not include source values. Nested leaf validation and default/template
resolution belong to the pinned upstream toolchain; this report deliberately
labels itself `section-boundary-only`. Unknown nested fields are not checked.

## Implementation sequence and acceptance gates

1. **Resolved-model contract and sites reporting.** Use the existing
   `NetworkControllerConfig`, common contract validation, ConfigMap/inline source
   union and projected Secret aliases. Define a verified upstream export and
   leaf-schema validation path without copying the Terraform default resolver.
   Implement read-only site hierarchy observation and deterministic differences
   for areas/buildings/floors first. Missing/partial API results must remain an
   observation failure, never an empty desired/actual snapshot. Report mode must
   have tests proving zero mutating calls. Bind results to source/controller
   UID, generation and revision; do not publish stale drift as current.
2. **Sites create/update with explicit ownership.** Add durable per-resource
   ownership, dependency ordering, plan digest/approval, write-ahead claims,
   async receipts and restart/unknown-outcome handling. Define parent deletion,
   resource adoption, scope overlap and retained-resource behavior before writes.
   Keep prune/delete unsupported until separately qualified. A controller task
   that changes devices must coordinate with CVK's canonical device mutation
   authority; controller-level ownership cannot replace that fence.
3. **Network settings and inventory assignment.** Add inherited settings,
   pool/reservation references and site/device identity binding. Resolve secrets
   only through the existing allow-listed projections; never put secret values
   in plans, hashes exposed as status, logs or parity reports. Maintain a single
   active configuration owner for overlapping Terraform/CVK resources.
4. **Templates and profiles.** Separate configuration of a template from its
   deployment to devices. Preserve upstream project/name/version identity and
   content dependencies. Template deployment requires coordinated device
   admission and verifiable postconditions; it is not an unrestricted command
   escape hatch.
5. **Fabric, wireless and remaining operational workflows.** Add dependencies
   and rollback/retention semantics section by section. Qualify fan-out,
   pagination, rate limits, cancellation, expired sessions and partial outcomes
   before parallel writes. Reuse the existing SWIM handoff for software actions;
   do not create a competing upgrade executor or lock domain.

For each slice, require pinned upstream fixtures, negative/unsupported-field
coverage, deterministic plans, fake-API request assertions, stale-identity and
restart tests, and an isolated live read/report then apply/verify qualification.
Advance the capability catalog only when that stage is usable and tested.

Product-specific mappings stay in the Catalyst Center adapter. The neutral
controller provider, ND behavior, REST transport, credential projection and
existing direct-device drivers remain the common foundation. Configuration
ownership/task contracts should be shared only where their semantics match;
do not move SWIM-specific grants into a generic configuration executor.

## Deployment impact

The current alpha extends CRD status/operation protocols, admission policies,
worker permissions and bounded controller mutation paths in addition to the
original report reconciler. Install matching CRDs, admission/RBAC, manager and
workers from the same checkpoint. Do not mix the earlier report-only scaffold
with the current mutation runtime. Adoption, cleanup and downgrade support are
resource specific; the presence of a schema or permission does not authorize an
unqualified operation. See the [alpha deployment contract](catalyst-center-alpha.md#alpha-operating-contract).

## Site reporting contract

Use `examples/configs/catalyst-center/sites-report.yaml` with matching manager
and worker builds. Only `mode: report`, global scope, supported managed sections,
and Retain policies are accepted. Inline JSON or a same-namespace ConfigMap YAML
source uses the existing source union. Source ConfigMap changes enqueue a fresh
report; unchanged intent is also checked at the configured drift interval.

Every site requires explicit `name` and canonical `parent_name`. Areas support
those two attributes; buildings additionally support `address`, `country`,
`latitude`, `longitude`; floors support `floor_number`, `rf_model`, `width`,
`length`, `height`, `units_of_measure`. Floor dimension/RF/unit defaults must be
expanded upstream. Coordinates and dimensions follow the pinned module's
rounding precision. Floor maps, AP placement, unknown fields, unresolved input,
Secret injection and asserted schema digests are rejected, not ignored.
This is subset validation, not validation of the entire upstream schema.

The modern `/dna/intent/api/v1/sites` reader requires HTTP 200, bounded pagination,
unique IDs and paths, a Global root and consistent parent identities/types.
Missing managed fields and partial observations fail reporting. The planner
emits redacted Add/Update differences, retains unmentioned objects and refuses
type replacement. It never sends site mutations or claims apply success.
Controller/config/source identities are rechecked before publishing status.
Failure clears current drift rather than presenting stale success. Drift status
is capped at 50 entries with an explicit truncation message.

The [12 October live record](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-12/README.md)
qualifies the real API reader and planner against the existing lab area/building,
including local synthetic drift. It does not qualify floor behavior live,
configuration writes or an in-cluster deployment of the new reporter.

## Network settings reporting contract

`examples/configs/catalyst-center/network-settings-report.yaml` selects the
single managed section `network_settings`, report mode, global scope and Retain
policies. It uses the same reconciler, authenticated REST client, source watch
and stale-observation guards as site reporting. Observations have a two-minute
overall timeout; failed reads never publish a partial drift result.

The supported upstream subset is `network_settings.network`, containing named
profiles with explicit `ntp_servers`, `dhcp_servers`, and/or the pair
`domain_name` + `dns_servers`. Bind profiles by name through
`sites.global.network_settings.network`, or the same field on area/building/floor
references with explicit `name` and `parent_name`. The `sites` section here is
reference context, not another managed section. Only those reference fields
are allowed in this reporting subset; use a separate site report for geometry.
Unknown fields, missing references, unused profiles and unresolved defaults
fail closed. Between one and 100 distinct site references are accepted.

The reader uses the modern site-specific
[NTP](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/retrieve-ntp-settings-for-a-site/),
[DHCP](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/retrieve-dhcp-settings-for-a-site/)
and [DNS](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/retrieve-dns-settings-for-a-site/)
APIs with `_inherited=false`. A null setting represents inheritance and differs
from an explicit requested setting; an empty object represents an unset setting.
Malformed, missing or partial responses fail the report. NTP/DHCP server lists
are compared independently of order; DNS resolver order is preserved. Status
contains field paths and change kinds, never server/domain values. The local
100-server parsing bound is a reporting limit, not an appliance write limit.

AAA credential comparison, credentials and other network settings remain
unsupported. None of these reports writes configuration, adopts ownership or
implements prune. The capability catalog labels this as partial reporting only.


### Timezone and banner profiles

The same `network_settings.network` profile now accepts explicit `timezone` and
`banner` strings, following the pinned module's `identifier` and Custom banner
mapping. The reader uses the documented
[time zone API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/retrieve-time-zone-settings-for-a-site/)
and [banner API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/retrieve-banner-settings-for-a-site/)
with the same inheritance and completeness rules. Timezone validation checks
identifier representation, not membership in a version-specific appliance
catalog. Banner text is preserved exactly (including whitespace), with a local
64 KiB limit and no NUL bytes. A custom empty banner differs from an unset or
Builtin banner. Null intent is rejected; inheritance is not inferred from an
omitted value. Only `/timezone` or `/banner` changes appear in drift status,
never their values. These additions are reporting-only and grant no write or
prune capability.


### Telemetry profiles

`examples/configs/catalyst-center/telemetry-report.yaml` uses the upstream
`network_settings.telemetry` collection and
`sites.<site>.network_settings.telemetry` name reference. A site may reference
both a network and telemetry profile; names are scoped to their collections.
The shared reader uses the modern
[telemetry settings API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/retrieve-telemetry-settings-for-a-site/)
with `_inherited=false`; inherited groups are resolved through verified
ancestor identities when needed.

This reporting subset requires all of the following resolved fields explicitly:

- `wired_data_collection` and `wireless_telemetry` booleans.
- `catalyst_center_as_snmp_server` and `snmp_servers`.
- `catalyst_center_as_syslog_server` and `syslog_servers`.
- `catalyst_center_as_network_collector` and `enable_netflow_collector_on_devices`.
- For an external collector: `netflow_collector_ip_address` and integer
  `netflow_collector_port` (1–65535). For a built-in collector, omit both.

Missing defaults, null lists/booleans, unknown fields and incompatible collector
fields are rejected. No upstream defaults are guessed. External server lists
are normalized as sets; duplicate addresses are rejected. All five API groups
must be present. Each group's null (inherited), empty object (unset) and explicit
values remain distinct, including explicit false. Missing managed fields in a
populated group fail observation. Drift contains only group paths, never server
addresses. Report mode never writes; bounded native network-setting apply is
described below. Prune/delete remains unsupported.

### AAA and ISE metadata profiles

`examples/configs/catalyst-center/aaa-report.yaml` selects named profiles from
`network_settings.aaa_servers` using a site's `network_settings.aaa_servers`
reference. Network, telemetry and AAA profile references can coexist. Each AAA
profile selects `network_aaa`, `client_and_endpoint_aaa`, or both.

Each selected group requires explicit `server_type` (`AAA` or `ISE`), `protocol`
(`RADIUS` or `TACACS`) and `primary_ip`. `secondary_ip` is optional and compared
only when requested. ISE additionally requires an explicit `pan` IP address;
the upstream fallback to `primary_ip` must be resolved before submission. PAN
is rejected for AAA. IP addresses are canonicalized; unknown fields and null
intent are rejected. This is a bounded metadata subset, not full AAA parity.

The modern [AAA settings API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/retrieve-aaa-settings-for-a-site/)
is read with `_inherited=false`. Both response groups must be present; inherited,
unset and populated objects remain distinct. Mandatory observation fields and
ISE PAN must be valid. Differences identify only group/field paths, not values.
Unselected groups and omitted optional intent fields are not managed.

`shared_secret` and `shared_secret_version` intent are rejected before API access.
Any returned `sharedSecret` is excluded from normalized observations and status.
Successful reports explicitly say that AAA shared secrets are not compared.
Neither an InSync metadata report nor this capability authorizes authentication
changes, confirms that authentication works, or establishes credential parity.


## IP address pools and reservations

`examples/configs/catalyst-center/ipam-report.yaml` consumes the upstream
`network_settings.ip_pools` collection. Pools require explicit name, type,
address family and canonical CIDR. Gateway and DHCP/DNS fields are compared
only when present in intent. IPv4 and IPv6 address spaces are validated,
including gateway containment and subnet alignment. The reader uses the modern
[global pools API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/retrieves-global-ip-address-pools/)
and [site pools API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/retrieves-ip-address-subpools/)
with bounded pagination and strict HTTP 200/identity validation.

Nested `ip_pools_reservations` are assigned by name through a non-global site's
`ip_pools_reservations` list. A reservation must have exactly one site. Following
the pinned module, IPv6 augments a matching IPv4 reservation by name; IPv6-only
reservations are rejected. Each explicit child subnet must fit its parent pool;
dual-stack types must match. IPv6 /64 implies SLAAC as in upstream. Tunnel pools
cannot supply reservations. No values are included in drift output.

Reports distinguish absent objects and changed fields, and retain unrelated
objects. Missing requested optional fields fail observation rather than being
guessed empty. Report mode never writes. Native apply now supports pool/reservation creation
and optional-attribute updates through the shared execution journal. Allocation
preflight rejects overlapping pools/reservations, pool resizing, reservation
reparenting and site relocation. Pruning, deletion and owner transfer remain
unsupported.

## Global authentication templates

`examples/configs/catalyst-center/authentication-templates-report.yaml` uses
`authentication_templates` with the three built-in profiles: Open Authentication,
Closed Authentication and Low Impact. Authentication order, timeout, Wake on LAN
and host count must be explicit. Low Impact additionally requires explicit
pre-auth ACL enabled state, implicit action and ordered access contracts.
Description changes are ignored as in the pinned module's lifecycle rule.
Global BPDU Guard, fabric overrides and unknown fields are rejected.

The [authentication profiles API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/get-authentication-profiles/)
is filtered to global profiles. Missing built-in profiles, duplicate identities,
fabric-specific results and missing managed fields fail reporting. This does
not modify access-control behavior or verify authentication against a server.

## Multi-section reports

A single model can select any combination of the currently supported `sites`,
`network_settings` and `authentication_templates` sections. All selected sections
are parsed before any appliance read. Known cross-section site references are
projected into each parser only when their owning section is also selected;
unknown fields and unselected source sections are rejected. `sites` may also be
reference-only context for network settings. No arbitrary leaf is silently
ignored. Source numbers retain their precision during projection.

Section status is published only after every selected observation succeeds;
a later failure publishes no partial drift or current-success timestamp.
Successful reports retain per-section InSync/Drifted state and share the existing
50-entry drift bound and stale controller/config/ConfigMap checks. This is
all-or-nothing status publication, not a transactional appliance snapshot.

## Native execution journal

`NetworkController.status.configuration` now has bounded global section owners
and one outstanding operation. Claims bind config name and UID and survive
manifest deletion or replacement. The operation binds controller generation,
config generation, ConfigMap UID/resourceVersion where applicable, section,
resource identity and action. No payload or secret digest is persisted.

A status compare-and-swap records `Submitting` and its timestamp before the
single resource API invocation. Restart, status conflict, lost acknowledgement,
timeout, missing receipt and task acceptance never authorize another submission.
The submission helper records `Accepted` with a sanitized task identity, or
`Unknown` on uncertain outcomes. Recovery must pass through `Verifying` and
resource-specific authoritative read-back before `Verified` can release the
operation slot. An unsubmitted `Prepared` operation can be cancelled. Neither
path automatically releases section ownership.

The existing manager finalizer also retains a deleting controller while the
journal contains an operation, even if its referring manifest has been removed.
Recovery status can be recorded after pause or policy changes; new submissions
retain the strict active-controller and source-snapshot gates. No RBAC permission
or existing device/SWIM lease behavior changes. The API field is optional, and
inventory-only adapters leave it absent.

This foundation is fixture-qualified and remains absent from the deployed lab
image. Report manifests do not invoke it. Native site executors now use it;
explicit ownership transfer, prune/delete policy and the remaining resource
executors are pending.
Endpoint fencing retains the existing exact-text, same-namespace identity
contract; endpoint aliases and cross-namespace representations of one appliance
are not covered by this journal. Upgrade the CRD and matching manager/worker
before any future executor uses the journal. Do not claim configuration parity
or enable remote writes based only on these primitives.

## Native site apply

`examples/configs/catalyst-center/sites-apply.yaml` opts into create and attribute
updates for areas, buildings and floors, with global section ownership and
Retain policies. Install matching CRDs, manager and controller-worker together:
older binaries do not preserve the new status journal. Incompatible or pruned
journal state cannot issue a submission permit.

The complete desired hierarchy is validated before submission. Site names are
limited to 40 characters, and a floor requires an explicit floor number for execution. Each reconcile submits at most
one request, resolving the parent's observed ID before its children. Building
updates preserve observed, supported attributes omitted from intent. Pinned
provider endpoints are used: v1 areas, v2 buildings and v2 floors. Task identity,
submission time (with a bounded two-minute controller/worker clock-skew allowance)
and terminal success are checked before independent read-back
of site identity and requested attributes. Existing site and parent IDs are
journaled for restart verification. Converged manifests also claim ownership.

Changed source revisions, conflicting manifest UIDs, ambiguous submissions,
failed/mismatched tasks, and changed resource identities retain the operation
fence. Unknown outcomes are not automatically replayed or discarded; automatic
receipt discovery and explicit ownership transfer remain recovery work.
Deletion or omission retains remote sites. Maps, AP placement, renames/moves,
pruning and compound execution across other sections remain unsupported.

The manifest-cycle fixture test creates a full hierarchy across simulated worker
restarts, verifies convergence and no additional writes on a subsequent reconcile.
The opt-in live resource test separately qualifies isolated create/update/cleanup;
it does not establish an in-cluster journal rollout.

Floor units returned by Get Sites describe the requested/default response
representation, not a stored preference. The controller defaults to feet; CVK
compares physical dimensions in the desired units and does not generate an
update solely for equivalent meter/foot representations. Invalid/missing units
still fail observation. Site task timeout follows `spec.taskTimeout` (default
30 minutes); expiry retains the journal as Unknown and reports failure.

## Native network-settings apply

`network-settings-apply.yaml` targets an already-existing empty `CVK-Lab` area.
A named `network` profile can configure NTP, DHCP, DNS, timezone and banner;
a resolved `telemetry` profile can select collection, SNMP traps,
syslog and application visibility. Partial telemetry updates require complete
known effective companion state because the native PUT resets omitted groups.
DNS resolver order is preserved. Explicit
empty DNS lists use native omission to clear resolvers; domain-only profiles
preserve the current effective resolver list when an update is required. Explicit
empty NTP/DHCP lists use native null encoding and converge on an empty group.
The collector is encoded under the API's nested
`applicationVisibility.collector` object. AAA/shared secrets and credential
writes are rejected before any API read or partial apply.

Site and network-setting executors share one operation state machine and one
controller journal. They supply resource planning, single-request submission and
read-back semantics; no new transport, retry loop, role or device lease is added.
Each manifest currently selects one executable section, uses global section
ownership and Retain policies. All referenced site identities and selected
settings must be observed before a write plan is released. The journal pins the
site ID so deletion/recreation cannot redirect verification to a new target.

Catalyst Center may collapse child values equal to their parent into inheritance.
Both reporting and execution resolve only explicitly inherited fields/groups by
walking the verified site parent-ID chain. Missing parent observations fail;
empty/unset values are not guessed. The NetAsCode model declares desired values,
not a force-explicit-override flag. This prevents repeated writes after the
controller normalizes a successful update. AAA metadata retains its separate
explicit-observation contract until its execution and secret handling land.

A changed source can safely cancel an unsubmitted Prepared operation or release
an already Verified operation owned by the same manifest. Accepted, Submitting
and uncertain operations retain the original revision binding and cannot replay.
The live resource qualification uses a new empty hierarchy, not the existing
Global settings or switch assignments. In-cluster rollout and full-section
parity remain pending; the external NetFlow collector branch has fixture
coverage only unless independently qualified with collector infrastructure.


## Native IPAM apply

`ipam-apply.yaml` demonstrates explicit global pools and site reservations.
It shares the `network_settings` section owner with scalar and telemetry settings;
combine them in one owner manifest rather than applying competing manifests.
All selected resources are observed before the first write. Parent pools are
created and verified before reservations resolve their real pool UUIDs. Updates
preserve omitted gateway, DHCP, DNS and IPv6 settings. Pool CIDR/type changes,
reservation relocation/resizing/reparenting and ambiguous reservation names are
rejected, including conflicts with allocations outside the manifest. Existing
matching identities are managed under explicit section ownership; Retain policies
do not delete them.

The isolated live test on 2026-10-12 verified an IPv4 pool and site reservation,
exact task receipts, read-back convergence, and removal of the complete fixture.
IPv6/dual-stack execution, live optional-attribute updates and Kubernetes journal
rollout still need qualification. This is bounded support, not complete IPAM or
full NetAsCode parity.


## Native global authentication-template apply

The `authentication_templates` section now has a native executor for the global
Open Authentication, Closed Authentication and Low Impact built-in profiles.
It resolves their actual UUIDs, submits one profile per PUT list payload and uses
the same operation journal, receipt polling and authoritative verification as
sites and network settings. Missing/replaced profiles fail closed. Low Impact
includes the explicit pre-auth ACL; other profiles omit that field. Fabric IDs
and BPDU guard are not sent on global updates. ACL descriptions follow the pinned
module's ignore-changes behavior.

`authentication-templates-apply.yaml` requires the matching journal CRDs, manager
and worker. These global profiles may affect fabrics, so review intended policy
changes before applying. Fixture tests cover successful updates, convergence,
missing/replaced profiles and lost receipts. Live mutation and fabric-specific
overrides remain pending; full authentication parity is not claimed.


## Template project dependency

The `templates.projects` parser and executor now support project names and
optional descriptions. `template-projects-report.yaml` and
`template-projects-apply.yaml` demonstrate the model. Reads validate the complete
project collection and reject duplicate names or UUIDs. Creation and description
updates use the existing task journal; update requests carry the UUID in both
the JSON body and the API query parameter. Omitted descriptions do not drift.
The built-in `Onboarding Configuration` project is a reference only, matching
the pinned module: CVK neither creates nor edits it, and requires it to exist.

Live qualification created an empty isolated project, updated its description,
verified both task receipts and convergence, and removed the fixture. Template
content, regular/composite versions, tag assignment and device deployment remain
pending. Unknown template fields fail before API access; this dependency layer
is not full `templates` section parity. Retain policies apply, and the matching
journal CRDs/manager/worker are required for Kubernetes execution.

Template identity resolution is implemented in the shared NetAsCode model package.
Canonical identities use `project#template`; unique bare names remain accepted
for managed references. Composite member order is preserved. Missing, repeated
or composite members fail validation, and ambiguous members use the composite's
own project as specified upstream. An external template reference must be
project-qualified and still requires appliance metadata/version lookup before
execution. The offline report can exercise this graph with
`--check-template-references`; device deployment and tag assignment remain pending.

External template-content resolution now follows the pinned file precedence
(`project#template` before bare `template`) and newline normalization. It consumes
an explicit file snapshot rather than reading worker-local paths. The migration
tool's `--template-directory` checks this input contract; it does not create or
commit templates. Native regular-template execution uses the same content resolver
with the source binding described below.

### Atomic template source assets

For a ConfigMap-backed `templates` source, the same ConfigMap may include
`data["cvk-template-assets.json"]`: a JSON object mapping original filenames
(such as `Project#Template.j2`) to their text contents. JSON keys can contain the
project separator even though Kubernetes ConfigMap data keys cannot. Keep the
model under a different key, for example `model.yaml`. BinaryData assets,
duplicate filenames/stems, non-text values and path entries are rejected.

The loader reads model and assets from one object snapshot. Its UID and
resourceVersion already participate in the existing operation journal and source
watch. An asset-only edit invalidates a Prepared operation before submission;
accepted work retains its original revision fence. This introduces no additional
CRD, permission or external file access. Inline sources have no external assets.
The native regular-template executor consumes these assets from that snapshot.

### Template definition reporting

`template-content.yaml` demonstrates a model and external file map in one
ConfigMap. Reporting now parses regular/composite definitions, device type
selectors and NetAsCode variable fields, including the nested API selection
object. It resolves member references and reads the uncommitted template
inventory followed by project/UUID-checked detail reads. Device selectors and
variables compare as collections of managed fields; composite member order is
preserved. Drift exposes only template identity and `/definition`, never bodies
or variable values. Failed/partial observations discard the report.

Language, software type and device selectors must be explicit. Unknown template
fields, tags and unresolved file content fail compilation; defaults, tags and
redeployment policy are not silently discarded. Apply supports regular templates
and composite templates with verified member dependencies. A draft
read does not establish that a deployable committed version exists.

Live read qualification observed 26 templates and verified three detail
identities. This validates the read API contract, not complete live field parity
or template mutation/deployment. Full-section coverage flags remain false.

### Committed-version verification

The version reader selects the greatest numeric committed version and rejects
ambiguous IDs/numbers or wrong template parents. A null/zero version is a draft;
the appliance also omits `version` on the entry whose UUID equals the base template
UUID. Only that specific omitted-field case is accepted as a draft. It never
counts as committed completion. Version comments are not completion evidence.

Committed detail reads use the version UUID without `unCommitted=true`, and
verify the returned version UUID, project, name and numeric version. The lab's
existing 26 entries were drafts, so isolated qualification created a harmless
regular template, committed version 1, verified a distinct committed UUID and
matching body, then removed both template and project. No device deployment
occurred. This established the API contract used by the native executor below.


## Native regular-template execution

`template-content-execution.yaml` now runs the regular-template lifecycle from a
single ConfigMap snapshot: project dependency, draft create/update, commit, and
committed-body verification. The executor shares the controller journal and
source revision checks. Each reconcile submits at most one mutation, and all
selected template/version reads complete before a write plan is released.
Parent project and base template UUIDs are pinned into the operation identity.
Template content stays in memory and API requests, never status or error text.

Convergence requires both desired draft content and a matching latest committed
body. Saving a draft alone cannot report completion. A changed file triggers a
draft update followed by a new commit; a matching committed version prevents a
repeat commit after executor recreation. Omitted project/template descriptions
and software-version attributes are retained. Kind replacement is rejected.
Composite definitions wait for matching committed member bodies before execution;
tags and device deployment remain pending.

The native regular executor passed a live create/commit/update/commit cycle,
including read-back and fixture cleanup. This supersedes the earlier API-only
qualification. Matching CRD/manager/worker rollout and Kubernetes journal
qualification are still required; full template-section parity remains false.


## Native composite-template execution

`template-composite-execution.yaml` uses the same ConfigMap-bound source and
shared journal. Composite order in the model does not determine write order:
regular members must have matching draft and committed bodies before a composite
can be created or committed. Member nesting/cycles are rejected by the pinned
model's regular-member contract. Kind replacement remains unsupported.

Catalyst Center's draft and committed composites retain member base UUIDs,
not version UUIDs. CVK therefore records a commit marker derived only from the
ordered base/version UUIDs of verified members. A member's new committed version
changes this marker and causes a new composite commit, even when membership is
unchanged. Completion requires the marker AND an independently matching committed
composite body; neither alone suffices. This marker is not a claim that the
appliance's composite object pins embedded member versions. Device deployment
must resolve and supply committed member versions separately and is still pending.

The native lab cycle verified composite create/commit, then member draft update,
member commit and composite recommit, with no extra writes after convergence.
Both templates and their isolated project were removed. Same-project membership
was live-qualified; cross-project membership and device deployment have not been
live-qualified. Matching journal CRD/manager/worker versions are now deployed in
the lab, with in-cluster tag create/update restart qualification complete. Template
lifecycle qualification remains native-only.


## Tag definitions

`tags-report.yaml` and `tags-apply.yaml` use `templates.tags` with name,
description, system-tag flag and dynamic-rule model fields. Rule fields translate
into the API's `memberType` and nested `rules` object. Unknown attributes and
invalid field types fail compilation. Templates and tags must share the section's
single owner manifest. Their planners use separate operation namespaces but one
journal, transport and source snapshot; every selected planner completes its
observation before a mutation is released.

Static tag creation and description updates passed live task/read-back/cleanup
qualification. Updates preserve omitted observed tag attributes. Existing system
tags or missing protection metadata block mutation before any other selected tag
write; creating system tags is not enabled. Dynamic rules have fixture coverage
but are not live-qualified. Template/device membership and the upstream merge
with `inventory.tags` remain pending. Retain policies do not remove tags or their
memberships. This is not full tag-resource or template-section parity.


## Template tag associations

`template-tag-execution.yaml` combines tag definitions, template definitions and
per-template `tags` references under one templates-section owner. Missing declared
tags and template identities wait for their native creation. Undeclared tags are
external references: they must exist before execution can begin. Missing or
protected external tags fail preflight instead of allowing a partial write.

Association requests POST only the missing template UUID. Retain policies never
remove omitted members, and unrelated existing members remain untouched. The
journal pins both tag and template UUIDs; replacement of either fails verification.
Membership reads are filtered to `memberType=template` and fully paginated.
Operation identities use the tag name plus a digest of nonsecret association
identity to remain bounded without name collisions. Report output contains no
content or variable values.

The live native cycle created a tag, associated an isolated template, verified
membership/convergence, and removed the entire fixture. Device memberships,
protected tag associations, inventory tag merging and removal/pruning remain
pending. No device deployment occurred; full NetAsCode parity is still incomplete.

### Inventory tag definitions and device identities

Inventory tag-only models now compile for report and apply using the same tag parser,
executor, task journal and readback as template tags. See
`examples/configs/catalyst-center/inventory-tags-apply.yaml`. Static tag create/update
uses Retain semantics. Unsupported inventory fields fail compilation before writes.

Inventory and templates share a controller tag namespace. Until resource-level
ownership is implemented, a different config identity cannot claim either section
when the other is owned. This also protects no-op reconciliation and existing
persisted template claims. A single config may now select templates and inventory
together for tag definitions and template objects, using inventory-over-template
tag precedence. Inventory device actions remain excluded from this apply path.

The configuration device resolver corroborates hostname/FQDN, management IP and
serial selectors, rejects ambiguous or conflicting identities, and requires serial
identity for APs whose management IP is ephemeral. It has been read-only qualified
against all three lab switches. It does not replace the SWIM identity checks and
does not yet enable inventory device provisioning or tag memberships.

### Device tag association executor

Device and template tag memberships now share one mutation and verification
implementation. Device associations corroborate inventory identity, pin tag and
device UUIDs in the existing journal representation, add only missing members,
and preserve unrelated members. Replacement identities fail verification.
An isolated association on lab switch `.101` passed native API qualification,
including convergence and verified association/tag cleanup.

This executor is not yet exposed through inventory device manifests: NetAsCode
conditions tags on the requested site and assignment/provisioning state. The new
assignment reader provides separate site membership evidence; discovery alone
must not satisfy that dependency. Device state planning, manifest integration,
and persistent Kubernetes journal qualification remain pending.

### Inventory assignment reports

`inventory.devices` now supports read-only comparison of explicit `ASSIGN` state,
site path, and tag references using name/FQDN/IP/serial identity selectors. The
report distinguishes assignment drift from missing tag membership. Every desired
device is resolved uniquely, and target sites must already exist. Site creation,
role defaults, provisioning and reprovisioning are not inferred or reported as
implemented. Unsupported device fields and states fail compilation before reads.
See `examples/configs/catalyst-center/inventory-report.yaml`.

Tag-only inventory apply remains available. A source containing device actions is
rejected by apply until those actions participate in the shared device mutation
lease and durable recovery path. The existing SWIM handoff is upgrade-specific;
configuration authorization must preserve its identity and reservation checks,
not manufacture an upgrade to obtain permission for unrelated device writes.

### Native assignment execution prerequisite

The native assignment executor now plans one device per operation through
`networkDevices/assignToSite/apply`, with device and site UUIDs in the existing
operation identity. Execution requires an explicit serial selector. Planning
resolves every target before releasing a write, rejects missing/duplicate
identities, and skips devices already assigned. Verification independently
re-reads assignment and rejects changed device, site, or serial identity.

This executor remains disconnected from manifest apply while device mutation
lease authorization and recovery are unfinished. Its mutation/receipt path has
fixture coverage; that is not evidence of a live assignment mutation or durable
Kubernetes lease qualification.

### Durable physical-device binding

Configuration operations can now retain `targetSerial` alongside `targetID` and
`parentID`. Native assignment verification requires all three bindings and rejects
older device operations with no serial. Non-device resource operations retain
their existing optional identity behavior.

The submission permit compares the requested identities with the persisted journal
before entering Submitting. An older CRD that prunes a new identity field cannot
silently authorize the API request. Unit fixtures cover serial persistence through
an uncertain outcome and simulated storage pruning with zero HTTP submissions.
Both CRD distributions carry the additive field. This does not grant a device
mutation lease or enable assignment apply; managed-worker authorization and device-operation recovery qualification remain
pending. The journal schema and controller images have been rolled out and tested
in Kubernetes for tag operations.

### Managed target resolution and final permit readback

Before dispatch, configuration submission re-reads the persisted Submitting
operation and checks owner, source revision, action, resource and target bindings.
If the permit write lost identity fields, no HTTP request is made and the durable
fence remains for recovery. A successful status-write acknowledgement alone does
not establish that the API server retained the complete operation.

The managed-device resolver reuses `topologyidentity.CanonicalPhysicalIdentity`
and requires a unique declared CiscoDevice, matching namespace/address/driver,
and matching device and Node identity UIDs. It never adopts an inventory record or
changes the operator declaration. The future authorization caller must provide
an authoritative CiscoDevice inventory; the helper itself does not acquire a lease
or validate the live Node/worker/admission contract. Assignment apply remains gated.

### Managed authorization prerequisite qualification

The controller inventory-to-CiscoDevice mapping has been checked against all three
lab switches using credential-free Kubernetes identity projections. A separate
live-Node validator checks the Node UID and compares both MachineID/SystemUUID
with the declared physical identity using CVK's existing topology identity helper.
Missing or conflicting observations cannot authorize a replacement device.

The existing maintenance request contract accepts software-upgrade leaves and
software-drain/software-upgrade holder identities. Configuration operations must
use a distinct manager authorization contract on the same disruptive-mutation
lease family. They must not synthesize software-upgrade objects or reuse SWIM
permits for unrelated configuration actions. Maintenance acquisition, acknowledgement,
managed-worker admission and lease recovery remain outstanding.

### Combined tag definition precedence

Combined `templates` and `inventory` reports now implement the pinned upstream
name-keyed union: inventory definitions override template definitions of the same
tag. Unique template tags remain in the template section; overridden tags are
counted and reported once under inventory. This is independent of section order.
Both raw lists are validated before merging, including shadowed entries, and an
unselected inventory section cannot silently influence a template report.

Combined apply now uses the same precedence rule through the canonical template
executor. Single-section apply remains supported and conflicting owners are still
excluded across the shared namespace.

### Combined template and inventory tag apply

`managedSections: [templates, inventory]` now accepts inventory tag definitions
alongside template projects, objects, commits and associations. Both section
claims are reserved atomically under the same config UID. Inventory tags override
same-named template definitions before the existing executor compiles the source;
there is one effective tag mutation and one durable task journal. The journal uses
a stable templates namespace independent of section order, while status reports
resource counts for both sections without double-counting shared tags.

See `examples/configs/catalyst-center/merged-tags-apply.yaml`. Device assignment or
provisioning fields are still rejected, and other multi-section apply combinations
remain unsupported. A transition from a single-section config can release a
Prepared or Verified old operation; accepted/uncertain work retains its source
binding and requires recovery before new intent proceeds. Ownership itself is
retained; this is not an owner-transfer or pruning implementation.

### Kubernetes journal qualification

The lab now runs the matching manager and controller-worker image
`cvk-catc-nac:20261012-0146d7a983a4`, with the additive configuration-journal CRD
schema. Device-worker images remain pinned to the previous tested image.

A combined inventory/template manifest was first observed in report mode with one
absent tag, then applied. The worker was replaced after an Accepted task receipt;
the same operation/task advanced through verification to InSync. A second source
generation updated the tag while the manager restarted. Both section owner records
survived, and both task journals settled. See the October 12 evidence for receipts.

The live `catc-nac-journal-qualification` config and its isolated
`CVK-NAC-Journal-0146d7a983a4` tag are retained as the owned baseline for continued
qualification. Reuse this config identity for further template/inventory testing;
creating another owner will correctly conflict. This qualification does not cover
ambiguous task recovery, owner transfer, pruning, physical-device authorization,
or all remaining resource types.

## Switching network profiles

The native `network_profiles` compiler accepts the pinned module's `switching`
collection: `name`, `dayn_templates`, `onboarding_templates`, and `sites`.
Profile creation/update and additive site assignments use the existing REST
transport, controller ownership, operation journal, task polling and independent
readback. The compiler rejects unknown fields and collections before API reads.

Templates must already exist. Project-qualified references are preferred;
unqualified names must be unique across the observed projects. Regular and
composite references resolve to base template UUIDs. Two aliases selecting the
same UUID are rejected. Verification binds the resolved template UUID set as
well as the profile UUID, so a replaced dependency cannot satisfy an earlier
operation. All requested dependencies are checked before the first write.

The legacy profile detail endpoint requires `populated=true`; its default
response contains metadata without template attributes. Populated detail is
checked against the listed UUID, name and switching namespace. Template
membership comparison tolerates ordering and omitted empty groups. Unsupported
attribute groups are rejected before replacement rather than dropped. The
server-materialized `site.settings` subtree is preserved opaquely during
updates and excluded from drift and operation hashes; it is never logged or
published in Kubernetes status.

Site assignment resolves an existing canonical site path and submits only
missing associations. Existing unrelated associations are retained. Both the
site UUID and the profile UUID are pinned during verification. Assigning a
profile to a site does not deploy a template to a device.

See `examples/configs/catalyst-center/network-profiles-report.yaml` and
`examples/configs/catalyst-center/network-profiles-apply.yaml`.
Use the same config identity when switching from report to apply. Global scope
and Retain policies remain required. Automatic creation of dependencies across
sections, managed-site scope, wireless profiles, association removal and profile
deletion are not yet implemented. Whole-section parity remains false.

The isolated lab flow passed profile creation, regular-template association,
site assignment, subsequent template removal/restoration, zero-drift readback
and verified fixture cleanup. See the [qualification evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-12/README.md#switching-network-profiles-and-site-assignments).
Onboarding/composite reference lab coverage and deployment of this profile code
to the Kubernetes worker remain pending.

## System external authentication

`system_settings.external_authentication` accepts `enabled` and the optional
`aaa_attribute` name. The pinned module's default for `enabled` is false when
this object is present. Policy-server and ISE definitions are still rejected
explicitly; they are not ignored while applying these global authentication
settings. The model must describe an already configured authentication service
before enabling external authentication.

The two endpoints return synchronous HTTP 200 responses, not task receipts.
Their executors validate the response shape and use the existing controller
journal's durable submission permit. A successfully recorded response enters
`Verifying`, where an independent API read confirms the requested value. No
synthetic task ID is created. HTTP 202, missing or malformed responses, and
transport failures retain uncertainty. A crash or lost Kubernetes acknowledgement
cannot become permission to repeat the request. Asynchronous executors retain
their existing task receipt and polling flow.

See `examples/configs/catalyst-center/system-external-auth-report.yaml` and
`system-external-auth-apply.yaml`. The examples explicitly disable external
authentication; they are policy examples, not discovery manifests. Custom
attribute removal and authentication-server definitions/integration remain
pending, as does secret-reference injection for those server definitions.

The lab currently reports no authentication-policy servers, external
authentication disabled, and an empty custom attribute. Both mutation endpoints
reject requests without a registered AAA server. The executor now checks that
prerequisite before preparing a mutation. Live report/no-op coverage is distinct
from live mutation qualification, which remains pending server registration.

## Authentication-policy servers

System-settings reports now accept explicit non-ISE server metadata under
`authentication_and_policy_servers.aaa`: literal `ip_address`, RADIUS/TACACS
protocol selections and ports, retries, and timeout. The reader uses
`instanceUuid` identities and canonical IP addresses. Duplicate IDs/addresses
and malformed inventories stop planning. Its projection intentionally excludes
shared secrets and other credential values, even if the appliance returns them.
See `examples/configs/catalyst-center/policy-servers-report.yaml`.

Native create-only registration is implemented internally for isolated
qualification. It refuses to adopt an existing address and verifies task
completion plus returned UUID and metadata. It does not establish that a
RADIUS/TACACS service accepts the credential. The subsequent manifest execution
contract below adds version-bound non-ISE writes. ISE integration and key wrapping
remain outstanding. A metadata report cannot
claim that masked or unreadable credentials match desired state.

Subsequent isolated registration qualification created a temporary non-ISE
RADIUS server pointing at the lab runner. With that prerequisite present, the
disabled-flag request and two custom-attribute changes passed native readback.
The test restored the empty attribute/disabled baseline and deleted the server.
This qualifies those API operations, not actual RADIUS authentication, external
login enablement, durable credential rotation or manifest-driven server writes.

### Projected credential snapshots

The adapter now has an internal resolver for the common worker's existing
per-key intent Secret projections. It requires both a controller-authorized
source alias and an exact destination supplied by the product parser. It uses
the common config/section/path/source mapping, confines filesystem reads to
the projection root, and supports Kubernetes atomic-writer symlinks. It never
reads complete Secret objects or creates a second credential store.

Injection makes an in-memory model copy and accepts only missing/null object
leaves beneath existing parents. RFC 6901 escaping and canonical array indices
are checked; inline values, appended elements and object replacement are
rejected. Credential bytes are preserved, bounded and excluded from diagnostic
errors. The journal checks the ephemeral snapshot before preparation, before
issuing the submission permit and immediately before the API callback. Alias
remapping, revocation, identity changes and changed projected material stop the
write. Re-reading an identical value after a projection symlink rotation is
allowed. These checks do not claim atomicity with concurrent Secret updates;
the eventual request must use the captured bytes.

The resolver is used by the server-only AAA manifest compiler; other secret
destinations remain gated. An in-memory snapshot is not evidence of a credential
applied before a worker restart. Tests cover rotation at both sides of the submission permit
and prohibit replay after reconstructing a snapshot for an uncertain operation.

The journal now supports explicit positive write-only version counters bound
to the operation's credential paths and authorized alias/Secret-key mapping.
Both submission checks require the exact persisted binding; absent or pruned
fields cannot authorize a write. Generic metadata verification cannot mark a
credential-bearing operation Verified. A separate internal completion path
requires a correlated successful task and the resource executor's observed UUID,
then records Verified and the applied-version receipt in one status update.
The receipt is bound to the config UID, resource UUID and operation ID and
survives journal-slot release. Release refuses a missing applied receipt.
Neither credential values nor their digests are stored.

These mechanisms are tested through the AAA manifest reconciler, including
worker reconstruction, rotation, no-op convergence, lost acknowledgements and
schema pruning. Receipt count and serialized-size capacity are checked before
submission. A receipt proves the controller accepted the requested version
through a successful task; it does not prove an external RADIUS/TACACS service
accepts the credential. The updated CRD and matching worker are now installed
in the lab; the live manifest qualification is recorded below.

### Versioned AAA manifest execution

`examples/configs/catalyst-center/policy-servers-apply.yaml` shows the bounded
server-only contract. Resolve ports, retries (1..3) and timeout (2..20) upstream,
use a positive `shared_secret_version` counter, and reference the absent/null
`shared_secret` leaf through a controller-authorized `secretRefs` alias. Inline
credentials are rejected. ISE uses the separate integration contract below.
RADIUS key wrapping uses the separately
versioned credential contract below. Scope is global and retention
is Retain. External-authentication settings may be included using the combined
execution contract below.

The selected Secret key must contain a JSON object with exactly `version` and
`value` fields. The integer `version` must equal the model's
`shared_secret_version`; `value` is the non-empty credential string. Both fields
must be in the same key, so Kubernetes projects them atomically. Bare strings,
duplicate/unknown fields and mismatched versions are rejected. This wrapper is
the CVK credential transport format, not an added NetAsCode model field. Only
the decoded credential is sent to Catalyst Center; neither field's containing
Secret payload is persisted in the journal.

Update the projected wrapper and model counter for each rotation. Their order
does not authorize a mismatched write: if the worker sees either update first,
it waits for a matching pair. The regression test advances the model counter
while retaining the old projection and confirms zero API writes and no new
journal operation; convergence resumes after projection catches up. Finish an
in-flight operation before advancing its credential version.

New addresses are created. Existing addresses require a receipt owned by the
same config UID and bound to the same controller server UUID. Matching metadata
and version/source references converge without resubmitting credentials. An
increased version triggers an update; decreasing the version or remapping its
source without an increment fails planning. Array order is not server identity.
Metadata updates use the API's full-object PUT, including the projected secret.
Increment the version whenever that Secret value changes: the adapter cannot
compare write-only credentials or detect a remote credential edit, and does not
use secret digests as a substitute. Protocol additions may select RADIUS_TACACS;
protocol removal/replacement requires a separate lifecycle. Externally added
ISE and externally managed key-wrapping configuration are not overwritten.

The live API qualification created a temporary non-ISE server, performed a
version-driven update, verified the same UUID and no-op planning, and removed
the fixture with baseline readback. It used in-memory fixture bindings, not a
deployed Kubernetes journal. Subsequent real-worker qualification installed
`cvk-catc-nac:20261012-43741637f05c` and the receipt schema. The manifest created
the server, recovered the same accepted task after worker replacement, rejected
a newer model counter while the old projection remained, and converged after
the version-2 wrapper arrived. The same server UUID and two distinct operation
receipts were verified. Cleanup removed the server, Secret and alias and restored
the zero-server baseline. `catc-aaa-qualification` remains report-only with its
config UID and ownership retained for future tests; reuse that identity for
system-settings qualification instead of creating a competing owner. The three
XE nodes and their existing workers remained healthy. This still does not test
an actual RADIUS service or external login enablement.

### Combined server and external-authentication execution

`examples/configs/catalyst-center/system-settings-apply.yaml` updates the same
config identity as the server-only example and adds external-authentication
settings. This preserves section ownership and the existing server receipts.
The compiler validates every selected field before resolving projections or
reading the appliance. The executor observes external-authentication settings
and fully plans the server collection before returning any write.

Server operations use asynchronous tasks and UUID-bound credential receipts.
Only when all desired servers converge can the executor return a dependent
external-authentication write. Those operations use the existing validated
synchronous receipt and independent readback. Resource identities distinguish
credential verification from singleton verification even when a CRD has pruned
credential fields; a server operation cannot fall through to metadata-only
verification. Every operation still uses the same controller-wide journal.

The combined manifest test reconstructs the worker between reconciliations,
verifies server-before-flag-before-attribute ordering, then rotates a credential
without repeating unchanged external-authentication settings. Read failures
on any selected surface prevent a write. The local suite also verifies strict
field validation and the combined example.

Live qualification installed `cvk-catc-nac:20261012-c3d4574c3167` and reused the
retained `catc-aaa-qualification` config UID. The version-3 server application
receipt preceded the custom-attribute operation. The worker was replaced after
that synchronous operation reached Verifying with no task ID; its replacement
completed the same journal entry and reached InSync. API readback confirmed the
custom attribute and disabled external authentication. Cleanup restored the
empty attribute using DELETE, removed the exact server UUID and deleted the
temporary Secret/alias. The config remains report-only, its ownership and
receipt retained for subsequent qualification. Final XE node/worker health and
the existing inventory/template configuration passed. ISE, live key-wrapping acceptance and
actual external RADIUS authentication remain unqualified.


### RADIUS key-wrapping credentials

`examples/configs/catalyst-center/policy-servers-keywrap-apply.yaml` extends the
non-ISE AAA contract with NetAsCode's `protocols.radius.enable_key_wrap` object.
Both `encryption_key_version` and `message_key_version` must be positive explicit
counters. Reference the absent/null `encryption_key` and `message_key` leaves
through separately authorized aliases, using the same atomic version/value
Secret-key format as the shared secret. Inline credentials are rejected.

The existing executor submits all three credentials on full-object writes and
records their versions independently in the shared journal. Adding key wrapping
to an owned plaintext server and rotating an individual key are supported.
Reordering the AAA array preserves resource identity; duplicate bindings,
rollback, stale projections and source changes without a counter increment are
rejected. Removing wrapping or overwriting externally managed wrapping is not
supported. Successful task and UUID/metadata verification prove configuration
acceptance, not authentication against a real RADIUS service.

Fixture tests cover create, independent rotation, convergence, stale projections,
removal refusal and malformed bindings. The live qualification is gated by
`CATC_KEYWRAP_EXECUTION=isolated-lab-server` within the isolated policy-server
test. Worker-level key-wrapping qualification remains separate from this API
executor test; neither establishes whole-section system-settings parity.


The 2026-10-12 live executor test exposed a compatibility gap: the API accepted
an update containing `encryptionScheme: KEYWRAP` and both keys, and its task
completed successfully, but subsequent GET still returned an empty encryption
scheme. CVK refused convergence. Independent key rotation was therefore not
reached. The isolated server was retained for inspection before targeted
cleanup. This is **not live-qualified key-wrapping support**. Some published
[edit API schemas](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/edit-authentication-and-policy-server-access-configuration/)
mark these fields read-only. Resolve appliance/API support before enabling this
flow in the lab worker; successful task completion alone is insufficient.


### ISE registration and integration execution

`examples/configs/catalyst-center/ise-policy-server-apply.yaml` supplies the
pinned `authentication_and_policy_servers.ise` object. The executor now accepts
explicit IP, FQDN, username, pxGrid flags, resolved protocol ports/retries/timeout
and positive shared-secret/password counters. Both credentials use authorized,
atomic version/value projections; inline values are rejected. Optional RADIUS
key wrapping uses the same three-key contract and remains subject to the live
API limitation above. Global scope and Retain still apply.

Registration and credential updates reuse the policy-server executor and its
UUID-bound credential receipts. Password rotation is independent of the shared
secret; source changes without a counter increment, stale projections, adoption,
server-type changes and replacement of an existing ISE at another address are
refused. The observer decodes only ISE metadata, excluding passwords and
server-generated subscriber names from comparison. Requests supply the
subscriber name from the IP, matching the pinned upstream module.

The payload and sequence follow the pinned
[NetAsCode system-settings module](https://github.com/netascode/terraform-catalystcenter-nac-catalystcenter/blob/a435555fe828f03cf3311d52fe1ab6572a247916/cc_system_settings.tf)
and Cisco's
[ISE integration status API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-4/cisco-ise-server-integration-status/).

After registration converges, a separate shared-journal operation accepts the
certificate when the matching ISE integration status requires user input. It
uses the native `integrate-ise/{id}` endpoint, validates the synchronous empty
JSON acknowledgement, and verifies the same server UUID through
`ise-integration-status`. Pending, failed, contradictory or other-server status
cannot release the operation or allow dependent external-authentication writes.
The shared journal retains uncertain acknowledgements and prevents replay after
worker reconstruction. No separate ISE retry engine or credential store is added.

Fixture tests cover registration, independent password rotation, stale
projections, status correlation, pending/failed status, generated-field exclusion,
acknowledgement refusal, restart fencing and example compilation. **Live ISE
qualification is pending a reachable lab ISE and its credential references.**
The subsequent global-credential worker rollout includes this code, but does not
qualify ISE integration. Task acceptance
and current UUID-correlated integration status do not prove that every external
RADIUS authentication attempt succeeds or establish a new authentication event
for each credential version. ISE lifecycle removal remains outstanding; this is not whole-section parity.


### ISE reporting and manifest recovery verification

`examples/configs/catalyst-center/ise-policy-server-report.yaml` reports ISE
registration metadata and integration state without reading projected Secrets
or submitting changes. It uses the same IP, FQDN, username, pxGrid and protocol
parsers as execution. Credential values and version counters are rejected in
report input; returned passwords and generated subscriber names are excluded
from the observation model. Reports explicitly state that credentials are not
compared.

A missing ISE produces separate registration and integration additions without
querying integration status for a nonexistent server. An existing ISE's status
must refer to its observed UUID. Pending integration is reported as drift;
failed, malformed or other-server status prevents a successful observation.
Successful metadata reporting cannot establish credential correctness.

The combined ISE manifest now has a full reconciler fixture test with actual
projected credential files and persisted fake-Kubernetes journal state. It
reconstructs the worker on every reconcile, confirms registration receipts before
certificate acceptance, retains the synchronous operation while integration is
pending, and verifies integration before enabling external authentication.
Subsequent password-counter changes cannot submit with an old projection; a
matching projection performs one update, retains the unchanged shared-secret
version and converges without replaying certificate acceptance or login changes.
This is regression evidence, **not live appliance qualification**. Live ISE
access is still needed to qualify those API response contracts and behavior.


### Global device credential definitions

`examples/configs/catalyst-center/device-credentials-apply.yaml` defines CLI,
HTTPS read/write, SNMPv2 read/write and SNMPv3 credentials using the pinned
`network_settings.device_credentials` collections. Names map to API descriptions;
HTTP ports and SNMP security fields must be resolved explicitly. Each active
secret requires its matching positive NetAsCode version counter and an
authorized `secretRefs` projection containing an atomic version/value object.
CLI uses `enable` and `enable_version`, matching the upstream model. Inline
values are rejected, including values for inactive SNMP security modes.

One executor handles the six API envelope types. Create uses a one-item array;
update uses the existing credential UUID in a single object. The shared
credential resolver, counter checks, task journal and durable UUID/version
receipts are reused. Existing definitions without a matching receipt cannot be
adopted; replacements, rollback, unversioned source changes and removal of a
managed credential leaf are refused. A pruned version binding cannot release a
verified global-credential operation. The reader retains metadata only, even
when Catalyst Center returns credential values.

The manifest contract is global and Retain-only. Credential definitions may be
combined with supported network settings and existing-site assignments as
described below. Removal/pruning and live device authentication remain pending.
SNMPv3 AUTHPRIV and AUTHNOPRIV have execution contracts; NOAUTHNOPRIV is parsed but
cannot yet execute because ownership must be recorded independently of secret
versions. It must not be represented with a fabricated credential counter.

All six types passed full manifest/restart/projection-lag fixture tests and
isolated live native create/rotation/readback/cleanup tests (SNMPv3 AUTHPRIV).
The deployed worker subsequently passed create/restart/rotation, projection-lag
refusal, report-mode transition and cleanup for all six types. See the
[native evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-12/global-credential-qualification.json) and
[worker evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-12/global-credential-worker-qualification.json).
No full `network_settings` parity is claimed.


Global credential definitions also support metadata-only reporting through
`examples/configs/catalyst-center/device-credentials-report.yaml`. Reports compare
names, usernames, ports and selected SNMP security metadata, without projecting
Secrets or comparing masked credential values. Credential counters and values
are rejected in report input. Reporting may include other supported network
settings; credential apply remains a separate bounded execution contract.
Metadata-only input cannot bypass the version-bound apply gate.


### Named device credential assignments

`network_settings` now supports the pinned model's `cli_credentials`,
`https_read_credentials`, `https_write_credentials`, `snmpv2_read_credentials`,
`snmpv2_write_credentials`, and `snmpv3_credentials` references on existing
`sites.areas`, `sites.buildings`, and `sites.floors`. A reference resolves by
credential type and exact description; a missing or ambiguous name fails the
entire observation before any write. There is no fallback to a global default
when a declared name is missing. Assignment-only manifests use an explicit
`network_settings: {}` and the existing network-settings section owner.

The executor updates one declared slot, preserving omitted slots. It records
the site UUID as the journal target and credential UUID as its parent dependency;
replacement of either identity prevents verification. Each accepted task must
complete and the local-only `deviceCredentials?_inherited=false` readback must
match before journal release. No credentials are copied into the assignment
payload, journal, status, or examples. Controller fixture tests rebuild the
reconciler between operations, verify all six assignments and no-op reconciliation,
and cover missing dependencies, incomplete observations, and credential replacement.

Reporting distinguishes local assignment, inherited `null`, and explicitly
disabled `{}`. **Explicit-null removal is not qualified for execution.** The lab
completed `{credentialsId: null}` successfully but returned a disabled slot, not
inheritance. A supervised top-level-null correction failed with `NCND00010`.
Apply rejects null before submission rather than claiming inheritance or trying
alternate mutations automatically. The temporary credential and area from that
investigation were removed; see the inheritance qualification evidence.

Global assignment, prune/ownership transfer, and real-device credential
synchronization remain pending. Combined credential-definition creation plus
assignment is implemented and deployed-worker create/restart/no-op qualification
is recorded below. This addition assigns controller settings; it does not change device
passwords or prove successful device authentication. See
`site-credentials-apply.yaml` and `site-credentials-report.yaml` for references.

The local/inherited/disabled distinction follows Cisco's
[site credential read API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-9/get-device-credential-settings-for-a-site/).
The lab removal behavior differs from the documented
[update API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-9/update-device-credential-settings-for-a-site/)
and the provider's nested-null inheritance assumption; the evidence and execution
gate take precedence over assuming task success proves semantic convergence.

Native assignment qualification passed for all six credential types on a new
empty area, including task completion, UUID readback, no-op reconciliation, and
isolated cleanup. SNMPv3 used AUTHPRIV. The original credential inventory IDs
were preserved and the temporary area was deleted. This is resource-executor
evidence, not deployed-worker or real-device authentication qualification.


### Combined credential definitions, settings, and assignments

One `network_settings` apply manifest may now contain versioned
`device_credentials`, supported network/IPAM settings, and named credential
references on existing sites. The compiler preserves the original secret JSON
pointers and feeds the remainder through the existing network executor. It does
not add a second task loop, credential store, or controller-provider mechanism.

The planner validates every downstream site/read/reference before releasing a
credential write. A missing credential reference is allowed during this preflight
only if that exact type/name is declared in the same manifest. Credential create
or rotation operations run first. Only after the shared journal has persisted all
required UUID/version receipts can settings and assignment operations proceed.
Assignments never receive placeholder UUIDs. The strict standalone assignment
