path remains unchanged. Explicit-null removal remains rejected during compilation.

Fixture qualification covers all six types, each as both standalone and combined
manifests, with a fresh reconciler on every tick, real temporary secret projections,
credential-before-NTP/assignment assertions, independent version rotation, stale
projection refusal, and no duplicate assignment after rotation. Missing sites,
undeclared credential references, incomplete reads, and unsupported intent prevent
writes. Live combined-worker create/settings/assignment qualification is recorded
below. See `network-credentials-combined-apply.yaml`.


The deployed `cvk-catc-nac:20261012-c3dc1d2bffb8` worker qualified one combined
manifest on a newly created empty area: six credential definitions, one NTP
setting, and six site assignments reached `InSync`. Every downstream operation
was observed with all six persisted UUID/version receipts present. Deleting the
worker during an accepted CLI assignment resulted in the replacement pod
verifying the same operation and task, with no replacement task observed.
Changing only the polling cadence triggered a new-generation reconciliation that
returned `InSync` without an operation or credential receipt change.

The capture contains 12 distinct task IDs for the 13 resources. The first CLI
credential was already complete when the watcher attached; its completion evidence
is its persisted UUID/version receipt and subsequent authoritative readback. The
original watcher's exact task-count assertion failed for this capture gap, not a
runtime failure. Separate completion checks verified every resulting resource,
restart recovery, and the new-generation no-op. The evidence keeps this distinction
explicit rather than inventing the missing task ID.

Cleanup first reached a report-only `InSync` boundary, then disabled the isolated
slots under supervision, deleted the six credentials and empty area, verified the
original credential ID sets, removed the temporary Secret/aliases, and restored
the prior report spec on the same owner. Ownership and application receipts were
retained. All three Cisco nodes remained Ready with unchanged direct-device worker
images; the existing inventory/template configuration remained `InSync`.

This qualifies the combined create/settings/assignment path and restart/no-op
behavior. Combined credential rotation still has fixture coverage rather than
live qualification. Inheritance removal, real-device password synchronization,
real-device authentication, and other SNMPv3 modes are not established by this run.


### Inventory discovery jobs

The `inventory.discovery` model now supports explicit global-credential references,
IPv4 SINGLE/RANGE/MULTI RANGE/CDP/LLDP/CIDR input validation, protocol order, address
filters, neighbor depths, NETCONF port, retry/timeout, and preferred management IP
metadata. Unknown fields and inline credentials are rejected, including secret
lists; credential material is never decoded from discovery API responses. Only
global scope is executable at present. Credential names must resolve uniquely
across all six global credential types; the upstream map merge's implicit winner
for colliding names is not used.

Create execution shares the existing ownership, task journal, transport, timeout
and recovery handling. The executor validates all declared jobs and credential
dependencies before releasing a write. Once a task completes, verification reads
its exact `discoveryId`, checks it against the uniquely named job, compares declared
metadata and credential UUIDs, and waits for `Complete`/`Inactive`. An unchanged
completed job causes no request. A changed existing job is rejected: the pinned
upstream schema requires replacement, and CVK has not yet implemented the
ownership-qualified replacement/delete contract. It must not silently accept the
new model or implicitly rerun discovery.

Reporting can combine jobs with inventory tags/device observations. A tag-only
projection rejects discovery intent instead of discarding it. Apply manifests can
combine templates and inventory discovery through the existing configuration group:
inventory retains tag precedence, all dependencies are observed before the first
write, and both sections are claimed atomically by one owner. Discovery uses a
separate resource prefix in the shared journal; existing tag-only manifests retain
their previous operation identities. Restart tests verify tag creation once,
task-correlated discovery completion, no-op reconciliation, and section counts.
`discovery-templates-apply.yaml` illustrates this composition. Its deployed-worker
SINGLE/SSH qualification passed on existing .101 with an accepted-task restart. Standalone discovery or discovery plus tags can also
execute through the inventory section; physical device-changing intent still follows
its separate admission gate.

Fixture tests cover restarts, a task completing before the scan, no-op reconciliation,
changed-job refusal, cross-type name ambiguity, malformed/repeating pages, mismatched
task/job identities, and unsupported/secret-bearing input. Native qualification
against the already-managed `.101` switch passed using its existing registered
credential references: task-correlated create, complete metadata readback, no-op,
unchanged device UUID/serial, temporary-job deletion, and restoration of the original
discovery IDs. Only SINGLE IPv4/SSH was live-qualified. Other discovery modes and
optional field write/readback combinations still need live qualification. See `discovery-apply.yaml`, `discovery-report.yaml`, and the
`discovery-qualification.json` evidence.

A completed discovery job does not prove successful device authentication or full
inventory collection. Report mode now enumerates paginated job/device outcomes
and publishes bounded CLI/SNMP/NETCONF success, failure and unverified counts, plus
Managed/Reachable collection counts. Empty or unknown outcomes are unverified;
raw errors and unknown status strings are never published. These are observations
for the selected discovery jobs, not a fresh authentication probe or globally
deduplicated inventory. Operational failures do not cause replacement of an
otherwise converged job. Missing/null/duplicate or incomplete pages fail observation.
Inline secret projection, per-site scope, replacement/rerun, combined credential creation and prune remain
open. The existing SWIM and direct-device paths are unchanged.

API contracts were checked against Cisco's
[start discovery](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-5/start-discovery/)
and [discovery range read](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-5/get-discoveries-by-range/)
references and the pinned provider resource/model, then checked against the lab.


### Device roles

Resolved `inventory.devices` entries in `ASSIGN` state can declare `device_role`
and `role_source` together. The pinned roles are ACCESS, CORE, DISTRIBUTION and
BORDER ROUTER; sources are MANUAL and AUTO. CVK requires both fields rather than
silently substituting defaults. Omitted role intent retains existing behavior.
Report mode compares both fields against complete controller inventory and counts
the role independently of site assignment and tag memberships. Missing or unknown
observed values fail observation instead of being treated as a match.
See `device-roles-report.yaml`.

The native role executor uses the existing paginated inventory reader, physical
selector resolver, configuration write contract and task receipt. It preflights
all targets, binds each write to a UUID and serial, and verifies both role fields
on the same physical identity. A task receipt alone is not completion evidence.
Tests cover recovery with a reconstructed executor, no-op, replaced identities,
unresolved references and incomplete metadata. The manifest compiler continues to
reject device apply until shared mutation admission and durable lease recovery
are integrated. No reporting support is presented as permission to write.

Native read-only qualification confirmed ACCESS/AUTO on all three lab switches
and a no-op plan with UUID/serial resolution. See
`device-role-noop-qualification.json`; no role change was attempted.

This is partial resource coverage: PROVISION/AP model branches, manifest execution,
role changes on the lab, and AUTO-role behavior after topology recalculation still
need qualification. API semantics were checked against the pinned provider's
`device_role` model/resource and Cisco's
[Update Device role](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/update-device-role/)
contract.


### Deployed discovery qualification

Image `cvk-catc-nac:20261012-cf64cdf17b9e` includes discovery, outcome reporting,
combined template/inventory execution and the native role implementation. The
manager and Catalyst Center worker rolled out successfully. XE application and
network worker images remained unchanged, and all three bound Cisco nodes were
Ready after the run. The retained inventory/templates owner was extended with
one temporary SINGLE/SSH discovery for existing `.101` using registered global
credential names.

The worker was replaced after task acceptance. Its replacement resumed the same
operation and task, verified the completed discovery, and reached InSync. The
UUID and serial of `.101` remained unchanged. Report mode initially showed
successful CLI/SNMP but incomplete collection; later the API and refreshed report
showed Managed/Reachable. NETCONF was NOT-PROVIDED because the manifest did not
request a NETCONF port. This verifies honest reporting of asynchronous collection,
not an assertion that all protocols succeeded.

The original manifest was restored before the temporary job was deleted. The
original discovery inventory and controller journal were then verified. Evidence:
`discovery-worker-qualification.json`. This closes the bounded combined-worker
execution/restart/reporting gap; it does not qualify replacement, per-site scope,
inline credentials, device-role changes or physical device provisioning.


### Global credential assignments

The pinned `sites_to_creds_map` derives the Global entry from `sites.areas` with
`name: Global` and no `parent_name`. This form now resolves to the existing site
of type `global` and uses the same credential assignment executor as child sites.
It does not create a new area. All six named credential types retain the same
preflight, task receipt, UUID-bound verification and omission semantics. Explicit
null remains blocked for apply because inheritance removal is not qualified.

The example `global-credentials-apply.yaml` manages `network_settings` through its
existing owner. Parentless names other than Global, null parents, and Global site
pool reservations are rejected. A root entry may also bind a named network profile;
expressing that profile twice via `sites.global` and `sites.areas` is rejected.
Combined geometry reporting with a root area marker remains outside the supported
`sites` projection; this addition targets the network-settings model.

Tests exercise all six root assignments through reconciler reconstruction,
completion, no-op and removal refusal, and verify that root handling does not alter
subsequent area identities. Live root mutation and inheritance propagation remain
unqualified; child-site mutation evidence does not establish root qualification.

Lab read-only qualification returned null for all six Global slots. This proves
the root response shape only; no existing named assignment was available for a
live no-op test. See `global-credential-assignment-read.json`.


### Fabric L3 virtual-network definitions

`fabric.l3_virtual_networks` now accepts explicit name objects for global,
unanchored definitions. Report and apply use the existing paginated transport,
section ownership and write-ahead journal. A missing user-defined network is
created with a one-element request and a task receipt, then independently read
back before the journal advances. Worker-reconstruction tests verify create and
no-op behavior. Existing memberships are retained, matching global definition
ownership; no fabric or device association is requested by this model subset.

Missing INFRA_VN or DEFAULT_VN resources are not created. Existing anchored
networks, unsupported fields (including anchor declarations), duplicate identities,
malformed inventory, and unresolved collections prevent writes. New-definition
verification requires no associations or anchor. Name changes retain the old
resource under Retain policy rather than deleting or renaming it.

See `fabric-l3-apply.yaml` and `fabric-l3-report.yaml`. This is partial fabric
coverage: site and zone associations, anchors, merge settings, fabric devices,
other fabric resources, pruning and deployed-worker qualification remain open.
Contracts follow the pinned provider and Cisco's
[add L3 virtual networks](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/add-layer-3-virtual-networks/)
and [list L3 virtual networks](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/get-layer-3-virtual-networks/)
APIs.


The first fabric lab run is **not qualified**. The appliance rejected
`CVK-Test-20261012-201929` with NCHS20631 (malformed name), without creating a
resource. A shorter uppercase fixture `CVK_12202211` was accepted as task
`01a131c8-d578-7032-a183-3dc6223368a3`, but the task failed with NCSP11000 during
business-intent preprocessing. The task tree did not identify a more specific
cause. Readback showed only DEFAULT_VN and INFRA_VN; no temporary resource required
cleanup. Exact name constraints and the backend prerequisite/failure need further
investigation. See `fabric-l3-qualification.json`. Fixture success is not evidence
that this lab can create fabric definitions.


### Confirmed task failures

A correlated Catalyst Center task with `isError: true` now produces the
`ControllerTaskFailed` condition and Failed configuration phase, rather than an
observation-failure message in Waiting. Only a bounded `NC` plus two uppercase
letters and five digits machine code may be published. Missing or malformed codes
fall back to the generic failure message. Raw failure reason, progress and task
data are not decoded or placed in status.

The Accepted journal operation and receipt remain intact; there is no automatic
replay or release based on a failed task. Existing timeout behavior still retains
the operation for recovery. Restart fixtures prove that a failed fabric task is
not treated as successful even when a matching resource appears in inventory.
Foreign task IDs and timestamps still fail correlation before diagnostics are
classified. These changes are local to configuration execution and do not change
SWIM handoff or direct-device lease behavior.

A lab prerequisite read found zero policy servers and zero registered ISE servers.
That is relevant deployment context, not a proven explanation of NCSP11000. No
new prerequisite rejection has been inferred from this incomplete evidence.


### Global IP transit definitions

`fabric.transits` supports explicit `name`, `type: IP_BASED_TRANSIT`,
`routing_protocol_name: BGP`, and integer or decimal-string
`autonomous_system_number` (1–4294967295). `create_per_site: false` is accepted;
per-site expansion and SDA control-plane device bindings remain pending. Type,
protocol and ASN differences require explicit replacement and are rejected
before any mutation. Retain policies do not automatically delete definitions.

The fabric compiler composes transit and global L3 definition executors through
the existing journal group. It preflights both collections before submitting the
first write. Restart/no-op, replacement refusal, malformed inventory and
pagination are covered by fixtures. Examples: `fabric-transits-apply.yaml` and
`fabric-transits-report.yaml` under `examples/configs/catalyst-center`.

Live qualification failed with **NCSP11008**: the appliance reported that its
ConnectivityDomain application package was unavailable. Task
`01a131d3-9a96-7e67-8cc6-ae49aacf1fd7` was retained as evidence; inventory read-back
was empty. No replay or cleanup was necessary. This is not worker qualification.


### Wireless interface definitions

The resolved `wireless.interfaces` collection accepts `name` and `vlan_id`
(integer 1–4094). Create and VLAN update use the existing configuration journal,
task validation and independent read-back. Updates retain the interface UUID;
a same-name replacement cannot satisfy the accepted operation. Unspecified
interfaces are retained, and no device deployment is performed. The appliance's built-in `management` interface is readable with VLAN 0; its reserved name
is rejected in manifests. Missing VLAN values still fail inventory validation. Unknown fields
and other wireless collections fail validation before API calls.

Examples: `wireless-interfaces-apply.yaml` and
`wireless-interfaces-report.yaml` in `examples/configs/catalyst-center`.
Manifest create/update/restart/no-op and UUID replacement refusal are fixture
tested. Other wireless resources, prune/delete and deployed-worker
qualification remain pending. API contract:
[Create Interface](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/create-interface/),
[Get Interfaces](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/get-interfaces/),
and pinned provider 0.6.1 wireless interface resource.


Native lab qualification passed for wireless interfaces: temporary
`CVK_12204015` was created with VLAN 3998, updated to 3999 with the same UUID,
verified unchanged on subsequent planning, and deleted. Baseline inventory was
restored. Task IDs and scope limits are recorded in
[wireless interface evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-12/wireless-interface-qualification.json).
This does not establish deployed-worker or device deployment qualification.


### Wireless pre-authentication ACL definitions

`wireless.security_settings.pre_auth_acls` maps the pinned model's `name`,
`acl_name`, `ipv6_enabled`, `include_auto_generated_rules`, `rules`, and
`walled_garden_urls`. Rule order is retained. Address families, protocol sets,
prefix lengths and port ranges are validated before API access. The pinned
module defaults apply: ACL name equals list name, IPv6 false, automatic rules
true, prefixes 32, ports `0-65535`. Resolved input should explicitly override
these defaults where needed, especially IPv6 prefix lengths.

Omitted URLs are not owned; update preserves the observed set. An explicit
empty URL list requests removal. Unknown/null fields fail validation. Rules must
be an explicit list. Renames are new retained definitions rather than implicit
deletes. Updates verify the recorded UUID, and interface/ACL combined manifests
preflight all collections through the existing configuration group and journal.
This configures controller definitions; device and SSID deployment remain separate.

Examples: `wireless-acls-apply.yaml` and `wireless-acls-report.yaml` under
`examples/configs/catalyst-center`. Manifest create/update/restart/no-op,
UUID mismatch, malformed inventory, and cross-collection preflight are fixture
tested. Native and deployed-worker qualification are recorded separately.


The lab rejects the upstream port default `0-65535` with `NCND13014`, requiring
ports 1–65535. CVK does not silently rewrite the pinned model's default. The ACL
examples and live fixture explicitly specify `source_ports: 1-65535` and a
nonzero destination port. Exported models using port 0 need that explicit
compatibility adjustment for this appliance. The first rejected fixture was
absent from inventory; a diagnostic repeat confirmed the same validation error.


Native IPv4/TCP ACL qualification subsequently passed with the explicit
nonzero source port range: create, destination-port update, UUID-bound read-back,
no-op and deletion restored the original empty inventory. Evidence is in
[ACL qualification](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-12/wireless-acl-qualification.json).
IPv6, walled-garden updates/removal, deployed-worker execution and actual device
policy behavior remain unqualified. Fixture tests cover IPv6 validation and
explicit URL removal versus omission preservation.


### Wireless power-profile definitions

`wireless.power_profiles` supports `name`, optional `description`, and an
explicit ordered `rules` list. Each rule maps `interface_type`, `interface_id`,
`parameter_type`, and `parameter_value` using the pinned provider's enums.
Rule order is significant. Unknown/null fields and invalid enum values fail
before API access. Hardware-dependent combinations remain controller-validated.

An omitted description is retained during updates. An explicit empty string
requests clearing. Updates bind to the observed UUID and verify the ordered
rules after the task finishes. Unspecified profiles are retained; changing a
name creates a new definition. Power profiles can share a wireless manifest
with interfaces and ACLs using the existing all-collection preflight and journal.
This does not deploy the profile to an AP.

Examples: `wireless-power-apply.yaml` and `wireless-power-report.yaml` under
`examples/configs/catalyst-center`. Fixture coverage includes manifest
create/update/restart/no-op, UUID replacement refusal, rule-order comparison and
optional-description ownership. Native and worker qualification are tracked
separately. The pinned contract is
[provider 0.6.1 power profile](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/resource_catalystcenter_power_profile.go).


Native power-profile qualification passed for an Ethernet SPEED rule: creation
at `100MBPS`, update to `1000MBPS` with the same UUID, no-op verification and
cleanup restored the original inventory. See
[power-profile evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-12/wireless-power-qualification.json).
Other rule combinations, live description changes, deployed-worker execution
and AP hardware behavior remain pending; those are not implied by the native
controller-definition test.


### 802.11be profile definitions

`wireless.dot11be_profiles` implements the pinned model's `name`,
`ofdma_down_link`, `ofdma_up_link`, `mu_mimo_down_link`, `mu_mimo_up_link`, and
`ofdma_multi_ru`. The pinned provider defaults OFDMA down/up to true and the
remaining three booleans to false. Explicit false is preserved; null, quoted
booleans and fields outside the pinned model are rejected before API calls.
Missing API boolean values fail observation instead of masquerading as false.

Creates and UUID-bound updates use the existing task journal. On newer APIs,
observed `default` and `mloGroup` values are preserved during an update but are
not added to the pinned NetAsCode model. Renames leave prior definitions retained.
Profiles can share the wireless compiler's all-collection preflight with
interfaces, ACLs and power profiles. Examples: `wireless-dot11be-apply.yaml` and
`wireless-dot11be-report.yaml` under `examples/configs/catalyst-center`.

Controller definition convergence does not prove device behavior. The
[current API contract](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/create-a-802-11be-profile/)
describes provisioning differences across IOS-XE releases, including deprecated
fields. Wireless controller/profile association and actual hardware behavior
need separate qualification; the current lab inventory contains three Catalyst
9300 switches and no wireless controller. The compatibility target remains
NetAsCode 0.5.0 and provider 0.6.1.


Native 802.11be qualification passed for creation with pinned defaults followed
by `ofdma_multi_ru: true`: UUID-bound read-back, unchanged-intent no-op, and
cleanup restored inventory. See
[802.11be evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-12/wireless-dot11be-qualification.json).
Other boolean transitions and worker execution remain pending. The lab's lack
of a wireless controller prevents WLC/radio qualification; no device-level
claim follows from this successful controller-definition test.


### RRM FRA feature templates

`feature_templates.wireless.rrm_fra` supports `name`, `radio_band`,
`fra_freeze`, `fra_status`, `fra_interval`, and `fra_sensitivity`.
Pinned defaults are false/false/3 for freeze/status/interval. Model bands
`2.4GHz_5GHz` and `5GHz_6GHz` map to API enums. For `2.4GHz_5GHz`, the default
sensitivity MEDIUM maps to `Medium`; the other pinned sensitivity labels map to
the provider spellings. Explicit sensitivity with another band label is rejected
rather than silently discarded by the compiler. API-enum band labels without
explicit sensitivity are accepted, matching the module's passthrough behavior.

The [feature summary API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/get-feature-template-summary/)
pages at 25 instances inside the selected type group. CVK checks count
consistency, missing pages, duplicate names/IDs and explicit system-template
flags. Detail reads must match summary UUID/name. Every desired design is
preflighted before the first write; changed system templates block mutation.
Existing unlocked attributes are retained during updates but are outside the
pinned model. Updates bind to UUID and verify independent detail reads.

The lab returned task receipts for create, matching the current
[create API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/create-rrm-fra-configuration-feature-template/).
The pinned provider's synchronous `response.data` shape is not treated as a
completed task: missing task receipts retain an uncertain journal outcome.
Examples: `wireless-fra-apply.yaml` and `wireless-fra-report.yaml` under
`examples/configs/catalyst-center`. Definition convergence does not prove WLC
provisioning, profile associations or radio behavior.


Native FRA qualification passed for the 2.4/5 GHz design: create with pinned
defaults, interval update from 3 to 6 hours, UUID-bound detail read-back and
no-op, then cleanup with original inventory restored. The earlier receipt probe
was also deleted and its absence verified. See
[FRA evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-12/wireless-fra-qualification.json).
Both protected default designs remained present. Summary pagination beyond the
small lab inventory, protected-template refusal and manifest restart are fixture
tested; live 5/6 GHz transitions, deployed-worker execution and WLC behavior
remain pending.


### CleanAir feature templates

`feature_templates.wireless.cleanair` supports name, description, radio band,
`enable`, `device_reporting`, `persistent_device_propagation`, and all 19 pinned
`interferers` keys. The three top-level booleans default to false; model bands
2.4GHz/5GHz/6GHz map to API enums. Explicit false is compared by presence and
value. Unknown/null keys fail validation. Omitted descriptions and individual
interferer settings remain unowned and are preserved on PUT; an empty interferer
object does not disable existing settings. An explicit empty description clears
that owned field. Band changes currently require explicit replacement.

CleanAir reuses the feature summary/detail readers and protected-system-design
checks. FRA and CleanAir can share one feature-template manifest using the
existing group executor: all designs preflight before the first write.
Unlocked attributes are retained. Examples: `wireless-cleanair-apply.yaml` and
`wireless-cleanair-report.yaml` under `examples/configs/catalyst-center`.

Native 2.4 GHz create, enable update, UUID read-back/no-op and cleanup passed,
restoring original inventory. See
[CleanAir evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-12/wireless-cleanair-qualification.json).
All interferer mappings, optional-attribute preservation and combined preflight
are fixture-tested; individual live interferer changes, other bands, worker
execution, profile associations and actual spectrum/radio behavior remain
pending. No WLC is present in the current lab inventory.

### Wireless worker qualification and receipt conflicts

The six-definition combined worker qualification is recorded in
[the live evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-12/wireless-worker-qualification.json).
The wireless section completed create, accepted-task restart, update, report and
cleanup. Feature templates completed the same sequence after supervised FRA
receipt restoration: the successful controller task identified the exact design
UUID and name, and an operation/resource-version guarded status patch restored
that receipt without replaying creation. This is not evidence of unattended
recovery from a lost receipt. Original definitions and direct-device workers were
preserved; no WLC/AP provisioning was exercised.

Receipt persistence now retries bounded Kubernetes conflicts, rereading and
validating operation identity and phase on every attempt. The controller request
is outside the retry loop. Tests reproduce the prior failure and cover concurrent
status preservation, synchronous completion, replaced-operation refusal, retry
exhaustion with a retained fence, and exactly one external submission. Generic
ambiguous acknowledgements are not retried. The actual cause of the lab's lost
receipt was not established; the conflict vulnerability was independently
reproduced and fixed.

### Wireless anchor groups

`wireless.anchor_groups[]` now compiles into the existing wireless configuration
group and task journal. Each group accepts `name` and `mobility_anchors`, with
all eight pinned peer fields: device name, public IP, priority, managed flag,
peer type, MAC, mobility group and private IP. Required managed flags retain
explicit false; unknown/null fields, duplicate peers and malformed inventory
are rejected. MAC and IP forms are normalized for comparison; peers are compared
by sorted name rather than response order. Omitted optional fields are retained
on updates to the same peer identity.

Inventory resolves short hostnames to unique FQDNs, matching the module's
lookup. Ambiguous names and absent managed anchors block the entire wireless
preflight. Definitions use the shared transport, ownership journal, task receipts
and UUID-bound update verification. They do not provision WLCs or establish
mobility tunnels. The lab qualified an external IOS-XE anchor definition,
PRIMARY-to-SECONDARY update, no-op and cleanup; managed anchors and physical
wireless behavior remain unqualified. Examples are `wireless-anchor-apply.yaml`
and `wireless-anchor-report.yaml`.

Contract references: [NetAsCode anchor groups](https://netascode.cisco.com/docs/data_models/catalyst_center/wireless/anchor_group/),
[create API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/create-anchorgroup/),
and pinned provider 0.6.1. The current API documents 24 peers; the pinned provider's
attribute prose says three but does not enforce that maximum. CVK accepts up to
24; multiple-peer live qualification remains pending.

### AP profile implementation in progress

The AP profile model layer maps the pinned metadata fields, defaults, mesh and
management settings, power references, calendar schedules, timezone and client
limits. Calendar times normalize to the API's 12-hour form; day/date sets are
normalized. Three password-version destinations use the common credential-intent
representation with source indices preserved through profile sorting. Inline
passwords are refused; this layer does not resolve or persist secret values.

The paginated reader retains only allowlisted public fields, including calendar
metadata. Built-in appliance sentinels (`unconfigured`, uppercase timezone and
empty usernames) have observation-only handling and do not widen manifest input.
Passwords returned by an appliance never enter the metadata model. Manifest
report/apply, projected-secret binding and power-profile dependency planning are
implemented through the existing wireless compiler and shared journal.

Pinned provider 0.6.1 documents that monthly calendar-date updates may not
persist and substitutes the old date in its request. CVK must retain the requested
dates and expose a failed verification if the appliance ignores them. That live
behavior has not yet been qualified.

The native AP executor now plans task-based creation and updates, preserving
unowned public attributes and requiring UUID-bound read-back. It preflights power
references and feature/authentication combinations, protects both built-in
profiles, and refuses adoption of an existing credential-bearing definition
without a valid owner/version receipt. Credential rotation uses the existing
atomic projected-secret representation and version comparison. Tests cover
stale projections, replaced UUIDs, public no-ops without password read-back,
optional-field preservation and refusal to verify ignored calendar changes.

Native lab create, client-limit update (0 to 10), read-back/no-op and cleanup
passed; both built-in profiles were preserved. Subsequent worker qualification
below covers durable credential execution. The manifest wiring preserves
credential-resource identity even if Kubernetes prunes version fields, delegates
the common credential verifier, and orders power definitions before AP references
without losing full preflight. Calendar behavior remains unqualified.

AP profile manifest report/apply is now enabled for the bounded model above.
`wireless-ap-apply.yaml` and `wireless-ap-report.yaml` show public intent;
`wireless-ap-credentials-apply.yaml` shows version-bound Secret references.
Credential-bearing operations use a distinct `ap-credential-profile:` identity;
missing version metadata cannot downgrade them to ordinary verification or
release a verified fence without its receipt. Removing credential bindings from
retained ownership is refused. Existing credential resources require ownership
receipts before mutation; adoption/transfer remains unimplemented.

The wireless wrapper plans all APs before releasing prerequisite changes, permits
references to pending power definitions only while a prerequisite write remains,
and submits APs only once referenced definitions exist. It delegates task and
credential completion to the existing shared journal. Reconciler tests cover
power-before-AP creation, accepted-task restart, durable version receipt, stale
projection refusal, subsequent rotation, no-op and ownership-removal refusal.
The complete adapter race suite and example compiler pass. Real-worker password
rotation is qualified below; monthly calendar transitions still require live
qualification.

The deployed worker qualification now covers a combined power/anchor/AP manifest
using all three versioned password projections. The AP create task survived a
worker replacement and produced a durable UUID-bound receipt. Version-2 intent
with version-1 projections failed planning without admitting an operation. After
projection update, the existing worker submitted one AP update, verified the
client-limit change, and recorded all three version-2 bindings. The original
report-only manifest and inventory baseline were restored; test definitions,
Secret and authorized source aliases were removed. XE and NXOS workers remained
healthy with unchanged images. See [worker evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-12/ap-manifest-worker-qualification.json).

The test harness needed corrections to alias syntax and condition observation;
its saved run was resumed without repeating any controller request. No journal
repair was needed. This demonstrates successful tasks, public metadata and
version receipts, not password authentication on an AP or decrypted password
read-back. Calendar changes, additional AP attributes, managed anchors, device
associations, adoption and automatic pruning remain open.

### RF profile definitions and default transitions

`wireless.rf_profiles[]` maps all 88 attributes of the pinned 0.5.0 model to the native `wirelessSettings/rfProfiles` API. It reuses the wireless compiler, controller transport, configuration ownership and task journal. Report mode compares explicitly managed attributes; apply mode creates or updates definitions and verifies update UUIDs. The required radio-enable flags remain explicit, and `default_rf_profile` defaults to false as in the pinned model.

Nested unknown keys, nulls, invalid scalar types, duplicate profile names and multiple requested defaults are rejected. Effective power/DBS/spatial-reuse bounds and mandatory-rate subsets are checked after merging retained settings. Channels and data rates compare as canonical numeric sets. Optional mapped controller values are retained on update; unmapped API fields block updates to avoid silently discarding them. Built-in LOW/TYPICAL/HIGH profiles can be observed but cannot be mutated. Their inherited 6 GHz parent values are accepted only on read; the pinned write schema still permits only CUSTOM for that field.

Promoting a profile requires the existing default to appear in the same manifest with a false default value (including the pinned default). Deselection is submitted and verified before promotion. This is a sequenced transition, not an atomic transaction: an interruption between the two tasks can temporarily leave no default. Normal journal recovery resumes the manifest; no automatic rollback or unrelated default takeover is claimed.

Examples: `wireless-rf-apply.yaml` and `wireless-rf-report.yaml` under `examples/configs/catalyst-center`. [Worker evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-12/rf-manifest-worker-qualification.json) qualifies two-profile creation, accepted-task restart, client-limit updates, default selection/transfer/clear, report restoration and cleanup. Remaining field combinations, AP/WLC provisioning and radio behavior, associations, adoption and prune remain pending.

### SSID definitions and credential execution

The internal `wireless.ssids[]` parser covers 63 pinned scalar fields, the `nas_options`, `auth_servers` and `acct_servers` sets, and multi-PSK metadata. NetAsCode radio labels map to their API enum values; `OPEN_SECURED` maps to `OPEN-SECURED`. The module's zero-as-unset handling is preserved for session timeout, client rate limit and CCKM tolerance. The pinned client-exclusion timeout default is 180; other absent fields remain unowned. SSID names retain spaces and are bounded to 32 bytes.

Inline passphrases are rejected. Top-level `passphrase_version` and nested `multi_psk_settings[].passphrase_wo_version` produce source-indexed credential intents for the shared versioned Secret mechanism. Sorting SSID names does not change their source paths. Multi-PSK priority and source order are preserved. The wireless compiler now resolves these references through the existing credential projection and journal mechanisms.

The site-bound inventory reader uses the existing authenticated transport and 500-record paging, retaining only public mapped fields and inheritance/sensor identity. Both main and nested returned passphrases are excluded. Empty/zero observation sentinels remain distinguishable from absent intent. Fixture tests cover redaction, malformed metadata, duplicate names/priorities, mapping, bounds and credential source indices.

SSID apply/report compilation and native create/update now bind Global-site and SSID identities, preflight ACL/OPEN-SECURED dependencies, and use the existing journal. Fixture reconciliation tests cover accepted-task restart, durable main-passphrase versions, stale projections, rotation and removal refusal. Live worker rotation, wireless deployment, adoption and prune remain unqualified. Contract references: [pinned provider](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/tree/v0.6.1) and [SSID API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/get-ssid-by-site/).

SSID payload construction now merges public observations with explicit intent while obtaining every submitted credential from the shared versioned Secret resolver. A returned passphrase is reduced to a presence flag; it is never retained or reused. Existing main credentials and every retained multi-PSK entry require projected values for a write. Multi-PSK metadata is merged by priority, while injection follows original manifest indices. Payload construction copies each nested entry, so plaintext cannot mutate the parsed intent or observed metadata. ASCII/HEX constraints, PMF/cipher/AKM requirements, guest external authentication and enterprise ACL posturing receive preflight checks; controller validation remains necessary for complete device/version-specific combinations.

Unmapped API fields and sensor SSIDs block payload construction. Known custom-NAS metadata is preserved. Fixtures cover retained HEX metadata after priority reordering, missing/stale sources, owner mismatch and public-metadata isolation. Native task submission, site/SSID identity, compiler wiring and durable main-passphrase receipt recovery are implemented and fixture-tested. Multi-PSK receipt identity now uses the priority-based key described below rather than treating an array index as a stable identity.

SSID credential versions add an optional, non-secret `key` to the existing operation and application-receipt entries: `passphrase` or `multi-psk:<priority>`. The actual JSON-pointer source path remains recorded separately. The shared credential resolver carries this key only when supplied by the SSID parser; existing AP, AAA and global-credential records omit it. SSID rotation checks project copies to semantic keys before reusing the existing version/source comparison logic, so reordering SSIDs or PSKs does not reset or cross-assign their counters.

Admission validates each SSID key and counter against the resolved source model and rejects missing, substituted or duplicate keys. Tests cover reordered priorities with unchanged credentials, version rollback, explicit rotation and source-key tampering. The generated NetworkController CRDs in both distribution locations include the optional field. They have not yet been applied to the lab. Tests now reject generic verification with pruned credential versions and journal release when both persisted records lose their semantic keys. SSID worker qualification must install/verify this schema before enabling writes and exercise real task recovery and durable receipts. Existing RF/AP worker images remain deployed.

Live native qualification created the disabled, unassociated OPEN SSID `CVK_12224801` and verified create/no-op. Two update preflights refused extra appliance response fields before submission. The reader now accepts empty IPv6/URL ACL and disabled load-balancing placeholders, validates duplicate MAC-filter flags, and recognizes the alternative inheritance UUID. Populated unsupported ACLs, enabled load-balancing extensions and conflicting aliases still fence mutation. After SSH access recovered, the same fixture updated client exclusion from 180 to 240 seconds, verified no-op, and was deleted; the empty baseline was restored. This native evidence does not qualify worker deployment or device authentication.

Examples: `wireless-ssid-apply.yaml`, `wireless-ssid-report.yaml` and `wireless-ssid-credentials-apply.yaml` under `examples/configs/catalyst-center`. They define disabled Global SSIDs without AP/WLC association. Credential examples require a separately authorized versioned Secret source; no password belongs in the model.

### Wireless profile and tag model

The internal parser now covers `network_profiles.wireless[]`, including SSID details, additional interfaces, AP zones, feature-template references, sites, site tags and policy tags. It retains unresolved names for authoritative lookup rather than omitting missing dependencies. Pinned defaults include the `management` interface where neither an interface nor VLAN group is selected, empty zone SSID sets, and `default-flex-profile` on site tags. Fabric suppresses interface/VLAN-group payload fields; VLAN mapping is emitted only when FlexConnect is enabled. Conflicting explicit interface and VLAN-group names are rejected rather than silently discarded. SSID reference names preserve spaces and `#` consistently with SSID definitions.

This is model groundwork, not enabled execution. Profile/tag identity reads, reference resolution, native create/update, compiler and journal integration, assignment ownership and live qualification remain pending. Contract sources are the [pinned module](https://github.com/netascode/terraform-catalystcenter-nac-catalystcenter/blob/v0.5.0/cc_wireless.tf) and [pinned provider](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/tree/v0.6.1).

SSID multi-PSK reconciliation now has an end-to-end fixture test: two independently projected keys create a definition, reordering their source indices causes no request, and a later single-key rotation persists the correct priority key and updated source path. The HTTP fixture checks each submitted secret against its priority and excludes secrets from subsequent readback. This does not qualify real wireless authentication.

Wireless profile inventory now uses the shared authenticated transport and bounded 500-record paging. The reader validates profile IDs, unique names and nested list identities, normalizes set ordering, and preserves known public metadata for later comparison. Unknown fields, including unknown nested fields, are excluded and mark the object unsafe for update; no opaque response subtree is retained. Tests cover multiple pages, duplicate IDs/names, malformed flags/VLAN values, missing nested identities, reference IDs and exclusion of unknown secret-like fields. The request contract follows [Get Wireless Profiles](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/get-wireless-profiles/). This reader is not yet wired to profile execution or live-qualified.

Wireless profile payload construction now consumes a validated inventory snapshot. It resolves explicit 802.11be and feature-template names to IDs and checks SSID, interface/VLAN-group, anchor, RF and retained feature dependencies. Known unowned nested fields are preserved without aliasing the observed state. Explicit interface/VLAN-group selection removes the conflicting prior selection; disabling FlexConnect removes the old local VLAN. AP-zone and retained feature SSID membership is checked against the final profile SSID set. Missing dependencies, foreign-site or sensor SSIDs, unknown observed fields and mismatched profile identity fail before a payload can be submitted. These are fixture-tested construction rules; the inventory collector, write executor, dependency identity revalidation and journal integration remain pending. Payload support for an explicit empty collection does not itself authorize destructive removal; ownership checks still belong to the executor.

The request-local wireless profile dependency collector now reuses existing Global-site/SSID, interface, 802.11be, anchor, RF and feature-summary readers. It queries only referenced classes, including references retained from matching observed entries. Payload generation and collection share interface/VLAN/FlexConnect normalization so replaced dependencies are not accidentally required. CleanAir and FRA names and IDs must be unambiguous across both inventories. Tests cover collection-to-payload binding, cross-kind name collisions and removal versus retention of an old VLAN reference.

VLAN-group inventory remains explicitly unqualified: models that still reference a VLAN group return a specific error before inventory collection or mutation. This is a remaining parity gap, not evidence that the appliance lacks a suitable API. Profile write execution, dependency identity revalidation, assignment/tag ownership and live qualification remain pending; the collector is not deployed.

The native wireless profile executor now plans create/update operations with full desired-profile preflight. Its resource identity includes a non-secret digest of the Global site and only the dependencies used by the final payload. Parent/profile IDs keep their existing journal meanings; no new foundation status field is introduced. Submission rereads the profile, its dependencies and merged payload before issuing a single request. Verification checks the Global site, update target ID, dependency digest and public readback. Tests qualify native fixture create/update/no-op, update-target replacement, dependency replacement before submission and during verification, and stability under unrelated inventory changes. Removal of profile list members remains blocked until ownership evidence is implemented. This executor is not yet compiler-enabled or live-qualified, and create readback still follows the shared task-plus-name lookup semantics rather than claiming a task-returned object ID.

Wireless profile definitions are now connected to apply/report compilation for `network_profiles`, including models containing both switching and wireless definitions. The shared configuration group keeps the existing `profiles/` and `sites/` switching resource prefixes and adds `wireless/` for the new executor. No new retry or task state machine is introduced. A reconciler fixture qualifies create and update through accepted-task restart, no-op convergence, operation-slot release and read-only report. Site and policy tags are now compiled with the dependency ordering described below. Removal of list members and VLAN-group references remain explicit gaps. Examples are `wireless-profile-apply.yaml` and `wireless-profile-report.yaml`; their referenced Global SSID must already exist. This integration has not been deployed or live-qualified.

Wireless profile site assignments now reuse the existing additive assignment executor with a neutral name/site intent and a wireless-profile inventory resolver. Switching inventory resolution and resource prefixes are unchanged. Wireless assignments use the separate `wireless-sites/` journal prefix and distinct report identities. All target sites are resolved during group preflight, profile creation precedes assignment, and both profile/site IDs are reread immediately before POST. The planner preserves unrelated assignments and performs no implicit removal. Fixtures qualify combined profile-create/assign/update recovery across reconciler restarts, no-op/report behavior, preservation of a foreign assignment, and refusal of replaced site/profile targets before submission. Real controller assignment, removal ownership, site tags and policy tags remain unqualified or unimplemented as recorded in the resource matrix.

Site-tag and policy-tag inventory readers now use the shared authenticated client, bounded paging and public-field projection. Results carry the parent wireless-profile ID, validate unique tag IDs/names and site IDs, and normalize set order. Unknown fields are excluded while marking the tag unsafe for future full-object updates. Site and policy metadata have separate schemas; policy AP-zone membership is required. Tests cover both tag kinds, invalid parent paths, duplicate identities/names/sites, malformed fields and unknown-data exclusion. Tag writes and compiler enablement remain pending. The policy-list contract is documented in [Retrieve all Policy Tags](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/retrieve-all-policy-tags-for-a-wireless-profile/); pinned provider mappings supply the site-tag fields and paths. Live behavior, including release-specific pagination, is not yet qualified.

Tag payload construction now resolves site paths to unique IDs and requires existing assignment to the parent wireless profile. Policy-tag AP zones must exist in that profile, including retained zones when the manifest omits them. Site-tag AP/flex references are checked against supplied validated inventories, including retained references. A changed parent/tag identity or unknown observed fields blocks construction. Inputs and observations are copied, and explicit empty zone sets remain distinct from omitted intent. Tests cover site ordering, assignment prerequisites, parent replacement, unknown fields, retained dependencies and duplicate site identities. Inventory collection for these dependencies, mutation/ownership checks, task recovery, compiler enablement and live qualification remain pending. In particular, a supplied fixture flex-profile ID does not prove a live flex-profile lookup contract.

Tag dependency collection now reuses validated site inventory, profile assignments and AP-profile metadata. Policy AP zones come from the supplied parent profile observation, with duplicate/name checks. AP inventory is fetched only when referenced, including a retained AP reference. The pinned built-in `default-flex-profile` is handled by its documented model name without fabricating a UUID; this changes the earlier supplied-snapshot-only construction requirement. Custom flex-profile inventory remains unqualified and explicitly returns an error before any write. Tests exercise both tag kinds, collection-to-payload binding, missing site assignment, selective AP lookup and custom-flex refusal. Native tag writes, ownership/recovery, compiler enablement and lab qualification remain pending.

Native tag execution now plans a single-item bulk POST for creation and a tag-ID PUT for updates. Resources bind hashed profile/tag names plus the parent, target sites and used AP/flex or zone dependencies; no credential values enter these bindings. All desired tags are observed before returning a write. Submission rereads parent/tag identity, dependencies, desired payload and prior public fields; changed observations fail before mutation. Verification checks identity and public readback. Tests exercise both tag kinds through create/update/no-op, site/parent replacement and refusal to remove existing site or zone memberships. The pinned module's zero-target-site condition produces no tag operation. Shared-journal/compiler wiring, task recovery, ownership-based removal and live qualification remain pending. This native fixture does not prove controller task completion or physical wireless provisioning.


Wireless site and policy tags are now connected to `network_profiles` apply/report compilation using separate `wireless-site-tags/` and `wireless-policy-tags/` journal prefixes. Before releasing a prerequisite write, the compiler validates tag dependencies against the intended final profile and additive site assignments. This preflight does not invent parent IDs or submit tag requests before the parent exists. It is repeated immediately before prerequisite submission. Once profile and assignment convergence is observed, native tag execution uses actual identities and the existing task journal. Existing switching prefixes are unchanged.

The combined reconciler fixture covers profile creation, site assignment, both tag creations, subsequent profile and tag updates adding a second site, accepted-task restart, no-op convergence and drift reporting. Additional fixtures reject missing sites, absent assignments, missing zones and custom flex references before profile creation, including a dependency disappearing before submission. Both tag types now have shared-journal update recovery coverage: the second assignment precedes their PUT requests, journal target identities are checked, and convergence causes no replay. Ownership-based removals and real-appliance qualification still require work. The Catalyst Center credential failure continues to block live qualification.

The `wireless-profile-tags-apply.yaml` example shows the supported combined profile/site/tag manifest. Existing Global SSID and site dependencies are required; membership removal remains blocked, and this example does not deploy configuration to WLCs or APs.


Wireless controller provisioning now has a native submission primitive for the pinned module's empty-body provision/reprovision request. It uses the shared transport and configuration write identity, resolves the device from inventory, requires a physical serial and wireless-controller family, and rereads UUID/serial/address/reachability immediately before submission. A missing task receipt, including empty HTTP 202, remains an uncertain outcome rather than successful provisioning. No automatic retry or new task state machine is introduced. Local HTTPS fixtures cover both actions, replaced identities, family/address/reachability changes and malformed acceptance. Manifest compilation remains gated pending device mutation admission, site and managed-AP prerequisites, durable recovery and terminal readback. No WLC or AP has been changed by these tests.

Contract references: [pinned module device provisioning](https://github.com/netascode/terraform-catalystcenter-nac-catalystcenter/blob/v0.5.0/cc_device_provision.tf), [Wireless Controller Provision API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/wireless-controller-provision/) and [device inventory example](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-5/api-quick-start/). The provider's repeated-apply reprovision behavior must be translated to explicit CVK operation intent; a reconcile loop must not repeatedly reprovision an unchanged manifest.


The wireless controller provisioning status reader now uses the shared authenticated GET path. It validates the returned network-device ID, required network-intent and feature-template status enums, and the required out-of-sync boolean. Optional site metadata and decimal epoch timestamps are validated; timestamps retain their original units because the documented contract does not specify the unit. Missing status, unknown enums and malformed responses are errors. Null/absent timestamps remain absent evidence. The reader never classifies task acceptance or an old SUCCESS observation as completed work. Persisted task correlation, freshness checks, manifest admission and appliance qualification remain pending. Contract: [Wireless Controller Provision Status, API 3.1.5](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/wireless-controller-provision-status/). Availability on the lab release has not been confirmed.


Primary, secondary and anchor managed AP location readers now normalize the documented nested `managedApLocations` response into the existing bounded inventory paginator. Site IDs and paths must be valid and unique. Counts are read before and after traversal; count disagreement or truncation fails the observation. Count agreement does not imply an atomic snapshot or prevent same-count replacements, so mutation planning will still require dependency revalidation. Fixtures cover all three endpoints with 501 records, malformed envelopes, duplicate identities/paths, invalid sites, truncated inventory and changed counts. Assignment writes, ownership, manifest prerequisites and live qualification remain pending; pagination units have not yet been checked against the lab appliance.

Contracts: [primary locations](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/get-primary-managed-ap-locations-for-specific-wireless-controller/), [secondary locations](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/get-secondary-managed-ap-locations-for-specific-wireless-controller/), [anchor locations](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/get-anchor-managed-ap-locations-for-specific-wireless-controller/) and [location counts](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/get-managed-ap-locations-count-for-specific-wireless-controller/).


Managed AP assignment payload construction now handles the API's complete-replacement semantics. Primary and secondary arrays are both emitted for the managed-location endpoint; the anchor endpoint receives its own array. Omitted desired lists preserve their validated observed memberships. Explicit desired lists resolve site paths to unique IDs and refuse removal of observed members until ownership evidence is implemented. Missing observations, ambiguous IDs, disappeared or replaced site identities and invalid paths fail before payload creation. Fixtures cover additive updates, omitted secondary preservation, anchor mapping and removal/ref replacement rejection. These helpers are not yet connected to assignment submission or manifest execution.

Contract: [Assign Managed AP Locations for WLC](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/assign-managed-ap-locations-for-wlc/).


Native managed AP assignment execution now uses the existing configuration-write interface for standalone wireless controllers. It resolves UUID/serial and sites, observes current memberships, builds the full replacement payload, and binds the selected device, address, site paths/IDs and desired memberships to the operation resource. Submission reobserves all dependencies and rejects changed public state before POST. Verification checks operation identity and assignment readback; no-op convergence prevents repeated submissions. The anchor endpoint and primary/secondary endpoint share this implementation. Fixtures cover both endpoints through acceptance, delayed readback, executor reconstruction and no-op, plus site/device/membership replacement before submission and serial replacement during verification. This is native fixture coverage, not persisted task-journal or real-appliance qualification. Manifest admission, dependency ordering, embedded-controller support and ownership-based removal remain pending.

Configuration managed-device binding now has an API-reader resolver. Given an uncached Kubernetes reader, it lists CiscoDevices across namespaces to detect physical aliases, reuses the existing declaration/physical-identity checks, reads and validates the live Node incarnation, and rereads the declaration to reject a changed UID or resource version. Fake-API tests cover valid binding, missing/replaced nodes, cross-namespace aliases and a declaration changed between reads. This is identity evidence only, not mutation authority or an atomic snapshot. The ordinary device-worker maintenance coordinator owns process/session-scoped leases; controller configuration still needs durable reservation/recovery integration before manifest-driven device writes can be enabled. Existing foundation lease code is unchanged.

The generic configuration apply entry point now explicitly rejects physical-device submissions (`TargetSerial` present) until durable device admission exists. This also covers synchronous native writes. Existing physical-operation journal records are retained in every phase rather than automatically cleared or verified without reservation evidence. Tests exercise both submission forms and all six journal phases. Native executor tests still exercise resource semantics directly; they do not establish managed admission.

The next admission implementation must preserve the existing division of authority: the Catalyst Center worker submits controller API requests, while the device worker owns and renews the canonical mutation Lease. A configuration reservation must bind immutable config/controller/device/Node identities and the exact journal operation, attest readiness before submission, survive controller-worker restarts, and retain uncertain remote work beyond Lease expiry through canonical risk detection. Release must require verified completion or proof of no dispatch. The SWIM handoff is image/upgrade-specific and cannot be impersonated with a synthetic upgrade to authorize configuration. This gate is a pending implementation requirement, not completed device mutation support; no ND, direct-device or SWIM lease logic was changed.


Wireless inventory placement projection parsing now represents PROVISION/REPROVISION state, controller type, fabric site/roles and the three managed AP location lists. It validates unique non-Global site paths, preserves omitted versus explicitly empty lists, and checks the pinned module's controller role/type/location relationships. Anchor-with-fabric combinations and conflicting embedded/standalone controller roles are rejected. The projection rejects unknown fields; the enclosing inventory compiler must separately validate identity, other device fields and the full fabric-role vocabulary. That compiler connection remains pending, and the projection grants no execution authority. Fixtures cover standalone, fabric, embedded and anchor intent and malformed/contradictory inputs. The local device-provisioning source was byte-compared against the upstream v0.5.0 file before implementing these rules.


The shared inventory parser now retains validated wireless PROVISION/REPROVISION placement together with device identity, site, tags and role fields. ASSIGN entries cannot carry provisioning-only fields, and unknown device fields still fail parsing. Explicit empty secondary-location intent remains distinct from omission through the full inventory model. Apply compilation continues to reject device execution; report compilation and direct report evaluation explicitly reject wireless provisioning until they can represent the full request. Tests prove that accepted model parsing cannot silently become partial site/tag reporting or bypass execution admission. Full report integration and manifest execution remain pending.


Native wireless provisioning verification now combines the existing task-completion validator with device UUID/serial/address/family checks and provisioning status at the expected site. Network intent must succeed, design must be in sync, and required feature-template provisioning must succeed. NOT_STARTED is accepted for model configuration only when the caller explicitly does not require it; any rollback, failure or abort is an error. A supplied pre-submission appliance timestamp must advance, preventing an unchanged prior SUCCESS from proving a new operation. Epoch values are compared without converting units; consistent appliance timestamp semantics remain to be live-qualified. Tests distinguish running/stale/failed tasks, old or missing timestamps, required model configuration, rollback, changed identities and out-of-sync status. This verifier is not yet wired into manifest execution: baseline evidence must be durably bound before submission, and the device reservation and recovery lifecycle still need implementation.


Wireless provisioning baselines now have a versioned, canonical record encoding in the existing operation resource field. It retains only device UUID/serial/address, target site, prior appliance timestamp, action, feature-template requirement and a digest of the model device name. Record size is capped below the journal limit to allow an executor namespace. Restoring rejects alternate/unknown/truncated encodings, mismatched names, changed target/action metadata and oversized records. A fake-API journal test persists and reconstructs the record; provisioning verification fixtures now restore their baseline from that representation. No new CRD fields are introduced. Automatic baseline capture at submission, device reservation and manifest wiring are still pending; the record is recovery evidence, not a mutation grant.


Native provisioning planning now requires the resolved target site and whether model configuration is expected. It captures the status baseline before creating a write and encodes it in the operation resource, using the existing bounded record. Planning rejects a different site/hostname, active CONFIGURING/PENDING work, or missing timestamps on previously started provisioning. Submission reobserves the full status baseline after checking the device identity and refuses changes before POST. Tests verify restoration from the planned resource, status changes between planning and submission, and invalid/busy baselines. This closes native baseline capture; managed admission, generation-bound execution receipts/no-op semantics, manifest compilation and real-appliance qualification remain pending.


The configuration status now includes optional bounded action-application receipts. Each receipt keeps a stable action key and the verified operation's existing source/target binding, including the provisioning baseline record. The Catalyst Center recorder rechecks the source, ownership, task and readback, then persists the receipt and Verified phase in one CAS. Release refuses missing or mismatched receipts for provisioning operations, including missing physical identity. The revision matcher allows an unchanged action to be recognized despite advancement of its baseline timestamp, but does not reuse a receipt across config/controller/source revisions or target changes. It is not a compliance assertion or mutation grant.

Fixtures qualify record persistence, executor reconstruction, old-success refusal, revision matching, deepcopy isolation, missing-receipt release refusal and receipt survival after operation release. Adapter, migration and API race regressions pass. The generated optional `actionApplications` CRD field has not been installed in the lab. Device admission and receipt-aware manifest planning remain pending; action receipts do not by themselves enable device writes.


Native provisioning now has a revision-aware planner that connects baseline capture to persisted action receipts. It checks the source and operation slot before API reads and refreshes both afterward. Matching verified config/controller/source revisions and target semantics return no write; a changed revision yields a new native plan. Outstanding journal operations prevent replanning. Fixtures extend the receipt lifecycle through release, same-revision no-op, new-revision planning, admission rejection and source changes during inventory reads. The planner remains outside manifest compilation pending durable device admission; it performs no mutation or journal update itself.

An additive `ControllerConfigurationReservation` API contract now separates configuration delegation from the upgrade-specific SWIM handoff. Its immutable spec binds controller/config/device/Node incarnations, worker Pod identities, generations, operation ID/digest, inventory/physical identity and worker revision. Status separates the device-worker grant from the controller-worker one-shot claim. Generated CRD and deepcopy artifacts are present; the CRD has not been installed in the lab. No manager, worker or adapter consumes this API yet, and creating it grants no authority.

The shared `internal/controllerconfiguration` package supplies reservation names, UID-based holder identities using the existing devicecoordination helper, and a digest of immutable non-secret journal fields. Phase, task receipt and submission timestamp do not change that digest; source and target changes do. Tests cover these identity rules and nested deepcopy isolation. Actor-specific admission, grant/claim/revocation transitions, canonical Lease acquisition/renewal, expired-operation quarantine, completion release and runtime wiring remain pending. Existing SWIM, direct-device and ND runtime behavior is unchanged. The new contract must not be enabled until those enforcement paths are complete.

The reservation contract now has pure live-grant and journal-binding validators. The grant validator requires a canonical mutation Lease name, a trusted caller-supplied Lease namespace, matching reservation and Lease incarnations, holder and transition count, a Held grant, and non-expired renewal evidence with consistent acquisition/grant timestamps. Deleting, replaced, revoked, expired and future-dated evidence fails closed. The journal validator checks the immutable operation digest plus explicit config/controller revisions and inventory target; advancing task phases does not change the binding. Tests cover lease replacement/expiry and operation source, revision, target and action changes.

These validators do not acquire a Lease, verify live worker/device/Node incarnations, authorize submission, or implement claim CAS. They have no runtime consumers yet. Actor admission, manager/device-worker integration, canonical risk retention and release are still required before enabling physical configuration manifests. Local race fixtures pass; the lab remains unqualified for these additions while Catalyst Center authentication returns HTTP 401.

Configuration reservations now include an unconnected `ClaimOnce` protocol primitive and preparation-only `RevokeUnclaimed` helper. Claiming rereads the exact versioned reservation and canonical Lease, checks the operation binding and live grant, then writes the claim using the reservation resourceVersion. It never retries a conflict or an existing claim. Persistence is reread; ambiguous writes and mismatched evidence return errors and cannot authorize dispatch. Revocation uses the same status CAS and refuses claimed work. Tests exercise both winners, revocation between the claim's read and update, expired leases, and a persisted claim whose update response was lost. These fake-client tests verify the helpers' CAS behavior; they do not substitute for API-server admission or live integration qualification.

These helpers have no runtime consumers yet. Actor-specific admission, live device/Node/worker validation, retained risk after dispatch, manager creation, worker Lease renewal, verified release and manifest compiler wiring remain outstanding. They do not change existing provider runtime behavior or enable physical device configuration by themselves.

The managed Helm chart now contains a dedicated configuration-reservation admission policy. Immutable spec fields identify both worker service accounts, while bound token Pod UIDs identify their exact incarnations. Only the manager can create empty reservations with the evidence finalizer. Device workers can publish the initial grant and revoke/release never-claimed preparation; controller workers can add one matching claim against a Held grant. The policy rejects claim removal, regrant after revocation, changes to immutable bindings, and deletion/finalizer removal for claimed evidence. Claimed-operation completion/release is deliberately not admitted until verified receipt semantics are implemented.

A local Kubernetes 1.35 API-server test installs the generated CRD and rendered policy, exercises authorized grant/claim operations, rejects wrong actors and replacement Pods, proves claimed evidence retention, and verifies the unclaimed Held → Revoked → Released cleanup path. Race-enabled API-server and contract tests pass. This is local admission qualification, not lab deployment or full runtime integration. Manager/worker RBAC has not been widened, and runtime consumers remain absent; completion receipts, recovery fencing, live binding checks and worker/manifest wiring still block physical configuration enablement.

Reservations now have an optional immutable completion receipt (operation/digest, task ID, submission and verification timestamps). The shared completion validator requires the bound controller incarnation and exactly one retained Verified action receipt; it correlates the claim, operation digest, task and submission time, and rejects a conflicting retained journal. Journal release does not erase completion evidence because action receipts survive it. Tests reject missing/duplicate receipts, task or physical-target changes, premature submission timestamps and future verification times, and check deepcopy isolation.

The completion field is schema-only evidence at this stage: admission explicitly prevents publication until controller completion and device-worker release are wired together. Local API-server tests verify this restriction, so adding the optional field does not open an alternate release path. The generated CRD is not installed in the lab. Runtime publication, independently verified release, risk retention, worker renewal and physical manifest execution are still pending.

Completion publication and release now have shared persistence helpers. `PublishCompletion` rereads the exact reservation version and bound controller, validates the retained action receipt, persists completion with CAS, and verifies the stored evidence. Retrying an already-persisted completion preserves its original verification timestamp. `MarkVerifiedReleased` independently rereads the receipt and rejects a canonical Lease still held by the reservation, even when expired; it records Released only after observing that ownership is gone. Neither helper acquires, renews or releases the Lease itself.

Admission now permits the bound controller Pod to add one matching completion and the bound device-worker Pod to transition Held to Released while preserving claim/completion evidence. The manager may remove evidence only afterward. Local API-server tests cover actor separation, mismatched completion, immutable completion, premature release/deletion rejection and successful completion/release. Fixture tests cover missing retained receipts, stale reservation versions, lost completion-write responses and retained Lease ownership. These supersede the earlier temporary prohibition on completion publication. Runtime consumers, worker Lease management, recovery quarantine and manifest execution remain pending; no new RBAC grants or lab deployment were made.

Configuration reservation recovery is now integrated into the shared mutation guard. Granted or claimed unresolved reservations participate in deterministic canonical risk selection; Lease expiration and deletion requests do not age out their risk. A Released claim requires matching completion identity and consistent grant/claim/submission/verification timestamps. The device-worker release protocol remains responsible for the independent controller-receipt and Lease-ownership checks before that terminal status. The guard adds no configuration dispatch authority.

Existing guard participants receive read-only reservation access through the matching managed role contracts and Helm roles, including the manager and legacy worker. Clusters whose discovery reports the additive API absent retain the existing guard behavior; RBAC and transport failures fail closed. Producers must not be enabled until every relevant worker has the reservation-aware guard and current discovery/RBAC. Tests cover restoration of an expired Lease fence, incomplete release evidence, unknown/deleting records and failed risk reads. No manager creation or device-worker grant reconciler has been enabled yet; lab deployment and qualification remain pending.

The guard/maintenance/software-upgrade/reservation/managed-protocol race suites and targeted controller RBAC tests pass. The complete managed topology Helm render contract passes using the CI-pinned Helm 3.21.4; assertions now include the new policy/binding and read-only resource. The installed Helm 3.17 emits older schema-error formatting and cannot satisfy that existing test contract. Strict documentation build and diff whitespace checks pass.

The reservation package now validates live device-worker evidence before grant publication can be wired: exact CiscoDevice generation/UID, canonical physical identity and literal management IP, manager-bound Node UID/annotations, observed dedicated network-worker revision, and a Running/Ready Pod with the bound UID and service account. Its uncached reader rechecks the CiscoDevice resourceVersion after gathering Node/Pod evidence. Tests cover replacement, generation/address/serial changes, absent worker proof, unready/terminating Pods, wrong accounts and a device change during the reads. This is a prerequisite validator, not a grant publisher or registered worker reconciler; controller-worker/source binding and Lease acquisition/renewal wiring remain outstanding.

The bound device worker now has a `PublishGrant` primitive. It requires current device/Node/Pod evidence, the caller's exact runtime Pod UID, the bound controller incarnation/generation and Prepared journal, matching physical serial, and an already-owned canonical Lease.
