It checks the journal revision again after Lease reads, publishes the initial grant with a reservation CAS, and verifies persistence. Regrant, changed journals, unready workers, expired/foreign Leases and uncertain writes are rejected. It does not acquire a Lease or replace maintenance preparation, controller/source checks or rollout admission, and no reconciler invokes it yet.

Grant validation now compares acquisition ordering at the whole-second precision used by persisted metav1.Time grants while retaining exact Lease renewal/expiry checks. A JSON round-trip fixture covers acquisition and grant within the same second, where Lease microseconds previously caused a false rejection after persistence. Worker Lease acquisition/renewal, reconciliation registration and manifest execution remain pending; no lab changes were made.

A device-side configuration-reservation reconciler now composes the shared helpers. It requires an uncached reader, a pre-existing canonical Lease, the exact runtime device/Pod identity, and explicit authorization/maintenance hooks. Initial work checks live bindings, consults canonical mutation risk, acquires the Lease, prepares maintenance, rechecks authorization, and publishes the grant. Held grants renew without repeating preparation; invalid unclaimed bindings are revoked before release. Claimed work renews canonical quarantine before attempting completion reads, so missing inventory or malformed receipts do not stop fencing. Verified completion releases the Lease and then records Released; revoked preparation has a separate unclaimed release path.

Fixtures cover the full grant/renew/claim/verified-receipt/release lifecycle, retention across failed completion reads and expired Leases, revoked-preparation cleanup, and rejection of a replacement worker Pod. Reservation, guard and maintenance race suites pass. This reconciler is **not registered** in worker startup and receives no new status-writing RBAC yet. Concrete authorization/maintenance hooks, controller/source binding, admission rollout verification, manager reservation creation, takeover/recovery policy and manifest wiring remain required before enablement. Tests use a simulated verified controller receipt; they do not establish wireless hardware execution or lab qualification.

Device-side reconciliation now invokes a concrete uncached intent-binding gate before acquisition and after maintenance preparation. It requires the bound controller type/incarnation/generation, an unpaused controller, the exact Prepared journal, current apply-mode config identity/generation, resolved model metadata, declared section and exclusive section owner, and an unchanged inline or ConfigMap source revision. It rechecks config/controller resourceVersions after source reads. Credential-injected physical actions remain outside the current reservation protocol; no Secret values are loaded. Tests cover mode/pause/revision changes, lost ownership, already-submitted journals, ConfigMap mutation and changes during source reads. The full reservation lifecycle fixture now includes real config/ownership evidence rather than relying solely on an authorization stub.

The existing authorization callback remains necessary for concrete controller-worker identity and deployed admission/rollout checks. Managed maintenance integration and startup registration are still pending, so this does not enable physical manifests or establish lab qualification. Reservation/reconciler/guard/maintenance race tests and strict documentation checks pass.

Controller-worker identity validation is now part of the device-side authorization path. It follows the manager's existing retained Deployment annotations (not an invented controller ownerReference), requires a current single-replica Recreate Deployment, matches the template contract hash, and verifies the exact reserved Ready Pod through its ReplicaSet/Deployment UID chain. It rejects overlapping active Pods, stale/replaced ownership, wrong service accounts and controller argument overrides, including split-form duplicate flags. Config/controller and Deployment versions are rechecked after the reads. The full reservation lifecycle fixture now includes this real ownership chain.

Reservation and provider race suites pass. The remaining authorization hook covers deployed admission/RBAC and rollout compatibility; concrete managed-maintenance integration, manager reservation creation, worker registration, takeover policy and physical manifest execution remain pending. No additional runtime permissions or lab deployment were enabled by these checks.

The existing DeviceMaintenanceSession schema now has an additive `controller-configuration-v1` / `ConfigurationMutation` protocol pair. It retains the existing session fields and transition rules, adds an exact reservation-UID holder requirement and canonical UUIDv4 session token, and does not reinterpret rollout-v1 or pdb-drain-v1 sessions. CRD CEL tests exercise valid configuration sessions/recovery and reject wrong purposes, holders and tokens alongside the existing upgrade/drain cases.

An unexported maintenance request publisher reuses the canonical Lease request annotations and existing published-request structure. It requires the exact managed network worker, bound Node and live reservation-owned Lease, preserves request identity across retries, and rejects foreign/malformed request metadata. The acknowledgement validator recognizes the new explicit pair and rejects mismatched protocol/purpose/timing. Tests cover JSON persistence, repeated requests, foreign-session refusal and expired Leases. The manager does not yet acknowledge or settle this new protocol; Lease admission must also be extended before worker registration. The publisher is not invoked by runtime code, and these schemas have not been installed in the lab.

The manager maintenance validator now dispatches the new configuration protocol after the existing canonical Lease metadata/timing and Node/worker-envelope checks. Before dispatch, it validates the reservation and live device, intent and isolated connector bindings. For claimed work it requires an already-acknowledged exact session and a matching live grant; it cannot invent a first acknowledgement after submission. Claim time must follow acknowledgement. Matching claims advance the session to Active, while changed intent/worker readiness cannot silently reinterpret the operation as a new upgrade request.

Manager tests cover retaining an acknowledged configuration claim and rejecting missing acknowledgements, foreign sessions, replacement Nodes, mismatched claim digests, absent initial intent and wrong purpose, alongside existing maintenance regressions. The component validators already cover the live initial bindings, but a complete initial manager-acknowledgement integration test and session settlement still remain. Worker registration, Lease admission and deployment remain disabled/pending; this is not evidence of live physical provisioning.

Configuration maintenance settlement now independently validates the released reservation against the manager session, device/Node identities, and the exact idle canonical Lease incarnation. Claimed work additionally requires a retained verified controller action receipt, with claim timing following manager acknowledgement. Missing/replaced/busy Leases, wrong identities, incomplete evidence and missing receipts retain the guard. An unclaimed, Released reservation without completion evidence can settle cancelled preparation. Existing software-upgrade settlement is unchanged.

Completion evidence can now be audited after release, while publishing new completion evidence still requires a Held grant. Tests cover that distinction and both successful and rejected manager settlement. A complete initial acknowledgement fixture includes the live device/network worker, desired configuration and controller Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod chain; changing desired configuration invalidates acknowledgement. Reservation, worker reconciler, maintenance, mutation guard and managed protocol race suites pass. This remains local validation: Lease admission still needs the configuration request protocol, concrete preparation/registration and manager reservation lifecycle remain pending, and no physical configuration manifests or lab deployment were enabled.

The retained mutation Lease admission policy now accepts `controller-configuration-v1` requests with the explicit `ConfigurationMutation` purpose, UUIDv4 session token, positive configuration revision and exact reservation-UID holder. Acquiring, requesting on, renewing or releasing a configuration Lease requires the bound network worker's service-account and token Pod UID; the app-hosting worker and replacement Pod cannot use that holder. The compiled manager preflight contract digest and chart shape assertion were updated together.

A local Kubernetes 1.35 API-server test exercises acquisition, request publication, renewal and release, plus rejection of foreign actors, replacement Pods, app workers, mismatched purpose/operation UID/namespace, invalid token version, zero revision, unknown protocol and changed session identity. Existing rollout-v1 and pdb-drain-v1 software-mutation forms remain accepted. The complete local reservation/Lease admission suite passes under the race detector. These chart changes have not been installed in the lab. Concrete worker preparation, manager reservation lifecycle, rollout compatibility and execution registration remain prerequisites for enabling physical configuration manifests.

`PrepareConfigurationMaintenance` now provides the configuration-specific coordinator hook for manager-owned scheduling preparation. It requires a current unclaimed reservation, publishes the existing Lease request envelope, verifies the exact persisted manager acknowledgement and device generation, rereads the Node to prove the maintenance taint remains installed, and revalidates reservation and Lease/request identity after those reads. It never patches Node spec or publishes a grant. Tests reject absent acknowledgement/guard, changed reservation/device/session, claimed work and foreign Lease ownership, and verify repeated preparation preserves the request.

This hook is not yet registered in worker startup. It establishes the scheduling guard only; it does not assert workload evacuation. Configuration execution still needs workload policy/evidence integration, manager reservation creation/retirement, rollout admission, and registration before the existing physical-action gate can be removed. Existing upgrade/drain preparation remains unchanged. No lab deployment or hardware qualification is implied by these local tests.

The shared configuration package now constructs a deterministic manager reservation candidate from a Prepared physical journal operation and observed device, Node, network-worker and connector snapshots. The candidate binds controller/config/device generations, operation digest, canonical serial, controller inventory UUID, management address and worker identities, and retains the evidence finalizer without assigning a Kubernetes UID or any status authority. Device snapshot validation reuses the existing binding checks; the public runtime validator still rejects UID-less candidates.

Tests cover stable construction, unchanged source journal, binding after simulated persistence, and rejection of submitted/receipt-bearing operations, changed physical/controller targets, replaced or unready workers, foreign namespaces, paused controllers and credential-bearing operations. Reservation and device-reconciler race suites pass. This is candidate construction, not manager registration or admission: exclusive physical-device selection, live source/connector ownership and deployed rollout checks must precede creation. Runtime wiring and hardware qualification remain incomplete.

`ReadReservationCandidate` now gathers the candidate from uncached Kubernetes evidence: cluster-wide declared physical identities, the selected device's manager-bound Node/network Pod, and the sole active connector selected by its Deployment. It reuses current apply-intent and connector ownership validation and rereads contributing objects to reject changed UIDs/resourceVersions. Duplicate serial declarations across namespaces are rejected, including declarations outside the controller's namespace. This is a sequence of corroborated reads, not an atomic cluster snapshot; the runtime must repeat admission checks before grants and claims.

The existing full reservation lifecycle fixture now also exercises live candidate construction and checks that its immutable spec matches the expected binding. It rejects a cross-namespace duplicate physical device, report-only intent, stale controller state and use of a UID-less candidate through the runtime intent gate. Candidate-only validation shares the operation-spec checks without weakening the public UID-bound runtime checks. Reservation and reconciler race suites pass. Manager creation/retirement, rollout gating, workload evidence and worker registration remain outstanding; no lab deployment was made.

`EnsureReservation` now supplies the manager creation boundary. It returns matching existing reservations unchanged, including claimed evidence after journal advancement, and rejects collisions, missing evidence protection and stale controller snapshots. New creation requires an explicit admission/rollout authorization callback, followed by a fresh candidate read; callback changes to its copy cannot alter the binding. It verifies the API-assigned UID and persisted spec after creation. Creation errors, including ambiguous outcomes and AlreadyExists, are returned without destructive retry; the next reconciliation can read retained evidence.

The full lifecycle fixture now starts with this creation path, tests missing/rejected authorization and source changes during authorization, then proceeds through grant/claim/receipt/release. Existing-evidence tests cover preservation with new creation disabled and rejection without modification. Reservation/reconciler race suites pass. The manager callback implementation, lifecycle registration and status-writing permissions remain disabled/pending; this helper alone does not enable execution or demonstrate live Catalyst Center behavior.

Controller workers now receive their own Pod name/UID from Kubernetes downward-API field references, passed through the existing adapter options. Catalyst Center retains these process identities for the upcoming reservation-claim bridge. The fields are optional for adapters that do not use Pod-bound protocols; Nexus Dashboard behavior is unchanged. The deployment test permits only these exact field references and continues to reject literal, Secret, ConfigMap or resource-field environment values. This carries identity only, grants no permission, and does not remove the physical configuration gate.

The controller-side claim boundary now verifies the process Pod identity, current apply intent, device/network-worker bindings, isolated connector ownership, live canonical grant and manager-acknowledged scheduling guard. `ReadGuardedGrant` correlates the exact reservation/session/Lease identities, request annotations and acknowledgement ordering with the Node maintenance taint. `ClaimForController` requires a separate admission/workload authorization callback, repeats its live reads afterward, advances observation time across those reads, and invokes the existing non-retryable claim CAS. Catalyst Center exposes this through its runtime Pod identity without gaining device Lease write authority.

The lifecycle fixture now uses this claim path and rejects absent acknowledgement/guard, replacement connector identity, missing authorization, guard removal during authorization and replay. Shared reservation, device reconciler, maintenance and managed-protocol race tests pass, as do the Catalyst Center physical-gate and recovery regressions. The existing taint constants were moved to the neutral protocol package with maintenance aliases retaining their values. The physical-submit gate remains in place: concrete workload authorization, post-claim dispatch checks, journal/receipt recovery wiring, manager lifecycle registration and live qualification are still required.

Successful controller claims now return a process-local `DispatchPermit`. Its private shared state is consumed exactly once, including on failure; copying the value or serializing/reconstructing it cannot restore authority. After the journal enters Submitting, the permit rereads the exact immutable reservation/claim, source revision, connector/device bindings, live Lease and maintenance acknowledgement, with submitted-time ordering and no existing task receipt. It reruns the required workload/admission authorization and corroborates live state afterward. It performs no remote request itself.

The complete fixture now persists Submitting and consumes this permit before simulating a verified remote receipt. Tests cover copied-permit replay, concurrent consumption, failed evidence reads and serialization/zero-value restoration. This closes a claim-to-dispatch protocol primitive; it does not enable physical manifests. Concrete workload authorization, submission/recovery integration and runtime registration remain pending, and no new lab qualification is claimed.

Physical asynchronous writes now have an admission-aware route through the existing Catalyst Center receipt pipeline. With an installed configuration admission hook, the sequence is Prepared journal, one-shot reservation claim, Submitting journal, dispatch-permit check, and one native API invocation, followed by the existing Accepted/Unknown receipt handling. No second receipt engine was added. Without the hook, runtime Pod identity or supported asynchronous task receipt, physical writes remain disabled. The lower-level unguarded submission helper also rejects physical identities.

Sequencing fixtures verify claim/check/submit ordering, rejected claims, missing or rejected permits, unknown remote outcomes, retained journal evidence and no replay. These journal tests inject the narrow permit boundary; the separate reservation lifecycle fixture exercises real Kubernetes binding/claim/permit helpers. This is not yet an end-to-end deployed physical executor. Runtime hook installation, physical apply/recovery reconciliation, workload policy and lab qualification remain incomplete.

Verified physical operations now publish their retained action receipt as reservation completion, using the exact bound controller-worker Pod identity. The adapter waits for the device worker's Released grant and the matching manager Settled session before clearing the physical journal. `finishConfiguration` applies this reservation fence to physical operations, including Prepared cancellation, so direct helper calls cannot discard outstanding device coordination. Retained action receipts survive journal release. Completion receipt validation now allows a deletion request on the same controller UID, avoiding a recovery deadlock without authorizing any new submission.

Tests exercise missing reservation, replacement worker, completion publication, waiting for worker release, waiting for manager settlement, final journal release and receipt retention. Existing wireless provisioning receipt/restart tests now include explicit settled reservation evidence. Catalyst Center and shared-reservation race suites pass. Runtime integration must preserve this settlement-to-journal-release ordering before admitting a subsequent device session; manager retirement/serialization, Prepared/Accepted physical reconciliation, workload policy and lab qualification remain incomplete. The runtime admission hook is still uninstalled.

Manager settlement now has durable, immutable `managerSettledAt` evidence on the reservation. The manager records it from the exact persisted Settled device session before considering another maintenance request; admission denies workers access to this field and denies changing or removing it. Physical journal release checks this retained evidence, so a subsequent device session cannot strand a completed journal. The local API-server admission test verifies actor separation and immutability, and the completion test verifies journal release after the device advances to another session. Manager status RBAC is included; this change does not enable new physical submissions.

`RetireSettledReservation` supplies the subsequent cleanup boundary. It requires durable settlement, the same controller UID, an idle configuration journal and, for claimed work, the retained verified receipt. It removes only the evidence finalizer and deletes with UID/resource-version preconditions. Stale or replaced objects and ambiguous writes cannot trigger a destructive retry. Tests cover rejected cleanup preserving evidence, successful cleanup and recovery after a lost finalizer-update response. This helper is not yet registered in manager reconciliation and does not cancel ungranted preparation.

Manager startup now checks the reservation admission policy's exact rule/variable shape and compiled CEL digest alongside the existing topology policies. The Helm contract checks include the new policy. This detects missing or changed protection before topology startup; concrete workload authorization, runtime creation/retirement and device-worker registration, physical recovery reconciliation and live qualification are still outstanding. These changes have not been deployed to the lab; Catalyst Center API qualification remains blocked by the last observed HTTP 401 until credentials/access are restored.

Physical configuration preparation now has an empty-workload path through the existing maintenance coordinator. `PrepareConfigurationWorkloads` verifies the exact manager scheduling guard, lists active Kubernetes Pods across namespaces, invokes the driver's explicitly supported strict application inventory, and rereads maintenance authority and Kubernetes workloads afterward. Missing capability, incomplete scans, unknown native entries, remaining applications, terminating Pods, changed authority and cancellation block preparation. It neither evicts Pods nor deletes applications. Runtime wiring must supply `DrainPodInventoryProvider.ListPodsForDrain`; compatibility inventory is not an acceptable fallback.

The Kubernetes active-workload selector is shared with the existing software-upgrade path without changing its treatment of terminal or terminating Pods. Controller claim and one-use dispatch checks also read current workloads, including after their authorization callback. Lifecycle tests verify that a newly bound Pod prevents the initial claim, or consumes an already issued permit without submission and retains claimed evidence for recovery. Preparation and upgrade race suites pass. This is an empty-workload prerequisite, not PDB-aware automatic evacuation, persistent native-inventory freshness evidence or runtime activation. Those integrations and live hardware qualification remain pending; the physical admission hook is still disabled.

The device reservation reconciler now requires a strict native inventory scanner independently of its maintenance callback before publishing a new grant. The scan, follow-up workload/source reads and grant publication share a one-minute deadline. Grant publication starts a separate two-minute submission window checked at controller claim and dispatch; renewing the canonical Lease never extends that window. An expired unclaimed grant is revoked and follows the existing Released/manager-settlement path, rather than silently refreshing old preparation. This bounds evidence age; it does not prevent out-of-band device changes or replace the future runtime compatibility authorizer.

Missing new-work dependencies no longer stop claimed recovery, verified completion or revoked-grant release. Tests exercise unavailable strict capability, nonempty/unknown or failed scans, expiry without re-preparation, and quarantine renewal after new-work gates are removed. Shared reservation, maintenance and workload race suites pass. The grant helper has one production caller, this reconciler; runtime registration and cancellation/re-preparation orchestration remain pending. No new live device action has been performed.

Physical Prepared journal reconciliation now clears an unclaimed operation after its reservation reaches Released with immutable manager settlement evidence, when the configuration admission integration is installed. Replanning creates a fresh random operation ID, so it cannot reuse the old grant. Missing, Held, Revoked, claimed, or Released-but-unsettled evidence keeps the journal intact. The existing `finishConfiguration` reservation fence remains the single release boundary. Local apply-state tests verify these cases and new-ID replanning; no native API request is involved. Fresh Held-grant dispatch, cancellation before any grant, runtime registration and hardware qualification remain outstanding, and the admission integration is still disabled by default.

The receipt pipeline now supports an exact existing Prepared journal as well as new preparation. Both routes share admission, the Submitting write-ahead record, its readback, the one-use dispatch permit and Accepted/Unknown receipt handling. Resume checks the current journal, source revision, resource/action and physical identity before admission; a stale Prepared snapshot cannot replay an Accepted or uncertain operation. Tests cover successful single submission, lost response, changed journal/source/target/resource and absent admission.

With a fully installed admission hook, apply reconciliation can persist a physical Prepared journal without submitting, then replan and resume it after a fresh Held reservation appears. Incomplete hooks do not enter that planner. Released/unclaimed preparation retains the settlement/replanning behavior above. The complete Catalyst Center race suite passes after this integration. These local tests cover journal resume sequencing and existing executor regressions, not deployed end-to-end physical execution. Physical Accepted/Verifying action-receipt recovery, concrete runtime registration/authorization and live qualification still need completion before enabling the hook.

Physical Accepted/Verifying journals can now enter the existing task observation and executor readback path when their exact retained reservation claim and controller-worker identity agree. Recovery does not reuse a dispatch permit and does not apply the two-minute new-submission window to an already accepted task. Unknown outcomes remain fenced. Generic physical readback records the full verified action receipt atomically with the Verified transition; missing task evidence, foreign receipt ownership and an older reservation still depending on the prior receipt prevent replacement. Wireless provisioning retains its separate baseline/stable-key verification requirement and is not enabled by the generic receipt path.

Settled reservation retirement now also permits a different current operation, while still requiring the old operation to have left the journal and its verified receipt to remain present. This avoids blocking receipt replacement behind an unrelated active journal; retirement does not alter that journal, its Lease or the receipt. Local tests cover accepted-task recovery after the grant submission window, wrong/missing claims and worker identities, atomic receipt publication, old-receipt protection and retirement alongside a later operation. The adapter regression suite and focused reservation tests pass. Live qualification, concrete runtime authorization/registration, specialized imperative recovery and remaining resource coverage are still incomplete.

The fully admitted apply path now has a managed inventory compiler for ASSIGN intent. It reuses the existing tag/discovery/assignment/role/membership executors in the shared group, preserving each action's journal namespace and preflighting all parts before returning a write. Explicit device serials are required. The ordinary compiler still rejects device mutations, and wireless provisioning intent remains rejected rather than discarded until its specialized manifest recovery is connected. Compiler tests retain assignment, role and membership counts; native fixtures verify assignment-before-role ordering, independent readback and no-op after recompilation. This does not enable the runtime hook or establish deployed end-to-end qualification.

Wireless provisioning and generic physical actions now share action-receipt retention and persistence. Wireless still supplies its baseline-derived stable key and performs its task/identity/provisioning readback first. Both paths enforce ownership, capacity and protection of an older receipt while its reservation remains retained; both reread the persisted journal and exact receipt before reporting success. A schema-pruning fixture confirms that a successful status-write acknowledgement with a missing receipt is rejected. The complete adapter suite passes after consolidation. Wireless dependency compilation and runtime qualification remain pending; this removes duplicate bookkeeping rather than claiming additional provisioning coverage.

Wireless Verifying recovery now resolves the durable device-name digest against the revision-checked inventory source before invoking its specialized receipt verifier. It rejects changed names, serials, explicit addresses, provisioning actions, embedded-controller routing and operation targets. The recorded appliance timestamp and model-configuration requirement are restored unchanged; recovery does not create a new provisioning plan. Focused tests cover the source/record bindings and Unknown-phase rejection. The apply recovery branch calls this resolver and the existing authoritative verifier, but wireless inventory compilation remains blocked until site/profile/managed-AP dependency execution is complete. This is local recovery support, not a claim that wireless manifests or live provisioning are enabled.

Manager retirement is now wired for Catalyst Center reservations when managed topology (or detected topology retirement) is active and the reservation CRD is available. The NetworkController reconciler watches reservation changes, reads evidence uncached, retires manager-settled reservations whose operation has left the journal, and polls while evidence remains. A deleting controller retains its finalizer and existing worker while any matching reservation is pending; a completed DELETE response is corroborated before treating cleanup as finished. Manager RBAC gains reservation update/delete, without creation permission. Managed-topology startup requires the reservation CRD; retirement discovery tolerates older installations without that CRD.

Tests verify automatic retirement, Held/current-journal preservation, deletion fencing, disabled and other-adapter isolation, and the uncached-reader requirement. Receipt auditing also tolerates a deletion request on the same protected reservation without weakening the dispatch rejection of deleting objects. Focused manager/reservation/startup regressions and Helm topology contract checks pass. These changes have not been installed in the lab. New reservation creation, device-worker runtime registration, concrete admission authorization, wireless dependencies and full deployed qualification remain outstanding.

The dedicated managed IOS-XE read-write network worker now registers reservation recovery at startup, independently of optional gNOI upgrade/action gates. It uses one uncached Kubernetes client for journal reads, status writes and canonical Lease renewal. The worker's namespace/device UID and Pod identity must match its maintenance coordinator. Standalone, read-only, app-hosting and other-platform workers do not register this reconciler. No new-work authorization/preparation hooks are supplied yet: accepted claims are quarantined, valid completion can settle, and unused Held grants are revoked before release. This does not enable new physical configuration submissions.

The network read-write role and its binary authorization contract now include reservation status get/update/patch; reservation object create/update/delete authority is not added to that worker. Startup isolation tests, recovery without hooks, reservation protocol race tests and the full Helm topology contract pass locally. These changes are not lab-deployed. Concrete admission authorization, new reservation creation, replacement-worker recovery, wireless dependency compilation and remaining NetAsCode resource execution/qualification are still outstanding.

Manager restart discovery now treats a retained configuration reservation as managed-topology state even when its device, Node and worker bindings are gone. Held, Released and incomplete rows all retain the admission preflight/retirement path until the API object is removed; the bounded list spans all namespaces. A genuinely absent additive CRD remains compatible with older installations, while Forbidden, unavailable and cancelled reads prevent startup from assuming evidence is absent. Race-tested fixtures cover these outcomes. This closes a restart gap in retirement discovery; it does not authorize new grants or provide replacement-worker recovery.

New reservation creation now independently corroborates the bound network worker's namespace-scoped read-write role. It reads the exact bound Pod, the canonical reusable-account RoleBinding and the fixed ClusterRole through the uncached reader, validates the role against `managedprotocol.WorkerClusterRoleContracts`, and rereads UID/resourceVersion evidence before creation proceeds. Read-only profiles, missing reservation-status permission, broadened/aggregated roles, foreign or extra subjects, noncanonical bindings and replacement during reads are rejected. Existing reservation lookup/recovery remains independent of this new-work check. Reservation creation still requires the caller's separate admission/rollout authorization; this role check does not substitute for controller-worker permissions, Lease access or the namespace delegation audit.

The shared reservation and device-worker lifecycle race suites pass, including creation refusal with no live network role and preservation of existing evidence without creation authority. Runtime creation/admission wiring and lab qualification remain incomplete.

Manager reservation creation is now registered for active managed topology when the reservation CRD is available. After ordinary connector reconciliation, a fresh Catalyst Center Prepared physical journal is passed to the shared idempotent creation helper. Retirement-only, paused, deleting, nonphysical and other-adapter paths cannot create reservations. Existing evidence is returned without rewriting or reauthorizing it. The manager gains reservation create permission; device and controller workers do not gain object-create authority.

The creation callback reuses the manager's live topology-policy identity, full native-admission digest/binding and compiled worker-role preflights, corroborates the bound connector's descriptor argument, and requires empty Kubernetes workload inventory. The shared creation helper independently checks the network worker's actual read-write binding and revalidates the candidate. The callback is not the final device authorization gate: strict native inventory, maintenance acknowledgement, device/controller runtime authorization and one-shot dispatch remain separate and are not enabled by creation.

Catalyst Center operation-journal changes now wake the manager despite being status-only updates. Clearing an operation also wakes retirement. Availability-only updates do not cause a self-triggering loop, and the ND status predicate is unchanged. Focused manager/startup race tests cover scope, existing evidence, descriptor mismatch/duplicates and journal events; the Helm topology contract passes. Full deployed creation-to-grant-to-dispatch qualification is still pending, as are the remaining NetAsCode components.

The manager's native-admission verification now separates authenticated-manager identity discovery from verification of the installed typed policies and bindings. Both callers can reuse the same digest, status and binding checks; workers must use the configured manager identity rather than substituting their own service-account name into the expected CEL contract.

Active managed-topology startup captures a validated, non-secret installation binding (protocol, manager identity, policy/ledger names, admission prefix, functional accounts and lease namespace). It is injected after the app/network template split only into managed IOS-XE read-write network workers, and into Catalyst Center connector templates. It is absent from read-only, app-hosting and other-adapter templates. An empty lease namespace preserves the existing per-device namespace convention. The binding participates in the network template revision and Catalyst Center contract hash, so identity changes require a rollout. It is verification input, not an authorization result, and the worker grant hooks are still disabled until their live verification and permissions are connected.

Race tests cover binding validation/round-trip, missing legacy input, unsupported documents, account/namespace errors, template-copy isolation, duplicate injection, Catalyst Center hash changes and unchanged ND templates. Existing managed-worker/controller tests and the full Helm topology contract pass. No lab rollout or new grant qualification is claimed.

Device-side new-grant preparation is now connected for eligible managed IOS-XE read-write workers with a valid installation binding and strict native inventory capability. The existing reservation reconciler verifies the shared installed admission policies/bindings, compiled worker roles, current network read-write grant, connector descriptor, and identical installation data in both bound Pod incarnations. It then uses the existing maintenance acknowledgement and strict inventory/empty-workload checks before publishing a grant. Missing legacy input, invalid setup or unavailable strict inventory preserves recovery-only operation; it does not stop renewal/settlement of existing claims.

The network global observation role gains GET-only admission-policy/binding and ClusterRole inspection. The read-write network profile gains namespace-scoped GETs for connector Deployments/ReplicaSets, NetworkControllerConfig and RoleBindings. No RBAC mutation, token minting or new controller API privilege is added. Compiled role contracts and Helm tests agree on these specific reads. Manager creation now also requires the same installation binding in both workers, preventing creation during a mixed installation rollout.

Local tests cover startup gate combinations, absent/mismatched/duplicate/indirect Pod bindings, replacement workers and wrong accounts. The Helm verification now exercises the shared typed policy GET path using rendered policies with simulated observed status, rejecting missing bindings, modified CEL, unobserved policies and a mismatched manager identity. This is not a live API-server authorization test. Connector dispatch activation, preparation cancellation/replacement recovery, remaining resource execution and deployed lab qualification are still pending.

The isolated Catalyst Center worker now installs an optional configuration-reservation adapter hook from its manager-provided installation binding. Claim and one-shot dispatch use the shared live authorizer. Missing binding preserves the previous nonphysical/default path; incomplete or duplicate hook installation is rejected. Other adapters do not implement or receive this optional hook. The Catalyst Center namespace role now permits reservation GET and claim/completion status GET/UPDATE plus the connector/RoleBinding reads needed to corroborate identity. It still cannot create reservations, write device Leases, or read credential Secrets.

Before deploying an eligible connector, the manager reuses the existing network global observation role through a controller-UID-scoped ClusterRoleBinding. When the installation uses a separate Lease namespace, it also grants the existing read-only Lease role in that namespace. Both role definitions must match the compiled contract. Names/subjects/ownership are exact; foreign or changed grants are not adopted. These read grants are retained through foreground connector deletion and retired before its ServiceAccount/bootstrap cleanup. Retirement discovers prior Lease-namespace grants by controller UID, and retained global grants keep default-off manager restart cleanup active. Binding events map back to the controller namespace, including cross-namespace Lease bindings.

Local tests cover grant creation/idempotence, role drift/collision refusal, namespace scope, retention during worker deletion, cleanup without current installation settings, and one-time adapter-hook installation. The complete Catalyst Center adapter and shared adapter/reservation race suites pass, as do the Helm topology contracts. This connects the runtime dispatch path but does not establish live end-to-end qualification. Preparation cancellation, replacement-worker recovery and retirement while physical work remains active require further work; remaining NetAsCode resource coverage is unchanged.

Ungrantable preparation now has a distinct immutable `preparationCancelledAt` status marker. The shared CAS helper permits only the bound device worker to cancel an ungranted/unclaimed reservation and verifies persistence. It does not fabricate Held/Revoked grant evidence. The CRD and native admission enforce that cancellation cannot coexist with a grant, claim or completion, cannot be removed, and cannot be followed by a grant. Cancelled evidence cannot be deleted before manager settlement. The reservation admission digest is now `sha256:225c6e865164c7ae3f54f0755356e6f964f8c1dce876cf71d3559c30e5564993`; CRD and chart policy must roll out together before new work is enabled.

When the device reconciler observes valid cancellation, it releases only that reservation's canonical Lease holder and stops preparation. It leaves foreign ownership untouched and rejects future/inconsistent cancellation evidence. Manager settlement and journal clearing are not inferred from the marker. Unit/race tests cover stale evidence, wrong Pods, grant/claim refusal, idempotence and exact-holder cleanup. A local Kubernetes 1.35 API-server test verifies cancellation actor separation, immutability, post-cancellation grant rejection and manager-only settlement/removal. Automatic cancellation triggering and manager cleanup for never-granted preparations are still pending; no live lab cancellation is claimed.

Manager settlement now also handles a cancelled, never-granted preparation that already has an exact acknowledged configuration maintenance session. It requires the same canonical Lease incarnation to be idle, the reservation/session/device/Node bindings to match, and cancellation no earlier than acknowledgement. Future cancellation, conflicting grant/claim/completion, foreign holders and replacement Leases retain the guard. Cancellation prevents a new maintenance acknowledgement. The existing Node projection/status sequence removes the manager's guard before persisting Settled; only that persisted exact session permits the retained manager marker. No grant is fabricated.

The connector can clear a Prepared journal for such a cancellation only after validating retained manager settlement. Verified/accepted operations cannot use this cancellation shortcut. Focused manager and journal tests plus the shared reservation, device lifecycle and Catalyst Center adapter race suites pass locally. Cancellation before any maintenance acknowledgement, automatic cancellation triggering, replacement-worker recovery and live qualification remain outstanding. This change adds no NetAsCode resource coverage and has not been deployed to the lab.

Cancellation before maintenance acknowledgement now has a manager settlement path after successful Node projection and maintenance status persistence. For the exact cancelled reservation/device/Node, uncached reads must show no active session, no maintenance taint, an idle canonical Lease with valid managed metadata, and no retained request or holder timing. Device, Node and Lease UID/resourceVersion are reread before the reservation status CAS. An exact acknowledged session continues through the existing session settlement path; unrelated active sessions and Lease holders are left untouched. The helper does not create a session, grant, claim or receipt.

Reservation discovery is shared by device and controller managers, and a device-manager reservation watch wakes cleanup even when cancellation occurred before any Lease mutation. Local race tests cover idle and previously settled sessions, active/exact sessions, busy or malformed Leases, residual requests, guarded/replaced Nodes, conflicting evidence and idempotence. Automatic cancellation triggering, replacement-worker recovery, remaining resource execution and lab qualification remain pending. These changes are not lab-deployed and do not increase the resource parity count.

The bound device worker now automatically publishes pre-grant cancellation when required preparation hooks are missing or device/controller/intent/runtime authorization fails, including the recheck after preparation. It returns the original failure and any cancellation-CAS failure. Lease cleanup is deliberately deferred to the next authoritative reconciliation: an ambiguous write or competing grant/claim must never cause an early release. The cancellation recovery path releases only its own holder, then manager settlement and connector journal cleanup complete the existing flow. Temporary preparation/acknowledgement and strict inventory failures continue to retry without publishing a grant; they do not yet have a bounded cancellation deadline.

The maintenance coordinator explicitly rejects cancelled reservations both at request publication and during preparation reads. Local race suites cover automatic cancellation from missing capabilities/lost binding, unchanged Lease on the publication pass, own-holder release on the next pass, and preservation of foreign holders. Existing grant/claim recovery remains separate. Replacement-worker recovery, bounded preparation retries, remaining NetAsCode resource execution and deployed qualification remain incomplete; no new resource parity or live success is claimed.

Wireless provisioning now has an adapter-aware configuration executor for revision-aware planning, Prepared-operation recovery and native verification. Empty journals use the existing revision receipt planner; a Prepared journal can be replanned only against the same durable baseline/resource, action, device identity and input/controller revisions. Accepted operations cannot be replanned. Source/controller evidence is rechecked after inventory reads, and verification preserves the recorded baseline. This helper does not submit during planning or grant device authority.

Local HTTP/race fixtures cover initial planning, same-baseline Prepared recovery, changed baseline/model requirements, accepted-operation refusal and revision mismatch without native mutations. It is not yet enabled in the managed inventory compiler: site/profile/AP prerequisites, the pinned ten-second AP-location wait and combined manifest restart tests must be connected first. Fabric/embedded controllers and live WLC qualification remain outstanding. Resource parity counts are unchanged.

Physical action receipts now retain an optional `verifiedAt` timestamp alongside the atomically persisted Verified operation. Repeated recording of the same receipt preserves its first verification time. The NetworkController CRD/deepcopy and chart schema include this additive field; legacy receipts remain readable. Receipt corroboration uses Kubernetes semantic timestamp equality across API serialization.

The wireless provisioning executor can require exact managed-AP receipts from the same config/source/controller revision before planning. Missing/legacy timestamps, duplicates, unverified tasks and invalid chronology cannot satisfy pacing. The ten-second upstream interval starts from independent verification, with one extra second to account conservatively for persisted timestamp precision. This survives executor restart without sleeping or creating another task loop. Compiler dependency selection and combined wireless manifest activation remain pending; this is not a claim of live provisioning or increased resource parity.

A wireless inventory stage executor now separates prerequisite writes from dependent imperative provisioning while implementing the same configurationExecutor interface. Unlike an all-members group preflight, it does not require provisioning to be plannable before the assignments it depends on exist. An explicit complete prospective-validation callback is mandatory before any staged planning. Prerequisite group prefixes and provisioning baseline resource identities remain unchanged, so shared journal/task recovery can retain its existing formats. Recovery routes provisioning by a unique durable name digest and rejects ambiguous or missing owners.

Local race fixtures cover prerequisite-first planning, pending dependent actions, preflight failure before writes, unchanged resource identities and exact recovery ownership. The staged executor is not yet constructed by the manifest compiler: concrete site/profile/AP prospective validation, dependency receipt selection and combined native/manifest tests remain necessary. No live activation or increased resource coverage is claimed.

Prospective wireless stage validation now has a request-local collector using the existing authenticated device, complete site-tree, wireless-profile and profile-assignment readers. Assignments pointing to absent sites are rejected. A standalone placement resolver binds explicit serial/device identity, target site and each managed-AP location's explicit profile identity; missing/ambiguous profiles, unknown profile fields, unreachable/replaced devices and fabric/embedded intent cannot pass this resolver. It performs no writes and does not infer inherited profile selection.

Local model and HTTP fixtures cover identity/site/profile failures, read-only collection and stale assignment rejection. Profile dependency content validation, inherited/fabric resolution, compiler construction, dependency receipt selection and end-to-end wireless manifest/live qualification remain pending. The collector is a component of the pending compiler integration; resource coverage is not advanced to complete.

Standalone wireless preflight now validates selected profile contents through the existing wirelessProfileReferences collector, preserved-field payload validation and UUID-binding helper. Placement evidence includes a digest of the profile payload and referenced identities, so an SSID replacement under the same name changes the evidence. Unselected profiles do not trigger content dependency reads. A combined callback validates all standalone placements, rejects duplicate physical targets and checks shared selected profile content once per request.

Local HTTP/race fixtures cover complete preflight, missing SSIDs/profiles, referenced-SSID replacement, preservation of input bindings and duplicate target refusal; existing profile-reference regressions pass. This callback is ready for staged compiler construction but is not yet enabled by it. Inherited/fabric placement, AP observation/receipt linkage, compiler activation and live qualification remain pending. Full NetAsCode parity remains unproven.

Wireless provisioning now resolves managed-AP prerequisite receipts from the native assignment executor's observed desired/current location sets. Nonconverged assignments block planning; converged observations reproduce the assignment journal resource digest with its existing group prefix. Both primary/secondary and anchor fixtures confirm the same identity survives assignment completion and executor restart.

The provisioning executor wraps native submission with another source check, AP readback/digest comparison and receipt/pacing validation. Changed dependency resources, missing receipts or a changed source prevent the native callback. The wrapper does not replace the reservation's one-shot permission. Focused wireless race/HTTP tests pass. Compiler assembly, treatment of already-existing assignments without receipts, inherited/fabric dependencies and live qualification remain pending; wireless manifest execution is still disabled.

Existing matching AP assignments can now pass provisioning pacing without a fabricated CVK action receipt. After native AP readback, initial planning may persist Prepared; subsequent planning/submission requires the exact operation reservation to have existed for the settling interval (ten seconds plus timestamp precision allowance). Reservation creation follows the planned readback, so the timestamp survives restarts and supplies a conservative lower bound. The shared reservation reader verifies the operation binding. Cancelled/released/deleting reservations, missing/future timestamps and premature submission remain blocked. Static dependency keys without AP-executor readback cannot use this fallback; malformed or conflicting existing receipts are not ignored.

Focused wireless race/HTTP fixtures cover existing-placement timing and refusal paths, alongside prior assignment and provisioning tests. No ownership/adoption or task receipt is manufactured. Compiler assembly, inherited/fabric dependency handling and deployed end-to-end qualification are still pending; full parity is not achieved.

An adapter-level standalone wireless compiler now assembles the existing inventory assignment/role/tag group, primary/secondary and anchor AP-location executors, and the revision-aware provisioning executor. It requires the physical runtime admission hook and rejects fabric/embedded placements. AP group prefixes are shared with prerequisite receipt lookup. Prospective validation reuses the standalone placement/profile snapshot helper, resolves the target site and selected-profile SSID model requirement, and detects dependency changes within the plan. The default client compiler continues to reject wireless device execution.

Compiler shape tests verify admission gating, assignment-before-AP ordering, unchanged AP receipt namespaces, resource counts and preservation of REPROVISION intent. Runtime configuration reconciliation does not call this new compiler yet: combined API/journal/reservation tests, multiple-controller Prepared recovery and durable cross-reconcile profile dependency binding must be completed before activation. Existing code paths remain selected. Live WLC and broader resource qualification are still pending.

Wireless provisioning baseline records now optionally retain a canonical SHA-256 dependency digest in their existing bounded resource encoding. Legacy records keep the same encoding. Revision planning binds the digest before comparing retained receipts, and Prepared replanning requires the same encoded resource, preventing a rebuilt compiler from silently accepting changed profile content or referenced UUIDs. The compiler computes the digest from validated placement/profile bindings and reruns its validation immediately before native provisioning submission. Invalid/rebound digests are rejected; resource-size bounds remain enforced.

Multi-WLC Prepared planning now skips non-owning provisioning executors by the durable name digest, allowing the matching executor to handle the operation without unrelated dependency waits. Focused wireless race/HTTP tests cover bound/legacy record round trips, changed dependency refusal and non-owner selection. Combined manifest/reservation execution tests and runtime activation remain pending, as do inherited/fabric placement and live qualification. Full NetAsCode parity is not claimed.

Standalone wireless compilation is now selected by admitted inventory reconciliation; ordinary/nonphysical compilation and other controller types are unchanged. A stateful compiled/native fixture exercises site assignment, AP-location assignment, provisioning, independent task/model/timestamp verification, receipt persistence, supplied-settlement journal release and no-replay. Rebuilding the compiler with a Prepared operation preserves the same baseline; replacing a referenced SSID prevents its reuse. The fixture explicitly supplies reservation/settlement evidence and invokes native write closures: it does not prove real Kubernetes actor coordination or lab operation.

Resource-matrix rows for assignment, AP locations and wireless provisioning now distinguish this compiler/runtime connection from full qualification. Full actor/manifest integration, inherited/fabric/embedded dependencies and live WLC qualification remain pending. This local runtime change is not lab-deployed and does not establish full NetAsCode parity.

Wireless verification now revalidates the dependency digest from the recorded operation before either executor verification or specialized receipt persistence can succeed. The receipt path previously checked task/device/model convergence but did not independently corroborate the new profile dependency digest; this gap is closed using the same standalone snapshot validator. Legacy native records without a digest retain their prior baseline verification behavior.

The stateful fixture now also exercises actual manifest evaluation in Verifying. Replacing an SSID after submission leaves the journal Verifying with no receipt, despite successful task/device status; restoring the bound dependencies allows verification and retained receipt creation. Kubernetes reservation/claim/settlement evidence remains explicitly supplied by the fixture, so real actor coordination and lab qualification are still unproven. Remaining NetAsCode resources and inherited/fabric placement are not declared complete.

### Site AAA execution

The `catalystcenter_aaa_settings` path now has a dedicated credential-aware
executor for existing sites, including Global. It reuses the common source,
section ownership, task journal, secret projection and credential receipt
mechanisms. Both network and client groups must be explicitly configured because
Cisco's replacement API requires both; omission does not guess an inherited or
masked secret. The pinned module's ISE PAN-to-primary-IP fallback is supported.

Each group requires a positive `shared_secret_version` and an authorized
`secretRefs` leaf whose projected JSON envelope carries the same version.
Credentials are not persisted in operation status. Verification combines the
shared correlated successful task with exact public group readback and the
original site UUID. Existing populated settings without a matching CVK receipt
cannot be adopted. Rotation rollback, remapping without a version increment,
partial observations and replaced site identities are refused. Removing a
previous optional secondary server is a real update, not false convergence.

Local HTTP/race tests cover create/update, rotation, ownership refusals, optional
field removal and no replay. The manifest test rebuilds reconciliation across
phases, validates projection-lag refusal and checks retained receipts for secret
leakage. The example at `examples/configs/catalyst-center/aaa-apply.yaml` uses an
isolated pre-existing site. Inheritance/reset/delete and live AAA qualification
remain pending. No lab
mutation is claimed; the last lab authentication result was HTTP 401.

AAA manifests can now include the existing network and telemetry profile
categories, preserving their site references and secret paths. The composition
uses the existing network-setting executor before AAA, with complete observation
of both components before returning a write. A conflicting AAA ownership receipt
therefore blocks even an otherwise valid network-setting update. Resource keys
are unchanged between dedicated and combined models. Shared AAA profiles retain
one projected credential pair regardless of the number of referenced sites.
Combined Global/area manifest fixtures cover network and telemetry ordering,
secret rotation and reconciliation restart; partial observation and foreign AAA
ownership tests enforce refusal before the first mutation. This is local fixture
evidence, not lab qualification.

AAA composition now also accepts the existing IPAM and versioned device-credential
model components. The network-intent parser accepts a product-specific profile
parser while retaining its existing pool, site reservation and credential
assignment validation. The same network executor constructor is shared with
ordinary network settings, avoiding a parallel IPAM implementation. Original
credential JSON pointers survive projection and both credential families use the
same authorized secret snapshot and retained receipt collection.

The combined executor delegates credential verification to the correct component,
so successful device-credential tasks cannot bypass their durable version receipts.
Device credentials are established before dependent site assignments; AAA follows
the existing network work. The manifest fixture now exercises CLI credential
creation/assignment, global-pool creation, site reservation, NTP, telemetry and AAA
through repeated reconciliation, then rotates AAA without replaying the earlier
resources. Global and area AAA cases share the same test. These changes remain
local; lab qualification and the broader resource backlog are still outstanding.

### Planned AP model preparation

A separate parser now projects `sites.floors[].planned_access_points` from the
pinned model while passing the remaining floor geometry through the existing
strict site parser. It maps AP name/type, X/Y/Z coordinates, optional MAC and
radio band/channel/power/antenna fields without inventing omitted values. It
rejects duplicate names within a floor, unknown attributes, malformed MACs,
nonfinite coordinates and invalid radio/antenna values. Source bytes remain
unchanged. Coordinates remain as supplied by the model; they are not converted
based on the floor geometry's unit setting.

This is preparation for the independent planned-position lifecycle, not physical
AP provisioning. The normal site compiler continues to reject placement fields
until controller observation, ID-bound mutation, task recovery and independent
readback are implemented. Floor images are still rejected rather than silently
ignored. Local parser tests pass; no controller mutation or live qualification is
claimed.

Planned AP readback now uses the shared authenticated client against the floor's
planned-position endpoint. It validates AP/radio identities, required position
and antenna fields, MAC syntax and supported frequency values. Pagination starts
at offset one, validates every page and refuses missing/null/partial responses,
duplicate names/IDs, repeated pages and an exhausted inventory bound. It returns
no partial map on failure. A 501-record HTTP fixture verifies the second page;
malformed observation and duplicate-page race tests cover failure behavior.
This reader is not yet an active report or executor. Mutation, resource matching,
recovery, site compiler integration and live qualification remain pending.

The planned AP native executor now plans single-position create/update requests
through the existing authenticated mutation client and `configurationWrite`
contract. It observes all selected positions before returning a write, binds the
floor ID and existing AP ID, requires a task receipt, and independently verifies
selected attributes against complete floor readback. Unselected position, MAC,
radio and antenna attributes survive updates. A desired band must identify one
observed radio unambiguously; updates retain that radio's ID and omit its
read-only band field. Existing AP type replacement is rejected.

HTTP/race fixtures cover creation, update, preserved attributes, ambiguous radio
refusal, incomplete create payloads, missing task receipts, replaced floors and
no replay after convergence. These fixtures call the native executor directly;
they do not establish shared-journal recovery or active manifest execution.
Creation currently requires the API's complete payload; upstream optional
attributes need catalog/default resolution. Site compiler ordering, shared
journal integration, deletion and live qualification remain pending.

Planned AP execution is now selected by the site configuration compiler when
placement intent is present. Geometry retains its existing resource names and
executor; placement uses a separate stable resource key in the same journal.
The composite preflights existing placements before site mutations and requires
complete creation attributes for placements whose floors do not exist yet.
Floor geometry is reconciled first, then placement is replanned against the
actual floor ID. Ordinary site models continue through the original executor.

The manifest fixture exercises floor creation, placement creation, position
update, reconciliation restart and no replay after convergence. An ambiguous
native submission remains Unknown across repeated reconciliation even when the
planned AP is visible in controller readback. Incomplete creation intent blocks
floor creation. The example at
`examples/configs/catalyst-center/planned-ap-apply.yaml` documents complete input
and the separation from physical AP provisioning. Catalog/default resolution,
ambiguous radio selection, deletion and live qualification remain outstanding;
this is not full NetAsCode resource parity.

Inspection of the pinned Catalyst Center provider v0.6.1 revealed an additional
constraint: its planned-AP radio set uses `RequiresReplace` because `bulkChange`
has limited radio-update support. CVK now refuses a changed radio payload before
submitting an update; it does not claim that a native radio edit is supported.
Position-only edits continue to preserve the observed radio IDs and values.
Explicit replacement remains to be implemented. The provider's payload mapper
omits absent optional creation fields; it does not supply catalog defaults.
CVK's current complete-create requirement is therefore still a parity limitation
requiring qualification, not a claim that upstream requires those model fields.

Planned placements now participate in the sites Report compiler as well as
Apply. Reporting compares selected coordinates, MAC, type and radio fields using
complete floor-local readback. Missing floors/placements yield Add, differing
fields yield Update, and partial observations return no drift result. Type and
radio drift can be reported even when their mutation lifecycle is not supported.
HTTP fixtures cover these cases and confirm that absent floors are not queried.

Provider evidence: [planned AP resource v0.6.1](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/resource_catalystcenter_planned_access_point_position.go)
and [payload mapping v0.6.1](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/model_catalystcenter_planned_access_point_position.go).

Planned AP creation now follows the pinned provider's omission behavior for
optional MAC, Z and radio channel/power/antenna attributes. These values are not
fabricated from a static catalog or persisted as intended defaults. Readback
still requires a complete valid controller observation and compares only fields
selected by the source model. A nonempty radio collection with explicit bands is
still required by the current implementation; missing or ambiguous band
selection remains a model-parity limitation.

Native and manifest fixtures exercise omitted fields, simulated controller
assignment of defaults, position updates that preserve those values, restart and
no replay after convergence. Earlier complete-create restrictions in this
chronological log are superseded for these optional fields. These fixtures do
not prove acceptance by the lab appliance; live qualification remains pending.

Planned-radio verification now treats the model as a set of selected attributes,
not an array-index mapping. A bounded matching search requires each desired radio
to match a different observed radio. This supports omitted bands, repeated bands,
and partially specified radios without choosing a mutation target. The search
handles a less-specific selector preceding a more-specific selector and does not
reuse an observed radio. Verified matching leaves observed radio payloads intact;
a mismatch remains a replacement requirement rather than a bulkChange request.
Report mode still reports that mismatch as drift.

Parser, native and manifest fixtures cover band omission and controller defaults;
matching fixtures cover response reordering, overlapping selectors, repeated
bands and refusal to reuse one radio. Empty radio collections, explicit radio
replacement/deletion and live qualification remain outstanding. Earlier
explicit-band restrictions in this log are superseded by the matching path.

### Floor image transport preparation

The pinned floor-image provider uploads PNG, JPEG and PDF as an `image` multipart
field to the floor's `uploadImage` endpoint. Its Read method does not download or
compare image bytes, and Delete retains the image. CVK now has a bounded native
upload primitive using the same session, limiter, transport and no-replay
mutation path as JSON configuration. The multipart content type is supplied per
request; authentication headers and target origin remain controlled by the
existing client. Upload bytes are provided as a snapshot, not read from a model
path or fetched from a model URL.

The helper accepts PNG/JPEG/PDF filename/signature pairs up to 8 MiB, forwards
exact bytes, submits only the basename, requires an accepted task identity, and
does not retry a mutation after HTTP 401 or server errors. Signature checks are
format selection, not full file-content validation. HTTP fixtures exercise these
properties and sanitized failures. Source asset binding, durable upload evidence,
site/image/placement ordering and live qualification are still pending; the
manifest compiler still rejects floor images rather than claiming them applied.

Evidence: [floor-image provider v0.6.1](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/resource_catalystcenter_floor_image.go).

Floor-image source assets now use an optional `cvk-floor-image-assets.json`
index in the model's ConfigMap Data. The JSON object maps each logical NetAsCode
`image_path` to a BinaryData key on that same ConfigMap, for example
`{"maps/floor.pdf":"floor-pdf"}`. The loader copies validated bytes into the
existing source snapshot. No filesystem path or URL is resolved and no new
Kubernetes source, Secret read or RBAC path is introduced. Ordinary model-only
ConfigMaps remain unchanged.

Index parsing rejects duplicate names, malformed or trailing JSON, missing
binary keys, text/binary collisions, model/index key reuse, unsupported file
signatures and bounded-size overflow. Both the index and all referenced bytes
share the source ConfigMap UID/resourceVersion. A journal fixture proves an
image-only ConfigMap update prevents submission of an already-prepared operation
and leaves the original byte snapshot unchanged. This establishes source fencing,
not upload completion. Image model compilation, retained application evidence,
site/image/placement ordering and live qualification still remain pending.


### Floor image model and completion evidence (local qualification)

`sites.floors[].image_path` now has a private parser that resolves only the
explicit same-ConfigMap asset snapshot. Null follows the pinned module's
no-image behavior. Geometry and planned APs retain their existing validators;
invalid assets cannot return a partial plan. Each image has a stable floor
identity and a SHA-256 identity for the copied bytes. Formatting the snapshot
redacts its contents.

The bounded image executor uses the shared multipart transport. Its completion
check requires the correlated successful task and the original floor UUID.
Retained evidence validation binds the config owner, floor, operation, task,
image digest and verification time. Duplicate, foreign, malformed and replaced
floor receipts fail closed. A changed filename with identical bytes does not
force another upload; changed bytes require a new operation. Payload changes
without a corresponding digest are rejected.

Focused race tests cover upload completion, failed/running/wrong tasks,
uncertain operations, replaced floors, and rebuilding an executor with retained
completion evidence. These are local HTTP fixtures, not lab qualification or
an end-to-end manifest test. The pinned Terraform provider has no image-content
readback; upload completion cannot establish that an external actor has not
subsequently replaced the image.

The manifest compiler remains unchanged and still rejects floor images. Atomic
receipt persistence in the shared journal and geometry → image → planned AP
ordering must be implemented before enabling execution. No new worker, CRD,
transport, or physical-device reservation mechanism was introduced here.


### Floor image atomic completion journal (local qualification)

The dedicated image completion transition now revalidates config generation,
source UID/resourceVersion, section ownership, image intent, retained evidence,
the correlated successful task and the original floor UUID. It persists the
Verified operation and the digest-bound action receipt in one Kubernetes status
write, then reads both back using the existing shared receipt persistence
helper. No physical reservation or separate task state machine is involved.

Generic attribute verification cannot advance floor-image operations. Terminal
release requires an exact retained receipt; an API server that prunes the receipt
leaves the operation fenced. Journal fixtures cover successful retention and
release, pruned status, failed/running tasks, floor replacement, source changes,
foreign ownership and attempted generic verification. The manifest compiler is
still not enabled for images: geometry/image/AP orchestration and end-to-end
manifest recovery qualification remain next, followed by live validation.


### Manifest-driven floor images (local qualification)

Apply now loads `sites.floors[].image_path` from the bound ConfigMap asset
snapshot and composes site geometry, floor-image upload and planned AP placement
through the existing configuration journal. The planner validates existing AP
and image state before the first geometry mutation, checks retained receipt
capacity, and refuses to recreate a missing floor with an existing image receipt.
Floors settle before images; images retain completion evidence before AP writes.
Null/absent image paths retain existing images.

The manifest fixture reconstructs the reconciler every tick and verifies floor →
image → AP order, retained completion before placement, an AP-only update without
image replay, and an image-bytes-only update without floor/AP replay. A missing
upload task receipt remains Unknown across reconciliations and blocks placement.
The dedicated completion transition rechecks source binding and task/floor
identity; generic verification cannot substitute for an upload receipt.

`examples/configs/catalyst-center/floor-image-execution.yaml` documents the ConfigMap
asset format and supported Apply flow. No changes were made to ND or physical
upgrade orchestration. Report-mode image observation and lab qualification remain
pending. Successful task evidence does not establish remote byte equality or
provide detection of external image replacement; removal retains the image.


### Floor image preflight and release checks

Additional local fixtures prove that missing/invalid assets are rejected before
controller observation, and receipt-capacity exhaustion or an old receipt for a
now-missing floor blocks earlier geometry creation. A null image path permits
normal geometry/AP execution without counting an image mutation. Release also
validates operation/action/task/target identity independently of exact receipt
matching; altered, duplicate, missing-time and future-time evidence is rejected.


### Physical AP configuration identity groundwork

The pinned module's `cc_access_points.tf` and CiscoDevNet Catalyst Center provider
v0.6.1 map Configure Access Points to the inventory Ethernet MAC
(`apEthernetMacAddress`), not the base radio `macAddress`. Inventory now exposes
that field. A dedicated resolver reuses the existing configuration-device
selector, requires a stable serial for CVK physical admission, and rejects absent,
malformed, multicast, zero or duplicated Ethernet MAC identities. This serial
requirement is stricter than NetAsCode's hostname fallback and remains an explicit
limitation until an equally strong managed-device binding is supported.

The member payload contains `macAddress` and optional desired `apNameNew`, never
the current `apName`. Tests verify that a completed hostname change leaves the
next desired payload unchanged, including ambiguity/RMA-like duplicate inventory
cases and older APs identified by the Unified AP family. No AP mutation is enabled
by this groundwork. Named configuration and radio mapping, provisioning prerequisites,
physical reservation integration, authoritative readback and lab testing remain.


### Named AP configuration and radio mapping (local tests)

A private parser now maps resolved `wireless.access_point_configurations`
entries to the pinned provider's native payload fields. It derives configure
flags from non-null selection (including explicit false), maps AP mode,
failover priority, radio band/type, channel width and assignment enums, and
preserves optional values without manufacturing model defaults. Controller IP
addresses use the provider's nested `address` representation.

Validation covers named-profile uniqueness, reserved hostname-only names,
unknown fields, native numeric bounds, duplicate radio selectors, conflicting
location sources, serving-role requirements for channel/power changes, and
custom antenna/cable values that would otherwise be silently ignored. AUTO and
MONITOR omit radioBand while retaining radioType. Tests cover source immutability
and the supported native field mappings.

This parser is not yet connected to runtime execution. Device-to-profile
references, provisioning prerequisites, physical reservation admission, readback,
recovery and lab qualification remain incomplete. Existing wireless parsing
continues rejecting unimplemented physical AP configuration intent.


### AP inventory-to-profile binding (local tests)

The private AP device parser retains ASSIGN/PROVISION/REPROVISION, RF profile,
selected named configuration and hostname-management intent while reusing the
existing inventory parser for identity/site/tag/role validation. Undefined
profiles, per-device setting overrides, unsupported fields and rename without a
serial fail before observation. ASSIGN rejects selected configuration/rename/RF
settings that it cannot execute. Provisioning currently requires an explicit RF
profile. Settings-only hostname selection can be represented in the parser,
but the physical target resolver still requires a serial for execution.
