Tests cover settings-only, rename-only, provision, reprovision and assignment,
source immutability, bad references and malformed selectors. The generic
inventory path still rejects AP execution until the complete admitted lifecycle
is wired. Native provisioning must be checked against appliance API schema:
the pinned provider's generated model currently serializes its Reprovision
field with an empty JSON path, so that detail must not be copied blindly.


### Native AP provisioning request (local HTTP qualification)

The native request follows [Cisco Catalyst Center 2.3.7.9 AP Provision](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-9/ap-provision/):
POST `/dna/intent/api/v1/wirelessAccessPoints/provision` with networkDevices,
siteId and rfProfileName. The documented device entry has deviceId (and optional
meshRole), not reprovision. CVK preserves PROVISION/REPROVISION as action intent
and does not reproduce the pinned provider's empty-path serialization. Site
assignment is an explicit API prerequisite. Custom AP-zone provisioning and mesh
roles remain outside this currently bounded primitive.

A single-device transport helper reuses the authenticated shared task submission
path. Fixture tests check exact payload, task receipt, one submission on 401/500,
missing-task refusal, invalid inputs before dispatch, and sanitized errors.
No new manifest execution route is enabled: site/RF prerequisite verification,
physical admission, journal recovery and authoritative provisioning readback are
still required, followed by live qualification.


### AP keyed configuration readback (local HTTP tests)

The observation primitive follows [Get Access Point Configuration 2.3.7.9](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-9/get-access-point-configuration/)
using an exact Ethernet-MAC key. It validates the documented direct-object
response identity, AP name and unique radio slot/type identities; partial HTTP
responses, arrays/envelopes, wrong MACs and missing selectors fail closed.
Optional status/settings use pointers so missing values cannot become defaults.

The schema documents provisioningStatus only as a string and radio role/band
as unspecified objects. The primitive preserves these values without assigning
success semantics or guessing object members. Task-plus-provisioning verification
therefore remains incomplete pending authoritative native values and live
qualification; the new reader is not a claim of converged AP execution.


### AP dependency evidence and admission boundary

The AP prerequisite reader now reuses configuration inventory, sites, RF profiles
and exact-site assignment readers. It resolves the stable AP Ethernet identity,
requires a floor and a uniquely named RF profile, and returns assignment as
separate evidence. A digest covers the device UUID/serial/Ethernet MAC, floor UUID,
RF UUID and validated RF attributes. Fixtures prove changes to each identity or
RF content change the digest; missing/unknown RF observations and contradictory
site assignments return no usable evidence. This reader issues only GETs and
grants no mutation authority.

The current physical configuration admission contract in
`config_device_binding.go` requires driver XE, a declared CiscoDevice physical
identity and a matching live Kubernetes Node incarnation. A Catalyst Center-only
AP inventory record cannot satisfy it. AP execution remains disabled while this
admission design is unresolved; it must not be enabled by relaxing the existing
XE node fence or pretending an AP has an XE provider. Dependency/readback
primitives do not close that gap or constitute live qualification.


### Controller-only physical target admission requirements

The architecture review confirms that adding a serial-keyed AP lease beside the
existing node reservation would not establish shared exclusion. `DeviceKey` in
`internal/devicecoordination/mutation.go` hashes namespace/name; the existing
reservation also binds CiscoDevice, Node, worker Pod and device generation.
An AP inventory UUID or Ethernet MAC alone cannot substitute for these objects.

The extension must establish one canonical Kubernetes target declaration per
physical device before any controller-only mutation. A target already represented
by a managed CiscoDevice must use its existing key and node/device-worker path.
A controller-only target needs manager-owned identity validation and a retained
lease binding, an immutable operation/source/controller-worker binding, explicit
actor-scoped submission admission, and durable quarantine/recovery after an
uncertain response. Alias detection and promotion to a node-managed device must
prevent concurrent identities from gaining different lease keys. Controller or
inventory discovery by itself must not authorize that promotion.

The existing controller-configuration-v1 reservation contract, device worker
fence, workload drain and SWIM paths remain unchanged. Before enabling an
additional admission mode, tests must cover duplicate target declarations,
managed/unmanaged classification races, worker replacement, stale source and
inventory identity, ambiguous submission, retained receipt loss, and promotion
while an earlier operation is fenced. Current AP primitives remain disabled in
manifest execution; no new admission mode is claimed implemented here.

Separately, AP profile parsing now rejects HA IP/secondary/tertiary fields without
primary_controller_name, because that is the pinned module's configureHAController
gate. Such values previously parsed into a payload whose enable flag was false.
Focused tests cover each ignored-field case.


### Fabric-site creation and reporting (local qualification)

`fabric.fabric_sites` now accepts resolved name, authentication_template.name and
pub_sub_enabled, mapping to the native fabricSites collection. It requires the
referenced hierarchy site to exist and records that UUID as the operation parent.
Creation uses the shared task submission and configuration journal. Verification
re-resolves hierarchy identity and checks the authentication/pub-sub readback.
Missing booleans and duplicate fabric entries are not absence evidence.

The fabric compiler includes sites alongside existing transit and L3 VN resources.
Local manifest fixtures rebuild the reconciler every tick, verify one creation,
retain Unknown on missing task receipt, block drift before writes, and refuse
completion after hierarchy replacement. Apply/report examples compile through
their respective paths. Apply currently supports create/no-op only; changed
settings are reported but not mutated. Nested fabric site features, updates,
retention/deletion ownership, and lab qualification remain pending.

API contract: [Add fabric site](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-9/add-fabric-site/)
and [Get fabric sites](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-9/get-fabric-sites/).
The 2.3.7.9 listing documents pages up to 500 and reuses the existing bounded
inventory reader; older 2.3.7.6 documentation lists a lower bound and is not the
qualification contract for this reader.


### Nested fabric-zone model (local tests)

A private parser separates `fabric_sites[].fabric_zones` from the enclosing site
without bypassing existing site validation. It requires explicit zone
name/authentication_template.name, validates descendant paths, rejects duplicate
or nested zone declarations and conflicts with intermediate fabric sites, and
preserves source input. Unsupported zone gateway/VN fields remain rejected.
The runtime compiler is not yet switched to this parser.

The pinned provider and native [Add fabric zone](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/add-fabric-zone/)
contract send siteId and authenticationProfileName only. Parent fabric association
is inferred from hierarchy, so execution must independently validate the nearest
actual parent fabric site and bind that identity through submission/recovery.
Parent-first composition, native readback, updates/deletion and live validation
remain pending. Published pagination limits vary by appliance API version; the
reader must not treat a capped first page as a complete inventory.


### Fabric-zone native execution and parent identity (local tests)

A private zone executor observes hierarchy, fabric sites and zones before planning
creation. It rejects hierarchy/fabric collisions, a nearer foreign parent,
nested existing zones and incomplete observations. Missing parent fabric is
pending evidence, never a converged no-op. Create binds the zone hierarchy UUID
and a digest of the parent fabric UUID; readback cannot verify after either
identity is replaced. Authentication changes remain unsupported mutations.

The shared inventory reader now has an endpoint-specific page-size entry point;
existing callers retain 500. Fabric site/zone readers request 50, accommodating
older documented fabric limits without silently stopping on a capped first page.
The same duplicate, oversized-page and bounded-loop checks are reused. Fixtures
cover 51 entries, repeated pages, partial responses, exact create payload,
missing task receipts, wrong readback and parent/hierarchy replacement.

The zone parser/executor are not yet enabled by the manifest compiler.
Parent-first site/zone composition and manifest restart tests remain next, with
live qualification, update and deletion still pending.


### Fabric site/zone manifest composition (local qualification)

The fabric compiler now accepts nested fabric_zones and composes the site and
zone executors through the existing journal. Existing zone drift is preflighted
before site writes, sites settle first, and each zone requires its inferred
parent fabric identity. Resource identities remain distinct and verification
routes to the resource-specific reader. Report mode combines site and zone drift
without mutation.

Manifest fixtures rebuild the reconciler each tick and cover parent-first
creation, no replay, missing site task receipts, missing zone task receipts and
parent replacement after zone submission. Apply/report examples are included.
No lab deployment or qualification is claimed. Authentication updates, deletion,
zone gateways/VNs and other nested fabric dependencies remain pending.


### Fabric Layer 2 virtual networks

The pinned model's `fabric.fabric_sites[].l2_virtual_networks` definitions and
`fabric_zones[].l2_virtual_networks` name references now compile into the existing
fabric executor. Zone references inherit the full parent definition; overrides,
duplicate model names, duplicate VLAN names/IDs in one fabric, reserved VLANs,
invalid traffic types and unsupported fields fail before submission. Optional
VLAN IDs and wireless settings retain omission semantics. Resolved models must
supply the required VLAN name and traffic type explicitly.

Apply provisions sites and zones first, then site L2 networks and finally their
zone instances. An omitted site VLAN ID is allocated by Catalyst Center and read
back before the zone request. The zone uses exactly that allocation. Complete,
paginated native inventory is required; partial responses, repeated pages,
missing identity fields or conflicting inventory fail closed. Existing matching
networks converge without writes; attribute drift is reported and refused in
Apply until updates have an explicit ownership contract.

The shared task journal handles all writes and ambiguous submission outcomes.
Operation identities bind the target fabric UUID and, for zones, the parent
fabric/network UUID and allocated VLAN. An associated L3 VN must already exist
and be attached to the target fabric; defining a global L3 VN alone does not meet
that prerequisite. L3 UUID replacement or detached membership prevents successful
verification. Parent site/zone validation is repeated before L2 completion.

Local fixtures cover restarted reconcilers, parent/zone task receipt loss,
replacement of fabric and parent L2 identities, wrong zone VLAN readback,
pre-existing conflicts before parent writes, L3 association prerequisites,
pagination, Report and unchanged convergence. Examples are
`examples/configs/catalyst-center/fabric-l2-apply.yaml` and
`examples/configs/catalyst-center/fabric-l2-report.yaml`.

This is bounded creation support, not full resource lifecycle parity: L3
association creation, updates, deletion/pruning and live qualification remain
pending. No lab mutation or deployment was performed for this addition; the
previous Catalyst Center authentication failure remains unresolved.

Native contracts: [Add Layer 2 virtual networks](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-9/add-layer-2-virtual-networks/)
and [Get Layer 2 virtual networks](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-9/get-layer-2-virtual-networks/).
The model mapping follows the pinned module's `cc_fabric.tf`, including zone name
references and parent VLAN allocation fallback.


### L3 fabric association primitives

The next fabric dependency now has a strict nested parser and a private native
association planner. Site references support name strings or name-only objects;
zone references are strings, following the pinned `cc_fabric.tf`. Extraction
preserves the existing site, zone and L2 validators and never mutates the source.
Unsupported fields, duplicates, null collections and invalid hierarchy bindings
remain errors.

The native association API replaces the complete VN `fabricIds` array. The
planner preserves all observed memberships and `anchoredSiteId`, adds the requested
fabric once, and records a canonical hash of the complete expected result in the
operation resource. Network UUID and target fabric UUID occupy the existing
journal identity fields. A fresh membership/anchor snapshot must match immediately
before PUT; task receipts remain mandatory and mutation errors are not retried.
Verification checks the complete expected set and anchor, not just target presence.
Missing/null membership fields cannot authorize a replacement write; explicit
empty arrays remain distinct from unavailable inventory evidence.

The shared journal will serialize CVK operations when this primitive is connected
to manifest execution. The native contract exposes no compare-and-swap token, so
external Terraform/UI writers can still race between the final read and PUT; the
pre-submit check and exact readback detect observable conflicts, but do not claim
cross-client atomicity. This does not introduce an independent in-memory lock or
retry loop.

Local tests cover unrelated membership preservation, anchored VNs, no-op,
missing membership evidence, stale/replaced snapshots, lost task receipts,
401/500 no-replay, wrong-operation identity and post-write membership/anchor/UUID
changes. Runtime compilation still rejects these nested L3 fields until parent
resolution and creation/association/L2 dependency ordering are connected and
restart-qualified. Removal/pruning and live qualification are also pending.

Contract reference: [Update Layer 3 virtual networks](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-7/update-layer-3-virtual-networks/),
plus the pinned Terraform provider v0.6.1 association resource's full-list PUT and
anchor preservation behavior. No new lab access or deployment was attempted.


### L3 association target binding

A private L3 association executor now reuses the existing fabric site and zone
observers to resolve hierarchy paths. It validates all requested targets before
planning the first attachment. A zone's missing parent-site membership can only
be deferred when that parent attachment is explicitly present and ready in the
same intent set; a missing network, fabric or undeclared parent dependency is
not treated as convergence.

The journal resource combines hierarchy/site identity, the zone's parent fabric
UUID and the native primitive's complete membership/anchor digest. Target and VN
identity are checked again immediately before submission. Restarted verification
resolves the same hierarchy and requires the parent membership to remain present.
Fixtures cover parent-first attachment, unchanged convergence, replaced zone
before submit, replaced parent fabric/hierarchy after submit, missing network or
fabric, and lost parent membership. Existing site/zone hierarchy validation is
reused instead of introducing another topology implementation.

This executor is not yet activated by manifest compilation. The remaining wiring
must sequence parent creation, global L3 definition, membership attachment and L2
creation while retaining all-component preflight and existing operation recovery.
No runtime rollout or lab qualification is claimed for this addition.


### Manifest execution of L3 associations and dependent L2 networks

Fabric manifests with site/zone `l3_virtual_networks` references now activate the
association executor. The composition reuses the existing site, zone, global L3,
association and L2 executors, with the shared journal owning task submission and
recovery. Its sequence is fabric parents, global L3 definitions, site memberships,
zone memberships, parent L2 networks and inherited zone L2 networks.

All components are observed before returning an initial write. Missing L3
networks must be declared as global definitions in the same manifest. A zone's
missing parent membership must be explicitly declared. L2 preflight/report may
recognize pending associations only by exact declared hierarchy path and VN name;
L2 submission and completion always use strict observed association checks.
Existing unrelated models keep their prior executor composition and identities.

The Apply fixture reconstructs the reconciler on every tick, begins with empty
fabric/L3/L2 inventories and reaches InSync after seven ordered writes, without
replay. Report observes the same seven resources without mutation. Other fixtures
retain the operation fence after lost association task receipts or VN replacement,
and prove undeclared VN/parent dependencies prevent even the initial site write.
Examples: `fabric-associated-apply.yaml` and `fabric-associated-report.yaml` under
`examples/configs/catalyst-center/`.

Native membership evidence must contain an explicit array. Removal, anchor
creation/change, other fabric resources and live qualification remain pending.
No Catalyst Center lab deployment or mutation was performed for this addition.


### Anycast gateway attribute model

A private parser now maps all pinned single-gateway attributes from the module's
resolved model to native field names. It validates the primary pool and L3 VN,
traffic type, explicit auto-generated VLAN-name policy, reserved VLANs, TCP MSS
500–1440, strict booleans and critical-pool naming constraints. Optional nulls
remain omitted. Fabric UUIDs cannot be injected through the model and must be
resolved by the eventual executor.

`INFRA_VN` requires `FABRIC_AP` or `EXTENDED_NODE`. Fields the pinned module drops
for infrastructure pools are rejected when explicitly populated, rather than
silently discarded. Group-based enforcement is limited to the pinned module's
extended-node path. Ordinary VNs reject infrastructure-only flags.

`additional_ip_pools` is an ordered list of at most four distinct pool names,
excluding the primary pool. Native orders are 2 through 5. The pinned provider
v0.6.1 explicitly documents this feature as requiring Catalyst Center 3.2.3 or
later; the parsed intent records that capability requirement. These fields must
not be sent to an older appliance without capability validation.

The parser is not yet connected to runtime compilation. Nested site/zone gateway
extraction, pool/VN binding, version capability checks, native observation,
manifest execution and lifecycle ownership/recovery remain pending. Local parser
fixtures passed; no lab write or deployment was performed.

Sources: pinned module `cc_fabric.tf`,
[pinned provider schema](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/resource_catalystcenter_anycast_gateway.go),
and [native 2.3.7.9 gateway contract](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-9/add-anycast-gateways/).


### Nested anycast gateway definitions and zone references

The private fabric model now extracts site `anycast_gateways` definitions and
zone primary-pool-name references, as the pinned module does. Each zone reference
must resolve uniquely within its enclosing site's definitions. Source objects
are not changed, and parent/zone native payloads do not alias one another,
including ordered secondary-pool objects. Sites, zones, L3 references and L2
networks continue through the existing strict validators.

Duplicate primary pools within a fabric site, repeated/unresolved zone references,
zone definition overrides, null collections and unsupported fields fail parsing.
Explicit VLAN IDs/names must not collide between gateway definitions or with an
independently declared L2 network in the same fabric. Identical inherited VLANs
on separate fabric zones remain valid. Fixtures verify this behavior and prove
that mutating a child's future payload cannot change its parent.

Native observation is the next dependency. The published 2.3.7.9 GET schema does
not return `autoGenerateVlanName`; that input flag cannot be compared directly as
an observed Boolean. Completion will need resolved pool information and native
VLAN-name semantics, alongside allocated VLAN IDs and UUID-bound dependencies.
Secondary-pool readback requires its newer API capability. Runtime compilation
still rejects gateway fields until these observation/execution paths are ready;
no live qualification or lab change is claimed.

Reference: [Get anycast gateways](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-9/get-anycast-gateways/).


### Anycast native inventory evidence

The private anycast inventory reader now uses the shared authenticated GET and
bounded pagination path. It requires exact HTTP 200 responses and complete
identity, primary-pool, VN, traffic and allocated VLAN fields. Repeated pages,
duplicate gateway IDs, duplicate primary-pool identities within a fabric and
conflicting VLAN IDs/names return no partial result. Equivalent allocations in
different fabrics remain valid.

Optional Boolean and numeric fields retain omission evidence. An absent or null
secondary-pool collection is distinct from an explicitly empty collection.
Secondary pools are validated for distinct names and orders 2–5, normalized by
order, and cannot repeat the primary pool. Unknown top-level or secondary-pool
fields are flagged so a future mutation planner cannot silently overwrite an
unmodeled configuration. Native generated VLAN names are accepted as names rather
than being restricted to the stricter standalone L2 VLAN-name syntax.

Local race fixtures exercise malformed identity/flags/VLANs, secondary ordering,
unknown-field evidence, infrastructure pool types, pagination, repeated pages,
partial HTTP responses and per-fabric collisions. The reader does not infer the
write-only `autoGenerateVlanName` flag, nor does it prove newer secondary-pool
mutation capability just because a field is observed. Semantic matching,
pool/fabric dependency binding, execution and live qualification remain pending.
No runtime manifest activation or lab mutation is included in this addition.


### Anycast IP-pool dependency binding

The private anycast dependency resolver reuses the existing global-pool and
site-reservation readers plus IPAM allocation-graph validation. It selects the
primary and ordered secondary reservations and requires their owner site to
match an explicitly resolved reservation-site UUID. It does not infer eligibility
from a matching pool name elsewhere in the hierarchy.

The dependency digest binds reservation UUIDs, owner site, IPv4/IPv6 address
spaces, gateway/settings evidence and the corresponding global pool identities
and content. Replaced or resized resources therefore produce different evidence
even when their names remain unchanged. Missing, ambiguous, relocated or
out-of-parent reservations return no partial binding.

HTTP/race fixtures passed for primary and secondary selection, stable evidence,
reservation/global-pool replacement, prefix changes, wrong-site ownership,
ambiguous names and invalid allocation containment. Fabric-zone inheritance and
anchored-site eligibility must still determine the allowed reservation owner
before this resolver is used in execution. Semantic gateway verification,
manifest execution and live qualification remain pending; no lab mutation or
runtime activation is included here.


### Anycast secondary-pool release capability

Release observation is now shared through `installedRelease`, using the existing
`dnac-release` endpoint and exact HTTP 200 response requirement. Missing, malformed,
partial or invalid release evidence cannot authorize either feature. SWIM's
standard-reload path retains its exact `3.2.3-75346.100` qualified-build check;
only the release observation code is shared.

The private anycast capability helper implements the pinned provider's documented
minimum of 3.2.3 for secondary IP pools. It accepts recognized numeric release and
build formats, rejects ambiguous/prerelease formats and returns the exact observed
release for later dependency binding. It reads again on subsequent checks instead
of permanently caching appliance compatibility. Ordinary single-pool intent does
not make an unnecessary release request.

The numeric minimum is a prerequisite, not live qualification or proof that a
particular account may invoke the API. Future gateway submission must bind and
recheck the returned evidence alongside topology and pool dependencies. Gateway
runtime activation and live qualification remain pending. Tests cover supported
and old releases, malformed/missing/partial evidence, changed release observations
and preservation of SWIM's stricter build fence.


### Anycast semantic completion checks

The private matcher now requires evidence for every declared attribute rather
than converting absent native fields to defaults. Unknown native fields prevent
verification. The write-only auto-generation flag is checked against the native
contract's resulting VLAN name: bound IPv4 reservation CIDR plus VN for a
non-critical gateway, `CRITICAL_VLAN` for critical DATA, and `VOICE_VLAN` for
critical VOICE. Critical status must be observed when applicable; it is not
inferred from missing evidence.

When a parent gateway is supplied for inheritance, its pool/VN identity must
match and the child must use the same allocated VLAN ID and VLAN name. Declared
secondary pools require both known native secondary-pool observation and ordered,
UUID-bearing reservation bindings at the same eligible owner site. Drift returns
non-match; missing or incompatible evidence returns an error.

Local semantic fixtures cover generated/explicit/critical names, declared false
values, secondary bindings, missing fields, unknown fields, wrong pool binding,
parent VLAN/name/identity mismatch and the documented infrastructure naming rule.
These are contract fixtures, not appliance naming qualification. Target/fabric
and anchor resolution, execution/recovery, manifest activation and live tests
remain pending; no task-only success or live qualification is claimed.


### Anycast fabric, zone and anchor dependencies

The private target resolver now composes the existing L3-association topology
observer, fabric-site reader, IPAM binding, capability evidence and anycast reader.
The target must already be attached to its VN. A zone requires parent-site
membership and its parent gateway; an extended site on an anchored VN requires
the gateway on that VN's anchor. The eligible pool-reservation owner resolves to
the parent site for a zone, or the anchor site for an anchored VN. Matching pool
names at an unrelated owner site do not qualify.

Parent gateways must pass semantic comparison before dependency evidence is
returned. The digest binds hierarchy/target fabric, VN UUID, anchor UUID, pool
owner, pool evidence, capability release and parent gateway fields. The target's
own current gateway is observed separately, so successful creation does not
change its prerequisite digest. Missing memberships/parents, wrong pool owners
and parent drift return no partial binding.

HTTP/race fixtures passed for ordinary sites, zones, anchored extended sites,
missing membership/parent, parent drift, reservation ownership, replaced parent
UUIDs and replaced VN UUIDs. These fixtures validate the modeled native contract;
actual appliance topology and inheritance remain unqualified. The next execution
layer must bind/recheck this evidence around shared-journal submission, reuse
inventory snapshots across a multi-gateway reconciliation, and handle declared
parent dependencies without prematurely treating them as converged. Runtime
activation, lifecycle ownership/removal and live qualification remain pending.


### Anycast native creation planner

The private creation planner now returns the existing `configurationWrite`
contract. It sends one native gateway per POST through the shared authenticated,
non-replaying task transport, requires a valid task receipt and binds the target
fabric plus prerequisite digest into the operation identity. Immediately before
submission it re-resolves dependencies and refuses changed evidence or an
externally appeared target.

Zone/inherited creation copies the parent's allocated VLAN ID. When automatic
VLAN naming is disabled, it carries the parent's verified VLAN name; automatic
naming does not send a conflicting explicit name. Ordinary-pool creates require
all native required Boolean fields in the resolved model. Infrastructure pools
omit inapplicable ordinary-pool flags, matching the pinned provider. No defaults
are invented from missing resolved fields.

Verification checks the operation's action, fabric and dependency identity,
then requires semantic native readback. Existing matching gateways converge
without a write; existing attribute drift is refused until an update/ownership
contract is implemented. HTTP/race fixtures pass for create, zone allocation,
no-op, stale dependencies before submission, pool replacement after submission,
wrong readback, missing task receipts and incomplete native payloads.

The planner is not yet activated by manifest compilation. Multi-resource inventory
reuse, declared-parent ordering, full manifest restart/ambiguity qualification,
updates/deletion and live qualification remain pending. No lab mutation or rollout
was performed for this addition.


### Shared anycast inventory per reconciliation pass

Anycast dependency resolution now separates inventory collection from local
binding. One collection pass observes the distinct fabric/VN targets, validates
the IPAM allocation graph, reads gateways and, when needed, reads the appliance
release. All gateways in that pass reuse indexed reservations, global pools,
fabrics and native gateway records. Existing topology observers retain their
validation; their fixed read overhead does not grow per gateway.

The snapshot belongs only to that preflight/readback pass. Submission still loads
fresh dependencies, and subsequent reconciliations do not reuse old snapshots.
The native API does not offer a transactional snapshot; this collection is not
claimed to be atomic across endpoints.

A multi-gateway HTTP/race fixture asserts bounded collection calls, performs 100
rounds of local resolution with no further API calls, verifies distinct pool
bindings, and proves that a fresh check detects a replacement reservation without
changing previously collected evidence. All existing anycast model, observation,
dependency and native-creation fixtures continue to pass. Manifest activation and
live qualification remain pending.


### Multi-gateway execution and declared parent ordering

A private `configurationExecutor` now plans the gateway set from one collected
inventory pass. It can defer an absent parent gateway only when that exact fabric
and primary-pool identity is explicitly declared in the same set. All VN
memberships, pool ownership and capability prerequisites still require evidence.
An existing child with a missing parent is an inconsistent state, not permission
to adopt it or fabricate completion.

The executor validates every missing target's native creation requirements and
checks existing target drift before releasing any write. It selects a ready
parent independently of input ordering, then replans children after native parent
readback provides the allocated VLAN. Pending-parent evidence cannot generate a
submission payload or satisfy verification. Report can show both planned parent
and child additions without mutation.

HTTP/race fixtures pass with intentionally reversed input order, reconstructed
executors between writes, parent allocation inheritance, unchanged convergence,
parent replacement after child submission, missing parent declarations, incomplete
child payloads and missing zone membership. Invalid child intent prevents even a
valid parent write. Manifest composition with fabric/VN creation, full journal
restart/ambiguity fixtures, lifecycle ownership and live qualification remain
pending; runtime compilation has not yet enabled gateway models.


### Anycast manifest Report/Apply activation

Gateway models now compile into a composition around the existing fabric
executors. Gateway preflight runs before any fabric prerequisite write: it
validates complete pool inventory, the eligible reservation owner, capability
evidence and required creation attributes. It defers only missing fabric/VN
prerequisites explicitly declared in this manifest. Reservations must already
exist; same-composition IPAM creation is not yet supported.

The sequence reuses fabric site/zone creation, global L3 definitions and
membership executors, then the parent-first gateway executor. Native membership
and parent gateway evidence are mandatory by the time a gateway is submitted.
Gateway completion also checks that the preceding fabric composition still
converges. Existing models without gateways retain their prior composition.

The full journal fixture starts with empty fabric/VN/gateway inventory and
pre-existing hierarchy/IPAM. It reconstructs the reconciler at every tick and
reaches InSync after seven ordered writes: site, zone, L3 definition, site/zone
memberships and parent/zone gateways. Report returns seven planned resources
without writes. Lost parent-gateway receipts remain Unknown without replay;
parent UUID replacement after child submission retains the operation fence.
Missing reservations and incomplete native payloads prevent even the first site
write. Examples: `anycast-gateways-apply.yaml` and
`anycast-gateways-report.yaml` under `examples/configs/catalyst-center/`.

Creation and unchanged-state convergence are enabled with Retain policies.
Attribute updates/deletion, bulk optimization, same-composition IPAM creation,
broader anchored/secondary-pool manifest qualification and actual appliance
qualification remain pending. No lab rollout or mutation was performed here.


### Secondary-pool manifest qualification and gateway allocation conflicts

Full manifest fixtures now qualify ordered secondary pools through parent and zone
creation, including unordered native secondary-pool readback. Unsupported releases
prevent the first fabric write. Release changes, replaced reservation identities
and missing secondary-pool readback retain the gateway operation instead of
allowing completion or progressing to a child gateway.

Before creation, the inventory pass rejects another gateway in the same fabric
that occupies the requested VLAN ID, inherited parent VLAN, explicit VLAN name,
or determinable generated VLAN name. Submission refreshes that inventory so a
conflict appearing after planning still prevents POST. Other fabrics may reuse
allocations. Naming rules are shared with semantic readback verification.
HTTP fixtures cover conflicts introduced between planning and submission and
confirm zero gateway mutations; unrelated-fabric allocations still converge.

This is fixture qualification, not appliance qualification. Controller-side VLAN
auto-allocation remains authoritative, and the API does not provide atomic
reservation of a VLAN between inventory and submission. Cross-resource conflicts
with native L2 networks, broad anchored manifest qualification, lifecycle ownership,
bulk execution and same-composition IPAM creation remain pending.


### Fabric multicast replication primitive

The pinned module maps `fabric_sites[].multicast.replication_mode` to the
replication-mode resource independently of multicast VN configuration and wireless
multicast. A private native primitive now reads the complete paginated
`/dna/intent/api/v1/sda/multicast` inventory and plans the single-fabric PUT for
`HEADEND_REPLICATION` or `NATIVE_MULTICAST`. It reuses hierarchy/fabric inventory,
transport authentication and the existing configuration-write/task contracts.

The journal identity binds the site hierarchy UUID, native fabric UUID, path and
requested mode. Immediately before PUT, a fresh observation must still equal the
planned baseline, including whether native configuration existed. Readback must
match both immutable identities and the requested mode. Missing task receipts are
errors and are not retried by this primitive. A controller-side concurrent write
between that read and PUT remains possible; the API does not offer a CAS token.

The source contracts are the pinned provider's
[replication definition](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/gen/definitions/fabric_multicast_replication_mode.yaml)
and Cisco's [multicast update API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/update-multicast/).
The provider implements deletion as resetting to headend replication, which CVK
has not enabled without lifecycle ownership evidence.

This primitive is not runtime-enabled. Multicast VN prerequisites, composition,
physical device mutation coordination, shared-journal manifest qualification and
live appliance qualification remain outstanding. No lab mutation was performed.

Native HTTP/race fixtures passed for initial configuration, changed mode and
unchanged convergence; stale baseline and replaced fabric refusal before PUT;
replacement after submission, wrong/missing readback and lost task receipts;
and 501-row pagination, duplicates, missing fields, unsupported modes and errors
on later pages. These are primitive tests, not shared-journal restart evidence.


### Fabric multicast VN and RP model

A private parser now covers the pinned `fabric_sites[].multicast` object:
replication mode, explicit wireless enable/disable, virtual network name and pool,
IPv4 SSM ranges, and RP definitions. RP mapping includes external IPv4/IPv6
addresses, fabric device-name references, default flags and IPv4/IPv6 ASM ranges.
Fabric references remain unresolved names until inventory can validate UUIDs,
roles and site membership. Native fabric RP addresses are controller-allocated;
the pinned module suppresses supplied address fields for those RPs, and this
parser follows that behavior. RP `name` is retained only as a model-local label:
it is absent from the pinned provider's native resource definition.

Multicast prefix sets are normalized and deduplicated. Validation rejects
non-multicast/wrong-family/non-network prefixes, unsupported SSM ranges,
overlapping SSM/ASM intent, ambiguous external RP addresses, invalid cross-family
external RP settings, duplicate VN/label identities and multiple default RP
claims per address family. False remains explicit and null optional values stay
omitted. Explicit empty RP collections remain distinguishable from omission for
future ownership-aware updates. Input maps are not modified.

The field contract is grounded in the pinned provider's
[multicast VN definition](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/gen/definitions/fabric_multicast_virtual_networks.yaml)
and Cisco's [multicast VN API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/add-multicast-virtual-networks/).
Inventory-dependent constraints are not claimed here: dual-stack pool support,
fabric RP role/cardinality across VNs, live identity resolution, generated address
preservation, membership removal and native execution/readback still need their
respective implementation and qualification. The runtime compiler remains gated.


### Multicast VN native inventory

The multicast VN reader uses the existing authenticated transport and bounded
500-row pagination helper. Native configuration IDs and `(fabricId, VN name)`
keys must be unique across the complete result; an invalid later page returns no
partial inventory. Required identity/pool fields and nested types are validated.

The observation projection preserves controller-allocated IPv4/IPv6 fabric RP
addresses, which must not be discarded as create-only fields. RP device IDs and
multicast ranges are normalized as sets, RP list ordering is canonical, and
missing/null RP observations remain distinct from explicit empty lists. Unknown
fields are flagged without retaining their values. Consumers must inspect that
flag before treating the projection as a complete write/readback contract.
Duplicate RP identities, including the same fabric devices reporting differing
allocated addresses, are refused. Role, pool capability and cross-VN constraints
remain for dependency resolution.

The response shape follows Cisco's
[multicast VN inventory API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/get-multicast-virtual-networks/).
This adds observation support only; it does not activate runtime configuration or
establish ownership, task recovery, appliance compatibility or live qualification.


### Multicast VN payload and observation matching

Private payload construction now binds a target fabric UUID and resolved RP device
UUIDs. Unresolved names and multiple names resolving to the same device are
refused. RP matching uses external addresses or the sorted fabric-device set,
independent of list order and model labels. The inventory reader uses this same
identity rule when detecting duplicate observations.

Create requests omit IDs and appliance-allocated fabric RP addresses. Update
payloads retain the native configuration ID, allocated addresses and observed
optional settings unless explicitly declared. Missing allocation evidence,
unknown response fields, changed fabric/VN/pool identities and incomplete RP
observations prevent construction. Declared RP and ASM/SSM range removal remains
refused until lifecycle ownership is implemented. Merged intent is checked for
SSM/retained-ASM overlap and duplicate default RP claims.

Semantic comparison reuses payload construction, including all these evidence
checks, so omitted settings and reordered sets cannot create artificial drift.
This is not native execution or live convergence: device role/site membership,
dual-stack pool dependencies, operation receipts, composition and physical
mutation coordination remain pending, and the compiler has not enabled writes.


### Multicast reservation dependency binding

Multicast now reuses the fabric pool inventory's allocation validation and
reservation/global-pool identity/content digest. The existing anycast binding
extracts ordered-name binding into a shared method; its secondary-pool semantics
remain at the existing caller. Multicast selects its one declared reservation
with an explicit topology-derived owner UUID.

The binding requires IPv4 space, validates optional IPv6 space, and refuses IPv6
RP addresses/ranges/default intent on an IPv4-only pool. A dual-stack pool permits
at most one fabric RP device per RP definition. Retained native RP settings are
checked too, so omitting an RP declaration cannot bypass capability checks.
Reservation replacement and IPv6 prefix changes alter dependency evidence.

This does not yet establish fabric device roles, site membership, cross-VN RP
cardinality or resolved topology/anchor ownership. Those are separate prerequisite
checks needed before enabling native multicast execution. The runtime compiler
remains gated, and no live appliance mutation was performed.


### Fabric device membership evidence for multicast RPs

A fabric-scoped membership reader now uses the existing authenticated pagination
helper with the required `fabricId` query. It keeps native membership ID separate
from network device UUID, requires the returned fabric to match, normalizes role
sets and refuses missing/unknown roles and duplicate identities across pages.
This is a membership projection only; it cannot be used as a fabric-device update
payload because it deliberately excludes border configuration.

The accompanying RP-set validator accepts one border or edge device, two devices
only when both have border roles, and at most one device for dual-stack pools.
Control-plane-only membership does not establish RP eligibility. Repeated
references across VNs count once by network device UUID. The validator requires
its caller to supply the complete site-wide RP union; assembly of that union,
physical serial binding and mutation admission are not implemented here.

The inventory contract follows Cisco's
[fabric device API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/dna-center/2-3-7-5/get-fabric-devices),
with the additional wireless-controller role documented in the
[2.3.7.6 changelog](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/api-changelog/).
Native mutation, manifest convergence and live eligibility remain unqualified.


### Prospective site-wide multicast RP validation

The site validator combines normalized proposed VN payloads with native VNs
outside the manifest. Existing entries must retain their native configuration ID
and pool identity. Unknown or incomplete retained RP evidence prevents evaluation.
Foreign fabrics are excluded from the RP union, while every VN in the target
fabric contributes its validated pool dependency digest.

The resulting complete set of fabric RP device UUIDs is passed to the existing
membership/role validator. A third RP, an edge RP alongside another RP, and a
dual-stack fabric-RP VN sharing two site RP devices are refused. Repeated device
references across VNs count once. A dual-stack VN with no fabric RPs does not
itself constrain other VNs' fabric-RP count. Returned membership evidence is
ordered for later dependency binding.

This remains a pure snapshot validator. Its caller must gather complete fresh
native inventories, resolve physical serial identities and construct proposed
payloads through the existing preservation/ownership checks. It does not issue
writes or establish runtime convergence, and live qualification remains pending.


### Multicast RP physical inventory identity

RP name resolution now accepts exact/FQDN names or unambiguous short hostnames,
following the existing managed-anchor convention, then uses the shared device
selector. Selected devices require a unique canonical physical serial using the
existing topology identity implementation. Ambiguous short names, duplicate
controller UUIDs, missing serials and serial collisions across inventory are
refused without returning partial bindings.

Retained RPs are also bindable directly by UUID, so VNs outside the manifest do
not escape physical identity validation. The returned devices are sorted and
carry canonical serials; changing the hardware serial while preserving a UUID
changes this evidence. The source inventory is not modified.

These are inventory bindings, not Kubernetes admission or lease ownership.
Fresh combined snapshot collection, dependency hashing, reservation coordination
and native operation recovery remain required before runtime activation.


### Multicast combined preflight snapshot

A request-local collector now joins the existing topology/VN-membership observer,
IPAM reader, multicast inventory, physical device inventory and fabric membership
reader. Desired VNs must already belong to the target fabric. Payload construction
preserves existing native settings, then the prospective complete site is checked
against pool and RP constraints, including unmanaged VNs and retained physical RPs.

The snapshot carries per-VN payloads, existing target observations, selected
physical devices and a deterministic pre-submit digest. The digest includes
native site multicast state, proposed payloads, hierarchy/fabric/VN identities,
normalized membership sets, pool digests, native fabric membership IDs/roles and
canonical physical serials. Native generated IDs used only for internal candidate
validation are not included in create requests.

This digest represents a planning baseline; it is not a completion receipt and
must be refreshed before submission. Native task execution, separate post-task
readback, mutation reservations and shared-journal recovery remain unimplemented
for this VN path. The compiler is still gated and no live mutation was performed.


### Native multicast VN submission and readback

Private single-VN create/update planning now uses the complete-site snapshot,
returns the existing configuration-write contract, and requires a native task ID.
Create uses POST without a native configuration ID; update uses PUT with its
existing ID and preserved RP allocations. Unchanged declared state returns no
write. A newly collected pre-submit snapshot must match the planning baseline;
there is no automatic mutation retry after an ambiguous response.

A separate dependency digest binds hierarchy/fabric/VN identity, pool evidence,
fabric memberships, physical RP serials and retained VNs outside the manifest.
Unlike the full planning baseline, this digest allows the target's expected
creation or attribute change. Readback revalidates those dependencies, update
UUID identity and declared-state semantics, including allocation evidence.
Changes to retained VNs are also fenced during verification. API task completion
must still be established by the caller's shared journal; this helper alone does
not prove successful task completion.

The native update shape follows Cisco's
[multicast VN update contract](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/update-multicast-virtual-networks/).
There is no API CAS between preflight and mutation. Runtime compiler activation,
physical mutation coordination, durable ownership/removal, full journal restart
qualification and live validation remain pending. No lab mutation occurred.


### Complete fabric mutation footprint

Review of the current admission implementation found that
`configurationResourceIdentity` and `ControllerConfigurationReservation` represent
one target inventory UUID/serial. A multicast VN API request can deploy across the
fabric; serializing only its RP devices would not exclude upgrades of other
members. The multicast planning snapshot now binds every device returned by the
fabric membership inventory, including non-RP members. Both baseline and
verification dependency digests include their membership IDs/roles and canonical
physical serials. Missing or ambiguous physical identity on any member prevents
planning.

RP eligibility still uses the site-wide RP subset. It does not determine the
mutation footprint. This distinction preserves the existing single-device
reservation protocol while exposing the complete required target set for future
coordination. Runtime activation remains blocked on multi-device reservation
acquisition, all-target dispatch validation, retained fencing after ambiguous
submission and verified release; no single-device permit is treated as authority
for a fabric-wide mutation.


### Multicast manifest Report integration and explicit Apply gate

The fabric compiler now projects nested multicast VN and replication-mode intent
alongside existing site/zone/gateway models without modifying the source model.
Report uses fresh combined snapshots to emit Add/Update drift or unchanged state
for multicast VNs, and native replication observation for mode drift. It currently
requires the target fabric/VN attachments and reservations to exist; prospective
creation of those prerequisites is not report-qualified here. Wireless fabric
multicast remains explicitly unsupported instead of being silently ignored.

Accepting a Report model does not activate Apply. A compiler wrapper rejects
Apply before the first prerequisite write, and also refuses verification through
this unfinished path. Existing models without multicast retain the previous
executor. Example: `examples/configs/catalyst-center/multicast-report.yaml`.

This closes a read-only compiler path, not resource parity. Group reservation
coordination, Apply composition, durable ownership, recovery and live appliance
qualification remain open.


### Fabric footprint to managed Kubernetes identities

A group binding helper now resolves the complete physical footprint against the
existing CiscoDevice and Node rules. It uses canonical serial ordering, validates
all inventory UUIDs/serials, lists declarations across namespaces to detect
aliases, and independently checks each live Node incarnation and physical
inventory. Any invalid member returns no partial group.

The helper lists declarations once initially and once after reading all targets,
then rechecks each Node. New aliases, declaration resource-version changes and
Node replacements during collection invalidate the result. This requires an
uncached API reader and remains an evidence snapshot, not an atomic cluster
transaction or dispatch grant. The existing single-device resolver and reservation
protocol are unchanged; multi-device reservation acquisition/recovery is still
required before multicast Apply can be activated.


### Separate group operation identity contract

A non-runtime group identity contract now binds a logical configuration operation
to its complete canonical physical target set. Each target includes controller
inventory UUID, physical serial, CiscoDevice name/UID and Node name/UID. It refuses
empty/ambiguous target sets and single-device `TargetSerial` overloading. The
existing v1 digest and reservation naming are unchanged; v1 rejects operations
whose physical scope is supplied only through this new group identity.

The digest is independent of target order, serial letter case, task receipt and
operation phase, but changes with source identity, logical resource identity or
any physical target removal/replacement. Fresh validated fabric bindings can be
projected into this contract with repeated namespace/device/Node checks. This
identity format is not an enabled admission protocol: no CRD writer, manager,
worker or dispatch path currently persists or grants authority from it.

Remaining group work includes versioned persistence, mixed-worker/schema gating,
per-device reservation coordination, all-target dispatch revalidation, retained
fencing after ambiguous submission, and verified release/recovery.


### Bounded group identity record validation

The group identity contract now rejects repeated CiscoDevice or Node names even
when their UUIDs differ, malformed Kubernetes names, and oversized/control-bearing
inventory or object identity tokens. This prevents a proposed group from
representing two incarnations of one named managed target.

A bounded non-secret record encoder/decoder provides canonical restart evidence.
Decoding requires both the actual operation and a separately journal-bound
expected group digest. A record carrying a recomputed checksum for a reduced
target set is therefore insufficient. Unknown versions/fields, trailing JSON,
truncation, missing digest and changed operation/target evidence are refused
without a partial result. Operation phase/task transitions remain compatible.

No journal or CRD writer uses this format yet. Atomic persistence of the record
and expected digest, immutable admission, mixed-version worker gates and actual
reservation recovery remain pending. Encoding or decoding this evidence does not
confer dispatch authority.

### Typed group journal evidence and legacy-path isolation

The NetworkController operation schema now has an optional `physicalGroup`
record containing a version, operation-bound digest, and the complete physical
inventory/CiscoDevice/Node identity set. Generated deep copies and both canonical
and Helm CRDs preserve the record, including operation snapshots in action
receipts. A group cannot also declare a single-device `targetSerial`.

A local constructor binds only unsubmitted Prepared operations and refuses to
rebind existing group evidence. Validation recomputes the digest across the
immutable operation and complete target set; task/phase progression does not
change it. This adds persistence vocabulary, not a runtime group writer.

The Apply reconciler retains a group journal with
`GroupReservationRecoveryRequired`. Existing submission, advancement and release
helpers independently refuse these records, including Prepared and Verified
boundaries. This prevents logical-resource or single-device recovery paths from
silently clearing group evidence. Older deployed workers do not understand this
field, so schema/worker compatibility gating remains mandatory before runtime
writers are enabled. Per-device reservation coordination, complete-set claims,
pre-dispatch checks and verified group settlement are still pending. Multicast
Apply remains disabled; lab qualification has not been performed for this work.

### Complete group reservation candidates and retained-set binding

A group candidate constructor now maps every journal-bound physical target to
its observed CiscoDevice, Node and dedicated network worker, using the same
object checks as single-device reservations. It returns the complete set in
canonical serial order, or no candidates if any member is absent, duplicated,
replaced or unready. All members share the exact connector incarnation and
complete operation/group digest. Each member has a distinct reservation name
that incorporates the full digest, preventing reuse of another group's member
evidence after a source or target-set change.

Retained-set validation checks every persisted reservation UID, name, finalizer,
controller/source binding, native inventory ID, physical identity and managed
object reference against the journal. It refuses partial sets, mixed connector
incarnations, deleting records and garbage-collection ownership. Returned records
are copies, in canonical order. This verifies identity only: live intent/worker
ownership, grants, leases, claims and completion require separate checks.

The proposed group protocol remains unsupported by the installed reservation
CRD and existing runtime admission paths. No candidates are created by manager
reconciliation, and no lease or device state is changed. Atomic group preparation,
all-member claim/dispatch checks, cancellation and verified settlement remain
pending before multicast Apply can be enabled.

### Fresh group candidate collection

Group reservation preparation now has an uncached read-only collector. It binds
all physical targets from a cluster-wide CiscoDevice inventory, resolves each
Node's dedicated network worker, and reuses the existing connector ownership and
intent/source checks. Connector selection and source validation are shared with
the single-device path rather than duplicated for fabric operations.

After collecting dependencies, a second global device list rejects newly
introduced aliases and changed device versions. Final object reads corroborate
the controller, devices, Nodes, network workers, Deployment and connector
incarnations/resource versions. Any inconsistency discards the whole candidate
set. These reads do not constitute a cross-object transaction, and must be
repeated at future creation/claim/dispatch boundaries.

Race-enabled fixtures cover valid complete collection, late aliases, late
resource-version changes, missing network-worker binding, overlapping connectors,
changed intent and stale controller snapshots. This remains preparation support:
manager writes, group actor admission, coordinated grants/claims, recovery and
live qualification are not yet enabled.

### Complete-group lease and preparation validation

Group lease evidence now validates the exact journal-bound reservation set and
one canonical mutation Lease per member at a single observation time. The same
holder, UID, acquisition, transition, renewal and expiry checks used by existing
single-device reservations are reused. Missing, duplicate, foreign, replaced,
revoked, cancelled, completed or settled member evidence invalidates the group.
The trusted Lease namespace comes from caller configuration.

A separate preparation check requires an unsubmitted Prepared journal, current
controller generation, fresh native preparation on every member, and no existing
claims. Lease renewal cannot refresh the two-minute preparation bound. This
separation avoids interpreting a live lease as fresh preparation or treating a
partially claimed group as a new claim opportunity.

Both checks validate supplied evidence only. They do not create reservations,
acquire/renew leases, claim members, authorize dispatch, or release fencing.
Group protocol schema/admission, coordinated claim/cancellation/recovery and
live qualification remain pending. Existing v1 grant validation continues to
reject group reservations.

### Durable group claim coordination

A staged group claim coordinator now validates the complete unclaimed reservation
and live Lease set before and after caller authorization, then persists each
member claim in canonical order using the existing claim CAS/readback routine.
It rechecks controller identity, member version and current grant freshness
before each write, and verifies the complete claimed set afterward. Authorization
receives copies; it must establish installed group admission/worker compatibility,
intent/worker ownership and workload/maintenance policy.

Member writes are not a transaction. A conflict, lost response, changed
controller, revoked grant or failed readback stops the sequence without returning
partial results or clearing earlier claims. Existing claims cannot be reused by
this entry point. Fixtures verify retained evidence after interrupted sequences
and refusal of repeat claims. The successful result is claim evidence, not a
serializable or process-local dispatch permit.

No runtime path invokes this coordinator, and the installed reservation CRD still
rejects the group protocol. The group-specific one-shot submission transition,
final authority check, partial-claim recovery/cancellation and verified settlement
must be completed before enabling fabric-wide writes. No lab mutation was made.

### One-use group submission and dispatch permits

Successful group claims can now create a process-local submission permit through
a dedicated factory. Persisted claims alone cannot reconstruct it. Consuming it
revalidates all member claims/grants and caller authorization, then performs the
Prepared-to-Submitting journal CAS. Only an exact readback of the intended record
captured before the write returns a final dispatch permit. Kubernetes timestamp
serialization is handled without weakening operation/target identity checks.

The final permit is also consumed once, including on failure. Copies share atomic
consumption state. It repeats complete-group claim/lease/preparation validation
and authorization immediately before the caller's single no-retry request.
Fixtures cover concurrent/copied permits, authorization changes, revocation,
changed claims/controller, lost journal responses and pruned group identity. A
failed transition or final check retains the journal and claims for recovery.

These are staged protocol primitives. Their authorization callback must supply
installed schema/admission/worker compatibility, live intent/physical ownership,
manager-acknowledged scheduling guards and workload checks. Runtime integration
of that complete authorizer, group admission, cancellation/recovery and verified
settlement is still pending; multicast Apply remains gated and no lab mutation
has been performed for this increment.

### Live all-member authority checks

A group authority reader now corroborates current intent/source ownership,
exclusive cluster-wide physical declarations, isolated connector identity,
each Node/network-worker incarnation, and the exact acknowledged maintenance
session, canonical Lease and scheduling taint for every member. It reuses the
existing per-device configuration maintenance protocol and workload checks; it
does not add another device maintenance mechanism. Native workload preparation
is attested by each bound worker's fresh grant. Kubernetes workloads are queried
directly, and partial claims or an unclaimed Submitting group are refused.

The reader repeats global alias checks and object-version checks after collecting
all members, then rechecks intent, connector and workloads to catch changes during
a long group scan. Fixtures exercise missing guards, wrong session identities,
active workloads, changed connector/intent, revoked grants and partial claims.
A composed fixture runs live authorization through claims, journal submission
and final permit checking, including guard loss after claims and workload arrival
after Submitting.

Installed group schema/admission and worker compatibility remain separate gates.
The reader alone cannot authorize dispatch or release, and no runtime group path
or lab deployment is enabled by this work. Group manager/device-worker lifecycle,
cancellation/recovery and settlement are still required before multicast Apply.

### Verified group completion and resumable publication

Group completion evidence now requires one uniquely retained Verified action
receipt for the complete target set, with a submission time after every member's
claim and a persisted verification time. The reservation UID-bound holder,
controller/source/group digest, native task and every managed target must agree.
A missing member, duplicate receipt, uncertain journal, changed task or altered
completion is insufficient. Historical evidence remains auditable after journal
release, later controller generations or deletion requests on the same UIDs;
live dispatch validation still rejects deletion. Recovery preserves the receipt's
original verification time.

A staged publisher validates the whole set before writing any missing member
completion. Matching existing completions remain unchanged. Individual CAS/readback
failures retain earlier completions; a later fresh call can finish publication
without repeating the controller request. Final complete-set readback is required
before success. Fixtures cover partial publication, lost responses, conflicts,
changed existing evidence and idempotent recovery.

Neither evidence construction nor publication releases a Lease or scheduling
guard. Bound actor/admission validation is required by the publisher, and runtime
group reconciliation remains disabled. Device-worker release, manager settlement,
partial-claim cancellation/recovery and live lab qualification remain pending.

### Device release, manager settlement and verified journal closure

A staged per-device release recorder now requires the complete verified group
completion set and proof that the canonical mutation Lease no longer carries the
exact reservation holder. Expiration alone, including an expired or replaced
Lease still carrying that holder, is insufficient. It writes Released status
only and never deletes a Lease or removes a taint. Lost-response recovery retains
and revalidates the recorded evidence.

Manager settlement publication requires that member's Released grant and the
exact already-settled maintenance session, including device/Node/operation/Lease
identity and acknowledgement ordering. It reuses the existing per-device session
contract. Complete-group settlement validation requires every member's verified
completion, release and retained manager marker; one settled peer is insufficient.

The final staged journal closure accepts only the exact Verified operation and
complete manager-settled group. It uses a single controller CAS, retains action
receipts and section ownership, and verifies readback. Stale, uncertain or
incomplete groups remain retained. Fixtures cover owned/expired leases, wrong
workers/sessions, partial settlement, publication loss and journal-write loss.

These helpers record or validate evidence; they do not perform device lease
cleanup or maintenance-session transitions themselves. Manager/device-worker
runtime wiring, group schema/actor admission, mixed-worker gates,
partial-claim cancellation/recovery and live qualification remain pending.
Multicast Apply is still disabled.

### Durable pre-submission group cancellation fence

A Prepared group can now enter a persisted Cancelling boundary with a cancellation
request timestamp. This uses the same controller resourceVersion CAS as submission,
so cancellation and submission cannot both win. Submitting, Accepted, Unknown or
Verified work cannot be converted into pre-submission cancellation. Lost-response
recovery can observe the existing fence without rewriting it or changing the
group digest. This transition performs no member cleanup.

The operation schema requires group identity, no submission/task receipt and a
cancellation timestamp for Cancelling. Transition validation prevents removal or
change of that timestamp and prevents reversal into Prepared or Submitting.
Canonical and Helm CRDs and deep copies include the optional field. Existing v1
physical paths reject cancellation markers, and the Catalyst Center reconciler
retains even partially pruned cancellation records rather than entering legacy
submission/release paths.

Race-enabled fixtures prove a single winner between cancellation and submission
while preserving claims. Kubernetes API-server tests prove persistence and denial
of cancellation reversal. Member cancellation evidence, lease/session cleanup,
manager settlement of cancelled members and final cancelled-journal closure are
still pending. Group runtime admission/rollout gates and lab qualification remain
required before enabling multicast Apply.

### Per-member cancellation acknowledgement

An existing group member can now acknowledge the exact durable journal
cancellation fence even when peer reservations were never created. The
acknowledgement binds operation/group digest and cancellation time, preserves
existing claims and grants, and records no completion or release. It requires
the bound device-worker identity plus caller validation of installed actor and
recovery admission. A racing claim/grant wins its resourceVersion CAS rather than
being erased; a later fresh acknowledgement can retain that evidence safely.

The optional reservation status record is immutable. Schema transitions freeze
claim/grant presence and grant identity after acknowledgement, permit progress
toward Released, and forbid reopening a released grant. Group markers cannot
coexist with successful completion or the legacy preparation-cancellation marker.
The root schema restricts them to the group protocol and exact operation binding;
the currently installed protocol enum still disables creation of group objects.
Existing v1 reservations therefore cannot acquire these markers.

Race-enabled fixtures cover ungranted, held, claimed and incompletely created
groups, actor rejection, lost acknowledgement responses and concurrent claims.
Status CEL and API-server checks cover frozen transitions and v1 isolation. Lease
cleanup, cancellation-specific manager settlement and final cancelled journal
closure are still pending, as are runtime enablement and live qualification.

### Cancelled group member release and manager settlement (staged)

Cancellation now has separate release and settlement evidence helpers. A member
must retain a valid cancellation acknowledgement before its device worker can
record Released. The shared canonical lease check rejects a lease that still
holds the reservation identity even if it expired or its Kubernetes UID changed.
Claims and acknowledgement records survive release; no successful completion
receipt is created. This works when cancellation interrupted creation of other
members, without claiming that those absent members have settled.

Manager settlement additionally requires the exact already-settled maintenance
session, bound device/node/operation identity, canonical lease coordinates and
observed absence of the reservation holder. An ungranted member still requires
this proof: preparation may have acquired a lease before publishing its grant.
Existing settlement markers are retained for subsequent session advancement.
Lost write responses remain recoverable with fresh versions; stale writes and
actor authorization failures cannot erase evidence.

Race-enabled tests cover held/expired/replaced leases, missing peers, claims,
revocation, missing/wrong acknowledgements, active/missing/mismatched sessions,
ungranted preparation, invalid settlement times, lost responses and repeated
recovery. A composed fixture verifies acknowledgement → actual lease release →
Released → actual session settlement → retained manager settlement. Fixture
cleanup writes stand in for future worker/manager reconciliation; these helpers
only record checked evidence and do not perform device cleanup themselves.

Group runtime and multicast Apply remain disabled. Still required are cleanup
reconciliation, recovery for members with no session ever created, durable
whole-group cancellation closure (including interrupted member creation), actor
admission/rollout gates, adapter runtime wiring and live qualification. The lab
credentials previously returned HTTP 401; these changes have not been deployed
or exercised against Catalyst Center.

### Group cancellation before session acknowledgement (staged)

The manager now has a staged recovery path for an acknowledged group cancellation
whose device preparation never received a maintenance-session acknowledgement.
It uses the same read-only cleanup proof as the existing v1 cancellation path:
an exact live device/node binding, no maintenance guard, an idle canonical lease
with valid managed metadata, and no pending maintenance request or lease timing.
The device, node and lease versions are checked again before settlement is written.
An unrelated active session or the same reservation's acknowledged session must
use its own settlement path; neither is inferred to be absent or complete.

The group entry point additionally requires the durable group cancellation fence,
an exact member acknowledgement, no grant or claim, and a manager/admission
authorization callback. It performs a reservation status CAS and exact read-back,
retains the cancellation evidence, and does not create synthetic sessions or
successful action receipts. Runtime reconciliation still does not invoke it.
Tests exercise both legacy and group cancellation, including changed node
observations, rejected authority and recovery from a lost settlement response.

This closes the missing-session evidence primitive, not complete cancellation
reconciliation. Whole-group cancellation retention/closure, interrupted member
creation, runtime/admission wiring and lab qualification remain outstanding.

### Retained group cancellation and journal closure (staged)

A fully created, fully settled cancelled group can now release its exact operation
slot with one status CAS that retains a separate cancellation receipt. The receipt
contains the original operation/group identity, every member reservation name/UID
and settlement time. It is never stored as a successful action application.
Historical validation checks the full member set, acknowledgement and manager
settlement, including after the controller starts a later operation or reservation
deletion is pending. Replacement reservation UIDs cannot inherit cleanup evidence.

The optional NetworkController status list is bounded to 32 receipts; closure
refuses overflow rather than silently discarding evidence. Each retained entry is
immutable in the schema. Actor admission and eventual collection retirement must
still protect removal of entire entries; this schema field alone does not enable
the group lifecycle. The reservation protocol enum remains disabled.

Fixtures cover incomplete settlement, missing acknowledgement, partial member
sets, invalid phases, retention exhaustion, actor rejection, lost closure
responses and historical audit. Canonical and Helm CRDs include the receipt;
API-server tests check persistence and immutable entry updates. Whole-group
closure for interrupted member creation, guarded receipt retirement, runtime
wiring, rollout admission and live qualification remain outstanding.

### Anycast creation checks existing Layer-2 VLAN allocations

Anycast dependency snapshots now reuse the paginated Layer-2 VN inventory reader.
Before creating a gateway, the target fabric's existing L2 VLAN IDs and names are
checked against the requested, generated or inherited gateway allocation. The
same check runs again immediately before the POST, so an allocation introduced
after planning prevents submission. Allocation in another fabric is independent.
An L3 association alone does not authorize reusing an existing L2 allocation.
Existing gateway convergence remains governed by its authoritative gateway
readback; this change does not assume that absence of a gateway proves ownership
of a matching L2 object. An unavailable L2 inventory prevents creation.

The inventory fields follow Cisco's [Get layer 2 virtual networks API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/get-layer-2-virtual-networks/).
Fixtures cover late name/ID collisions, inherited zone VLANs, independent fabrics,
unavailable inventory and shared request-local inventory collection. Reverse
checks for L2 creation against native gateways and live qualification remain
pending. This does not add update/delete ownership or complete fabric parity.

Interrupted group cancellation remains fenced: observing a missing reservation
alone cannot rule out an already admitted creation request still in flight. That
path needs a durable creation/tombstone contract before its journal can close.

### Bidirectional fabric VLAN allocation checks

Layer-2 VN creation now reads the existing native anycast gateway inventory once
per observation and refuses an already allocated VLAN ID or name in the target
fabric. A matching L3 association is not permission to reuse that allocation.
Existing L2 convergence keeps its native readback contract. VLANs in other fabrics
remain independent, and unavailable gateway inventory prevents planning/writing.

The L2 submit closure now repeats observation immediately before its POST. It
requires the same target fabric, inherited VLAN and parent/L3 dependency identity,
and refuses to replay if the desired target appeared after planning. This closes
the previous gap where the standalone native submit closure used its earlier
snapshot. The shared configuration journal and existing submission boundary remain
in place.

Race-enabled fixtures cover late gateway ID/name conflicts, independent fabrics,
unavailable inventory, replaced fabric/VN identity, late target creation and an
inherited zone VLAN collision after parent creation. The full manifest fixture
retains its operation evidence when that zone becomes unsafe to create. Combined
with the preceding anycast change, both creation directions now check existing
cross-resource allocations. Neither direction can predict an undeclared VLAN ID
before Catalyst Center assigns it; final readback remains mandatory. Live lab
qualification, ownership-aware update/deletion and full model parity are pending.
