### IPAM native write revalidation before fabric composition

IPAM pool/reservation submission now rebuilds its native plan immediately before
mutation. It requires the same action, resource, target/site identity and exact
merged payload. Replacement pool/reservation UUIDs, changed parent pool or site
bindings, newly converged/created resources, and concurrent changes to preserved
optional fields invalidate the old plan. Replanning performs reads only; an
invalidated closure does not submit a different operation or retry a write.

The existing allocation validator and payload merger remain the source of truth.
The merged payload is held only in the request-local plan and is not added to the
journal. Stable updates still preserve unspecified fields. Tests cover both pool
and reservation updates, exact mutation targets, preserved DNS settings and zero
writes after stale observations. Earlier native IPv4 lab qualification predates
this change; the revalidation addition is fixture-tested only.

This is a prerequisite for composing IPAM reservation creation with fabric
anycast deployment. That cross-section compiler/executor, prospective dependency
validation and full-journal/live qualification remain pending. Existing standalone
network-settings IPAM semantics and journal boundaries remain in use.

### Prospective IPAM prerequisites for anycast (private, not compiler-enabled)

An IPAM prerequisite preview now distinguishes already observed reservations from
explicitly declared reservations/global pools that still need creation or update.
It reuses IPAM's complete allocation graph and site validation, checks the exact
reservation owner, and validates primary/ordered secondary pool references using
the same name parsing as native binding. Existing reservations also remain pending
when their declared parent pool attributes still need an update.

The preview carries only pending/readiness state. It invents no native UUID,
reservation, dependency digest or successful application receipt, and cannot be
passed as native anycast dependency evidence. Tests verify that planned pools
still fail native binding until observed; they also cover wrong owners, missing
sites, overlapping allocations, undeclared dependencies, pending optional-field
updates and secondary-pool declarations. Invalid graphs return no partial state.

This is a private planning component for the combined IPAM/fabric executor. The
cross-section compiler, prospective fabric preflight, journal sequencing and live
qualification remain pending; standalone gateway submission still requires real
observed pool identities through the existing dependency binder.

### Combined IPAM/fabric Apply and Report

A manifest selecting `network_settings` and `fabric` can now create declared
global pools and site reservations before fabric sites, VN memberships and
anycast gateways. Compilation reuses the existing network-settings and fabric
executors. Both sections are reserved by the existing ownership mechanism; one
canonical fabric journal with explicit resource-part prefixes serializes writes
independently of section order. Existing site hierarchy references remain required:
this combination does not create hierarchy sites from the `sites` binding block.

Fabric preflight uses one IPAM preview snapshot per pass for all gateway
references. Missing prerequisites are accepted only when explicitly declared and
valid in that same manifest. Native gateway submission and verification still
require real observed pool identities. IPAM writes use the fresh-plan validation
added previously. A requested pool change underneath an existing gateway is
refused in this combined flow pending a separately qualified transition.

Report mode also recognizes these declared prerequisites and preserves separate
section resource counts. Restart-per-reconcile fixtures cover end-to-end ordered
creation, reversed section order, report-only observation, conflicting section
ownership, wrong reservation site, incomplete gateway payloads and lost pool or
reservation task receipts. An ambiguous IPAM submission retains Unknown journal
evidence and prevents later fabric writes rather than inferring success from
readback. Existing standalone and other-provider paths remain covered by the
adapter regression suite.

Example: `examples/configs/catalyst-center/ipam-fabric-apply.yaml` (change mode to
`report` for inspection). Combined compiler and source-format checks cover both
modes. This combined flow is fixture-qualified only: dual-stack/secondary-pool
combined manifest qualification, broader anchor scenarios, ownership-aware
updates/removals and live lab execution remain pending. Group multicast Apply
and the remaining NetAsCode parity gaps are still incomplete.

### Combined secondary and dual-stack pool qualification (fixtures)

The combined manifest suite now creates secondary anycast reservations from the
same NetAsCode model. It follows the existing IPAM parser's canonical name order;
all prerequisite reservations must complete before fabric/gateway writes. Report
mode checks separate section counts. Unsupported appliance releases prevent even
initial pool creation. Missing secondary readback, changed release evidence and
replacement reservation UUIDs retain the active operation instead of progressing.
Lost secondary-reservation receipts remain Unknown and are not replayed.

Dual-stack cases create distinct IPv4 and IPv6 global pools and one merged site
reservation. The reservation request must resolve both native parent UUIDs and
retain the existing /64 SLAAC setting. Missing IPv6 readback prevents fabric
creation; replacing the IPv6 parent during gateway recovery prevents completion,
even when the replacement allocation is internally consistent. Successful Apply
and Report cases use the same existing combined compiler and journal.

The tests restart reconciliation between steps, assert mutation order and bounded
write counts, and retain section ownership checks. Resource-count assertions were
moved after reconciliation so they inspect actual Report status. These results
qualify fixture behavior only; live secondary/dual-stack execution, broader anchor
scenarios, ownership-aware update/delete and the remaining model components are
still outstanding.


### L3 VN anchor intent and read-only reporting

The fabric compiler accepts the pinned model's `l3_virtual_networks[].anchor_site`
as a site hierarchy path. It resolves the existing site and fabric inventories to
a fabric UUID, compares `anchoredSiteId`, and reports Add/Update/no drift without
owning or removing unrelated fabric memberships. Null means omission, not an
unanchor request. Native UUID fields, unknown fields, invalid paths, duplicates,
and system-VN anchor intent are rejected. A missing site or fabric remains an
unresolved dependency; no synthetic ID or successful status is generated.

An explicit anchor gates the entire fabric Apply composition, including its
prerequisites. Combined IPAM/fabric Apply also gates before prerequisite planning
or mutations. This remains necessary until the multi-device admission/handoff
path is enabled. Accepting the model for Report is not anchor execution parity.
Existing unanchored definition and additive association paths remain unchanged.

Example: `examples/configs/catalyst-center/anchored-vn-report.yaml`. Local HTTP
fixtures cover correct/different/absent anchors, missing dependencies, unrelated
memberships, strict model validation, and composition admission. Anchor creation,
reanchoring, removal, declared-but-not-created anchor dependencies, device-role
qualification, and live execution remain pending.

Native mapping reference: [Cisco's Layer-3 VN API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/add-layer-3-virtual-networks/).


### Fabric-device native onboarding primitive (not enabled in Apply)

A separate full fabric-device reader now captures border types and Layer-3
settings. The existing role/membership projection used by multicast is unchanged.
The full reader reuses authenticated pagination, rejects incomplete border data,
duplicate devices, incorrect fabric IDs and invalid roles, and retains native
ASN/default-exit/import-route/priority/prepend settings. Existing extended-node
memberships are readable, but cannot be created through this API primitive.

The resolved border-settings parser maps the pinned module's settings to native
fields. Explicit false values survive; Layer-3 settings require an ASN and both
booleans. Priority 10 and prepend 0 follow the pinned Terraform module's omission
rules. Layer-2-only intent cannot silently discard Layer-3 fields. Handoffs,
transit and inventory reference fields are not consumed by this settings-only
projection; the future composition must handle them separately.

The private create planner reuses configurationWrite, shared transport and the
native task receipt. It canonicalizes sets and snapshots caller-owned values,
refuses conflicting existing configurations, and refreshes the complete fabric
inventory before POST. A changed target or peer prevents submission. Readback
compares the declared configuration and recognizes native default values;
missing/ambiguous receipts remain errors rather than inferred success.

Local fixtures cover create/no-op/conflict, late target/peer changes, caller
mutation after planning, missing receipt, reordered native sets, wrong readback,
and incomplete/invalid second pages. This is not manifest or live qualification.
The primitive is not registered with Apply: physical serial/site/role resolution,
provisioning prerequisites, multi-device admission, journal integration and
ownership-aware updates/deletes remain required. No lab mutations were made.

References: [native create API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/add-fabric-devices/)
and [NetAsCode border-device model](https://netascode.cisco.com/docs/data_models/catalyst_center/fabric/border_device/).


### Wired fabric-device model and dependency snapshots

The staged fabric-device compiler now parses a bounded wired inventory/fabric
projection. It retains PROVISION/REPROVISION intent and reuses the existing common
inventory parser for selectors, site, tags and device-role validation. The ASSIGN
projection is internal validation only; it does not turn provisioning into an
assignment-only operation. Fabric and optional zone paths must contain the
placement site. Named border settings must match a declared border role; orphan
settings, duplicate roles and unhandled fields are rejected. Wireless roles,
handoffs, port channels and other resources still require their own composition
and are not silently ignored.

A fresh dependency snapshot resolves selectors against controller inventory,
uses shared canonical physical-identity checks, and requires exact site
assignment plus any explicitly requested device role/source. Fabric-site and zone
identities come from the existing readers. Zone onboarding also requires the same
device and requested roles in its parent fabric. The prospective footprint covers
the incoming device, current fabric members and, for zones, parent members;
missing or duplicate serial evidence prevents a usable snapshot. A digest binds
placement/fabric/zone identities, native configuration and the physical baseline.
Parent replacement and peer replacement change that digest.

Fixtures exercise wired/border/zone models, missing dependencies, assignment and
role mismatch, invalid/orphan fields, canonical serials and changed identities.
These are local preflight checks, not proof of provisioning completion, group
admission, journal recovery, manifest Apply, or live qualification. Those runtime
steps remain pending; neither existing inventory nor wireless compilation has
been redirected to the staged path.


### Dependency-bound fabric-device create and recovery

The staged wired-device executor now wraps native creation with the resolved
identity/assignment/fabric dependency snapshot. It refreshes that snapshot
immediately before submission and retains the native reader's final inventory
comparison. A target that appears during initial planning cannot be adopted as a
successful no-op under the previous observation. Mutable caller model fields are
copied into the planned intent.

The resource identity binds a recovery digest containing desired configuration,
placement/fabric/zone identity, the complete physical footprint, peers and parent
memberships. The new target membership itself is excluded from this stable digest
because creation is expected to add it; its configuration is verified separately.
Unknown operations and operations without a task receipt cannot become verified
from readback. The caller must still verify task completion through the shared
journal before invoking semantic verification.

Fixtures reparse intent for recovery and cover successful site/zone creation,
unchanged convergence, late target/peer/fabric changes, replacement parent-member
evidence, changed roles, missing readback, unknown submissions, missing task IDs,
lost receipts and caller mutation. They assert exactly one POST on successful
submission and zero POSTs for stale plans. This remains a private staged executor:
provisioning prerequisites, installed group admission, manifest orchestration,
retained completion/ownership and live qualification are still outstanding.


### Wired provisioning prerequisite and native execution

The staged wired path now reads the native provisioned-device resource through
`/dna/intent/api/v1/sda/provisionDevices`, scoped to one network-device UUID. Empty
inventory is absence; malformed, duplicate, wrong-device or incomplete native
records are refused. The reader does not infer asynchronous task completion.

PROVISION plans a singleton POST only when absent. REPROVISION requires the
existing record and plans PUT with its original native ID, site and device IDs.
The planner resolves canonical physical identity, supported wired family,
reachability, exact site assignment and any explicitly requested role/source.
Submission refreshes all of that evidence and the native baseline before using
the shared authenticated mutation transport. A missing task receipt remains an
error. Semantic verification runs in the shared journal's Verifying phase and
requires task completion/freshness plus current site/device/native identity.
There is no fabricated provisioning timestamp: the GET API supplies none.

Fabric-device dependency snapshots now require a matching provisioned-device
record and bind its ID into submission/recovery evidence. Missing provisioning
prevents membership planning; record replacement changes the digest. The staged
bound fabric verifier was also corrected from Accepted to Verifying to match the
actual shared journal call sequence.

HTTP fixtures cover provision/reprovision/no-op, missing prerequisites, wrong
site/family, stale submission, lost receipt, missing/replaced readback, unknown
operations, and failed/running/stale tasks. Production manifest orchestration,
retained reprovision application receipts (to prevent repeating an explicit
REPROVISION action), device/group admission, clean-up/delete and live lab
qualification remain pending. No existing wireless or SWIM path is redirected.

Sources: [native provision API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/provision-devices/),
[provisioned-device readback](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-5/get-provisioned-devices/),
and [reprovision API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/re-provision-devices/).


### Wired reprovision revision receipts

The staged wired revision planner now consumes the existing physical-action
receipt emitted atomically when the shared journal advances to Verified. No new
status collection, task loop or receipt writer was introduced. Matching requires
the same manifest UID/name/generation, controller generation, source UID/version,
action, native resource hash, device/serial and site. The retained entry must be
Verified, carry a task/submission ID and valid verification time, and remain under
one matching section owner. Missing, malformed, duplicate or foreign-owner
receipts cannot suppress an action as successful.

Native planning resolves current dependencies before consulting the retained
receipt. Source and controller state are read again afterwards; a new operation,
a source edit, controller recreation or controller-generation change prevents
returning a stale plan. An already-applied revision returns no write; an explicit
new revision can plan again. Shared journal tests generate the receipt used by
the matcher. HTTP fixtures cover revision suppression/new revision and changes
arriving during reads, with zero mutation calls from planning.

This is still staged plumbing. The public inventory parser and manifest compiler
have not enabled wired PROVISION/REPROVISION, and prepared-operation recovery,
prerequisite sequencing, admission/settlement and live qualification remain to be
connected and exercised as one complete flow.


### Wired provisioning executor restart handling

The staged wired executor now implements the common configurationExecutor
contract. With an empty journal it uses revision-aware planning. With a Prepared
operation it replans read-only and requires the exact recorded resource, action,
device UUID, canonical serial, site UUID and source/controller revision. A create
that becomes externally present cannot silently replace Prepared evidence with a
no-op. Accepted, Unknown, foreign-revision and group operations are not replanned
as fresh submissions. Source and controller resourceVersion are checked after
native reads.

Verification requires the exact current Verifying operation and reuses wired
task/readback validation. It then checks source and journal again before returning
success, so an edit during API observation cannot verify an obsolete operation.
The semantic verifier does not write receipts; the existing shared journal owns
that atomic transition.

Fixture tests recreate the executor and cover unchanged recovery, native-record
replacement, action/site/source mismatches, a newly existing create target,
foreign operations and source/journal changes during reads. They assert zero
mutation calls and no fabricated completion receipts. Public manifest routing,
prerequisite ordering, admission/settlement and live end-to-end qualification are
still pending; the executor remains private and staged.


### Staged wired inventory prerequisite composition

A private wired inventory compiler now keeps PROVISION/REPROVISION state while
reusing the common inventory parser for assignment, role, tag and discovery
fields. Fabric, wireless and cleanup fields remain explicit unsupported intent;
they are not removed to make the rest of a manifest appear supported. Compilation
requires the existing physical-admission hook and explicit serial references.
The existing managedInventoryPlan supplies prerequisite executors and ownership
semantics; there is no separate journal or transport.

Before planning prerequisites, the complete declared inventory is resolved to
unique physical identities and existing placement sites. Provisioning targets
must be reachable supported wired devices. Multiple aliases for one physical
device are refused. A request-local binding snapshot is checked again immediately
before any returned submission. Provisioning runs only after prerequisite
executors report no pending work. A pending wired Prepared operation cannot be
replaced by newly discovered prerequisite work.

Recovery routes to exactly one wired executor using the recorded canonical
physical serial. Duplicate/missing selectors are errors, and prerequisite drift
blocks provisioning verification. Fixtures cover ordering, late validation
failure with zero submissions, prepared recovery to a non-first device,
duplicate aliases, missing sites, ambiguous recovery and pending prerequisites.
The default production compiler still rejects wired provisioning: public routing,
real admission/settlement and full manifest/lab qualification remain pending.


### Admission-gated public wired inventory Apply

The configuration reconciler now selects the fully validated wired compiler for
wired inventory PROVISION/REPROVISION manifests. Existing assignment-only and
wireless intents retain their compiler. Unsupported mixed/fabric/cleanup intent
cannot fall back to a partial tag or assignment plan. Physical submission remains
behind the same installed reservation admission hook, one-shot dispatch path,
shared journal, retained physical-action receipt and settlement checks.

A stateful fixture cycle starts with an unassigned device, performs assignment,
then POST provisioning or PUT reprovisioning. It reconstructs compilation around
Prepared operations and uses the real manifest evaluation path for task polling,
verification, receipt retention and settled journal cleanup. The public reconciler publishes InSync after completion, and repeated evaluation
does not submit again. Lost receipts retain Unknown; failed
tasks retain Accepted and do not infer success from visible native resources.

This fixture uses a test dispatch permit and explicitly supplied worker/manager
reservation evidence, not real actor admission, Lease acquisition or a live
Catalyst Center. Those qualification requirements remain open. The example is
`examples/configs/catalyst-center/wired-provision-apply.yaml`; selectors must be
replaced with managed lab identities. Wired Report mode, cleanup/delete,
wireless/fabric composition and bulk provisioning remain incomplete.


### Wired provisioning Report mode

Wired inventory now compiles in Report mode through the same strict wired
projection as Apply. It reuses common assignment/role/tag/discovery reporting and
adds a provisioning observation per declared PROVISION/REPROVISION target. A
missing native record is an Add gap, a different provisioning site is an Update
gap, and an existing matching PROVISION record has no provisioning drift.
REPROVISION remains an explicit Update action; an existing record alone is not
proof that a new request has been executed.

Report does not consult/consume Apply receipts or acquire section ownership.
The section message explains the imperative distinction and that missing
provisioning/site relocation requires resolution before reprovisioning. Discovery
observation messages are combined with this explanation rather than replacing
it. These entries describe observed gaps, not a promise that Apply can perform
an unsupported relocation automatically.

Device/fabric-independent placement bindings are validated before reporting and
rechecked after native observations; replacement/ambiguous physical identities
and malformed native records refuse the entire report. Fixture tests assert
read-only HTTP behavior, stable resource counts, public InSync for matching
PROVISION intent, and no fabricated journal/ownership/receipt state. The example
is `examples/configs/catalyst-center/wired-provision-report.yaml`. Actor/Lease
handoff, live lab qualification, cleanup/deletion, mixed wireless/fabric actions
and bulk provisioning remain pending.


### Extranet policy reporting and admission boundary

The pinned 0.5.0 `fabric.extranet_policies` model now compiles into the existing
fabric Report path. It accepts policy names, provider and subscriber VN names,
and optional fabric site/zone hierarchy paths. Unknown fields, native IDs in
path fields, duplicate names/references and provider-as-subscriber inputs fail
validation. Native policy reads use shared pagination and validate identity and
set members before comparing drift.

Reporting resolves existing VN identities and fabric scope, then rereads those
dependencies before publishing results. A replacement VN or fabric during the
observation invalidates the entire report. Missing dependencies remain pending;
Report does not invent IDs for not-yet-created prerequisites. Missing policies
report Add; provider, subscriber or explicit scope differences report Update.
Provider Update is a drift classification, **not** permission for an in-place
provider change: the native API requires replacement for that change.

The pinned module emits null for omitted or empty `fabric_sites`. In this
bounded Report implementation these values do not express removal of native
associations; only a nonempty declared scope is compared. This is not a claim
of Terraform refresh/ownership parity. See the
`examples/configs/catalyst-center/extranet-policy-report.yaml` example.

Extranet Apply remains disabled at the entire fabric composition and combined
network-settings/fabric composition boundaries. No prerequisite network or
pool writes can precede an unsupported extranet operation. Enabling execution
still requires the shared multi-device reservation/handoff flow, affected-device
binding, ownership, native task verification, restart recovery and lab
qualification. No lab mutation or deployment was performed for this addition.

Source contracts: [NetAsCode 0.5.0 module](https://github.com/netascode/terraform-catalystcenter-nac-catalystcenter/blob/v0.5.0/cc_fabric.tf),
[Cisco native policy reads](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/get-extranet-policies/),
and [native update constraints](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/update-extranet-policy/).


### Extranet native creation and recovery primitives

Extranet creation now has a private native planner and verifier underneath the
unchanged public composition gate. The planner resolves all participating VN
fabric memberships, explicitly selected scopes and parent fabrics for zones.
It reuses the existing paginated membership readers, complete-fabric device
selection and canonical physical serial binding. The resulting physical set
includes remote subscriber fabrics and is not reduced to provider border nodes.
Missing VN membership data, unknown fabrics, missing inventory devices and serial
aliases refuse planning. Empty/omitted scopes remain Report-only because their
controller-dependent deployment footprint has not been established.

A submission binds VN/site/fabric/zone identities, memberships, physical devices
and other policies in a deterministic dependency digest. It rereads this evidence
and the native policy baseline before the single POST. A matching existing policy
is a no-op; a conflicting existing policy is refused rather than adopted or
replaced. Payload slices are copied so later caller mutation cannot alter the
prepared request. Missing task receipts remain errors and never cause a retry.

Recovery requires a Verifying operation, valid shared task completion/timing,
unchanged dependencies and matching native provider/subscriber/scope readback.
Running, failed, stale or missing task evidence and Unknown operations cannot
become success through readback. Verification performs no writes. Native
creation/readback alone does not establish durable ownership or bind a returned
policy UUID to a retained ownership receipt; that remains part of journal
integration.

Fixture coverage includes create/no-op/conflict, zones and remote VN fabrics,
late VN/member/device/policy changes, missing/aliased devices, lost receipts,
caller mutation, invalid task states, missing/changed readback and changed peers
during recovery. Public Apply is still disabled. Group reservation/actor
integration, journal ownership, update/delete/replacement, broader transit
impact qualification and lab testing remain outstanding. No appliance writes
or deployment occurred for this addition.


### Extranet native-identity ownership receipts

A private receipt builder now returns the existing `ActionApplications` type
only after task completion, dependency-bound native readback and exact matching
of the journal's complete group inventory IDs and canonical physical serials.
Its action key contains the logical policy-name hash and the observed native
policy UUID. The immutable Prepared operation is copied into Verified form,
without rewriting its original target fields. No additional API field, receipt
collection or persistence mechanism was introduced.

The receipt builder rereads the native policy and dependency footprint before
returning evidence; a different policy UUID between verification and receipt
construction is refused. A separate ownership predicate verifies the retained
receipt, native UUID, group digest, successful task metadata, timestamps and
exact section/config identity. Config generations may advance without losing
ownership, while a recreated config, replaced policy, foreign or duplicate
section owner, duplicate receipt or malformed operation cannot inherit it.
This predicate proves recorded provenance, not current compliance or admission.

Fixtures build receipts from real native HTTP/task fixtures, serialize status
through JSON and verify ownership after reconstructing it. They cover complete
and incomplete physical groups, policy replacement during readback and malformed
or conflicting retained evidence. These are **not** API-server persistence tests:
the builder does not write status. Atomic Verified/receipt CAS, actor authorization,
reservation completion and retirement remain group-coordinator integration work.
Public extranet Apply remains gated, and no lab deployment or mutation occurred.


### Atomic verified group receipt persistence (staged)

The shared controller-configuration group contract now provides
`PersistVerifiedGroupReceipt`. It accepts independently verified adapter receipt
evidence and the complete member set, then atomically writes the exact Verified
operation and its action receipt through a single controller status CAS. It does
not invoke an appliance API, release a reservation, clear the journal or retry a
failed write. The existing group completion validator checks the resulting
receipt against every member's claim and submission timing.

The writer requires a current Verifying journal, exclusive matching section
ownership, complete Held/claimed reservations and an explicit actor/protocol
authorization callback. It rereads the controller and members around that callback,
rejects changed controller/member versions, cancellation or early settlement,
and refuses replacing any retained receipt. Retirement/replacement rules remain
a separate operation. After a successful write, it independently reads back the
whole configuration status to confirm both records were retained together.

Fake API-client fixtures exercise successful persistence, denied/missing
permission, changed tasks, incomplete groups, absent claims, released/cancelled
members, ownership conflicts, duplicate receipts, invalid timestamps, late
controller/member changes, a final CAS conflict and a committed write with a
lost response. The latter retains both records while returning the ambiguity;
a stale retry is refused. The persisted receipt can feed the existing group
completion construction. These fixtures are not deployed actor or live API-server
qualification.

The helper is staged and has no runtime caller. Catalyst Center adapter wiring,
installed group-protocol admission, coordinator lifecycle and lab qualification
are still required. Legacy single-device, ND and SWIM paths were not rerouted.


### Extranet adapter-to-group receipt integration (staged)

The Catalyst Center adapter now has a private recovery entry point connecting
native extranet verification to `PersistVerifiedGroupReceipt`. It reloads the
inline or ConfigMap source, resolves the named policy from the pinned model and
requires the exact recorded operation/config/source/controller revision. It
rejects unselected sections, secret-bearing models, missing policies, mismatched
operation IDs and non-Verifying journals before persistence.

After task/native verification, the adapter rechecks the source and controller
snapshot. Its authorization wrapper repeats those checks before and after the
mandatory group actor/protocol callback. A source update or controller pause
therefore prevents retaining the receipt from the old observation. Successful
status writes use the shared atomic writer, retaining native-UUID ownership and
evidence consumable by the existing full-group completion logic.

The native lifecycle fixture now invokes this adapter path against a fake
Kubernetes API client. Inline and ConfigMap sources persist matching Verified
journals and ownership receipts. Tests cover denied authorization, late ConfigMap
and controller changes, unknown policy names, wrong operation IDs and committed
status writes with lost acknowledgements. A reconstructed adapter observes the
retained ownership after a lost response and refuses a repeat transition. The
entire test still performs only the original single native POST.

This qualifies the private recovery bridge, not production lifecycle activation.
Reservation grants/claims are fixture evidence; the installed CRD still refuses
the group protocol. Public reconciler dispatch, real actor authorization, group
creation/cancellation coordination and live lab qualification remain pending.
No new status store, API schema or ND/direct-device/SWIM path was introduced.


### Owned additive extranet updates (native path, staged)

The extranet native planner now supports adding subscribers and explicit fabric
scope to an existing policy with a retained CVK native-UUID ownership receipt.
The adapter wrapper rechecks the manifest source, controller incarnation and
ownership before planning and again before the native PUT. The update retains
the native policy UUID and provider VN; a same-name replacement cannot inherit
ownership. Unowned policies cannot be adopted, including through a no-op.

Only additive transitions are admitted by this primitive. Every existing
subscriber and fabric must remain in the desired set, and both old and desired
scope must be nonempty. This ensures that the desired model can reconstruct the
entire old-plus-new affected-device footprint after a restart. Subscriber/scope
removal, provider changes and previously unscoped policies remain refused until
retained old-scope evidence and replacement handling are implemented.

The PUT uses a UUID-bound dependency resource key, a fresh native baseline and
an independently refreshed ownership check. Native receipt loss returns an
error without retry. Recovery uses the existing task completion/timing validator,
then matches the exact native UUID, provider/subscribers/scope and dependency
digest. Matching current state converges to a no-op while retaining ownership.

Fixtures cover subscriber expansion, fabric-zone scope expansion, no-op, absent
ownership, provider/removal refusals, late native/owner/source changes, receipt
loss, Unknown/running/failed tasks, replaced or incomplete readback and recovery
without repeating the PUT. Existing creation/ownership/recovery fixtures pass.
The update completion receipt is not yet wired into group persistence; public
Apply remains gated. These are local HTTP/fake Kubernetes fixtures, not appliance
or real actor qualification. No lab mutation was performed.


### Extranet additive-update receipt integration (staged)

Create and additive-update recovery now share `recordExtranetApplication` and
the same native receipt builder. Update recovery first requires the original
native-UUID creation ownership receipt, then verifies the update task, matching
UUID/content, dependency digest and complete physical group before using the
shared atomic status writer.

The original creation receipt remains the ownership anchor. An update receives
a separate completion key based on the native policy UUID and canonical desired
policy content, excluding transient dependency observations. This avoids rewriting
ownership or discarding receipt evidence still needed by earlier reservations.
Existing duplicate/capacity checks still refuse overwriting a retained update
receipt. Retirement and subsequent repair of the same desired content require
explicit reservation-aware receipt lifecycle work; no implicit replacement was
added.

The existing application fixture now runs both subscriber and fabric-scope
updates through inline and ConfigMap source recovery. It verifies preservation
of the creation receipt, addition of matching update/Verified records, completion
evidence for the current full group, refusal without original ownership, late
source/controller changes, authorization denial and restart after a committed
write with a lost acknowledgement. Native PUT count remains one through recovery.
Creation, ownership and public group-recovery gate tests continue to pass.

This closes the staged update-to-receipt bridge only. Public dispatch, actual
actor/protocol admission, reservation creation/cancellation coordination, receipt
retirement/reapplication, destructive policy changes and live lab qualification
remain pending. Fake API clients do not establish deployed group-protocol support.


### Settled group reservation retirement (staged)

`RetireSettledGroupReservation` now provides the missing per-member cleanup step
after the old group journal has cleared. It requires the retained verified group
action receipt, exact member/controller identity, matching claim and completion,
a Released grant and manager settlement. It cannot retire the currently active
operation or use receipt absence, an expired lease or a changed task as cleanup
evidence. The installed-protocol/manager authorization callback is mandatory.

The completion receipt lookup and claim/timing validation are shared with the
existing full-group completion path. Retirement audits one already-settled
member because peers may have been deleted earlier; completion publication and
live release still require the complete group. Retirement preserves the original
controller receipt and ownership, all peers, devices and leases.

The helper rereads around authorization, checks UID/resourceVersion/spec,
removes only its own finalizer and deletes with UID/resourceVersion preconditions.
An ambiguous finalizer-write result is returned without retry. A later call can
resume from a fresh same-UID row whose finalizer was already removed. A missing
controller does not waive the receipt requirement for a reservation still present.

The full shared-contract race suite passes, including existing legacy and group
completion/release/settlement tests. New fixtures cover sequential retirement,
active journals, missing/invalid receipts, unsettled or held members, changed
completion, replaced identity, missing controller, denied/missing authorization,
late controller/member changes and recovery from a lost finalizer-write response.
These are fake-client lifecycle tests. Runtime group-protocol activation and
actor qualification remain pending; no runtime call site was enabled.

Action-receipt retirement is still separate: reservation deletion alone does not
remove an ownership receipt or permit overwriting retained completion evidence.
Cancelled/incomplete group creation also remains outside this successful-action
retirement path.


### Retirement of fully closed cancelled groups (staged)

`RetireCancelledGroupReservation` now supports cleanup of a member whose full
group cancellation was durably closed. It shares the successful-retirement
read/authorize/reread, finalizer CAS and UID/resourceVersion deletion mechanics,
but uses cancellation-specific evidence. The cancellation receipt and ownership
remain retained; no successful action receipt is fabricated.

The validator checks the complete canonical target-to-reservation-name mapping,
unique recorded member UIDs, this member's exact UID, the original cancellation
fence, acknowledgement, Released grant when present, manager settlement and
receipt timing. It rejects an active old journal, partial or duplicate membership
records, foreign/replaced identities and incomplete cleanup. Peers may have been
retired earlier only because the retained complete cancellation still binds them.
Canonical target normalization matches the existing group identity contract in
both successful and cancelled retirement paths.

The shared-contract race suite passed, and subsequent targeted tests cover both
retirement paths and canonical identity handling. Cancellation fixtures exercise
sequential cleanup, missing/duplicate receipts, partial/duplicate/foreign member
lists, wrong UIDs, invalid receipt times, uncertain or still-active operations,
missing acknowledgements, unsettled/held members, fabricated completion, denied
authorization and restart after a lost finalizer-write response. The controller's
cancellation receipt and peer state remain unchanged.

This handles retirement after a **complete** cancellation closure. Interrupted
member creation, uncreated sessions and cancellation-receipt retirement remain
separate work. The group runtime/CRD admission is still gated, and no live cluster
or lab changes were made by these fake-client tests.


### Template deployment request and completion contract (staged)

The regular-template deployment request builder now maps an explicitly selected
base template, committed version and single managed device to the v2 native
payload. Singleton parameter lists become scalar strings; multiple values and
explicit empty lists remain arrays. Explicit false copying/force options survive
serialization. Draft/base-ID versions, invalid identities and oversized payloads
are rejected. Parameters remain transient request material, never status, resource
keys or diagnostic content. Defaults and model/reference resolution remain the
responsibility of the future compiler; this helper does not submit requests.

Deployment receipts are separate from generic task IDs. The receipt decoder
accepts a deployment UUID or the pinned provider's progress marker, rejects
conflicting/malformed IDs and never assumes success when a receipt is absent.
The status reader requires the matching deployment, project, template version
and single target, successful overall and device status, and bounded start/end
timestamps. INIT and IN_PROGRESS remain pending; unknown, expired or unqueryable
receipts do not authorize replay. Epoch-millisecond and RFC3339 timestamps are
covered locally; appliance timestamp behavior still requires qualification.

The contract follows the pinned
[provider deployment resource](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/resource_catalystcenter_deploy_template.go)
and [payload mapping](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/model_catalystcenter_deploy_template.go),
with stricter receipt/completion evidence. The pinned module's regular deployment
uses managed-device UUID targets and committed version IDs. Redeploy is a
reconciliation policy, not a native payload field: ALWAYS must not become a
deployment on every reconciliation.

Targeted race tests pass for payload mapping, draft/identity/size rejection,
receipt extraction, malformed UUID suffixes, wrong target/version/project,
pending/failure/unknown states, absent devices, invalid times and unavailable
status. These are local fixtures. No public compiler, admission, native POST,
journal recovery, composite deployment or lab execution was enabled.

The full controller-adapter race regression also passed (Catalyst Center,
NetAsCode model, shared adapter and Nexus Dashboard), as did the strict
documentation build and whitespace check. Live qualification remains pending.


### Regular-template inventory intent (staged)

The deployment parser now extracts regular day-N targets from wired inventory
before reusing existing inventory/provisioning validation. Device state, identity,
site, discovery, tags and roles retain their existing validation. Deployments
require PROVISION or REPROVISION. Unsupported device fields, deployment fields,
composites and onboarding references are rejected rather than silently dropped.
No public inventory compiler was switched to this parser.

Reference resolution reuses the existing NetAsCode template index: unique bare
names, project-qualified names and explicitly qualified external templates are
supported. Ambiguous names and duplicate resolved targets are refused. Native
metadata and committed-version validation of external templates remains pending.
Pinned defaults are copying_config=true, force_push_template=true and
redeploy_template=NEVER; explicit false survives. Redeploy precedence follows
target, device, definition, then default. The existing template definition parser
now validates this policy without sending it as native template content. This
does not yet implement ALWAYS/ON_CHANGE/NEVER execution suppression.

Variable scalar and list values are normalized to request strings, including
primitive numeric and boolean values and explicit empty lists. Duplicate names,
nulls, nested objects and unknown variable attributes fail without publishing
values or partial executable intent. Parameters remain transient request data.

Targeted race tests passed across deployment intent, payload/receipt and wired
provisioning. Tests cover reference/default precedence, external references,
false options, primitive/list conversion, invalid states, ambiguity, duplicates,
onboarding/composite refusal and unknown-field rejection. Public wired parsing
still refuses the original day-N model, preventing a successful provisioning
result that silently omits template deployment. Native dependency preflight,
physical admission, journal execution/recovery, composite support and appliance
qualification remain outstanding. No lab mutation was performed.

The subsequent full adapter race regression passed, including Catalyst Center,
NetAsCode model, shared adapter and Nexus Dashboard. Strict documentation build
and whitespace validation also passed.


### Regular-template native dependency preflight (staged)

The regular deployment path now reuses the existing wired provisioning snapshot,
project reader, template inventory, latest committed-version selector and
committed-template reader. Preflight requires a reachable wired device with a
stable physical identity, the expected site assignment and an existing native
provisioning record at that site. Project/base-template/version UUIDs must resolve
and committed content must explicitly identify a regular template. Missing
prerequisites and draft-only versions cannot produce usable evidence.

A separate observation-only revalidation rereads those dependencies and rejects
changed physical identity, provisioning incarnation, project/template identity,
latest committed version or committed content. Committed content stays in memory
for comparison; it is neither journaled nor hashed into a resource key. This
helper is not mutation admission and does not submit a deployment. Platform and
parameter compatibility still require implementation before enabling submission.

Local HTTP/race tests pass for stable reads, unprovisioned/unassigned/unreachable
devices, absent projects/templates, draft-only versions, native composite/unknown
kind, mismatched version evidence, and late changes to serial, provisioning UUID,
project UUID, template UUID, version and content. The tests assert zero mutation
requests and no template-content disclosure through errors. Deployment model,
receipt, payload, version-reader and wired provisioning tests pass in the same
run. No deployed worker, real device or Catalyst Center lab qualification is
claimed; the public executor remains disabled for day-N deployments.


### Deployment parameter validation (staged)

Transient request construction from a native dependency snapshot now validates
supplied variables against committed template declarations before invoking the
payload builder. It checks duplicate/unknown names, required input, scalar/array
cardinality, non-parameter and section-divider entries, and basic INTEGER,
IPADDRESS and MACADDRESS syntax. Errors omit names and values. Defaults and
controller-bound values remain appliance-resolved rather than copied into
request/status data. Range, selection and platform compatibility remain pending.

The declaration fields follow Cisco's
[template details schema](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-4/gets-details-of-a-given-template/).
Local fixtures cover valid scalars/arrays, default/bound/optional inputs, missing
and empty required values, undeclared/duplicate variables, malformed metadata,
invalid numeric/IP/MAC values and scalar cardinality. The dependency fixture
checks that undeclared parameters cannot produce a request. This is bounded
pre-submission validation, not a deployment executor or full appliance semantic
validation. No public submission or lab mutation was enabled.


### Committed template selections (staged)

Deployment parameter checks now validate committed SINGLE_SELECT and
MULTI_SELECT metadata, supplied choice values, duplicate choices and controller
default selections. Single selection requires exactly one supplied value; multi
selection accepts multiple values without requiring a separate paramArray flag.
An optional multi-selection can be explicitly empty, but required empty input
is refused. Controller default selections can satisfy omitted required input
and are not copied into the request or status. Malformed selection kinds,
choice maps and defaults fail before request construction.

Local race tests pass for valid single/multiple/default/optional-empty cases and
unknown values, display labels used as values, duplicate choices, wrong
cardinality, malformed metadata and required empty inputs. Existing deployment
parameter, payload, dependency and receipt tests pass in the same run.

Range semantics, platform compatibility, native submission and recovery remain
pending. The shared Accepted journal phase still uses generic task completion;
a deployment-specific completion path must be added explicitly before enabling
template deployment. No generic task behavior or public executor was changed,
and no lab mutation was performed.


### Integer deployment parameter ranges (staged)

Committed INTEGER parameter constraints now validate numeric bounds and supplied
values before request construction. The local implementation treats intervals
as inclusive alternatives and checks every supplied array element. Missing,
reversed, fractional or string-encoded native bounds are rejected. Float64
bounds outside the exact safe-integer range are refused rather than silently
rounded; explicit exact JSON numbers retain precision.

The native minValue/maxValue shape follows Cisco's
[template API schema](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-4/create-template/).
Inclusive/alternative interval behavior still requires appliance qualification.
Non-integer nonempty ranges are rejected pending their specific semantics;
empty/absent ranges impose no range restriction. This does not claim string
length or other range parity. No submission path was enabled.

Targeted race tests passed for boundary values, separate intervals and gaps,
array violations, reversed/missing/fractional/string bounds, precision loss and
exact large integers, together with existing deployment model, parameter,
selection, payload, dependency and receipt tests. Platform checks, native
execution/recovery and lab qualification remain pending.


### Receipt-specific completion in the shared journal

The Accepted phase now observes completion through its compiled apply plan.
Plans with no specialized observer retain the existing generic task reader.
A future template deployment plan can instead use the deployment status reader
without introducing a second journal, timeout policy or reservation family.
The shared reconciler still controls timeout, failure, phase advancement and
physical reservation recovery checks. No production compiler sets a specialized
observer yet, so day-N deployment remains gated.

The dispatcher requires an Accepted operation, matching section, submission
time and receipt. A specialized observer receives a deep copy of the operation.
Pending or failed specialized observations never fall back to generic task
completion. Tests exercise the real deployment status reader through this
dispatcher for success, pending and unavailable receipts; they also check generic
behavior, invalid journal rejection and protection against observer mutation of
the retained operation. Public template submission and full manifest-cycle
qualification remain pending.

The full adapter race regression passed (shared adapter, Catalyst Center,
NetAsCode model and Nexus Dashboard). Strict documentation build and whitespace
validation passed. This is local regression evidence, not lab qualification.


### Template platform applicability (staged)

Regular-template preflight now reads the target's device details and binds the
result to its resolved UUID, canonical serial, family and observed software
version. Missing metadata, an unreachable device or disagreement between list
and detail observations fails preflight. Template-specific metadata stays out
of the shared Device model, preserving unrelated inventory snapshot digests.
The reader uses the existing transport and Cisco's
[device-details endpoint](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/get-device-by-id/).

Committed template applicability checks require matching software type and at
least one matching family/optional series/type entry. Explicit software versions
currently require exact equality; version-pattern semantics and software
variants remain gated pending qualification. Every native type entry is checked
for malformed metadata even when another entry matches. The bound metadata is
retained in the transient dependency snapshot and reread during revalidation.
Request construction repeats the applicability check before using parameters.

Local fixtures cover family-only/exact/alternative matches, incompatible family,
series, type, software and version, gated patterns/variants, malformed metadata,
missing device detail and replaced or stale identity. Deployment submission,
public compiler/recovery wiring and appliance qualification remain outstanding.
No lab writes were performed.

Platform/deployment race tests passed, including a final revalidation test
rejecting a changed device software version even without a template version
restriction. Strict documentation build and whitespace checks passed.


### Native regular-template submission plan (staged)

`planRegularTemplateDeployment` now connects existing preflight and request
validation to the shared configuration-write contract. It records physical
target/site/serial identity, freezes the payload, revalidates native dependencies
immediately before POST and requires a deployment-specific receipt. Template
base/version UUIDs and version number remain explicit in the resource key so
recovery can select the submitted version instead of assuming latest is unchanged.
The digest contains nonsensitive dependency identity and options, excluding
template content and parameter values.

The planner performs no mutation itself. Its submit function uses the existing
transport and returns an error for rejected or receipt-less responses. The
enclosing adapter still must provide source/owner binding, durable physical
admission, receipt suppression and journal recovery. No public compiler registers
this native plan yet; the helper alone does not provide restart/no-replay safety.

Targeted race fixtures passed for accepted deployment, missing receipt, rejected
POST, caller parameter changes and late committed-version/platform/content
changes. They check physical identity, version-bound nonsensitive keys, frozen
payload, zero POSTs for stale dependencies and one POST for an attempted native
submission. Existing deployment parameter, platform, receipt, dependency and
completion-dispatch tests also passed. These are HTTP fixtures, not lab tests or
a complete manifest deployment cycle.


### Submitted-version template recovery (staged)

Native recovery now parses the retained base/version UUID and version number
from the deployment resource key, validates that binding and reads the exact
committed version. It reuses dependency/platform/parameter validation and checks
the retained physical target, site, serial and resource digest before observing
the deployment receipt. It never substitutes the latest committed version or
performs a POST. Accepted and Verifying phases are supported; malformed receipt
IDs, invalid submission times and uncertain phases fail before API observation.

The dependency reader now shares its native resolution logic between latest
version planning and explicit submitted-version recovery. New commits therefore
do not strand an accepted operation merely because a newer version exists.
Replacement native identities and changed physical dependencies still fail
correlation. The enclosing adapter must separately validate source/owner and
retained admission before advancing the journal or writing completion receipts.

Targeted race fixtures passed for recovery success, newer latest version,
pending and failed deployment status, strict resource parsing and malformed
receipt rejection before IO. Repeated Accepted/Verifying observations preserve
the single original POST and perform no latest-version lookup. This establishes
the native recovery primitive only; public manifest execution, source/owner
binding, redeploy receipts and lab qualification remain pending.


### Source/owner-bound template recovery (staged)

The adapter recovery entry now binds native deployment observation to the
configuration UID/name/generation, controller generation, source UID/version,
unique inventory owner and exact retained journal. It uses existing source and
controller readers, then repeats source validation and controller
UID/resourceVersion/journal checks after successful native observation. Late
source or journal changes cannot yield completion evidence for the old operation.

This observer does not advance the journal or publish an action receipt. The
shared reconciler remains responsible for physical admission validation, phase
advancement and settlement. No public compiler calls this entry yet.

The existing native submission/recovery fixture now includes fake-Kubernetes
source/owner tests: valid observation, foreign/missing/duplicate owner, wrong
source revision, configuration/controller generation mismatch, different
operation and late inline-source/journal mutations. All targeted race tests
passed. Tests confirm no extra native POST/latest-version lookup and no
observer-created action receipt or phase transition. ConfigMap-specific races,
public execution/redeploy receipts, real actor qualification and lab testing
remain pending.


### Template completion action receipt (staged)

`recordOwnedTemplateDeployment` now verifies a retained Verifying operation
through the owned native recovery path and uses the existing physical action
receipt writer to persist Verified and its receipt atomically. It rechecks the
controller revision and source before bookkeeping. There is no new receipt
collection, lease family, journal or native mutation in this operation.

The shared writer retains existing reservation-aware overwrite checks, capacity
limits and persisted readback validation. A repeated completion call after
Verified is refused rather than rerunning verification/submission. Completion
recording does not release the reservation; shared settlement remains required.

The native/fake-Kubernetes fixture exercises persistence of the original
deployment receipt and verified timestamp, and verifies that foreign ownership
or late source/journal changes cannot create completion evidence. These fixtures
do not prove real actor qualification or public manifest execution. Redeploy
suppression, compiler/stage integration, ConfigMap-specific recovery and lab
qualification remain pending.

Full adapter race regression passed, including shared adapter, Catalyst Center,
NetAsCode model and Nexus Dashboard. Strict documentation build and whitespace
validation passed.


### Receipt-based deployment suppression (staged)

The adapter planner now brackets native planning with source/controller checks
and consults retained action receipts before returning a write. Receipt checks
validate ownership, operation/resource identity, physical incarnation, verified
status, deployment receipt and timestamps. Active journals, duplicate or invalid
receipts and foreign ownership cannot authorize another deployment.

NEVER suppresses a previously verified deployment to the same physical target
and base template. ALWAYS is defined as one deployment per explicit CVK input
revision, not every reconciliation. ON_CHANGE suppresses a known same-revision,
same-version action and permits a provable version change; a new source revision
reusing the same template version remains gated until effective-input comparison
is implemented without retaining sensitive parameter values. These are partial
policy semantics, not full NetAsCode redeploy parity.

Local tests exercise first deployment, repeated input, revised input, changed
version, owner/receipt corruption, duplicate receipts, uncertain state and
replaced devices. The completion fixture models a journal already cleared by
settlement, then confirms fresh planning yields no additional write under NEVER.
It does not simulate real reservation settlement. Recovery-only observations
still make no latest-version lookup; the separate fresh plan performs one.
Public compiler/stage integration and lab qualification remain pending.


### Regular-template executor bridge (staged)

Regular template deployments now implement the existing configuration executor
interface. Fresh planning uses owned receipt suppression. Prepared recovery
requires the current source/controller revisions, unique owner, matching native
resource and physical identity, and unchanged controller revision across native
replanning. Submitted, uncertain, cancelled or mismatched operations cannot
produce another write.

Accepted completion uses the owned deployment observer, and Verifying uses the
same owned native evidence through the standard verify method. Phase boundaries
are explicit. The enclosing inventory stage still must order provisioning,
route retained operations and acquire physical admission before submission; no
public compiler selects this executor yet.

Targeted native/fake-Kubernetes race fixtures passed for exact Prepared resume,
source/resource/owner mismatch, Accepted/Verifying observation and Unknown
refusal. They confirm that executor recovery leaves the original native POST
count at one and rejects verification through the wrong phase. Real worker,
reservation and complete manifest-cycle qualification remain pending.

Full adapter race regression passed across Catalyst Center, NetAsCode model,
shared adapter and Nexus Dashboard. Strict documentation build and whitespace
checks also passed. No live deployment was attempted.


### Inventory/template stage ordering (staged)

The inventory composition wrapper now orders existing provisioning prerequisites
before regular-template deployment when there is no retained operation. An
active template operation routes directly by its recorded base-template UUID,
device UUID and physical serial; it cannot fall through to prerequisite planning.
Missing or duplicate bindings refuse recovery. Other retained operations keep
the prerequisite plan's completion/verification path.

Both asynchronous and synchronous submission closures recheck the compiler's
validation callback immediately before invocation. The wrapper does not invent
physical identity or grant admission; compiler preflight must supply and
revalidate every binding. It remains outside public compiler dispatch.

Targeted race tests passed for prerequisite ordering, late invalidation of both
submission forms, prerequisite completion delegation, exact Prepared resume,
Accepted/Verifying routing, Unknown refusal and duplicate-binding rejection.
Existing wired sequencing/recovery tests passed in the same run. No deployment
was replayed by the stage fixtures. Public compiler integration, full manifest
cycle, real reservations and lab qualification remain pending.


### Staged inventory/template compiler

The inventory-only compiler now combines qualified existing regular-template
references with shared wired prerequisites, template stages and the specialized
completion observer. Parsed wired execution was factored into a reusable helper
without replacing the original configuration source snapshot. Template identity,
version and content resolution is shared between pre-provisioning validation
and post-provisioning deployment/recovery.

Preflight resolves device/site and template identities, validates platform and
parameters before returning prerequisite writes, and retains stable physical
and base-template bindings for revalidation. When recovering a retained template
operation it selects that recorded version. The existing managed-inventory Apply
requirement for an explicit serial remains in force. A name-only compiler fixture
correctly failed that existing gate; deferred name/IP-only binding remains work,
not a capability of this compiler.

The revised composition fixture uses an explicit serial, checks rejection without
the admission hook, and exercises template validation before native provisioning
exists. It then models completed provisioning and expects deployment planning
without changing the source snapshot. Public compiler dispatch is deliberately
unchanged pending full manifest-cycle qualification. Combined template-definition
creation plus inventory, composite deployment and lab qualification remain pending.

The explicit-serial compiler fixture and full adapter race regression passed,
including Catalyst Center, shared adapter, NetAsCode model and Nexus Dashboard.
Strict documentation build and whitespace checks passed.


### Public regular-template manifest cycle

Inventory Apply now selects the template compiler for a fully parsed regular
day-N model, behind the existing configuration-reservation admission hook.
This enables existing project-qualified regular templates with explicit physical
serials. Wired and wireless routing retains its previous paths for other models;
unsupported template fields cannot fall through to successful partial execution.
The example is `examples/configs/catalyst-center/template-deployment-apply.yaml`.

The stateful local manifest fixture now exercises assignment, wired provisioning
and template POST through the public reconciler/compiler/shared journal. Worker
instances are reconstructed between reconciliations. Deployment receipts use
the specialized status endpoint, successful verification retains action receipts,
and simulated settlement clears each operation. Repeated reconciliation reaches
InSync without additional POSTs. Lost deployment receipts remain Unknown and
failed deployment status remains retained rather than automatically replayed.

The fixture uses the existing test-only dispatch permit and synthesized reservation
claim/completion/settlement evidence. It is not a real actor/Lease or appliance
qualification. Targeted race tests passed, including the existing wired manifest
cycle. Lab validation, ConfigMap-specific races, combined template-definition
creation, composites, complete ON_CHANGE comparison, deferred name/IP-only
binding and broader version/range semantics remain pending. This enables a
bounded regular deployment path, not full NetAsCode component parity.


### ConfigMap-backed regular deployment qualification

The public manifest-cycle fixture now also runs from a ConfigMap source. The
successful path retains the source UID/resource version across assignment,
provisioning and deployment, then converges without a repeated POST. Updating,
deleting or replacing the ConfigMap after planning prevents native deployment.
Changing it after an accepted deployment preserves the original operation and
source binding instead of declaring success, clearing the journal or replaying.

These are local fake-Kubernetes/native-HTTP tests with simulated reservation
settlement, not live appliance or actor qualification. No new source tracking
mechanism was added: the existing configuration snapshot and operation journal
provide these guards. The full adapter/reservation race regression preceding
this expansion passed, including Nexus Dashboard. Lab authentication remains
unqualified after the previously observed HTTP 401; no live validation is claimed.


### Multiple regular templates and composite request mapping

The public inventory fixture now deploys two regular templates on one physical
device in source order, reconstructing workers and settling the shared journal
between actions. Each uses its own committed version and deployment receipt.
Repeated reconciliation preserves four receipts (assignment, provisioning and
two deployments) without additional native writes. Failure or an ambiguous
receipt on the second deployment retains that operation; the first deployment
is not replayed. This is local fixture qualification with simulated reservation
actors, not multi-device or lab qualification.

A private composite request builder now maps the pinned module's managed and
existing-composite deployment shapes. Parent and ordered members use committed
UUIDs as `templateId` and base UUIDs as `mainTemplateId`; members retain their
individual copying/force options and scalar/list/empty parameters. Both parent
and members target the same physical device. The existing regular parameter
encoder is shared. Duplicate/cyclic UUID bindings, mixed physical targets,
uncommitted versions, invalid parameters and oversized payloads are refused.
No parameter material is added to operation status or resource identities.

Mapping evidence is the pinned module's `cc_templates.tf` composite resources and
[provider v0.6.1 native serializer](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/model_catalystcenter_deploy_template.go).
The [Cisco deployment API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/deploy-template/)
also describes composite/main-template fields, but its older schema is not used
to infer the complete nested v2 member shape. Native dependency resolution,
member-specific model parsing, committed membership recovery, adapter/journal
integration and lab qualification remain pending. Composite execution is not
publicly enabled by this request builder.


### Composite committed dependency graph

A private composite content reader now resolves the committed parent and its
ordered regular members through the existing project, definition, committed
version and native content readers. Member UUIDs must agree with the independent
definition inventory; optional native name/project metadata and declared model
member order must agree too. Missing, duplicate, recursive, nested-composite or
ambiguous member-name bindings are refused. Fresh revalidation compares native
membership, order, version identities and transient content. Recovery can supply
explicit parent/member version bindings and performs no latest-version lookup.
These bindings have not yet been integrated into a durable operation format.

The bound graph now feeds the composite payload builder after parent/member
platform validation and per-member parameter validation. Unknown variable-member
names are rejected instead of dropping their values. Parameter values and native
content remain in memory; they are not written into status or resource keys.
Shared regular content reading retains its regular-only kind check.

Local HTTP fixtures cover stable and cross-project membership, declared order,
version-pinned recovery, missing/reordered/replaced dependencies, changed member
content, malformed graph metadata and parameter/platform rejection. This remains
private preparation code. Composite manifest parsing, physical dependency
binding, durable recovery metadata, native submission, public compiler routing
and live qualification remain pending; no composite CLI deployment was performed.


### Composite physical dependency binding

Composite preflight now composes the existing wired provision snapshot, exact
native device-detail identity and committed template graph readers. It requires
an assigned/provisioned reachable wired target and checks the parent plus every
member against that platform. The combined payload path corroborates the device
UUID and canonical serial before using per-member variables. Fresh revalidation
compares the full transient physical and template evidence; it grants no mutation
permit and does not POST.

Targeted race fixtures passed for a stable bound payload, unassigned,
unprovisioned and unreachable targets, plus late serial, provision-record,
software-platform and member-version changes. Existing regular preflight and
composite graph/parameter fixtures passed in the same run. These are local native
HTTP fixtures, not physical reservation actors or live appliance qualification.

Durable composite graph recovery is still required before execution. The existing
operation resource key is limited to 512 characters and cannot encode arbitrary
ordered parent/member version graphs. CredentialVersions is credential-specific
and must not be repurposed for template versions. A bounded nonsecret dependency
binding extension needs schema, digest/admission, journal and recovery coverage;
no such extension or public composite submission is claimed by this increment.


### Staged durable template dependency identities

The operation schema now preserves an optional `dependencyVersions` envelope:
`kind: template-graph-v1` and an atomic ordered list of 2–1001 base UUID,
committed UUID and positive version-number entries. Parent comes first; member
order follows. The envelope contains no native content, parameters, credentials
or content hashes. Generated DeepCopy code isolates the list and canonical/Helm
NetworkController schemas preserve it in active and retained operations.

Composite graph encoding/decoding now converts between this typed envelope and
the existing pinned content-reader bindings. Decoding rejects unsupported kinds,
invalid/duplicate/cross-colliding UUIDs, uncommitted versions and bound violations.
The envelope is not yet populated by the journal/compiler. Existing single-device
and staged group operation digests explicitly reject it, preventing schema
availability from implicitly admitting an unqualified execution path. Empty-field
legacy operations retain their existing serialized/digest representation.

Targeted schema preservation, DeepCopy, decoder, candidate and protocol refusal
tests passed. Full journal persistence, digest/admission activation, composite
executor recovery and live qualification remain pending. This schema increment
alone does not enable composite deployment.

API-server static validation and envtest initially rejected a redundant per-entry
CEL base/version inequality check: nested retained-receipt cardinality multiplied
its estimated cost beyond the Kubernetes budget. The rule was removed from the
schema; the strict graph decoder still enforces distinct/non-colliding identities
and runtime admission still rejects the entire envelope. Regenerated schemas
passed the Kubernetes envtest suite after this correction.


### Dependency graph journal persistence

The shared Catalyst Center operation identity can now carry the typed dependency
version envelope. Preparation validates composite-only physical inventory scope
and deep-copies it into the Prepared operation. Start/resume and post-Submitting
readback require exact equality with the expected graph, alongside existing
source, target, parent, serial and credential bindings. Missing metadata cannot
silently downgrade a graph-bound operation into a legacy submission.

The validator accepts graphs only for Update actions with the reserved
`template-composite-deploy:` resource prefix, a physical target/site/serial and
no credential-version operation. Graph decoding enforces the previously defined
kind, bounds and identity constraints. Other operation paths retain nil envelopes.
Production physical digest/admission still rejects these graph-bearing operations;
no public composite compiler or production submission was activated.

Local journal fixtures cover copy isolation, absent/changed expected graphs,
invalid scope, accepted receipt preservation and graph change/removal during
admission. Additional fixtures prune the graph from Prepared and Submitting
status writes; both retain the operation fence and prevent native dispatch. The accepted fixture uses the existing test-only dispatch permit;
it is not evidence that manager/worker admission or live deployment is enabled.


### Private composite native submission and observation

Composite native planning now freezes a validated request, exposes the physical
identity plus explicit dependency graph for journal preparation, and revalidates
the full physical/content snapshot immediately before POST through the existing
transport. The response must contain a valid deployment receipt; missing receipts
are errors, never generic-task substitutions. The private helper itself grants
no replay or mutation permission and remains outside public compiler dispatch.

The compact operation resource hashes only physical/provision/platform evidence,
parent/member project identities, ordered version identities and nonsecret
copying/force options. Template content, variables and their hashes are excluded.
Accepted/Verifying observation reconstructs the explicitly retained graph, checks
the resource and physical binding, then uses the shared deployment-status reader.
Observation performs neither a POST nor a latest-version lookup.

Local native fixtures cover one POST, missing receipt, stale member rejection,
pending/failing deployment, altered retained graph and recovery after a newer
member version appears. Resource tests distinguish parent/member project changes
while proving variable/content changes do not enter the resource key. These are
native primitives exercised directly by fixtures, not manager/worker admission,
owned adapter recovery, public manifest execution or live appliance qualification.
Those integration and qualification steps remain pending.


### Owned composite recovery observation

Regular and composite deployment observations now share one owner/source/journal
validation bracket. The adapter requires the exact retained operation, config
identity/generation, controller generation, source UID/version and exactly one
matching inventory owner before native observation. After successful native
verification it rereads source and controller state and rejects any intervening
change. The composite observer uses the previously retained version graph and
never advances the journal or publishes an action receipt itself.

The stateful native fixture now also exercises fake-Kubernetes owned recovery:
valid recovery, missing/foreign owners, a changed requested graph, and source or
journal changes during native reads. It reloads the persisted operation before
observation, including Kubernetes timestamp normalization. Targeted race tests
passed for these cases and the existing regular recovery/journal fixtures.
This is observation qualification only; physical admission, atomic composite
completion bookkeeping, redeploy policy and public compiler integration remain
pending. No real reservation actors or appliance deployment were exercised.


### Atomic owned composite completion

Regular and composite completion now share the existing bookkeeping sequence:
require the exact Verifying operation, perform owned native observation, recheck
controller/source state, then persist Verified and its action receipt atomically.
