The composite receipt retains the full dependency-version graph through the
existing operation DeepCopy and action-receipt writer. Completion does not POST,
release a physical reservation or clear the active operation.

Local fake-Kubernetes/native fixtures passed for graph-preserving completion,
repeat refusal, foreign ownership, and source/journal changes during verification.
The existing regular submission/recovery fixtures passed after factoring the
common bookkeeping helper. These fixtures synthesize retained Verifying state;
they do not prove real admission, settlement or live appliance operation. Public
composite execution and admission remain disabled pending executor, redeploy,
compiler and reservation qualification.


### Composite receipt-aware planning

Composite and regular planning now share source/controller checks and the same
receipt policy evaluator. The evaluator validates composite resource keys and
retained version envelopes, compares the full ordered parent/member graph, and
keeps regular/composite identities distinct. Composite planning supplies its
explicit graph to the desired operation. A verified retained composite receipt
suppresses repeated NEVER execution after the active journal has been cleared.

Local policy fixtures cover unchanged revisions, first deployment, new input
revisions, parent/member version changes, added members, missing/malformed graphs,
foreign ownership, duplicate/unverified receipts and replacement devices. The
owned native fixture records completion, models settlement by clearing the slot,
then replans and observes no new write. This is not actual actor settlement.
ALWAYS remains once per explicit CVK revision. ON_CHANGE supports same-revision
graph equality and provable graph changes, but still refuses unresolved new-source
revisions with the same graph; full effective-input comparison remains pending.
No secrets or content hashes are persisted to implement this comparison.

Production composite admission, executor/public routing and live qualification
remain pending. Receipt suppression is neither device compliance nor mutation
permission.


### Composite configuration executor

A private composite executor now implements the existing configuration interface.
Regular and composite executors share source/owner/exact-Prepared resume checks;
resumed writes must match the retained dependency graph as well as resource,
action and physical identity. Prepared operations containing a receipt or a
submission timestamp are refused. Native planning remains observation-only until
the separate journal/physical dispatch path invokes a write.

Composite Accepted operations use owned deployment observation, Verifying uses
owned verification, and other retained phases cannot produce another write.
Fixture coverage includes exact Prepared resume, altered graph, missing owner,
stale source, a premature receipt, Accepted/Verifying routing and Unknown refusal.
The stateful native fixture checks that executor observation causes neither POST
nor latest-version lookup; only fresh/Prepared planning resolves latest versions.

This executor is not registered in public inventory stage routing yet. Composite
manifest parsing, stage integration, production physical admission and complete

### Composite model parsing and mixed inventory extraction

Regular/composite target parsing now shares identity resolution, defaults,

variables additionally require a bare `template_name`, are scoped by member and

against the model index; qualified external composite references require native
membership validation later. Onboarding/regular definitions cannot be used as

A private inventory extractor now retains both regular and composite lists per
device, reusing existing wired validation after extracting the complete day-N
intent. Same-reference regular/composite conflicts and unsupported sections are
refused. The public regular-only wrapper explicitly refuses composites rather
than discarding them. Missing serial parsing retains the existing wired semantics;

Targeted race fixtures passed for composite/default/policy/member variables,
mixed/composite-only inventories, malformed models and unchanged regular manifest
cycles. Public composite dispatch, stage integration and physical admission are
still pending. An empty regular list may accompany composite targets without losing intent;
parsing is not execution or live validation.


### Shared regular/composite inventory stages

The existing inventory stage wrapper now accepts a common deployment executor
interface for both template kinds. Retained routing uses validated receipt
identity plus deployment kind, base-template UUID, device UUID and serial; a

passed after the change. The public compiler still constructs only regular
executors; mixed compiler binding/preflight, production admission and full

### Private mixed inventory compiler preflight

The inventory template compiler now has a private mixed mode that constructs
regular and composite executors in the existing stage wrapper. It reuses the

Before returning prerequisite writes it resolves device/site/project/template
identities, validates platform and all variables, and retains stable physical
and base-template bindings. Retained composite operations select their explicit

Local compiler fixtures cover composite-only and mixed intent before/after native
provisioning, explicit serial/graph retention, rejection without the admission

The public compiler remains regular-only. Production dependency-graph admission,

still pending; private compiler availability does not enable those capabilities.
Combined template-definition creation and inventory deployment also remain work.


### Scoped dependency-graph reservation binding

The shared single-device operation digest now admits validated dependency graphs
only for inventory Update operations with a canonical composite resource key and
physical target/site identity. Its existing immutable-operation serialization
includes the complete ordered graph, so parent/member UUIDs, version numbers and
order affect the reservation digest. Phase, task receipt and submission time
retain their existing non-identity treatment. Legacy nil-envelope serialization

Graph validation is shared between the contract and Catalyst Center decoder,
avoiding independent identity/bounds rules. Candidate fixtures now construct
valid graph-bound single-device reservations, retain the normal worker/physical
checks and reject a graph changed after reservation creation. Invalid scope,
missing graph, malformed resource key, duplicate identities and unknown kinds
remain refused. Candidate creation itself still grants no lease or dispatch permit.

Targeted contract/adapter tests passed. This enables scoped digest/candidate
support, not public composite manifest execution or lab qualification. The public
compiler is still regular-only; a full graph-bearing manifest and reservation
actor cycle remains to be exercised before opening that route.


### Public bounded composite manifest execution

Inventory Apply now routes fully parsed composite or mixed day-N models through
the shared mixed compiler and existing physical admission setup. Existing
project-qualified, committed composites on explicitly identified wired devices
are supported with per-member variables. Assignment/provisioning prerequisites,
parent/member preflight, graph-bound operation digests, exact Prepared resume,

The example is `examples/configs/catalyst-center/composite-template-deployment-apply.yaml`.

Stateful local manifest fixtures exercise composite-only and mixed regular plus
composite cycles through the public reconciler/compiler/journal, reconstructing
workers between steps. Successful cycles reach InSync without repeated POSTs.
Missing deployment receipts remain Unknown; failed status remains retained.
Prepared composite operations contain the complete graph and qualify for the
shared operation digest. Reservation claims and settlement are synthesized by
fixtures using the existing test-only dispatch permit, not real actor/Lease tests.

A further fixture publishes a newer member version after submission to verify
that recovery continues to observe the submitted graph. Live composite deployment
and real manager/device-worker qualification remain outstanding.

ConfigMap-backed composite fixtures also cover successful convergence, source
changes before and after submission, deletion and replacement with a different UID.
Pre-submit changes prevent a native POST; post-submit changes retain the accepted
operation without replay or retirement. Two already provisioned devices can share
one committed composite while retaining separate deployment receipts; local fixtures
cover ordered convergence without repeat writes and refusal of a success response
that names the other device. These are native/compiler/journal tests with synthetic
