Combined definition creation, full ON_CHANGE semantics, broader multi-device
lifecycles and other unqualified deployment options remain work. Public routing
is bounded support, not full NetAsCode deployment parity.


### RMA model and native observation groundwork

The pinned `cc_rma.tf` keeps inventory devices in `PROVISION`; its separate
`rma.action` selects `MARK_FOR_REPLACEMENT` or `REPLACE`. The new RMA parser
retains this distinction and delegates common inventory validation to the wired
parser. It requires explicit old/new serials for replacement, compares identities
using the shared topology canonicalizer, and rejects self-replacement, reused
replacement identities, duplicate declared hardware and unknown intent. Marking
can retain an unresolved serial for later authenticated inventory binding.
The current parser is inventory-only; combined fabric/template RMA and stacks
remain unsupported rather than being stripped from the model.

Native mark and workflow payload builders follow the pinned CiscoDevNet
[replacement model](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/model_catalystcenter_device_replacement.go)
and [workflow model](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/model_catalystcenter_device_replacement_workflow.go).
The read-only replacement inventory uses the shared authenticated transport and
pagination checks for the documented
[replacement details API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/return-list-of-replacement-devices-with-replacement-details/).
It preserves workflow/readiness identifiers and status without treating an
unknown status as success. Malformed identities, ambiguous faulty devices,
null/partial responses and repeating pages are refused. Serial spelling is
preserved for native requests; canonicalization is used for identity comparison.

Model, payload and HTTP/race fixtures are local evidence only. No public RMA
route or native mutation is enabled. The upstream workflow resource submits
without waiting; CVK still needs durable workflow receipts, readiness and final
replacement evidence, old/new device fencing, identity handoff, owned cleanup
and restart recovery through its existing journal/reservation mechanisms.
Removing the RMA block does not yet authorize unmarking. Live appliance and
replacement-hardware qualification remain outstanding.


### RMA identity binding and private native mark planning

Replacement snapshots now resolve the faulty device through the existing
configuration selector and shared canonical physical identity checks. They retain
an optional replacement-device binding and native replacement record, reject
conflicting old/new serials and records belonging to another workflow, and detect
native identity or workflow changes on a fresh read. Faulty-device reachability is
not required for this observation. An absent replacement in network inventory is
not evidence of PnP readiness or mutation authority.

The private native mark planner requires an explicit faulty-device serial, refuses
an existing unowned replacement record, and returns the existing configuration-write
type with the physical target identity. Before POST it repeats the native snapshot
checks. It uses the shared transport and mandatory task-receipt parser for the
[mark API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/mark-device-for-replacement/).
Missing or object-shaped task IDs are refused rather than guessed; the documented
taskId schema is insufficient to qualify an appliance-specific alternate receipt.

Local race/HTTP fixtures cover unreachable faulty-device identity, absent/appearing
replacement inventory, cross-workflow serial conflicts, late native changes,
mark payloads and ambiguous receipts. Native records appearing after a lost reply
are not adopted. These fixtures do not prove journal restart recovery: public Apply
remains gated until owned completion, recovery, physical admission and old/new
identity handoff are integrated and qualified. No lab RMA mutation was performed.


### Native RMA mark completion evidence

Mark planning and observation now share a physical resource identity builder.
The native observer accepts only submitted Accepted/Verifying inventory-create
operations with the matching target/resource/serial and no group, dependency,
cancellation or credential envelope. It uses the existing task completion reader,
then requires a fresh serial-bearing replacement record with a mark/ready status.
A second unchanged snapshot closes late native identity/workflow changes before
returning the record UUID as evidence for future owned receipt persistence.

The observer never submits, changes the journal or adopts an Unknown operation.
A selected replacement, workflow ID or replacement completion timestamp is beyond
the mark effect and is refused. Fixtures cover pending/failed/wrong/stale tasks,
missing readback, old/future records, missing/wrong serials, unknown statuses,
progressed workflows, identity changes and late changes. Creation timestamps are
currently interpreted as epoch milliseconds with the shared task clock-skew bound;
this interpretation and appliance task receipt shape remain live qualification
requirements, not established RMA lab behavior.

Native completion evidence is not yet adapter-owned completion: atomic receipt
persistence, retained-source/owner checks, journal recovery, mark/unmark lifecycle,
replacement workflow handoff and public manifest execution remain pending.


### Owned RMA mark evidence and atomic completion

The RMA adapter now uses the existing inventory owner/source/exact-operation
observation bracket around native mark verification. Native record evidence is
discarded if the owner is missing/foreign/duplicated, the source or controller
revision differs, or the source/journal changes during native reads.

Shared atomic inventory completion now permits a resource-specific result key.
Template completion preserves its existing operation-resource key. RMA records
`rma-mark-record:<native-record-id>` in the action receipt while preserving the
admitted operation resource, target, serial and task. No API/CRD field or reservation
digest semantics are changed. The existing writer persists Verified and the action
receipt together; it neither submits native work nor releases the device fence.

Fake-Kubernetes/native fixtures cover owned observation, atomic receipt persistence,
foreign/missing/duplicate owners, wrong operations and source/journal races. A
synthetic reservation checks compatibility with the shared completion contract;
this is not real actor/Lease qualification. Receipt-aware re-planning, retained
native UUID validation after settlement, unmark lifecycle, public compiler wiring,
replacement workflow handoff and lab qualification remain pending.


### Receipt-aware RMA mark planning

The idle adapter planner now consults retained action receipts before proposing a
mark. Ownership binds the native replacement-record UUID and faulty-device UUID
and canonical serial, with validated operation and verification timestamps. A
changed source revision or intended spare does not erase the completed mark;
this supports the pinned model's mark-to-replace transition without another POST.
The later replacement workflow is still a separate unimplemented admission step.

An absent receipt cannot adopt an existing native mark. A deleted/recreated record,
changed faulty-device identity, ambiguous/foreign ownership, malformed receipt,
selected replacement or progressed workflow prevents mark replay. New marks require
an idle journal and current section ownership, then reuse the existing native
planner. Native/source/controller-version checks run again before returning a plan.

Local fixtures cover receipt validation, source/spare changes, deleted and replaced
native records, new-mark planning, active-journal refusal and late owner/source
changes. The owned-completion fixture simulates settlement, reconstructs the
adapter, verifies no repeat write and rejects replacement of the retained native
record UUID. These are fake Kubernetes/native fixtures, not live actor tests.
Exact Prepared dispatch/resume, owned unmark/receipt retirement, compiler routing,
replacement workflow execution and lab qualification remain pending.


### Staged RMA mark executor

The mark executor now uses the same exact Prepared-write reconstruction helper
as regular and composite templates (renamed `nextPreparedInventoryWrite` to reflect
its shared use). It binds the retained source/owner/operation, compares native
resource and physical identity, and rechecks source/controller state. Submitted,
Verified and Unknown journals cannot return writes. Idle planning delegates to
the receipt-aware RMA planner.

Accepted observation and Verifying readback use the owned native observer.
The executor's separate completion method calls atomic RMA receipt persistence,
retaining the native record UUID. It must be connected through a specialized
completion path when public compiler routing is added; generic Verified advancement
would lose that UUID. No public RMA route is enabled by this change.

Local fixtures cover phase refusal, task/submission markers, owner/identity/graph
mismatches, native record/device changes, late source changes, owned verification
and completion. Regular/composite public manifest cycles also pass after sharing
the helper. Public plan completion routing, full manifest execution, physical actor
qualification, cleanup and replacement workflow execution remain outstanding.


### Shared optional atomic completion hook

Configuration plans can now provide `recordCompletion` for native-result receipts.
The reconciler invokes it in Verifying instead of generic verification/advancement;
a nil hook preserves existing behavior, including the existing image, wireless
and credential completion paths. Errors do not fall back to generic verification.

The helper checks the exact retained Verifying operation before invoking the
callback with a deep copy. Afterwards it requires the same controller identity
and generation, the unchanged operation in Verified, and exactly one matching
retained action receipt with a valid verification timestamp. A callback that
returns success without persisting both operation and receipt is refused.

Local tests cover missing/duplicate receipts, changed operation identity,
callback errors/no-op results, invalid input phases/sections and copy isolation.
RMA's owned native/atomic receipt fixtures now execute through this hook. Public
RMA compiler wiring is still pending; these tests do not constitute a deployed
manifest/actor flow. Unmark cleanup, replacement execution and lab qualification
remain outstanding.

Site execution now submits selected coordinates and geometry at the same pinned
precision used by drift comparison, preserving source intent and unselected
building attributes. Whole-intent execution preflight refuses dimensions rounded
to zero before parent writes. Site race regression passed (3.826s); live isolated
area/building/floor creation, floor-width update, native convergence and verified
cleanup passed (11.32s). See [site execution evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-14/site-execution.md).
Bulk requests and installed Kubernetes actors remain unqualified.

Native bulk-site creation is now implemented through a bounded guarded primitive
which reuses singular validation, payload construction and existing transport.
It refuses existing divergent sites (the API skips existing objects), validates
all descendants and rechecks complete native identity evidence before its
one-use guard. Fixture race tests passed (5.630s). A real single-request
area/building/floor creation, independent complete readback, normal floor-width
update, no-op and verified cleanup passed (11.89s). See
[bulk-site evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-14/site-bulk.md).
Public manifest activation remains gated pending durable batch selection,
ownership and partial-batch/restart recovery. The three bulk resource rows are
now in progress, not complete; complete-section capability flags remain false.

Bulk-site recovery now has a source-bound compact member-selection descriptor
and pre-existing member/ancestor UUID digest, fitting the existing operation
resource envelope. Partial-result fixtures reconstruct the original batch rather
than replanning remaining drift, reject replaced anchors and verify only after
all attributes converge. Maximum selection, malformed descriptor and logical
source-change cases are tested alongside the singular manifest restart flow.
An isolated lab batch verified the retained binding and existing task-tree
observer, then completed a normal floor update, no-op and verified cleanup
(10.72s). See [binding evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-14/site-bulk-binding.md).
Actual public journal persistence/dispatch and partial-failure/restart recovery
remain pending; this is not an advertised bulk manifest capability.


### RMA retained provisioning identity

RMA parsing now carries the declared site into its action intent. Native collection
resolves the site UUID, confirms assignment and reads the existing scoped wired
provisioning record. Missing or mismatched prerequisites are refused; PROVISION in
this flow is retained state and never triggers a provisioning POST to a faulty
or unreachable device.

The mark resource now binds faulty-device UUID/canonical serial, site UUID and
provisioning-record UUID; the operation parent also records the site UUID. This
is the stable scope of marking the old device. The intended spare and volatile
device metadata remain part of fresh pre-submit snapshot checks but do not force
mark replay when the source advances to REPLACE. Native observation and retained
receipt validation compare the same stable mark resource, refusing site movement
or recreation of the provisioning record after restart.

Local fixtures cover missing assignment/site/provisioning, mismatched sites,
late site/provisioning changes, accepted-operation recovery, persisted receipt
scope and spare-independent mark identity. Low-level native helpers without a
site remain fixture primitives; parsed manifest RMA intents always supply the
site. Public compiler wiring and live qualification remain outstanding. No public
RMA deployment has relied on the previous private resource-digest shape.


### Private RMA mark inventory compiler

A private inventory compiler now assembles the existing mark executors and shared
plan completion hooks for explicitly identified devices with MARK_FOR_REPLACEMENT.
It parses the full model before observation, requires physical admission setup and
refuses REPLACE, unmarked devices mixed into the same model, or unimplemented role,
tag and other effects. Those combinations cannot partially execute marking.

The staged plan validates every target's physical/site/provisioning identity and
retained mark ownership before selecting the first write. Duplicate physical
bindings and stale/foreign marks are refused. Source and controller versions are
checked around native collection; the complete preflight runs again immediately
before submission. Recovery selects the retained operation by device/serial/site
and delegates to the exact-operation executor. Accepted observation and atomic
completion preserve the native record UUID through the plan hooks.

Local compiler/native fixtures cover one and two targets, missing admission,
unprovisioned or unowned later targets, changes to a later target before the first
POST, completion-hook assembly and unsupported model refusal. Public routing
remains closed pending complete compiled manifest-cycle qualification. Real
reservation actors, live appliance behavior, unmark cleanup and replacement
workflow execution remain outstanding.


### Bounded public RMA mark manifest cycles

Public inventory routing now sends fully parsed RMA intents to the mark compiler.
MARK_FOR_REPLACEMENT is supported for explicitly identified devices whose site
assignment and wired provisioning already exist. REPLACE, unsupported mixed
inventory effects and absent physical admission are refused before mutation.
The example is `examples/configs/catalyst-center/rma-mark-apply.yaml`.

Stateful local fixtures exercise the public reconciler/compiler, exact Prepared
reconstruction, shared dispatch implementation, Accepted/Verifying observation,
atomic native-record receipts, completion-contract evidence, simulated settlement
and restart convergence. Both one- and two-device manifests reach InSync without
additional mark POSTs. Missing task receipts remain Unknown; failed tasks remain
Accepted; a recreated native record is not adopted after settlement.

The dispatch permit, reservation claims and manager/device settlement are supplied
by fixtures. No real actor/Lease or appliance qualification is claimed. In
particular, actual maintenance handoff for a faulty/unreachable device remains
unqualified. ConfigMap-specific RMA races, mark removal/unmark/receipt retirement,
REPLACE execution and broader composition remain outstanding. This bounded public
route is not complete NetAsCode RMA parity.


### Native RMA unmark primitives

The private unmark planner maps the pinned provider's cleanup action to PUT
`/dna/intent/api/v1/device-replacement` with the native record ID and NON-FAULTY
status. It requires a serial-bearing marked/ready record, refuses selected
replacements or progressed workflows, and rechecks the complete native snapshot
before submission. Read failure or record absence never causes speculative PUT.

The cleanup operation binds the stable physical/site/provisioning scope plus the
native record UUID and creation timestamp. Accepted/Verifying observation requires
a valid completed task, the unchanged physical scope, and either NON-FAULTY on
the same record incarnation or complete native record absence, followed by fresh
snapshot validation. A missing task receipt remains an error; Unknown operations
cannot use absence to infer success. No observation performs a PUT.

Local HTTP/race fixtures cover successful nonfaulty/absent readback, pending/failed
tasks, unchanged marks, missing receipts, wrong/recreated records, started workflows
and malformed recovery bindings. This does not enable cleanup from manifest
removal or deletion. The adapter still must prove retained ownership and explicit
PrunePolicy/DeletionPolicy authorization, persist cleanup completion, settle the
reservation and safely retire mark receipts. Appliance response/readback behavior
and actual unmark execution remain unqualified; no lab mutation was performed.


### Owned RMA prune planning

Private cleanup planning now derives the selected device from the current model,
requires Apply with PrunePolicy Delete, and requires removal of its RMA block while
the device remains explicitly declared in PROVISION with a serial and site. Retain,
Report, still-marked/replacement intent, malformed RMA, whole-device removal and
CR deletion are refused by this bounded planner.

Mark and unmark planning share the current source/owner/native-receipt checks.
Cleanup can only select the retained verified native mark UUID; missing or foreign
marks cannot be adopted. The returned native PUT is guarded by fresh source/policy
and ownership checks around native reads, followed by the existing native snapshot
revalidation. Original mark receipts remain retained after submission.

Local cycle fixtures first complete a public mark and simulate settlement, remove
the RMA block with explicit Delete policy, then qualify private cleanup planning
and native dispatch. Retain, foreign records, and policy/owner changes both before
and during submission preflight refuse the PUT. This is not an admitted cleanup
journal cycle or live actor qualification. Public pruning still requires owned
cleanup completion, reservation settlement and safe receipt retirement; complete
device removal, DeletionPolicy handling and live appliance qualification remain
outstanding.

### Owned RMA cleanup recovery and completion

Historical mark authority is now validated independently of the current native
mark status. Cleanup recovery requires the retained verified mark receipt, its
native record UUID and creation interval, the same device/site/provisioning scope,
and a cleanup submission after mark verification. Missing, foreign or duplicate
receipts cannot be replaced by observing native absence.

The private owned observer derives explicit Delete prune intent from the current
model and uses the existing source/owner/exact-journal bracket around task and
native readback. The shared atomic completion writer retains a separate cleanup
receipt and leaves the original mark receipt intact. Unknown operations do not
use this completion path. No new transport, API fields or reservation protocol
were introduced.

Local fixtures extend a completed public mark through private unmark dispatch and
an explicitly prepared cleanup journal, including adapter reconstruction,
NON-FAULTY and absent native readback, missing/replaced ownership receipts and
source/owner changes during recovery. The cleanup journal and reservations are
synthetic: public cleanup dispatch, real actor coordination, settlement-aware
receipt retirement, whole-device/CR deletion and appliance qualification remain
outstanding. This does not make full RMA or NetAsCode parity complete.

### RMA cleanup executor and settlement contract

The cleanup executor now reuses `nextPreparedInventoryWrite` for exact Prepared
recovery and the owned cleanup observer/completion writer for later phases.
Both initial planning and resumed planning revalidate the original mark ownership;
submission repeats source/owner/native snapshot checks. Accepted, Verifying,
Verified and Unknown journals cannot return another cleanup write.

Local lifecycle fixtures now prepare a cleanup operation before dispatch, supply
synthetic reservation claims, submit through the shared receipt journal, recover
through the executor, persist completion, and require worker release plus manager
settlement before clearing the journal. Both original mark and cleanup receipts
survive settlement. A lost cleanup task receipt remains Unknown with no replay.
Mismatched scope/serial, missing original ownership and preexisting task evidence
refuse Prepared recovery. These tests exercise the journal/contract with fake
actors, not real device Leases. Public cleanup composition, safe receipt retirement,
whole-device/CR removal and lab execution remain pending.

### RMA mark receipt retirement after cleanup

A private retirement step now removes only the original mark receipt while
preserving the verified cleanup receipt as a tombstone. It requires current
explicit prune intent, an idle journal, matching mark/cleanup lineage and timing,
unchanged physical/site/provisioning identity, and native NON-FAULTY readback or
complete native absence. A verified cleanup receipt is mandatory: native absence
alone is not evidence of successful cleanup.

Both mark and cleanup reservation objects must already be absent through the
existing manager-owned retirement lifecycle. The adapter never deletes a
reservation or releases a Lease. Source/controller and reservation checks surround
native revalidation; the status update is conflict-checked and read back. Repeated
retirement is read-only and retains the cleanup tombstone.

The local admitted-cleanup fixture now invokes the shared manager retirement
contract after synthetic settlement, then verifies receipt retirement and
idempotency. Retained reservations, a replaced native record and missing cleanup
proof all refuse removal. These are fake-client/HTTP fixtures; public cleanup
composition, tombstone-aware convergence/reapplication, whole-device/CR deletion
and real worker/lab qualification remain pending.

### Cleanup tombstone convergence

Idle cleanup planning now recognizes a retained verified unmark receipt before
checking for a still-marked native record. The same validator is shared with
receipt retirement: original physical/site/provisioning scope, native record UUID
and creation time, owner, operation metadata and completion timing must agree.
Existing mark lineage is checked until that receipt is retired. Native NON-FAULTY
or complete absence converges without another PUT; a foreign or re-marked record
is refused rather than adopted as completion of the previous operation.

Read-only planning uses the shared source/controller/native snapshot bracket.
Tests reconstruct the executor before and after receipt retirement and verify
no-repeat convergence, including absence and foreign/re-marked state. The public
manifest cleanup router and reapplication after a new mark remain pending; this
change does not enable unqualified native mutation or claim full RMA parity.

### Public manifest-driven owned RMA cleanup

The admitted inventory route now selects cleanup when retained RMA history exists
and the current model removes all RMA blocks with explicit PrunePolicy Delete.
Every target remains declared in PROVISION with explicit serial and site, and
must have retained RMA evidence. Missing old targets, unrelated newly declared
targets, roles/tags/discovery and other mixed effects are refused before writes.
Ordinary inventory without RMA history retains its existing compiler; generic
inventory Delete pruning remains unsupported. The shared Apply metadata gate
permits this compiler-validated inventory policy without changing Report,
DeletionPolicy or other sections.

Mark and cleanup share one multi-target preflight/selection executor, retaining
physical/site/provisioning bindings and checking inactive targets before dispatch.
Cleanup uses the shared Prepared/submission/recovery/completion/settlement flow.
Public lifecycle fixtures cover removal of the RMA field, restart, lost cleanup
receipts, completion, reservation settlement and no-repeat convergence. Synthetic
reservation claims still stand in for real manager/device actors. The cleanup
example updates the original NetworkControllerConfig UID; it is not a standalone
way to adopt foreign native marks.

Automatic scheduling of original mark-receipt retirement, new-mark reapplication,
mixed mark/cleanup and other inventory effects, whole-device/CR deletion, multi-
target cleanup lifecycle qualification, and live worker/appliance qualification
remain pending. The private retirement primitive remains separately tested.

### Automatic cleanup ownership finalization

The cleanup plan now opts into a finalization hook after every native effect has
converged. The hook validates all targets and invokes the existing owned mark
receipt retirement for each cleanup target. Other plans leave the hook unset and
keep their existing behavior. This is controller-status bookkeeping only; it does
not submit a native request or delete/release a reservation.

Reconciliation reports Waiting/ApplyFinalizationPending while either reservation
object still exists, including after an acknowledged DELETE held by another
finalizer. The manager's existing retirement loop depends on settlement and the
cleared journal, not on the config being InSync. Once the rows disappear, the
obsolete mark receipt is removed automatically, the verified cleanup tombstone
remains, and the public reconciler reports InSync.

The public lifecycle fixture now tests automatic finalization, retained-reservation
waiting, another finalizer holding a deleted reservation, and repeated convergence.
Manager/device settlement remains simulated; real actor/Lease and appliance
qualification are still required. New-mark reapplication, multi-target cleanup
lifecycle qualification, mixed effects and full RMA replacement remain pending.

### Multi-target public cleanup qualification

The shared public lifecycle fixture now marks two explicitly identified devices,
removes both RMA blocks, and executes cleanup sequentially through independent
operation receipts and synthetic reservations. Both tasks complete and settle
before automatic ownership finalization; repeated reconciliation retains only
the two cleanup tombstones and publishes InSync without additional PUTs.

Failure fixtures lose the second cleanup receipt or report a failed second task.
The completed first target is not replayed, the second journal remains fenced
(Unknown or Accepted respectively), and original mark ownership is retained.
Foreign native ownership on the second target blocks the first request, and a
second-target change between planning and submission is refused by fresh
all-target preflight. These fixtures qualify controller/journal composition only:
real device actors, Leases and appliance behavior remain unqualified.

### Fresh-record mark/cleanup reapplication

An explicit later MARK_FOR_REPLACEMENT model can now retire a completed cleanup
tombstone before starting a new cycle. Original mark ownership must already be
retired, the old cleanup reservation must be absent, and a complete fresh native
snapshot must contain no replacement record. The current model, physical/site/
provisioning scope, owner and verified cleanup evidence are revalidated around
the status CAS. This shares reservation-absence checks and status retirement/
readback with cleanup finalization.

Successful bookkeeping returns ApplyProgressing without a native write. The next
reconciliation freshly prepares and admits the new mark. A public lifecycle
fixture completes two mark/cleanup cycles against independently observed native
record UUIDs, checks that a retained old reservation blocks tombstone retirement,
and verifies that the second cleanup cannot reuse the first receipt. Native
mutation counts remain exactly two marks and two cleanups.

This supports reapplication only after native record disappearance. Re-marking a
retained NON-FAULTY record remains refused pending appliance qualification of its
UUID/creation-time semantics. Fake-client generation increments model real API
server revisions; reservation actors remain simulated. Mixed effects, complete
RMA replacement and live qualification remain pending.

### Mixed owned mark and cleanup composition

The retained-history inventory compiler now accepts per-device MARK_FOR_REPLACEMENT
alongside removal of owned RMA marks in the same model. Removal still requires
PrunePolicy Delete and an explicitly declared, already provisioned serial/site.
A new marked target need not have a previous receipt, but its existing native
state is checked by the mark executor; it cannot adopt a foreign mark. Every
previously owned RMA serial must remain declared, and REPLACE or unrelated
inventory effects still fail whole-plan validation.

All targets share the existing RMA preflight, binding, journal and completion
hooks. Finalization visits only cleanup entries, preserving receipts for retained
or newly created marks. Public fixtures qualify cleaning one target while keeping
another marked, and cleaning two owned targets while adding a third mark. They
converge through independent task receipts and synthetic reservations without
replaying earlier effects. Real actor/Lease and lab qualification remain pending.

### Owned pre-workflow replacement readiness

The pinned provider only starts the replacement workflow and performs no
completion readback ([provider v0.6.1](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/resource_catalystcenter_device_replacement_workflow.go)).
The [2.3.7.6 inventory API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/return-list-of-replacement-devices-with-replacement-details/)
provides readiness task IDs, workflow identity and failure-step evidence. CVK now
preserves the documented `workflowFailedStep` field and refuses that evidence in
mark/cleanup success paths instead of silently discarding it.

A private read-only owned readiness observer now binds explicit REPLACE intent to
its retained mark receipt, native record UUID/creation interval, provisioned old
device/site and a distinct known replacement inventory serial. It requires the
legacy READY-FOR-REPLACEMENT state, no existing workflow/replacement/failure, and
successful referenced readiness tasks when present. Both physical identities are
returned using the existing canonical binding helper, with source/controller and
native snapshot revalidation. It does not acquire admission or POST a workflow.

Local tests cover foreign/missing ownership, absent/aliased spares, record/site
changes, failed/pending readiness tasks and late source/owner/spare changes.
PnP-only replacements, newer API status spelling, dual-device reservation and
identity handoff, durable workflow receipt/completion/recovery and public REPLACE
execution remain pending. No lab mutation or qualification was performed.


### Replacement participants use shared managed identity binding

The private replacement readiness observer now resolves both native participants
through the same complete-footprint CiscoDevice/Node binder used by fabric
coordination. The helper has a configuration-wide name; its existing fabric
behavior is retained. Canonical group targets preserve native UUIDs, physical
serials and Kubernetes object UIDs. Repeated native and Kubernetes observations
reject changes before returning the evidence. Tests cover missing participants,
cross-namespace serial aliases, mismatched Node identity and late native/Node
changes. This creates no journal, reservation, Lease or replacement workflow;
group admission, execution, completion and identity handoff remain pending.

### LAN automation link model and physical identity groundwork

The pinned NetAsCode link stripe now has a bounded parser for explicit ADD_LINK
and DELETE_LINK actions, primary/secondary IPv4 endpoints, interfaces and pool
names. Adds require an explicit pool; deletes may omit it. Unknown fields,
unsupported companion sections, missing fields, duplicate names and conflicting
port use are rejected as a whole model. This parser does not resolve upstream
defaults, interface abbreviations or native port identity.

The payload builder follows the [pinned provider v0.6.1 mapping](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/model_catalystcenter_lan_automation_link.go):
secondary fields become destination fields under linkUpdate. The [resource implementation](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/resource_catalystcenter_lan_automation_link.go)
uses PUT with LINK_ADD or LINK_DELETE in the feature query. The builder performs
no request. Endpoint binding reuses existing IP selectors and canonical native
UUID/serial checks, rejecting missing devices, IP/serial aliases and AP targets.

Local fixtures cover both action mappings, field validation, ordering, conflicts
and physical binding. Native interface/link/pool dependency readers, complete
physical admission, durable task and independent completion evidence, public
Report/Apply composition and lab qualification remain pending. No link or LAN
automation session has been changed in the lab.


### LAN link native interface and endpoint evidence

A device-scoped interface reader now uses the shared authenticated transport and
list decoder with the [documented 2.3.7.6 endpoint](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/get-interface-info-by-id/).
No undocumented pagination arguments are added. Only HTTP 200 array responses
are accepted; null, partial/no-content, duplicate identities/names/indices and
foreign-device rows are rejected. Native physical ports must match the exact
requested name; virtual or mapped ports and guessed abbreviations do not bind.
Unknown operational status remains observation, not successful link evidence.

Endpoint snapshots bind both port UUIDs to the native device UUIDs/canonical
serials and preserve primary/secondary direction independently of inventory
sort order. Revalidation repeats native device and interface reads, rejecting
replaced hardware/ports, changed observed configuration and disappearing ports.
HTTP race fixtures cover those transitions and malformed inventory responses.
This is endpoint evidence only: adjacency, free-port eligibility, pool scope,
LAN session readiness, mutation ownership and physical admission are not inferred.
Public Report/Apply, execution/recovery and live qualification remain pending.


### LAN automation session inventory

The native session status reader now reuses authenticated transport and bounded
pagination with the documented maximum of 10 sessions per page. It validates
session IDs, site paths, seed addresses, primary ports, pools and discovered
physical serial/address evidence. Duplicate pages, ambiguous dependency entries,
missing required arrays, null and partial/no-content responses are rejected.
Known set fields are sorted for stable subsequent comparisons. Historical
sessions may share devices; only duplicate serials within one session are rejected.

The [2.3.7.6 session API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/lan-automation-status/)
describes status as text and action as START/STOP; it does not supply a terminal
success enumeration. CVK preserves unknown native actions and state text and does
not interpret STOP as completed processing. Creation time is retained without
assuming an undocumented timestamp format. These observations are not ownership
receipts or permission to start, stop or change a link.

Local HTTP race fixtures verify multi-page completeness, repeated/oversized page
refusal, dependency validation and preservation of unknown status. Start/stop
model execution, projected secrets, dynamic physical footprint coordination,
owned recovery, independently qualified completion, public composition and lab
validation remain pending. No session was created or stopped in the lab.


### LAN session model and native start payload

The pinned module's session fields now have strict model validation and native
one-session array payload mapping. This covers primary/secondary seed addresses,
ports, both pool roles, optional multicast/BGP flags, hostname prefix, discovery
level and timeout, and per-device serial/hostname/site/address intent. Explicit
false values are preserved; omitted discovery depth uses the pinned provider's
value of 2. Invalid ranges, duplicate names/seeds/serials, conflicting device
addresses and non-descendant declared sites are rejected. Actual site type and
existence still require dependency resolution.

Native mapping follows the [provider v0.6.1 model](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/model_catalystcenter_lan_automation.go),
including its ManagmentIPAddress spelling. The private parser accepts START;
STOP and mixed session/link composition remain unsupported rather than silently
ignored. Unversioned projected passwords can be represented in the payload, but
public credential execution is not enabled. Versioned destinations are derived
relative to the managed section and fixture-tested using the existing Secret
injector. Inline credentials are rejected, ordinary intent formatting is redacted,
and version/name/status metadata is excluded from the native request. Ephemeral
payloads must not be persisted as receipts.

Local race tests cover mapping, shared credential injection, missing projections,
redaction, invalid ranges/types, duplicate intent and out-of-scope fields. No POST
is exposed or sent by these builders. Full dependency/physical admission,
credential receipt integration, owned start/stop recovery, completion observation,
public composition and live qualification remain pending.


### LAN session prerequisite identity snapshots

Session dependencies now reuse complete site/device readers, exact physical-port
binding and the existing IPAM allocation graph validator. A snapshot identifies
the session site, declared deployable discovery sites, canonical seed serials,
primary ports and each named LAN reservation's actual owner. Reservation and
parent-pool evidence use the existing IPAM dependency digest. No new credential
store, transport or device selector was introduced; password bytes are excluded
from the snapshot.

A fresh snapshot must match before proceeding. HTTP fixtures cover site, seed,
port, reservation, parent-pool and pool-owner changes; missing prerequisites and
non-LAN pools are rejected. Reordered inventories remain equivalent. Pool owner
binding deliberately does not infer version-specific visibility, shared-pool
eligibility or available capacity. See Cisco's [LAN pool planning guidance](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/cloud-systems-management/network-automation-and-management/catalyst-center/tech_notes/cisco-catalyst-center-sda-lan-automation-deployment-guide/planning-lan-automation/r_ip_pool_planning.html).

This is read-only prerequisite evidence, not a native start or physical grant.
Seed assignment/readiness, pool eligibility/capacity, PnP discovery identities,
dynamic mutation footprint, owned start/stop recovery, public composition and
live qualification remain pending.


### PnP identity evidence for LAN discovery

The PnP inventory reader adapts the native bare JSON array and zero-based offset
to the existing pagination guards. The [2.3.7.6 device-list schema](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/device-onboarding-pnp-get-device-list/)
and [pinned provider identity mapping](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/model_catalystcenter_pnp_device.go)
provide the typed record shape; the [official Cisco Ansible example](https://github.com/cisco-en-programmability/dnacenter-ansible/blob/main/plugins/modules/pnp_device_info.py)
uses offset zero. Appliance pagination still requires live qualification.

Only device, stack member, site and workflow identity/state fields are retained.
Native AAA credentials, HTTP headers, CLI output and day-zero configuration are
excluded before results are passed onward. Duplicate/repeating IDs, canonical
serial aliases across records, conflicting site identities, malformed arrays and
partial responses are rejected. Unknown state values do not imply readiness.

A private discovery binder requires explicit known PnP serials, includes complete
stack membership, and rejects partial stacks or targets already in network
inventory. This evidence does not authenticate a device or prevent unrelated
DHCP-discovered devices from being affected. Native PnP registration/claim,
readiness, dynamic physical fencing, version-specific LAN discovery enforcement,
owned execution/recovery and live qualification remain pending. Local HTTP and
binding fixtures cover pagination, sensitive-field exclusion and these identity
conflicts; no PnP claim/reset or LAN start has been sent.


### PnP registration and claim model mapping

A private PNP-only inventory parser now retains registration and claim intent
without sending either operation. It reuses ordinary inventory name/site/FQDN/IP
validation through a validated projection. All declared stack serials are
canonicalized for conflict checks while wire spelling/order remain intact; the
first serial identifies registration, as in the pinned module. Unsupported
companion effects fail whole-model validation instead of being discarded.

Registration mapping covers hostname, PID, first serial and stack indication.
The claim builder requires resolved native references and maps pinned defaults,
explicit image-skip values, RF profile, onboarding-template variables and stack
top/cabling. Stack empty image/config references follow the pinned provider.
Image names and template names remain unresolved intent until dependency readers
bind them; missing or unrequested resolved IDs are refused. Ordinary formatting
of template-bearing intent is redacted. Template credential projection and owned
receipt handling are not yet integrated, and payloads remain ephemeral.

Fixtures cover single/stack registration, default/stack/AP claims, explicit false,
config parameter mapping, serial conflicts, undeclared top-of-stack, unresolved
references and isolation from ordinary inventory parsing. Native create/claim,
existing-record adoption policy, prerequisites, physical admission, durable
ownership/recovery, completion/readback and live qualification remain pending.


### Private PnP registration and UUID readback

A native registration primitive now checks every declared serial against complete
PnP and network inventories, including stack-member aliases. It repeats absence
checks immediately before POST, using the existing authenticated no-replay
transport. A plan is one-use in memory; this is not a durable retry guarantee.
The [native Add Device response](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/device-onboarding-pnp-add-device/)
must be HTTP 200 with a created UUID. Any returned device information must match
the expected registration identity. Independent readback requires that UUID and
matching serial/PID/hostname/stack indication; a foreign UUID is not adopted.

HTTP fixtures cover existing/late records, network stack aliases, malformed or
lost responses, async responses, authentication errors, conflict responses,
missing readback and replaced UUIDs. No conflict-to-PUT fallback is implemented.
Registration completion is not claim completion, full stack readiness or device
authentication.

The primitive is intentionally not adapted to the existing submitCompleted hook:
that hook cannot retain a newly created native identity. Public execution still
needs a durable preparation/created-ID receipt transition, physical admission,
source/owner binding and recovery. No registration or claim was sent to the lab.


### Durable synchronous-created resource receipt

The shared configuration journal now has an optional CreatedResourceID response
field and a mutually exclusive submitCreated callback for synchronous creation.
Existing task and completed-response callbacks retain their paths. The new path
requires Create with no existing target, physical serial, dependency versions or
credential versions. A valid native UUID is written atomically with Verifying;
status readback detects a server schema that strips the receipt. Only rejected
Kubernetes writes are retried, never the native create request.

The optional field is preserved in active and retained-operation CRD schemas in
both source and Helm copies. Empty fields remain omitted from legacy serialized
operations. Single-device and group reservation digests reject populated created
receipts, preventing reuse as physical completion evidence. Schema-pruning,
restart, conflict, foreign-operation, lost-response and callback exclusivity
fixtures exercise the boundary.

The private PnP registration plan now bridges into this journal path and verifies
from a serialized operation plus current intent, without an in-memory response
closure. It requires the recorded native UUID and matching registration resource
hash; missing or changed identities remain fenced. Native registration fixtures
cover recovery after restart and prevent a second POST. Public composition,
atomic finalized ownership receipts, claim execution/physical admission and lab
qualification remain pending. The updated CRD must be installed before enabling
any future public consumer; no cluster schema or lab device was changed here.


### PnP finalized registration ownership

The private PnP registration bridge now finalizes through the existing atomic
inventory action-receipt writer. It validates that the intent remains declared
in the current manifest, brackets native UUID readback with source, section-owner
and exact-journal checks, and retains a `pnp-record:<UUID>` receipt together with
Verified. Clearing the active journal preserves that receipt. Generic Verified
advancement cannot bypass this path; missing, duplicated, altered or
schema-pruned receipts prevent journal release. Registration still does not
prove claim completion or device readiness.

HTTP and Kubernetes fixtures cover successful finalization, foreign ownership,
source changes before and during readback, undeclared intent, retained identity
and invalid completion receipts. LAN discovery scope now also checks each member
of comma-separated network-inventory stacks before treating hardware as new.
Public PnP composition, claim admission/execution and live qualification remain
pending. No lab operation or CRD deployment was performed in this increment.


### Reuse finalized PnP registration in later stages

A private registration-stage planner now resolves finalized ownership before
planning a native create. It reuses the existing action receipt, source snapshot
checks and native registration verifier. A matching record without a receipt is
not adopted. A retained record that disappears or changes UUID/identity is not
recreated. Duplicate receipts or section owners, a foreign configuration UID,
future configuration generations, changed controller generations and concurrent
operations prevent reuse. Source and controller status are rechecked after
native observation.

Later revisions of the same manifest can change claim settings while preserving
the original registration receipt, provided the registration payload identity
still matches. The returned UUID is evidence for a later stage, not permission
to claim or provision. Fixtures cover creation planning, finalized reuse,
manifest revision, missing/pruned/foreign receipts, missing/replaced native
records and source/owner changes during readback. Public PnP orchestration,
physical claim admission and lab qualification remain pending.


### PnP claim dependency resolution

Private claim dependency resolution now uses existing site, image, RF-profile
and template readers. It binds the exact site path and UUID, follows explicit
image-ID precedence over name, refuses ambiguous image names, and resolves
onboarding template references through the existing NetAsCode template index.
Qualified `project#template` references are now accepted by the PnP parser;
malformed or ambiguous references are refused.

The committed-template lookup is shared with Day-N deployment, while the Day-N
entry point retains its onboarding prohibition. PnP retains the base template
UUID used by the pinned module and the latest committed version/body as
transient preflight evidence. Supplied parameters are validated against that
committed definition. Template content is not persisted or printed. Dependency
revalidation rejects site/image/RF/template replacement and committed version or
content changes. HTTP fixtures also exercise missing references, draft-only and
composite templates, external references, parameter errors and image-name alias
compatibility.

This is dependency evidence, not device readiness, image compatibility or claim
admission. Physical target checks, projected template credentials, native claim
execution/receipts, public orchestration and lab qualification remain pending.
No lab changes were made in this increment.


### PnP claim physical target binding

Claim preflight now shares complete physical-set resolution with LAN discovery.
Every declared serial must be observed on the single owned registration UUID;
partial stacks, split records, foreign UUIDs, duplicate serial aliases, changed
primary serial/PID/hostname and members already in network inventory are refused.
Native observations retain only the existing safe PnP projection. The adapter
requires a finalized registration receipt, repeats native footprint observations,
and rechecks the manifest and controller status before returning evidence.
Local fixtures cover single and stacked targets, each rejection case, and a
state change between the repeated observations. Existing LAN fixtures exercise
the shared resolver after extraction.

The native [site-claim API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-5/claim-a-device-to-a-site/)
documents a string response rather than a task receipt. The pinned provider
stores the device ID without an independent completion read. CVK must not invent
a task ID or use this acknowledgement as provisioning completion. Physical
admission, durable claim acknowledgement/recovery, readiness and independent
onboarding completion remain pending; this preflight does not submit a claim,
reserve hardware or reset a device. No live lab mutation was performed.


### Private native PnP site-claim submission

A private site-claim planner now freezes the resolved payload, validates target
and dependency snapshots, and repeats both checks immediately before one native
POST through the existing authenticated no-replay transport. The resource key
contains only nonsecret resolved identities; template variables are neither
journaled nor hashed into it. Caller changes to nested template inputs cannot
alter an already planned request. Known incomplete AP, Sensor and WLC requests
are refused before transport.

Only the documented HTTP 200 string-response shape yields an observed-response
record. Free-form response text is discarded. This record contains the requested
device/site IDs, not a native task or workflow ID, and does not prove claim
acceptance or provisioning completion. Lost, malformed, asynchronous, conflict
and authentication responses are not retried. Local HTTP fixtures cover these
cases, late native/dependency changes and frozen payloads. The in-memory plan is
one-use; this is not durable restart protection.

This primitive intentionally has no configurationWrite conversion or public
route. Physical admission, readiness/API-version qualification, projected
credentials, durable acknowledgement and independent completion recovery must
be composed before public dispatch. No claim was submitted to the lab.


### PnP claim write-ahead journal bridge

A private single-target adapter bridge now requires owned registration and a
stable complete physical target, then submits through the existing physical
admission and journal sequence. It preserves the PnP UUID, canonical serial and
site UUID in Prepared, acquires/checks the supplied dispatch permit, persists
Submitting before native POST, and records an observed response as Verifying.
Lost or invalid responses remain Unknown. Reconstructing a worker cannot replay
an active claim. Stack targets and missing admission are refused before a claim
journal or native mutation is created.

No new journal store or task identifier is introduced. PnP acknowledgement
persistence now reads back the full operation to detect schema pruning; generic
Verified advancement and journal release are explicitly refused for site claims
until independent completion recovery is implemented. Fixtures inject the
existing narrow permit interface to verify sequencing, denied permits, lost/auth
responses, restart and pruned acknowledgement identity. They do not demonstrate
real PnP admission or hardware lease acquisition.

Public runtime dispatch, actual PnP identity admission, stack/group coordination,
readiness/version qualification, projected credentials, independent completion
and live qualification remain pending. No lab operation was performed.


### Independent PnP-to-network inventory observations

Post-claim observation now joins the original PnP UUID to the resulting network
inventory UUID by the complete canonical serial set. The two UUIDs are retained
separately. Partial/split stacks, extra or duplicate members, duplicate physical
aliases and contradictory PnP/site identities are refused. The site path must
still resolve to the exact submitted site UUID, and assignment uses the shared
assigned-to-site reader with the resulting network UUID.

Missing network inventory and missing assignment are represented as pending
observations. Repeated observations detect network UUID, software, PnP state and
assignment changes; stack-member ordering and case are normalized. HTTP and
serial-set fixtures cover these boundaries without performing mutations.

This evidence is deliberately not a completion boolean. It does not prove the
native workflow, requested image or onboarding template completed, and it cannot
release the active claim journal. Owned operation binding, native completion
semantics and live qualification remain pending. No lab operation was performed.


### Owned PnP recovery observations

The adapter now binds post-claim inventory observations to the exact active
operation and current source through the existing shared inventory observation
wrapper. A common retained-registration lookup serves both idle registration
reuse and active claim recovery; it verifies section ownership, configuration
identity, controller generation and the durable created UUID receipt.

Recovery requires the declared single-device serial to match the journal and
checks the expected PnP/site IDs. It repeats native observations and rejects
source, owner, operation or inventory changes. Both Verifying and Unknown can be
observed, allowing inspection after a lost response without resubmission or a
phase transition. Local fixtures exercise missing registration ownership,
foreign owners, pruned serials, replacement operations and changes during reads.

This observer neither records Verified nor releases reservations. Native
workflow/image/template completion semantics, actual PnP admission, group
support, public dispatch and live qualification remain pending. No lab operation
was performed in this increment.


### Durable PnP claim dependency version binding

The claim resource key now binds a versioned nonsecret identity projection:
PnP/site/image IDs, image version, complete serial set, template base/project ID,
committed template version UUID and number, and RF-profile UUID. Template content,
comments, parameter values and credentials are excluded; configuration generation
and source identity retain their existing responsibility for manifest binding.
Explicit image activation without observable image-version metadata is refused
before submission.

Owned recovery reconstructs this binding from native dependencies, compares it
to the persisted operation, and revalidates dependencies after the repeated
inventory reads. Fixtures cover changed image/template versions across recovery,
a change during observation, mismatched identities and secret exclusion. Older
private claim keys without the new binding cannot silently validate against it;
no public or lab claim workflow has been enabled by this change.

These dependency checks do not prove the device ran the image or template.
Independent native completion, actual PnP admission, group support, public
orchestration and lab qualification remain pending.


### PnP running-image outcome evidence

Owned recovery now returns image evidence separately from its inventory snapshot.
It distinguishes Skipped, PendingInventory, PendingReachability, PendingVersion
and Matched. An explicit requested activation requires a bound selected image
and observable image-version metadata before planning. Runtime comparison uses
the existing SWIM version matcher, including its build-suffix behavior; a device
must report Reachable before a matching version is recorded. Default image_skip
remains true as in the pinned model.

Fixtures cover missing/incorrect versions, prefix confusion, build suffixes,
unreachable devices, skipped images, unresolved activation and foreign site/PnP
identities. Owned recovery fixtures additionally check matching/pending image
results without a phase transition. Matched means only that the inventory reports
the expected version; it does not attest that this claim caused the activation,
that observations are device-fresh, or that the onboarding template completed.
Native completion, physical admission, public dispatch and lab qualification
remain pending. No lab operation was performed.


### PnP workflow metadata and configuration preview

The safe PnP reader now retains workflow image/configuration IDs, native timing,
and task state/type/sequence metadata. It rejects malformed identifiers, unsafe
numeric counters, reversed intervals and duplicate task sequences. Missing or
zero times remain unknown; the API schema does not establish timing units or
terminal-state semantics. Work-item commands/output, configuration bodies and
free-form descriptions are excluded. These fields participate in repeated
snapshot validation; a changed workflow timestamp now invalidates a planned
preview. This is observation, not proof of claim completion.

A private preview planner implements the pinned module's three-field
`site-config-preview` request through the existing transport. It excludes APs
as the module does, refuses unsupported CatalystWLC requests, requires an
observed matching PnP site, and repeats native identity/workflow/inventory checks
before its one-use POST. Only an HTTP 200 response with explicit completion/error
flags, the expected site and an optional valid task ID is accepted. Generated
configuration and native error messages are discarded. Failure flags remain
explicit even when the response also says complete. No preview result changes
the claim journal or proves device/template completion.

Local HTTP fixtures exercise request mapping, pending/failed previews, missing
metadata, native identity/workflow changes, malformed/foreign responses and
lost/authentication/conflict/async responses without replay. A closure prevents
replay within one plan only; durable owned post-claim sequencing, public dispatch
and live qualification remain pending. No lab operation was performed.

References: [pinned provider request mapping](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/model_catalystcenter_pnp_config_preview.go),
[pinned module ordering](https://github.com/netascode/terraform-catalystcenter-nac-catalystcenter/blob/v0.5.0/cc_pnp.tf),
and [Cisco preview response schema](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-4/preview-config/).


### PnP access-point floor qualification

PnP dependency resolution now requires an AccessPoint target site to be a floor.
The previous non-global-site check could accept an area or building and send an
invalid AP claim. This requirement is also rechecked through the existing
dependency snapshot immediately before submission. The existing RF-profile
lookup, physical identity checks, shared transport and one-use claim planner are
reused unchanged.

Local HTTP fixtures now exercise a complete AP claim request with a resolved
floor UUID and RF profile, plus invalid area/building/missing-floor/missing-RF
inputs and floor/RF replacement after planning. Successful HTTP acknowledgement
still does not verify onboarding. Public physical admission, durable completion
and lab AP qualification remain pending. No lab mutation was performed.

The floor requirement is also enforced by Cisco's
[PnP workflow manager](https://github.com/cisco-en-programmability/dnacenter-ansible/blob/main/plugins/modules/pnp_workflow_manager.py).
The native preview API remains a generation POST; a read/recovery contract must
be qualified before preview generation can be wired into durable post-claim
execution. No task or completion evidence is fabricated for that missing step.


### Pending fabric-event inventory and request mapping

The previously untouched `catalystcenter_apply_pending_fabric_events` resource
now has a private native reader and explicit single-event apply payload mapping.
The reader uses the existing 500-record pager with a mandatory fabric UUID
filter, requires HTTP 200 and rejects missing/foreign/duplicate event identity,
repeated pages and incomplete responses. Only event/fabric IDs are retained;
free-form native details are discarded. Stable ordering avoids list-order drift.
Empty inventory is an empty queue, never an implicit apply-all request.

Local HTTP fixtures cover a 501-event two-page response, empty inventory, bad
scope, duplicates, repeated pages, partial/malformed responses and exact native
payload shape. No native apply is enabled yet. NetAsCode's `fabric_sites[].reconfigure`
composition, prerequisite ownership, physical group admission, journaled native
submission/completion/recovery and lab qualification remain pending.

References: [pinned provider](https://github.com/CiscoDevNet/terraform-provider-catalystcenter/blob/v0.6.1/internal/provider/resource_catalystcenter_apply_pending_fabric_events.go)
and [Cisco pending-event schema](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/dna-center/get-pending-fabric-events/).


### Pending fabric-event model composition and native binding

A private parser now extracts strict boolean `fabric_sites[].reconfigure`
intent while delegating the remaining site/zone/gateway/multicast model to the
existing parsers. Absent/false flags produce no event action; invalid flags,
injected event IDs, duplicate sites and unsupported nested effects remain
errors. The input model is not mutated. Public parsers retain their existing
rejection until an executor can own this effect.

Native event snapshots reuse the existing fabric-site observer, require the
parent fabric site's desired authentication/pubsub state to be converged, and
bind both site and fabric UUIDs before querying events. Repeated observation
detects site/fabric replacement, event replacement and queue additions. Local
fixtures verify these transitions as well as empty queues and missing/drifted
parents. This is prerequisite evidence only: resource ownership, physical group
admission, native apply/task verification, durable recovery, public dispatch
and lab qualification remain pending. No lab operation was performed.


### Pending fabric-event native submission

A private apply planner now requires an explicitly selected native event UUID,
binds the resource to its site path/site UUID/fabric UUID/event UUID, and repeats
the entire native snapshot immediately before a one-use POST. It uses the shared
transport and mutation no-replay policy. Only HTTP 200 with a valid task UUID is
accepted; the response URL is discarded so subsequent tracking uses CVK's
configured task endpoint. An acknowledgement does not prove device convergence.

Local fixtures cover successful request mapping, missing events, queue additions,
fabric replacement, lost/malformed responses, authentication/conflict/async
responses and second-call refusal. The private primitive cannot be passed as a
generic configurationWrite: complete physical target admission and durable
journal ownership must be added before public execution. Independent completion,
restart recovery and live qualification remain pending. No lab operation occurred.

Native response contract: [Cisco apply pending fabric events](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/apply-pending-fabric-events/).


### Pending fabric-event task and queue observation

Private recovery observation now binds a submitted event's resource, site UUID,
fabric UUID, event UUID, task UUID and submission time before reading native
state. It reuses configurationTaskComplete for task identity/time correlation
and sanitized failures, then repeats the site/event snapshot. Task completion
and selected-event presence are returned separately: event disappearance alone
cannot mean success, and unrelated pending events are not substituted for the
selected event.

Local fixtures cover completed/running/failed tasks, stale and foreign task
receipts, missing/mismatched identity, unrelated events, and event/site changes
during observation. This helper does not create another durable store, mutate
status, grant ownership, or release reservations. Durable journal integration,
physical group admission, independent device convergence, public execution and
live qualification remain pending. No lab operation was performed.


### Pending fabric-event physical footprint observation

The native event snapshot now includes complete fabric membership and bound
network-inventory devices using the existing fabricDeviceMemberships and
bindFabricMutationTargets helpers. Role eligibility does not filter the mutation
footprint. Submission and recovery revalidation therefore also detect member
removal, role changes and physical serial replacement.

Local fixtures cover mixed edge/border membership, missing inventory, serial
aliases and late membership/role/serial changes; existing submission/recovery
fixtures now include these dependencies. This is native identity evidence only.
Managed CiscoDevice/Node binding, group reservations, resource ownership, durable
recovery/public execution and device/lab qualification remain pending. Existing
shared resolver limitations, including stack identity handling, are not claimed
as closed by this addition. No lab operation was performed.


### Pending fabric-event managed target binding

A private target observer now passes the complete native footprint through
resolveConfigurationManagedBindings and configurationGroupTargets. Native
inventory IDs, canonical physical identities, CiscoDevice UIDs and Node UIDs
therefore use the same rules and immutable target contract as the other
configuration flows. It repeats native and Kubernetes observations and requires
unchanged bindings; errors return no partial group.

HTTP/Kubernetes fixtures cover a complete two-device group, unmanaged members,
missing Nodes, late cross-namespace aliases, replaced Nodes and changed native
serials. These observations do not acquire reservations, grant a dispatch permit
or establish resource ownership. Group admission, durable owned journal/recovery,
device convergence, public execution and live qualification remain pending.
No lab operation was performed.


### Pending fabric-event group journal identity reconstruction

Recovery can now reconstruct native event observation inputs from the existing
NetworkControllerConfigurationOperation group record. It validates the shared
group digest, allowed recovery phase, task UUID/submission time, selected event
and fabric UUID, resource-bound site identity and exact refreshed managed target
set. No new journal format or durable store was introduced.

Serialized round-trip fixtures cover Accepted/Verifying/Unknown, while pruned
group/task metadata, changed source/group/event/fabric identity, replaced Nodes,
missing members, changed serials and future submission times are refused. This
is recovery input validation, not a status transition or dispatch permit.
Section ownership, group admission/lifecycle wiring, device convergence, public
execution and lab qualification remain pending. No lab operation was performed.


### Pending fabric-event owned recovery composition

The existing read-only inventory ownership/source/journal bracket is now shared
with fabric observations. Its inventory wrapper retains the same contract, and
the common helper additionally requires the operation section to match the
requested section. No journal transition or admission behavior was broadened.

A private pending-event observer checks explicit declared reconfigure intent,
resolves the native/managed group, reconstructs the retained operation's receipt,
observes task/event evidence and repeats native/managed reads under that bracket.
The current bounded declaration parser accepts fabric_sites composition only;
other model sections/effects remain rejected rather than discarded.

Declaration and ownership-bracket fixtures cover disabled/foreign intent, unknown
effects, source projection, missing/foreign owners, wrong operations and late
source/status changes. Full owned native recovery fixtures, prerequisite resource
ownership, group admission/lifecycle wiring, device convergence, public execution
and live qualification remain pending. No lab operation was performed.


### Composed pending fabric-event recovery fixtures

The private owned recovery path is now exercised as a composed HTTP/Kubernetes
fixture using a retained group journal, declared reconfigure manifest, managed
CiscoDevice/Node identity, fabric membership and native task/event responses.
A reconstructed adapter reads the persisted operation rather than relying on a
submission closure. Accepted and Unknown operations return consistent evidence;
running tasks and still-pending events remain distinct outcomes.

Failed tasks, foreign owners, altered group identities and owner/source/Node
changes during task observation are rejected. Every scenario verifies that the
operation record remains unchanged and native calls are GET-only. These are
local recovery fixtures, not group-dispatch or lab qualification. Prerequisite
ownership, reservation lifecycle, device convergence, public execution and live
qualification remain pending.


### Atomic pending fabric-event group preparation

The shared preparation helper now accepts a bounded pending-fabric-event group
identity and persists it with Prepared in one controller status CAS. It uses
WithGroupIdentity and verifies the exact persisted operation before returning.
Empty groups, missing group identity for the reserved event resource, or a group
attached to an unrelated resource are refused. Existing nongroup callers retain
their existing path.

The reserved pending-event resource key also prevents a schema-pruned group
record from falling through legacy start/advance/finish or reconciler recovery.
Fixtures cover atomic persistence, pruning detection, target-copy isolation and
legacy bypass refusal. The composed owned recovery fixture now starts through
this atomic preparation path. This does not acquire reservations or enable group
dispatch. Fabric ownership remains the existing exclusive section contract; no
parallel per-site ownership ledger was introduced.

Group admission, remaining lifecycle wiring, device convergence, public
execution and live qualification remain pending. No lab operation was performed.


### Manifest-bound pending fabric-event preparation

A private adapter preparation path now requires explicit declared reconfigure
intent, current source identity and an empty operation slot. It discovers the
selected native event and the complete managed group, rechecks source/controller
identity, and calls the existing atomic group preparation helper. Callers cannot
supply their own target set through this product-specific path.

HTTP/Kubernetes fixtures verify valid Prepared identity and reject disabled
intent, absent events, unmanaged members, foreign section ownership, source or
controller changes during discovery and repeated preparation. No native POST or
reservation creation occurs during this step. Group admission, remaining
execution/recovery lifecycle wiring, public dispatch and live qualification
remain pending.


### Prepared pending-event product revalidation

A read-only adapter preflight now validates the exact Prepared group operation
under the shared source/owner/journal bracket. It repeats declared reconfigure
intent, native site/fabric/event lookup and managed-target binding, then compares
the event resource and canonical target set with the retained operation.

Composed fixtures prepare an operation and then remove its event, replace a Node,
change section ownership/source generation, prune group identity or change the
operation phase. Each is refused before group admission; the valid case remains
Prepared. This check grants no permit and does not create reservations. Shared
group authority, scheduling/workload guards, dispatch/lifecycle wiring, public
execution and live qualification remain pending.


### Shared group task acknowledgement

The shared group dispatch permit now records an accepted native task only after
its dispatch check succeeds. Receipt recording repeats exact operation binding,
all-member grants/leases and the caller's authorization check, then performs one
status update and verifies the retained task through exact readback. Copies
share consumption state and cannot restore dispatch authority.

Fixtures cover recording before authorization, failed dispatch checks, changed
operations, denied authority, revoked or expired grants, paused controllers,
malformed task IDs, pruned writes and lost write responses. A lost response may
have persisted Accepted; recovery must inspect the journal rather than resubmit.
This shared primitive does not issue native requests or release reservations.
Pending-event dispatch integration, public group runtime and live qualification
remain pending. No lab mutation was performed.


### Pending-event group dispatch bridge

The private adapter dispatch path now consumes a real shared group submission
permit bound to the exact controller and Prepared operation. Native planning
retains the selected event identity; after the Submitting transition, the bridge
repeats source/owner/journal and native/managed group evidence, then consumes the
final group authority check immediately before the native POST. A successful
native response is recorded through that same permit's task receipt method.
Receipt failure returns both the known task and an error, preserving recovery
rather than authorizing another request or releasing reservations.

Native primitive fixtures now reject absent/denied dispatch authorization and
prevent replay. Shared permit fixtures reject foreign controller, namespace,
operation and group identities before journal transition. Existing preparation,
native submission and shared receipt fixtures pass. Public group reconciliation and live qualification
remain pending; this is not a claim of end-to-end deployment support.


### Composed pending-event dispatch qualification

HTTP/Kubernetes fixtures now prepare the manifest-bound operation, construct
shared group reservation candidates, retain grants and leases, claim through the
shared protocol, and invoke the adapter dispatch bridge with a real permit.
The accepted case persists the task UUID and Accepted phase after exactly one
POST. Lost native responses and revoked grants after POST retain Submitting;
a known task is returned alongside receipt failure. Re-entry cannot replay.
