### Pending-event verification transition

A shared recovery transition now moves Accepted or task-bearing Unknown group
operations into Verifying after a mandatory product observation/authorization
callback. It binds the exact journal, exclusive section owner, all reservation
identities and claims, repeats reads around observation, and verifies the status
write. Missing tasks, partial claims, released members and late changes fail
without completion receipts or reservation release. Lease expiry alone does not
prevent read-only outcome observation.

The private pending-event adapter bridge supplies the existing owned native
observer, requiring task completion and disappearance of the selected event
before entering Verifying. These are prerequisites for convergence verification,
not proof of every device's applied configuration. Cisco's
[provisioned-device listing](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-5/get-provisioned-devices/)
exposes device/site identity, not per-device convergence status. Stronger
convergence qualification and final receipt/release wiring remain pending,
as do public reconciliation and live qualification.


### Composed dispatch-to-verification recovery

The existing HTTP/Kubernetes dispatch fixture now continues through a fresh
adapter instance into owned recovery. It discovers the persisted reservation
set and verifies both Accepted and task-bearing Unknown operations can enter
Verifying after successful task observation and selected-event disappearance.
Running or failed tasks, still-pending events and denied writer authorization
refuse that transition. Every scenario checks exactly one native POST, retained
claims and Held grants, and absence of completion or manager-settlement receipts.

These fixtures exercise the private adapter/shared-contract integration, not

The bounded reader uses shared transport with HTTP 200 only, validates task IDs,
root/parent connectivity, cycles, duplicate IDs and submission-relative timing,
and refuses failed children. Unfinished children keep completion false. Native
free-form data, progress and failure text are not retained or exposed.

Fixtures cover nested trees, missing/foreign roots, orphan/cyclic branches,
missing error flags, invalid timing and HTTP partial responses. Fabric observer
fixtures confirm a successful parent cannot hide an unfinished or failed child.
SWIM's Inventory-service device matching is unchanged; its product-specific
progress text is not assumed to describe fabric application. Tree completion
remains controller execution evidence rather than per-device convergence. Public

### Fabric L2 handoff model and native dependency projection

The pinned module's two `l2_handoffs` forms now have a strict private parser:
anycast pool/L3-VN references expand across their interfaces, and non-anycast
VLAN names expand across the shared interface list. Expansion is bounded and
rejects duplicate/conflicting port mappings, unknown fields and invalid VLANs.
Internal VLAN IDs are resolved from native dependencies, not model defaults.

A scoped Layer 2 handoff inventory reader reuses shared transport/pagination and
validates HTTP status, native IDs, device/fabric scope and mapping uniqueness.
The dependency projection reuses border role/settings validation, exact physical
interface binding, existing anycast observations and L2 virtual-network objects.
It retains dependency and interface UUIDs and refuses ambiguous references or an
anycast gateway attached to a requested pure-L2 VLAN.

Local model/binding/HTTP race tests pass. These are private preparation components,
not public handoff support: inventory name-to-UUID/serial binding, complete native
dependency refresh, admitted execution, ownership, convergence/recovery, update/
delete and lab qualification remain outstanding. Public parsers continue refusing
unimplemented execution instead of silently dropping these fields.

References: [NetAsCode Layer 2 handoff model](https://netascode.cisco.com/docs/data_models/catalyst_center/fabric/layer_2_handoff/)
and [Cisco Layer 2 handoff API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-5/add-fabric-devices-layer-2-handoffs/).
The local pinned module `cc_fabric.tf` remains the field-mapping baseline.

The handoff dependency collector now combines the existing inventory selector,
