### Private L2 handoff create and readback lifecycle

The handoff create planner now uses the shared configuration write object. Matching
existing handoffs are no-ops; overlapping internal/external port VLAN mappings are
conflicts. Submission first repeats the composed dependency snapshot, then sends
the documented one-element native payload through shared authenticated transport.
Each write object is one-use, including after an error or unknown response. HTTP
200 and a task identity are required; missing receipts and unexpected acceptance
statuses never trigger a replay.

A separate readback helper requires the recorded Verifying operation/task and the
exact dependency-bound resource identity, then returns the matching native UUID
for future durable ownership publication. Its recovery baseline permits only the
expected handoff addition while retaining peer mappings and dependency identity.
The coordinator must independently verify task completion before using readback.

Local HTTP/race fixtures cover create, existing no-op, conflicts, late VLAN/handoff
changes, missing task receipt, unexpected status, failed write, repeated submit,
absent/wrong readback, changed border settings and missing recovery receipt. They
pass without a lab mutation. Public model composition, site/fabric scope binding,
physical admission, journal/ownership integration, update/delete and native
post-change convergence remain outstanding. In particular, interface state changes
caused by the handoff itself need lab qualification before broadening the strict
recovery baseline. This is not yet public resource support.


### L2 handoff declared scope and inventory intent composition

Dependency collection, create planning and readback now take the declared site
path. They resolve the complete native site hierarchy and site-to-fabric relation
on each observation, then bind the selected site UUID/path and fabric settings
into the submission and recovery digests. Supplying an unchecked native fabric
UUID is no longer the interface to these primitives. Missing sites/fabrics and
changed site or fabric associations prevent submission or recovery adoption.

A private combined parser now extracts only the pinned handoff fields and delegates
the remaining inventory and border settings to the existing strict fabric-device
parser. It preserves physical inventory selectors, provisioning intent and fabric
site paths, requires Layer 2 border support, bounds total handoffs and rejects
orphan/duplicate/unsupported fields. The original device-only parser continues to
reject handoffs rather than silently ignoring them.

Local race-enabled tests pass for combined intent parsing, retained site/serial
selectors, missing scope, pre-submit site/fabric replacement and replacement during
readback. Public multi-resource composition, native provisioning prerequisite
verification, admitted journal/ownership integration, expected post-change state,
update/delete and lab qualification remain pending. No lab mutation was made.


### L2 handoff native deployment prerequisites

The private deployment planner now reuses the existing fabric-device dependency
collector for site assignment, native provisioning-record identity, configured
device role and complete fabric membership. It requires observed border settings
and roles to match the declared device intent before planning a handoff. Their
dependency digest is retained in the handoff resource identity and rechecked before
submission and during readback. Mutable declared border settings are snapshotted
before the submit closure, which remains one-use even if a prerequisite fails.

The native lifecycle fixture now also runs through this combined deployment path.
Race-enabled tests pass for absent assignment/provisioning and a replaced
provisioning record, alongside existing scope, payload, no-op, conflict, lost
receipt and changed-state cases. Native provisioning-record existence does not
prove completion of a requested provision/reprovision task: the coordinator must
finish that stage before invoking this planner. Public multi-resource sequencing,
physical admission and journal/ownership publication, expected post-change
convergence, update/delete and lab qualification remain pending.


### L2 handoff group completion evidence

The private handoff receipt builder now requires a valid immutable shared group
journal, successful completion of the recorded native task tree, prerequisite-
bound native readback and an exact match between the current physical fabric
footprint and journal targets. It repeats native readback and rejects a replaced
handoff UUID, even when the replacement has equal configuration. The action
receipt retains the original group digest and operation fields, stores the
observed UUID in a separate logical-resource key, and does not mutate the caller's
Verifying operation. It performs no submission or Kubernetes status write.

Race-enabled local lifecycle tests pass for successful receipt construction,
running/failed child tasks, foreign physical identity, missing/corrupt group
evidence, invalid submission times/section and replacement between observations.
Existing deployment prerequisite and one-use submission tests also pass. These
are HTTP fixtures, not live qualification. Atomic ownership publication through
the shared group contract, admitted public dispatch, per-device post-change
convergence, update/delete and lab qualification are still pending. A native
controller task and configuration readback alone are not a device convergence
attestation.


### L2 handoff atomic action receipt publication

The private adapter recovery entry point now reloads and strictly parses the
manifest, matches its declared handoff, binds the exact config/controller/source
version to the Verifying journal, verifies native task/readback evidence and
publishes the action receipt through the existing shared group contract. Receipt
publication and the Verified transition are one status update. Source/controller
checks surround actor authorization; no new native submission occurs.

Extranet and handoff publication share the same source/controller persistence
guard and lifecycle fixture harness. The new fractional-second fixture exposed
a status readback mismatch: metav1.Time serializes whole seconds. The shared
adapter publication helper now copies and normalizes receipt verification time
before persistence, preserving the caller's evidence and the original journal.

Local race-enabled fixtures cover inline and ConfigMap sources, denied actors,
late source/controller changes, undeclared handoffs, mismatched operations, lost
status-write acknowledgements and restart without repeating the transition.
Missing section ownership, incomplete member sets and revoked grants are also
covered in the common harness. Actor authorization and reservations here remain
fixtures. Public dispatch, actual installed worker admission, device convergence,
update/delete and live qualification are still pending; this private publication
path alone does not enable handoff execution from a manifest.


### L2 handoff complete managed-target preparation

A private managed handoff planner now resolves the complete native prerequisite
footprint through the existing CiscoDevice/Node binding resolver and canonical
group-target contract. It binds the write's device/fabric identity and dependency
digest to that same footprint, repeats native prerequisites, then repeats managed
bindings to reject late replacement. It returns no partial plan or target set on
failure. A matching existing handoff yields no write while retaining the observed
managed-target evidence. No reservation or dispatch authority is created.

The two-device HTTP/Kubernetes fixture covers an unmanaged peer, absent peer Node,
a late cross-namespace alias, changed device/Node identity, changed native serial,
and a matching existing handoff. Native response validation remains strict,
including the Layer 2 VLAN wireless flag. Public journal preparation/dispatch,
installed actor admission, device convergence and live qualification remain
pending.


### L2 handoff durable preparation

The private adapter preparation path now selects the exact declared handoff from
the stored source snapshot, resolves the complete managed footprint, rechecks
source/controller state and atomically records Prepared plus group identity using
the existing journal. Matching native handoffs produce no write or operation.
An existing operation blocks preparation, including after an ambiguous status
write. Preparation neither creates reservations nor submits a native mutation.

The group-resource gate now recognizes dependency-bound handoff Create records
with both SHA-256 digests, while pending-event Update behavior is retained. The
handoff prefix remains reserved even when its group identity is missing/pruned:
legacy start, advance, finish, taskless synchronous completion and Apply recovery
cannot adopt such an operation.
Atomic fixture coverage includes missing/empty targets, wrong action/resource,
schema pruning, two-device source-driven preparation, undeclared intent, native
no-op, lost write acknowledgement and restart without overwriting uncertainty.
Public execution and installed group admission remain gated; preparation alone
does not qualify dispatch or prove post-change device convergence.


### L2 handoff owned pre-dispatch revalidation

The private preflight now re-observes a stored Prepared or Submitting handoff
operation through the existing owned-operation guard. It requires the current
manifest declaration, exact source/controller journal and section owner, then
replans against the complete managed footprint and compares the native resource,
parent/device IDs and canonical group targets to the immutable journal. An
existing matching mapping is not accepted as ownership evidence for unsubmitted
work. Declaration selection is shared by preparation, preflight and publication.

The source-driven fixture covers successful Prepared and Submitting observation,
changed manifest, removed owner, missing peer Node, corrupt group identity,
unknown phase and refusal to treat Submitting as Prepared. Preflight performs no
POST or journal transition and grants no reservation or dispatch permit. The
Submitting branch is for the holder of the shared one-use dispatch permit, not
for replay after restart. Public dispatch, installed actor qualification and
per-device convergence remain pending.


### L2 handoff permit-bound native dispatch

The private handoff dispatch bridge now requires the shared all-member claim
permit. It validates Prepared ownership/native evidence, binds the native plan
to that operation, and consumes the permit to persist Submitting before POST.
The native planner invokes an admission guard after its final dependency reads;
the guard rechecks the exact Submitting journal, owned source/managed footprint
and live dispatch permit immediately before the controller request. Native
submission remains one-use.

Task acceptance is retained using the existing group task-receipt writer. Failed
or ambiguous native responses leave Submitting retained. If a known task cannot
be recorded because a grant was revoked, its ID is returned with the error and
the group remains fenced. Restart cannot re-enter the Prepared dispatch path.
The composed fixture uses the shared reservation/claim/lease machinery and
simulated actor/workload authorization; it does not prove installed admission.
Tests cover successful acceptance, failed native response, revocation before
submission, revocation after POST, and no second POST on restart. Public
reconciliation, restarted task verification, device convergence and live
qualification remain pending.


### L2 handoff restart-to-verification recovery

The private recovery bridge now resumes an Accepted or Unknown operation with a
recorded task through the shared BeginGroupVerification contract. Under current
writer authorization and the existing source/owner bracket, it requires a
successful complete task tree, prerequisite-bound native mapping readback, and
repeated managed-device/Node bindings equal to the persisted group. Native
readback uses an observation copy; only the shared contract updates the durable
phase. No handoff request is replayed and no completion receipt or reservation
release occurs at this stage.

Composed dispatch/restart fixtures cover Accepted and Unknown success, unfinished
or failed child tasks, absent native mapping, denied writer, absent recorded task
and removed managed Node. Refused recovery retains the prior operation and Held
reservations; successful observation advances only to Verifying. These remain
local simulated-actor fixtures. Public reconciliation, installed admission,
per-device convergence, release/settlement composition and live qualification
remain pending.

The composed local handoff lifecycle now also carries the original operation and
claimed reservations from dispatch through restarted verification into atomic
action publication. It covers denied publication, an incomplete supplied member
set and a lost status acknowledgement. Successful publication can derive shared
group completion evidence; denied publication retains Verifying, and restart
cannot repeat a persisted receipt. All cases keep the grants Held and publish no
member completion. This is controller-side fixture evidence only, not device-side
convergence or release qualification.


### IP-transit Layer 3 handoff model

A private parser now expands border-device `l3_handoffs` using the pinned 0.5.0
module's transit/interface/virtual-network shape. It preserves device, transit,
interface, VN, VLAN, optional TCP MSS, IPv4/IPv6 host prefixes and border-level
external handoff pool references. Canonical ordering and bounded expansion
reject duplicate transit/interface/VN entries and conflicting interface VLANs;
strict decoding rejects unknown fields and invalid integer/address families.

The model preserves explicit addresses even when a pool is selected. The pinned
module suppresses those addresses in its native projection when
`external_handoff_pool` is present; the forthcoming payload builder must implement
that precedence explicitly. No native payload or API execution is enabled by this
parser. Native dependency binding, inventory, admitted execution, recovery and
live qualification remain pending. The SDA-transit handoff resource remains
separate. Reference: [NetAsCode Layer 3 handoff model](https://netascode.cisco.com/docs/data_models/catalyst_center/fabric/layer_3_handoff/),
with pinned module `cc_fabric.tf` resource and flattening mapping as the versioned
authority.


### IP-transit handoff native inventory

The private native reader now maps the documented Layer 3 IP-transit handoff
fields and uses the existing authenticated strict-200 paginated transport. It
requires fabric/device scope on every request and validates the complete result
before returning it, rejecting missing identities, foreign rows, malformed
address families/MSS and conflicting interface VLAN or transit/VN mappings across
pages. Model and native validation now share CVK's reserved fabric VLAN rule.

The 501-record HTTP fixture exercises both pages, malformed second-page rows,
duplicate native IDs and mapping keys, failed second-page requests, absent
response envelopes and unexpected status codes, with no partial result on error.
Dependency resolution, payload precedence, mutation/ownership/recovery and public
integration remain pending. Reference: [Cisco IP-transit handoff inventory API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/get-fabric-devices-layer-3-handoffs-with-ip-transit/).


### IP-transit handoff dependency projection

The private binding helper now reuses canonical border validation and physical
interface binding, resolves the named BGP IP transit, and requires known VN
membership in the target fabric. Its digest includes native border/interface,
transit UUID/settings, VN UUID/membership and projected handoff fields. Payloads
preserve explicit host prefixes for custom addressing; external-pool selection
omits the explicit address fields as the pinned module specifies. Optional MSS
and inventory values are copied rather than aliased into mutable caller data.

Local tests cover missing/wrong dependencies, non-physical interfaces, wrong
transit type/ASN, missing or duplicate fabric membership, pool precedence and
transit-setting changes. Anchored VNs are currently refused pending explicit
anchor-site semantics. External pool allocation and reservation ownership must
still be validated by the future complete dependency collector; the projection
only preserves the pool reference and is not dispatch authority. No mutation or
public configuration route was enabled by this addition.


### IP-transit handoff complete native dependency collection

The private collector now composes existing fabric-device prerequisites, physical
interface/transit/VN binding and scoped handoff inventory. When an external pool
is declared, it resolves the fabric/zone site path and uses the shared validated
IPAM loader plus reservation binder to require that exact owner. Its digest
retains provisioning, physical membership, border configuration, native binding,
pool UUID/allocation/parent evidence and the sorted handoff baseline. Custom
addressing does not query IPAM.

Race-enabled HTTP fixtures cover stable observations, custom addressing, missing
and wrong-site reservations, invalid allocation, and replacement of pool or
provisioning records and transit settings. This establishes recorded allocation
and ownership only: pool capacity and version-specific handoff eligibility are
not established by these IPAM records. Anchored VNs, mutation planning, admitted
execution/recovery, public composition and lab qualification remain pending.


### IP-transit handoff guarded create and native readback

The private create primitive now checks existing mappings for exact no-op or
interface/VLAN and transit/VN conflicts, retains the dependency snapshot, and
requires a guard callback after the final repeated native reads. It submits one
array item through the existing authenticated transport and accepts only a
strict-200 response containing a valid task ID. The write object is consumed even
when validation, the guard or the native response fails.

Recovery identity excludes only the desired matching handoff from the baseline;
all other dependencies and mappings remain bound. Native readback returns its
observed UUID only for matching Verifying operation inputs; absent mappings stay
pending and conflicting state is refused. This primitive does not independently
verify task completion, establish actor authority or publish ownership. Those
remain shared-journal integration requirements.

Race-enabled fixtures cover custom and pooled create payloads, no-op/conflict,
changed dependencies, denied guard, missing task, non-200/error responses, no
second submission, and absent/conflicting readback. Pool capacity/eligibility,
anchored VNs, public/admitted lifecycle and live qualification remain pending.


### Shared Layer 2/Layer 3 handoff manifest projection

The private combined compiler now extracts both pinned handoff forms and the
Layer 3 external pool reference from an owned parsed document, then delegates
remaining inventory/border validation to the existing strict device parser. It
returns every resource to its caller, preserves selectors and placement, checks
required border types and a shared expansion bound, and rejects orphan/duplicate
declarations and cross-layer interface VLAN collisions. Unsupported border
fields, including SDA-transit declarations, remain rejected.

The existing Layer 2-only entry point wraps this compiler but rejects returned
Layer 3 work; it cannot silently drop unexecuted resources. Mixed/L3-only model
fixtures cover selectors, pool propagation, unknown nested fields, wrong border
types, non-provisioned devices, orphan pools and cross-layer conflicts. This is
private intent composition, not public scheduling or execution of a mixed model.


### IP-transit handoff managed preparation and journal admission

The private Layer 3 handoff collector now resolves the complete native footprint
to immutable CiscoDevice/Node identities and repeats both observations. Its
resource prefix is reserved by the shared journal, including malformed/pruned
records, so legacy and taskless completion paths cannot bypass group admission.

Source-driven preparation selects the exact declared handoff, refuses mixed
Layer 2 execution, and retains Prepared uncertainty through lost acknowledgments
or pruned group fields. Preflight rechecks source, section ownership, native
dependencies and canonical managed targets in Prepared or permit-held Submitting.
An already-present mapping cannot become evidence that an unsubmitted operation
created it. The planning object has a denying guard; only a separately admitted
dispatch path may provide submission authority. This does not activate public
reconciliation or establish live lab qualification.

Race-enabled fixtures cover two-device identity collection, missing/replaced
managed members, native drift, lost acknowledgments, pruned groups, source and
owner changes, invalid phases, unchanged pre-existing mappings and denied
submission without replay. Separate selector cases verify MSS value equality
and reject changed values, mixed unsequenced work and missing source. The
focused preparation/journal suite passed, as did the strict documentation build.


### IP-transit handoff admitted dispatch and restart observation

The private dispatch bridge now consumes the existing group submission permit.
It validates owned source and canonical targets, persists Submitting before the
single native POST, repeats admission checks at dispatch, and records the task
through the shared journal. A failed native response or rejected task receipt
retains uncertainty; a known task is returned even if receipt recording fails.
A restarted adapter cannot replay that submission.

Read-only recovery uses the existing complete task-tree validator, native
dependency-bound handoff readback and repeated managed footprint collection.
Only the shared contract advances a recorded Accepted/Unknown operation to
Verifying. Missing native state, a missing managed node, unfinished/failed child
tasks, missing task identity or denied writer authority cannot complete recovery.
Reservations remain held, and no ownership receipt or completion is published.

The composed fixtures use the real shared permit/journal implementation with
simulated actor authorization and native HTTP responses. They are not installed
actor or device convergence qualification. Public reconciliation, runtime group
admission, verified ownership publication and live lab validation remain pending.


### IP-transit handoff verified ownership publication

The private receipt builder now revalidates the recorded task tree, native
handoff UUID, physical member identities and repeated native readback. Its
receipt carries a stable logical handoff identity plus the observed native UUID;
it leaves the prepared operation identity unchanged.

The adapter selects the exact current declared intent and delegates persistence
to the existing shared group receipt transaction. Verified status and ownership
are committed atomically after source/controller/owner and member authorization
checks. A lost acknowledgment retains the committed receipt, preventing repeated
publication after restart. The composed dispatch/recovery fixtures derive shared
completion evidence from that receipt but do not publish completion or release
reservations. Those integration steps, public reconciliation/runtime admission,
and installed lab qualification remain pending.

The shared persistence fixture also exercises inline and ConfigMap sources, late
source/controller changes, wrong operation, missing ownership/member and revoked
member evidence. These are simulated native/actor tests, not device convergence
or installed actor qualification.


### IP-transit handoff terminal completion integration

The composed Layer 3 handoff fixture now continues its actual generated receipt
through the existing terminal adapter route. It deletes the source first to
exercise retained-evidence recovery, refuses an unauthorized actor, publishes
completion without changing the Held grant, and repeats observation safely.
Simulated worker Released status alone cannot clear the journal; only subsequent
simulated manager settlement allows clearing, preserving ownership and receipt.
The fixture snapshots device Leases and verifies that this controller route did
not mutate them. No separate handoff release implementation was introduced.

This validates adapter integration with the existing shared completion contract.
It does not execute installed device-worker release, manager session settlement
or reservation retirement: those actors/status writes are simulated, and runtime
group admission/public submission plus live qualification remain outstanding.


### SDA-transit border handoff field model

The pinned module's separate SDA-transit handoff resource now has a private
typed intent parser for `sda_transit`, both affinity IDs, internet connectivity
and multicast-over-transit. It preserves optional null/omission versus explicit
zero/false, introduces no field defaults, rejects unknown fields and invalid
types, and enforces the documented 0..2147483647 affinity range. It owns decoded
values independently of caller input.

References: pinned `cc_fabric.tf` resource mapping and the
[NetAsCode border-device schema](https://netascode.cisco.com/docs/data_models/catalyst_center/fabric/border_device/).
This is not public support: border/inventory composition, native observation and
dependency binding, the complete admitted lifecycle and lab qualification remain
pending. Public group submission remains gated in the existing reconciler.


### SDA-transit shared manifest composition

The existing handoff compiler now has a complete private projection returning
SDA-transit, IP-transit and Layer 2 intents together. It extracts only the pinned
SDA fields, then delegates remaining inventory/border validation to the existing
strict device parser. Serial selectors, provisioning state, placement and explicit
optional values remain attached to the handoff. Unknown/orphan settings, duplicate
borders, missing inventory and non-Layer-3/non-provisioned devices are refused.
The shared 1000-action bound includes SDA handoffs.

Existing L2/IP-only compiler callers wrap this projection and reject any SDA
work; they cannot silently drop it. SDA zone placement remains explicitly refused
pending native site-scope qualification, since the pinned SDA resource binds the
fabric site rather than the IP-transit zone fallback. Native inventory/binding,
public sequencing, admitted lifecycle and live qualification remain pending.


### SDA-transit native handoff inventory

The private native reader now uses the shared authenticated strict-200 transport
and paginated inventory helper for fabric-scoped reads with an optional device
filter. It follows the documented fabric/device composite identity; SDA handoffs
do not expose the separate handoff UUID used by IP-transit handoffs. Duplicate
identities, wrong fabric/device scope, missing transit identity, malformed types
and invalid affinity bounds discard the complete result. Optional flags remain
pointers, preserving unknown/omitted versus explicit false.

Cross-page HTTP fixtures cover 501 records, one-device filtering, empty results,
duplicate devices with differing transits, invalid affinity, wrong scope and
failed/missing/non-200 responses. No native writes or new transport are added.
Native dependency binding and the admitted execution lifecycle remain pending.

API reference: [Cisco Catalyst Center 2.3.7.6 SDA handoff inventory](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/get-fabric-devices-layer-3-handoffs-with-sda-transit/).


### SDA handoff native dependency projection

The shared transit inventory type now retains SDA multicast and control-plane
settings previously discarded during decoding. Private handoff binding checks
the canonical Layer 3 border, exact transit name/UUID and SDA type, validates
control-plane identities, sorts an owned copy and preserves optional intent
values independently of caller memory. Its digest includes border, transit
settings/control-plane IDs and projected native handoff. Requested multicast
requires a multicast-enabled pub/sub transit.

Fixtures cover absent/wrong transit, missing/duplicate/invalid control-plane
IDs, invalid roles/affinity, multicast incompatibility, input isolation and
control-plane replacement changing the digest. This is configuration evidence
only: physical control-plane inventory, provisioning, complete managed group
collection, admitted lifecycle and live qualification remain pending.

Reference: [Cisco 2.3.7.6 transit inventory schema](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/get-transit-networks/).


### SDA handoff local and control-plane dependency collection

The private collector now composes existing fabric-device provisioning, site
assignment and border-role checks with SDA transit binding. It unions local
fabric members and transit control-plane IDs through the existing canonical
physical-identity binder, requiring unique serial identities and rejecting
missing devices. Repeated local inventory evidence must match the earlier
fabric snapshot. Its digest retains provisioning, transit settings, physical
identities and scoped handoff inventory.

HTTP fixtures cover stable collection, missing control-plane inventory, duplicate
serials, missing membership, mid-read local replacement and changes to transit,
control-plane or provisioning identity. This is deliberately local-plus-control-
plane evidence, not a complete cross-site mutation footprint: remote participants,
managed reservation admission and execution remain pending. No controller/device
mutation is performed and live qualification is unchanged.


### SDA cross-site participant discovery

The dependency collector now scans each native fabric site's SDA handoff
inventory, discovers sites sharing the selected transit and includes their
complete fabric-device populations alongside the local fabric and transit
control planes. Linked handoffs must refer to observed Layer 3 borders. Native
site/link/member evidence is sorted before hashing; failed scans and missing
linked borders return no partial participant set. Bounded site/member counts
prevent unbounded admission expansion.

Fixtures cover local and remote border/edge participation, unrelated sites,
failed scans, missing local/remote membership and digest changes when a remote
member or transit link changes. Physical identity resolution reuses the existing
canonical binder. This remains read-only dependency evidence: repeated managed
identity collection, group admission, execution/recovery and zone/live
qualification are still required.


### Shared SDA/IP handoff managed identity observation

SDA handoff dependencies now bind to the existing canonical managed target
contract. A shared typed observation helper, also used by IP-transit handoffs,
brackets managed identity resolution with fresh native dependency reads and
rechecks both physical evidence and managed bindings. Errors return no partial
snapshot or targets. The helper creates no write, reservation or authority.

Two-device SDA fixtures exercise unmanaged/missing nodes, late aliases, native
replacement and changed CiscoDevice/Node identities. Existing IP-transit
preparation, dispatch, recovery and publication fixtures exercise the same
helper through their composed lifecycle. Runtime group admission, SDA native
execution/recovery/ownership and zone/live qualification remain pending.


### SDA handoff guarded native create

The private create planner now requires a guard callback, rejects conflicting
existing handoffs and treats exact matches as no-ops. It repeats the dependency
snapshot immediately before the guard and submits one array item through the
existing authenticated transport, accepting only a strict-200 valid task receipt.
Its write object is consumed even when the guard, dependency check or response
fails, preventing automatic replay after an uncertain outcome.

HTTP fixtures cover native payload shape, existing/conflicting state, omitted
guard, denied guard, provisioning drift, missing task, non-200/error responses
and second-submission refusal. This primitive does not establish group authority.
Its current resource identity is a pre-submit dependency digest; recovery-stable
identity/readback and admitted journal/public execution remain pending.

Reference: [Cisco SDA handoff create API](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-5/add-fabric-devices-layer-3-handoffs-with-sda-transit/).


### SDA handoff recovery-stable identity and readback

The private create resource now uses a recovery digest built from the same
collected evidence as the pre-submit digest, excluding only an exact desired
local handoff from the cross-site and scoped handoff baselines. The local site
remains in the participant set before and after creation; all transit settings,
physical identities, native memberships and other handoffs remain dependencies.
No second independent inventory scan is used to manufacture that baseline.

Native readback requires a matching Verifying/Create operation and task identity.
It returns true only for the desired device/fabric/transit settings; absence stays
pending, while conflicting readback or replacement control-plane identity fails.
The fixture submits once then verifies this transition and rejects invalid phase,
missing handoff and changed evidence. This is not complete task verification,
admission or ownership: shared journal/task-tree integration remains pending.


### SDA handoff source preparation and shared journal gates

The SDA handoff prefix is now reserved by the existing shared journal checks.
Canonical group preparation requires a valid Create identity; malformed/pruned
records cannot enter legacy or taskless completion paths. Private manifest-driven
preparation selects exact declared SDA intent, rejects mixed unsequenced L2/IP
work, repeats source/controller/native/managed observations and retains uncertain
Prepared state after lost acknowledgments. Its planning object uses a denying
guard and cannot submit a native request.

Prepared and permit-held Submitting preflight revalidate owner/source, operation
identity and complete managed targets. Fixtures cover missing declaration,
pruning, lost acknowledgments, changed source/owner/node/group and invalid phase,
plus optional-value equality and rejection of mixed work. Actual admitted
dispatch, task-tree recovery/ownership and public/runtime qualification remain
pending. Existing ND, direct-device and SWIM paths are not wired to SDA handoffs.


### SDA handoff admitted dispatch bridge

The SDA adapter bridge now requires the existing non-reconstructible group
submission permit. It revalidates Prepared intent, persists Submitting through
the shared permit, repeats owned source/native/managed checks before POST and
records the native task through the shared journal. A known task is returned
even if durable receipt recording fails. Restart cannot replay submission, and
uncertain outcomes keep the journal and reservations.

The shared dispatch test helper now supports multiple members while preserving
its existing single-device callers. SDA fixtures reserve both the border and
transit control-plane device with distinct worker identities and real shared
grant/claim/lease validation. Cases cover denied admission, success, failed
response and post-POST grant revocation. Actor authorization/native responses
remain simulated; installed runtime qualification, task-tree recovery/ownership
and public submission sequencing are not established by these tests.


### SDA handoff recorded-task recovery

The private SDA recovery bridge now uses the shared group verification contract
to advance an Accepted or task-recorded Unknown journal to Verifying. It checks
the complete recorded task tree, revalidates source/owner, resolves and compares
all managed targets, verifies exact native handoff readback and repeats native
and managed evidence. Only the shared contract persists the phase transition.

The two-member dispatch fixture now continues through adapter restart into
recovery. It covers accepted/unknown success, running/failed child tasks, missing
native handoff, denied writer, missing task, deleted control-plane Node and an
incomplete reservation set. Failure retains the prior phase; success does not
publish ownership/completion or release the Held grants. Actor authorization and
native responses remain simulated. Ownership publication, public runtime wiring
and installed/live qualification are still outstanding.


### SDA verified ownership publication

Private SDA receipt creation now validates complete task evidence, exact native
readback, physical membership and repeated dependency observations. Ownership
uses the observed device/fabric/transit composite identity without inventing a
controller UUID. The API cannot distinguish an identical delete/recreate of that
composite object; this is a qualification limit, not a claimed recovery guarantee.

Publication reuses the shared atomic Verified/receipt transaction, selecting the
exact current source and checking controller/config identity and all members.
The two-device composed fixture covers denied authority, incomplete members and
lost acknowledgment; committed receipts survive uncertainty and cannot be
republished after restart. Shared source/owner/controller persistence fixtures
are also applied to this SDA receipt. Reservations remain Held, with no completion
or release published by this step. Public runtime admission, terminal integration
and live/zone qualification remain pending.


### Shared handoff terminal completion with multiple members

The composed terminal fixture is now shared by SDA, IP-transit and Layer 2
handoffs. SDA runs with its two-member border/control-plane receipt. After source
deletion it exercises denied actor authorization, a committed first completion
with lost acknowledgment, recovery of partial publication and repeated retained
receipt observation. It then simulates each worker release and each manager
settlement in sequence: no partial set may clear the journal. Only the final
settlement clears it, preserving ownership and receipts, while device Lease
contents remain unchanged by the controller adapter.

No separate SDA release code was added. The shared production terminal route
already accepts its generated group receipt. Worker release and manager status
evidence remain simulated; installed actors, retirement, public runtime
admission and live qualification remain outstanding.


### Explicit group runtime installation binding

The existing runtime binding schema now accepts either the single-device or
group protocol as an explicit, exclusive selection. Encoding/parsing still
requires the same non-secret installation identities and rejects blank, unknown
or combined/wildcard protocols. The installation reader continues to require
the reservation and both bound worker Pod incarnations to carry exactly the
same binding; it does not treat the two protocols as interchangeable.

Tests exercise both protocols against replaced/old Pods, mixed worker protocols,
wrong accounts, alternate installation identity, duplicate environment entries
and indirect environment sources. The manager authorizer's uninstalled-group
gate is unchanged and tested. This enables representation and verification of
an explicitly selected group installation, not automatic rollout, mutation
authority or public group reconciliation. Installed actor qualification and the
manager/reconciler activation steps remain pending.


### Group manager installation verification

Manager reservation authorization now recognizes the explicit group protocol
and uses that exact protocol when corroborating both bound worker Pods. It
retains the single-device path's live administrator policy, admission contract,
worker RBAC, connector descriptor and empty workload-node checks. Unknown or
combined protocols and the wrong worker service account are rejected before
installation discovery; either supported protocol still fails without the
installed policy. This supersedes the earlier single-device-only manager gate.

Worker preparation setup is tested with either explicit binding. The manager's
default generated worker binding remains single-device; recognizing a group
reservation does not silently convert existing workers or grant mixed-protocol
authority. Exact binding checks continue to reject such installations. Installed
actor qualification, intentional rollout and public group dispatch remain
pending; these checks do not establish live Catalyst Center parity.

### Retaining the group recovery worker during reconciliation

An observed Catalyst Center group journal now defers ordinary worker resource
reconciliation until that journal is cleared. Reservation creation/cancellation
preparation still runs through its existing manager authorization, and settled
reservation retirement still runs first. The connector retains its bootstrap,
service account, role binding and Deployment, including after native verification
while member completion and settlement remain outstanding. This prevents the
ordinary image/template reconciliation path from replacing a journal-bound
connector before explicit worker handoff is qualified.

Tests retain these resources through Prepared, Submitting, Accepted, Unknown,
Verifying, Verified and Cancelling, preserving the journal even with incomplete
evidence. Existing ordinary worker rollout and binding tests remain separate.
This is a reconciliation retention rule, not a completed handoff protocol: it
cannot prevent external Deployment/Pod deletion, process failure, or the race
between a new journal and an already-running rollout. Replacement recovery,
installed actor qualification and explicit group activation remain outstanding.

### Resolving acknowledged group members after restart

The shared configuration contract now provides a read-only journal member
resolver for Accepted, Unknown-with-task, and Verifying recovery. It resolves
canonical reservation names from the retained group, corroborates controller
revision and member identities with a second read, and requires unchanged
ownership and all held claims. Missing, released, settled or partially observed
members cannot become a usable partial set. A Prepared or uncertain taskless
Submitting journal cannot enter this path.

The existing verification transition and the new reader share ownership/claim
validation. Reading this evidence grants no worker authority, dispatch permit,
completion or release. Product recovery must still verify its source, bound
worker installation and native task/convergence evidence. Public recovery
routing and replacement-worker handoff remain pending.

### Public acknowledged SDA-transit recovery

The Apply reconciler now recognizes an already acknowledged SDA-transit group
operation before compiling new execution intent. It resolves the complete
retained member set, requires the exact bound connector and configured runtime
authorizer, checks the original source and controller revisions, and selects
the declared handoff by native target, fabric and recovery digest. Accepted or
Unknown-with-task can advance to Verifying; a subsequent reconcile independently
verifies and atomically publishes the owned action receipt. Existing terminal
group recovery then handles completion and settlement. No native POST is issued
by this new route.

The composed native/Kubernetes fixtures exercise the actual Apply evaluation
through verification and publication, denied runtime authorization and changed
source generation. The successful path continues through the existing terminal
fixture. Runtime actor authorization and device/manager settlement remain
simulated, so this does not qualify a live installation. New group submissions,
other handoff public recovery routes, mixed-intent sequencing and replacement
worker handoff remain outstanding. The normal source and actor fences remain in
place for acknowledged operations; source deletion is only supported after a
terminal receipt exists.

### Public acknowledged recovery for all three handoff families

The acknowledged handoff recovery route now covers L2, IP-transit and SDA-transit
creates. The source, journal, member-set and actor checks are shared. Each family
uses its existing native dependency binding, task/convergence verifier and owned
receipt publisher. L2 selection includes both its handoff baseline and its
fabric-device prerequisite digest; IP and SDA selection retain their existing
recovery digest. Exactly one matching declared action is required. Mixed-family
intent remains rejected until its sequencer is implemented.

All three native fixtures now exercise the same public Apply recovery harness:
Accepted to Verifying to Verified, denied authorization, changed source generation,
and successful terminal completion/settlement through the existing simulated
actor fixture. Recovery never dispatches a new native request. New group
submission and replacement-worker recovery remain pending, as does installed
actor and live lab qualification.

### Full reconciler handoff recovery qualification

The shared handoff recovery fixture now enters through `Reconcile`, including
contract validation, source/config rereads, persisted status conditions and the
five-second Apply requeue. It no longer stops at the Apply evaluation helper.
Fabric section status remains Applying during retained recovery instead of
falling through to Skipped. The native fixture still asserts no replayed POST.

Each handoff family covers Accepted and Unknown-with-task progression, denied
authority, changed source generation, a missing canonical member and a replaced
connector Pod UID. The latter remains denied: this validates preservation of
the existing identity boundary, not implementation of replacement handoff.
Runtime policy authorization and device/manager release evidence are still
simulated; installed/live qualification remains outstanding.

### Public pending fabric-event acknowledgement recovery

The shared acknowledged fabric recovery route now also recognizes retained
pending-event operations. It resolves declared reconfigure sites, matches the
original event/site/group identity, and uses the existing owned task/event
observer to advance an accepted task to Verifying. The full reconciler fixture
checks a second reconciliation leaves it Verifying with held claims, no action
receipt and no replayed POST.

This does not complete event deployment support. A completed task and absent
pending event are insufficient evidence of every device's convergence. The
Verifying path deliberately retains the operation and reservations until an
independent product convergence verifier and owned receipt publication are
implemented. New event submissions and installed/live qualification also remain
pending. The declaration parser is shared with existing owned recovery checks.

### Explicit pending-event convergence limitation

After pending-event task/event verification, config readiness now reports
`GroupConvergenceVerificationUnavailable` and explains that device convergence
verification is not implemented. The fabric section carries the same message;
the journal and held reservations remain retained. This separates a missing
implementation from a transient native task wait. The full reconciler test
asserts Ready remains false and no release/receipt is produced.

The documented [2.3.7.6 fabric-device response](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/get-fabric-devices/)
provides identity, membership, roles and border settings, without a per-device
deployment completion field. CVK's existing wired provision reader likewise
binds record identity rather than new task completion. These observations do
not prove no other API can supply convergence evidence; an event-specific
verification contract still needs qualification against the lab. No speculative
status field was added or treated as success.

### Explicit adapter group runtime selection

Controller-worker setup now dispatches the installation binding's exact protocol
to the adapter. The existing single-device interface is unchanged; group setup
requires an additional optional interface and cannot silently fall back to a
legacy adapter. Catalyst Center uses one shared setup implementation, records
the selected protocol, and rejects reconfiguration or partial identity/authority.
A dedicated readiness predicate distinguishes an explicit group installation
from generic reservation recovery capability.

Tests cover both setup paths, unsupported/unknown protocols, adapter setup errors,
missing worker identity and attempts to switch an installed protocol. These are
runtime wiring tests, not live policy qualification or dispatch authorization.
The manager default remains single-device. New public group preparation and
submission are not enabled by this change.

### Public manifest-driven handoff preparation

An explicitly configured group runtime can now prepare L2, IP-transit or
SDA-transit handoffs through the public reconciler. It parses the complete model,
requires one handoff family, verifies all declared base fabric/device effects
already match native state, claims section ownership and invokes the existing
managed planner/preparation path. At most one canonical group journal is
prepared per reconciliation. Already-matching handoffs are read back through
the existing planners before InSync is reported. Mixed-family and base
provisioning sequencing remain pending.

The composed tests now begin at public preparation for all three handoff families,
verify that a single-device runtime cannot prepare a group, and verify repeated
reconciliation retains the same taskless Prepared identity without creating
reservation objects. They then use the existing private permit/dispatch fixture
and return to public acknowledged recovery and terminal settlement. Public
all-member claim/dispatch, intentional manager group rollout, installed actors
and live qualification remain pending; preparation itself grants no mutation
permit.

### Journal-driven public handoff dispatch wiring

Prepared handoffs under an explicit group runtime now select the exact retained
native action, revalidate its source/owner/dependencies, and claim the complete
canonical persisted reservation set. The new journal claim entry point delegates
to the existing no-replay claim coordinator; missing members never become an
inventory-derived substitute or caller-selected subset. Runtime authorization
combines each exact bound worker's installed policy checks with the shared
all-member authority reader (worker identity, physical exclusivity, maintenance
guards, leases and empty Kubernetes workloads).

Only the existing one-use submission permit can move Prepared to Submitting and
invoke the native handoff request; accepted task persistence and acknowledged
recovery remain unchanged. Pending fabric events are excluded from new dispatch
while their convergence verifier is incomplete. Claim tests cover complete sets,
missing members, revoked grants, denied authorization and restart refusal after
claims. Existing public-preparation tests also retain Prepared when manager
reservations are absent. The successful composed public-dispatch path still
needs a fixture with full live worker/maintenance evidence; installed actors,
intentional manager group rollout and lab qualification remain pending.

### Composed public handoff dispatch qualification

All three handoff native fixtures now run preparation and dispatch through the
full public reconciler, then return through public acknowledged recovery and
terminal settlement. The grant fixture can stop before claiming; public dispatch
must resolve the retained journal members and claim them itself. The fixture
supplies the real authority reader with the sole connector Deployment/ReplicaSet/
Pod ownership chain, current network-worker revision and Node bindings,
manager-acknowledged maintenance sessions, matching annotated leases and empty
Kubernetes workload inventory. The production authority reader is not bypassed.

The successful path is now composed rather than only separately unit-tested.
Installed admission/RBAC verification remains represented by a fixture callback;
native workload preparation and device/manager settlement writes are simulated.
Consequently this does not qualify an installed cluster or live lab, nor does it
complete replacement handoff, mixed/base sequencing or manager group rollout.
The native fixture continues to require exactly one POST despite repeated and
restarted reconciliation.

### Stable InSync after public handoff settlement

The composed public recovery fixture now retains its manifest through settlement
and performs two more full reconciliations. All three handoff families must
report Ready/InSync with an InSync fabric section, return to the normal five-minute
interval, preserve their owned receipt and leave the operation slot empty. Native
fixtures still permit only the original POST, and no new mutation authorization
is requested during converged readback. Other terminal fixture callers retain
the existing source-deletion recovery coverage. This closes the fixture-level
lifecycle through steady state; installed actor and lab qualification remain
outstanding.

### Explicit manager protocol option

The manager now accepts `--configuration-reservation-protocol`, defaulting to
`contract.Protocol` (the existing single-device protocol). Selecting the group
protocol requires managed topology, readWrite network-management access and the
controller/reservation CRDs. The selected value is propagated through the same
verified worker installation binding; existing single-device deployments retain
their default behavior.

Before registering reconcilers, a read-only startup scan rejects incompatible
retained physical journals or reservation rows. Reserved fabric group prefixes
also identify pruned group journals. Tests cover both directions of mismatch,
unknown retained protocols, pruned groups, metadata-only journals and the option
prerequisites. This is an observed-state preflight, not a distributed migration
lock: concurrent work from an old manager/worker and worker replacement still
need installed rollout qualification. No lab deployment or automatic protocol
migration was performed. The subsequent Helm section records value wiring.

### Helm protocol selection

`topology.configurationReservationProtocol` now exposes the explicit manager
selection. Its default is `controller-configuration-v1` and emits no new manager
argument, preserving the default Deployment. Selecting
`controller-configuration-group-v1` emits the group argument and requires managed
topology plus readWrite network-management workers. Both JSON schema and template
validation reject unsupported protocols and incompatible settings, including
when schema validation is skipped.

A dedicated render test covers default/valid/invalid combinations and is included
in the existing topology render suite. The suite's reservation-policy shape
assertion was updated from 21 to the current 26 named variables: the group
cancellation policy had already added the extra evidence variables. The typed
rendered admission-contract checks remain unchanged. Helm rendering is not an
installed rollout or concurrent protocol migration qualification.


### Mixed fabric handoff sequencing

Public group preparation accepts L2, IP-transit and SDA-transit declarations in
one resolved model. It validates base fabric/device membership and preflights
all declared handoffs before preparing the first pending action, in L2, IP, SDA
order. Matching native state is skipped without an ownership claim. A missing
later dependency blocks initial preparation; no partial group is published.
The retained operation still routes through the shared all-member reservation,
one-use dispatch, verified receipt and settlement lifecycle before another
operation can start. Recovery selects the exact retained target, parent and
resource identity from the complete model. Legacy partial-model compilers still
reject omitted families rather than silently discarding work.

The mixed HTTP/Kubernetes fixtures cover ordering, all-converged models, a missing
last dependency, and each family's complete public lifecycle in a mixed manifest:
preparation, guarded dispatch, restart recovery, receipt, partial completion and
settlement, followed by repeated InSync reconciliation with exactly one native
POST. Reservation grants, policy authorization and release/settlement writers are
simulated evidence; these are not installed-actor or live lab results. Base
provisioning, fabric creation and other sections must already converge. Mixed
handoff updates/deletes and replacement-worker recovery remain separate gaps.
The example manifest is `examples/configs/catalyst-center/fabric-handoff-execution.yaml`.

The full Helm topology render contract now passes. Its schema-error checks accept
both JSON Pointer and dotted property paths and both supported validator wording
styles while preserving property and constraint assertions. Typed admission
contract checks still validate the rendered policies.


### Mixed handoff recovery isolation and reporting

Recovery now reads only the family identified by the retained operation resource.
The complete source is still strictly parsed and source/actor/member identities
remain mandatory. A disappearing future SDA dependency therefore does not prevent
an accepted L2 action from verifying and settling. A fixture confirms that later
preparation remains blocked after that settlement and preserves the receipt.
Preparation also checks the controller resource version across its full preflight.

The same mixed manifest supports `mode: report`. A dedicated read-only compiler
consumes the complete fabric and inventory-prerequisite model, using existing
native dependency readers and comparators. It distinguishes missing mappings
(Add) from conflicting mappings (Update); Update is a drift classification and
does not enable update execution. Two complete observations must agree on
prerequisite and handoff evidence before publishing a result. Unknown fields,
unselected additional sections, incomplete dependencies and replacement between
reads fail closed. Base provisioning/membership must already match; this path
does not yet report missing base prerequisites as actionable drift.

Full-reconciler fixtures remove managed devices and Nodes to prove reporting
requires neither physical reservation configuration nor managed Kubernetes
objects. Matching, missing, conflicting, incomplete and changing readbacks are
covered with no native mutations, ownership or reservation creation. Report
results attest native API configuration only, not device convergence or ownership.

Validation: the controller-adapter (including ND), controller-configuration,
reservation-provider, controller and manager race suites passed after initial
mixed sequencing. Subsequent targeted handoff race tests passed after recovery
isolation and preparation freshness changes. Mixed report/lifecycle and example
validation passed with local HTTPS fixtures. The strict documentation build and
full Helm topology render contract passed; installed actors and live lab remain
unqualified for these additions.

Lab availability check on 2026-10-14: `/tmp/catc` is absent on this host. No
new authentication attempt or live mutation was made. Restoring that credential
file and the `https://127.0.0.1:19443` tunnel was requested separately; the earlier
HTTP 401 is historical evidence, not the result of a new probe. Local coverage
work continues independently.

Final regression for mixed reporting: the complete Catalyst Center race suite
passed (150.520 seconds). Strict documentation validation and `git diff --check`
also passed. No live qualification, commit, push or deployment was performed.


### Fabric port-channel model and inventory

The pinned module's `inventory.devices.port_channels` now has a private strict
parser and payload mapper. The numeric `id` remains a model-local discriminator;
it is never emitted as a native channel number or UUID. Omitted protocol,
description and VLAN options remain omitted; an explicit empty description is
preserved. Extraction delegates base device/fabric validation to the existing
parser and rejects non-edge placement, duplicate IDs, overlapping member ports,
invalid protocol/type combinations and unconsumed effects. Physical member
binding reuses the existing exact interface identity checker, including rejection
of virtual, ambiguous, missing and foreign interfaces.

Native port-channel inventory reuses the shared authenticated transport and
bounded 500-record pagination, scoped by device and fabric UUID. Duplicate IDs,
names and shared ports, unknown protocol/type, malformed or partial responses
and repeated pages are refused. Normalization makes response ordering stable.
The [2.3.7.6 response schema](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/getportchannelsresponse/)
does not document native/allowed VLAN readback; no default or verification is
inferred from its absence. The private payload includes the pinned module's
optional VLAN inputs, but release-specific submission/readback support must be
qualified before enabling public execution. The
[NetAsCode model](https://netascode.cisco.com/docs/data_models/catalyst_center/fabric/port_channel/)
confirms the distinction between local discriminator and native channel identity.

These additions are prerequisites, not a completed component. Dependency
snapshots, native ownership and overlap handling, physical admission, durable
execution/recovery, public routing and lab qualification remain open. Existing
fabric and inventory compilers still reject port-channel effects rather than
silently dropping them. No appliance mutations were performed.


### Port-channel dependency binding and native create primitive

Port-channel dependency snapshots now reuse fabric-device provisioning/site/zone
and membership checks plus the exact physical-interface binder. They retain the
complete affected fabric population, selected interface identities/configuration,
requested attributes and existing channel inventory. Full and recovery digests
have separate purposes: only the matching created channel is excluded from the
recovery baseline; unrelated channels, fabric peers and provisioning changes
remain significant. Managed target collection uses the shared repeated native
and Kubernetes identity observation helper. Missing peers, replaced Nodes and
changing physical identities are refused.

A matching complete interface set is native compliance evidence only. Partial
member overlaps and conflicting attributes are not silently adopted or updated.
The model-local ID never selects a native channel number. Optional VLAN intent
remains gated because the 2.3.7.6 response does not provide verification evidence.

The private native create planner requires a guard and uses the shared transport's
single-submission policy. It rereads dependency evidence before dispatch, retains
only a valid task identity, refuses replay even after uncertain responses, and
verifies native UUID readback against the retained resource/target/parent scope.
The [2.3.7.6 create contract](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/add-port-channels/)
requires protocol: a new create with omitted model protocol is refused rather
than assigning an undocumented default. Existing matching channels remain
observable without rewriting them. The native primitive does not verify the task
tree, publish ownership, create reservations or release devices; those are still
required at the shared journal/adapter boundary before public execution.

Targeted race tests pass for parser/inventory, dependency changes, managed scope,
native payload, denied dispatch, stale caller intent, missing task, HTTP 401/500,
HTTP 202 uncertainty, one-use refusal, absent readback, foreign operation scope
and unrelated channel changes. Final targeted run: 3.783 seconds. No live device
or controller mutation was performed; journaled public execution remains pending.


### Port-channel group journal preparation and dispatch

Port-channel actions now have a private adapter bridge for strict declared-action
selection, repeated native/managed target planning and canonical shared-journal
preparation. A denying guard prevents a prepared native plan from acquiring
submission authority. Source and controller snapshots are rechecked before
journal persistence; Prepared and Submitting preflight also verify section
ownership, operation identity and the complete physical footprint.

The resource prefix is reserved independently of preservation of the group field.
A pruned port-channel journal therefore cannot use single-device start/advance/
finish helpers, and manager startup rejects a conflicting protocol selection.
The existing atomic group-preparation fixture now covers port channels as well.

Dispatch uses `GroupSubmissionPermit.BeginSubmissionFor`, the live dispatch
permit check and `RecordTask` from the shared foundation. It does not create a
parallel reservation protocol or auto-release mechanism. Unknown native outcomes
retain Submitting; a known task is returned even if receipt persistence fails,
without treating that response as a committed durable acknowledgment. Restart
cannot replay submission.

Targeted race tests passed for Catalyst Center (5.427 seconds) and manager
protocol checks (4.028 seconds). Cases include lost preparation acknowledgments,
schema pruning, missing permits, changed source/owner/Node/port/group,
accepted tasks, denied/revoked claims and lost native responses. The native and
Kubernetes fixtures do not qualify installed actors. Task-tree verification,
atomic ownership receipts, terminal recovery and public reconciliation remain
pending; no lab mutation or deployment was performed.


### Port-channel verification, ownership and public lifecycle

Port-channel recovery now verifies the owned task tree and native channel evidence
before the shared Accepted/Unknown-to-Verifying transition. Repeated physical and
managed snapshots must match the retained group. Receipt construction binds the
local model discriminator, device/fabric identity and observed native UUID, then
publishes the receipt atomically with Verified through the existing group receipt
contract. A changed UUID or incomplete/failed task cannot become ownership.

Public reconciliation uses the same fabric-group preparation coordinator as
handoffs, preflighting the complete port-channel declaration set before retaining
one operation. A separate strict parser handles port-channel-only fabric models;
mixed handoff/port-channel intent remains rejected. The common retained-group
route selects the exact operation identity and calls the tested preparation,
permit dispatch, verification and publication bridges. Generic terminal recovery
handles completion writes, device release, manager settlement and journal
retirement, including recovery after source deletion.

The composed public fixture reaches InSync and remains there across repeated
reconciliation with exactly one native create. It uses production managed-worker
and maintenance authority readers over fixture evidence, while policy decisions,
worker release and manager settlement writes remain simulated. Separate fixtures
cover failed/running tasks, missing native readback, replacement, unknown tasks,
denied actors, missing members, changed source/owner, failed receipt acknowledgment
and refused/incomplete publication. No completion or release is emitted merely
because task verification or receipt publication succeeded.

An executable-model example is saved at
`examples/configs/catalyst-center/fabric-port-channel-execution.yaml` and validated
against the strict parser. Base provisioning and fabric membership must already
converge. Explicit protocol is required on creation; VLAN options, updates/deletes,
Report mode, mixed effect composition, installed actors and live qualification
remain open. Targeted port-channel, handoff and pending-event race tests passed
(36.495 seconds). No live mutations or deployments were performed.

Final public port-channel regression passed across controller adapters (including
Nexus Dashboard), Catalyst Center model code, shared controller configuration,
reservation provider, controllers and the manager. Catalyst Center's full race
suite completed in 156.782 seconds. Strict documentation validation and whitespace
checks passed. These results do not replace installed-actor or live qualification.


### Port-channel read-only reporting (2026-10-14)

The public Report path now consumes the same strict whole port-channel model as
Apply. It observes every declared base device and the channel's physical members,
then classifies missing channels as Add and member/attribute conflicts as Update.
Update is a drift classification only; it does not enable updates. Observation
retains conflicts for reporting while the execution dependency wrapper continues
to reject them. Two complete observations must agree before drift is published.
Unsupported VLAN readback, missing prerequisites and changing native UUIDs remain
observation failures rather than false compliance.

Public reconciler fixtures remove all managed CiscoDevice and Node objects and
verify that reporting creates no ownership or reservations. Matching, missing,
overlapping, differing protocol, missing membership, unstable UUID and unsupported
VLAN cases are covered. Strict compilation rejects unknown/unconsumed source
fields. Port-channel lifecycle and handoff reporting race tests passed (9.594s).
No lab qualification is claimed; the credential file has not been restored on
this host. Mixed channel/handoff models, VLAN support and update/delete execution
remain open alongside the broader resource backlog.

Full Catalyst Center and NetAsCode model race regression passed (156.566s and
1.487s respectively). Strict documentation build and whitespace checks passed.


### Fabric port-assignment model and payload (2026-10-14)

Port assignments now consume the same strict edge-device envelope as port
channels through a shared generic extractor. Each extension validates its own
rows; the existing fabric-device parser still consumes every remaining field.
Unknown effects cannot silently disappear. The port-channel lifecycle continues
to use the same model semantics after extraction was shared.

The pinned module's `inventory.devices[].port_assignments` fields are represented,
including individual ports, inclusive slot/module/port ranges, device type,
data/voice VLAN names, security group, authentication template and description.
Optional omission and an explicit empty description remain distinct. Expansion
is bounded to 1,000 assignments per document. Empty/null lists are rejected rather
than interpreted as deletion. Overlaps, ambiguous selectors, reversed/overflowing
ranges and different end slot/modules are rejected; the latter prevents the
pinned Terraform expansion from silently using the start module for both ends.
This range guard is deliberate, not a claim that arbitrary range strings from
Terraform are executable.

Private payload mapping requires exact native physical interfaces, distinct
native interface identities, and a single resolved device/fabric scope. It emits
only the documented native fields and grants no mutation authority. Native
readback, VLAN/security-group dependency resolution, ownership, public execution,
reporting and reservation/recovery/settlement remain to be implemented.

Sources: pinned 0.5.0 `cc_fabric.tf` port-assignment locals/resource,
[NetAsCode port-assignment model](https://netascode.cisco.com/docs/data_models/catalyst_center/fabric/port_assignment/),
and [Catalyst Center 2.3.7.6 Add port assignments](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/add-port-assignments/).
No live mutation or lab qualification was performed.

Port-assignment model/payload and port-channel lifecycle race regression passed
(9.268s), including physical binding rejection and optional-field preservation.
Strict documentation validation and whitespace checks passed.


### Fabric port-assignment native inventory (2026-10-14)

Added the native port-assignment reader using the shared authenticated transport
and bounded pager. The
[Catalyst Center 2.3.7.6 GET schema](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/2-3-7-6/get-port-assignments/)
documents a 50-record page maximum; this reader uses that limit explicitly.
Requests are scoped to the resolved fabric and device, with returned scope,
identity, interface uniqueness, device type and optional settings validated.
Malformed, repeated, duplicate and foreign-scope results cannot become inventory.

Native comparison requires exact physical interface spelling and connected-device
type. Desired optional fields require present, equal readback; omitted desired
settings impose no defaults. An explicit empty description does not match absent
readback. Native unconfigured optional names may be empty strings without being
misinterpreted as configured values. This comparison alone grants neither
ownership nor permission to overwrite an assignment.

Fixtures cover 51-row pagination, repeated pages, duplicate identities/interfaces,
foreign device/fabric, incomplete response shape and invalid required fields.
Separate comparison fixtures exercise every optional field, missing/different
readback, explicit empty values and unresolved ranges. Dependency resolution,
managed scope, guarded execution, public reporting and full recovery remain open.
No live mutation or qualification was performed.

Port-assignment model, payload, native inventory and comparison race tests passed
(2.277s). Strict documentation validation and whitespace checks passed.


### Port-assignment VLAN prerequisites (2026-10-14)

Added reference resolution through the existing L2-network and anycast-gateway
inventory readers. Desired data/voice names must resolve within the target fabric
with matching traffic type. Missing references, conflicting VLAN numbers,
duplicate gateway views and using one name for both data and voice are refused.
When both native views identify the same VLAN, both are retained as evidence;
this does not grant ownership over either prerequisite. Gateway parsed fields
and native identity are retained for later dependency snapshot revalidation.
Omitted VLAN settings invent neither defaults nor inventory reads.

Resolver fixtures exercise L2-only, gateway-only, consistent dual views, missing
and foreign references, traffic/VLAN conflicts and native UUID replacement.
HTTP fixtures exercise the existing readers and reject incomplete reference
inventory. Full port-assignment scope, security-group resolution, execution and
recovery are still pending; this helper is not yet public Apply support. No lab
mutation or qualification was performed.

Port-assignment race tests passed (2.259s), including VLAN resolver and shared
reader fixtures. Strict documentation validation and whitespace checks passed.


### Scalable-group membership reader (2026-10-14)

Added a private VN scalable-group membership reader using the shared authenticated
GET transport. It requires the requested VN name, context identity, explicit guest
flag, successful native status and a present group-name list. Absent/null group
readback is not interpreted as an empty list. Duplicate case-insensitive names,
foreign VN responses, wrapped/partial payloads and failed status are refused.
The sorted result retains VN context and optional VPN evidence, not request-local
execution identifiers.

This endpoint reports associated names, not ISE group UUIDs. It is not ownership
proof or a complete security-group prerequisite resolver. Mapping port-assignment
VLANs to VNs, validating membership, and qualification on the actual lab release
remain open. The reader is not yet connected to public Apply.

### VLAN-to-SSID replacement selection and preservation (2026-10-14)

The pinned provider's resource description establishes that VLAN-to-SSID PUT is
full replacement: omitted VLANs and omitted SSIDs lose their mappings. Added a
pure selection layer that starts from complete observed inventory, retains every
undeclared mapping and empty VLAN entry, and deep-copies existing security-group
tags. It adds missing SSIDs without adopting matching pre-existing rows. Moving
an SSID requires supplied ownership evidence matching both its current VLAN and
tag; unowned or externally changed bindings reject the complete plan. This
function grants no authority: future execution must derive that evidence from a
verified source/fabric-scoped application receipt.

Inventory and selection share canonical validation/order normalization. Model
supplied tags are refused because the pinned module maps only name/vlan_name.
No implicit deletion is inferred from omissions or an empty declaration. The
native payload is not yet submitted; prerequisite resolution, durable ownership
lookup, guarded execution and recovery remain pending. Native API extensions
must also be accounted for before permitting replacement writes.

### VLAN-to-SSID native extension protection (2026-10-14)

Native mapping decoding now refuses unknown VLAN and nested SSID attributes.
The full-replacement payload cannot safely preserve a controller policy field
that its typed projection silently discards. Reports therefore return an
observation error for unsupported extensions instead of claiming compliance on
an incomplete projection. A future release-specific field must be explicitly
modeled before replacement execution can consume it. Recognized security-group
tags remain supported and preserved.

HTTP inventory and compiler-report fixtures inject unknown fields at both levels
and require rejection without a partial inventory/report. This closes the known
projection-loss gap before implementing guarded mapping PUT. No mutation route
was enabled, and no lab writes were performed.

anycast); missing, contradictory or disabled evidence blocks the binding.
Both views are retained when they describe the same VLAN, including native IDs.

enableFabric true and a matching non-sensor SSID definition. FlexConnect,

### Fabric mapping receipt-scoped ownership recovery (2026-10-14)

action receipts. Receipt keys bind fabric/site scope and the SSID hash, while

resolver requires the same config UID, a valid immutable physical-group journal,

revisions may change without discarding durable ownership by that same UID.

policy pointers do not alias native input.

### Retired-predecessor receipt replacement (2026-10-14)

entry point remains append-only and still rejects duplicate resource receipts.

a valid verified group identity and valid historical timestamps. Every expected
prior reservation name must be absent, and a namespace inventory check rejects
unexpected names carrying the previous controller/operation identity. These
checks run before and after authorization. The same CAS replaces the receipt and
advances the new operation; unrelated receipts are retained.
