appearing during authorization, foreign owner, invalid time, stale predecessor
and missing predecessor. The sequence fixture now invokes the real shared
reservation retirement contract after terminal cleanup instead of assuming that
release means retirement. Two additions followed by an owned VLAN move now pass,
with exactly two final receipts, stable ownership and two no-write public InSync
reconciles. This resolves the previously recorded failing sequence.

### Embedded-WLC model and native observation (2026-10-14)

Added the pinned embedded-WLC settings projection and native payload mapping,
including omitted-field defaults and explicit false values. Device intent parsing
requires exactly one embedded role and delegates the remaining fabric roles,
identity, site/zone and border settings to the existing fabric-device parser.
Declared managed AP locations use the existing wireless placement parser. Each
device retains its settings after canonical device ordering. Unknown effects,
duplicate names/roles, invalid sites and malformed settings are rejected.

Added authenticated fabric-scoped native settings reads using the existing
transport. The reader validates both switches independently, canonicalizes order,
and refuses duplicate device IDs, incomplete/unknown policy, invalid AP reboot
percentages and unsupported endpoints. Empty inventory is not promoted to evidence
of completed disablement. Public execution remains gated; native prerequisites,
physical admission, tasks, receipts and reload completion are still required.

The official [GET contract](https://developer.cisco.com/docs/catalyst-center/get-sda-wireless-details-from-switches/)
provides readback independently of Terraform's state-only Read implementation.

requires a separate reboot to remove wireless configuration. These API pages

resolved model.

These tests do not qualify native credential mutation or installed actors.

Automatic public ownership transfer remains disabled. Changed successor intent,
replacement, prune, config deletion, subsequent multi-owner retirement, empty or
unowned sources and mixed-source cleanup still need implementation/qualification.
The complete pinned model remains unfinished.

See [source-bound execution qualification](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-18/discovery-credential-custody-execution.md).


### Successor credential cleanup and sealed retirement

Delete-policy cleanup now consumes the initial successor custody through the
existing deletion lifecycle. Structural history checks serve capacity and receipt
validation; source/operation admission separately verifies the custody record,
original pre-deletion scope and complete archived seal. Deletion may advance
Kubernetes generation without changing the bound intent. New submission still
requires the exact current source and projected bytes. Acknowledged original
work may finish without those bytes and cannot fabricate replacement source.

The post-permit native observer reads a fresh controller revision, validates all
owned candidates and retired UUID absence, then checks the same revision at the
shared one-use dispatch guard. Taskless or lost-permit outcomes retain the fence.
Atomic retirement preserves delivered versions and original audit. Verified
completion replaces the active custody link with a new complete cohort seal;
the manager independently checks the full closure before releasing only its
existing discovery finalizer.

Controlled-native lifecycle tests run with controlled and isolated Kubernetes
persistence. They cover lost acknowledgements, source/projection loss, damaged
custody/archive/scope, native reappearance and a post-permit seal change. Accepted
and Unknown pre-deletion Creates finish through their original tasks before
cleanup. A three-owner cycle performs two private custody transfers, successor
Create/deletion/manager release and full-history retirement rollover, with fresh
native identities and increasing delivered-version floors.

Automatic public handoff remains disabled. Cancellation before the successor's
first delivery, changed successor intent, source replacement/pruning, mixed or
unowned sources, installed actors and native credential mutation remain open.
This closes a lifecycle gap, not full pinned-model parity.

See [source-bound cleanup evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-18/discovery-credential-custody-cleanup.md).


### Public credential handoff and first-preparation cancellation

The existing handoff route now delegates credential sources to the shared typed
observer and custody publisher. Only enrolled, pure credential-discovery Delete
sources with a validated current source scope can transfer a foreign reservation.
The old config must be gone, the complete closure/history seal valid, and native
absence and source/projection checks repeat. One status CAS changes custody;
normal native planning/dispatch runs on a later reconcile. Lost acknowledgements
are consumed from committed state; rejected writes can re-observe and retry.

A successor deleted at its first Prepared Create can now cancel with no native
submission. The original operation witness, sealed archive and slot release are
committed atomically in the existing retirement condition. Live cancellation and
source-free readback share structural proof validation. The manager verifies the
canonical closure; later handoff can verify it after the old config disappears.
No creator or credential-delivery row is fabricated. Queued versions remain
undelivered, including when the first owner never created a job. After the atomic
closure is committed, metadata/native observation can publish the unchanged
completion proof even after source/projection loss; reappearing native names or
archived UUIDs retain the finalizer. Source/projection loss before commit remains
fenced. Legacy unsealed
empty-history records stay manager-readable and cannot grant transfer authority.

The targeted lifecycle suite includes 24 successor-cancellation modes and 15
public transfer modes under both controlled and real isolated Kubernetes
persistence, plus existing first-owner cancellation cases. It covers archive
loss/reappearance, seal/scope/operation damage, projection/source drift, rejected
and lost CAS acknowledgements, same-name replacement, stale controller and
unenrolled actors. A changed projected snapshot first refuses cancellation and
can replan after a fresh stable observation without claiming delivery. A changed
ConfigMap before custody similarly requires re-attestation. A successor cannot
reuse its predecessor's cancelled operation ID.

Public transfer/creation/deletion and transfer after no-work cancellation are
qualified with controlled native responses; lab checks here remain read-only.
Native credential delivery and installed actors, successor revisions/replacement
and source pruning, mixed/unowned cleanup and full pinned-model parity remain
open. No provider, transport, CRD, finalizer or persistent store is added.

See [source-bound qualification](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-18/discovery-credential-public-handoff.md).


### Credential successor revisions, replacement and pruning

Strict initial custody publication/readback remains exact. A separate immutable
root validator checks the original controller/config identity, predecessor closure,
sealed archive, bounded current journal/history and cancelled-witness identity.
It does not invent a historical source or grant native authority. Current revision
admission additionally requires the canonical source-scope attestation, the live
source/projection contract and generation/source identity rules. A ConfigMap may
change UID/RV without changing config generation, but a body change cannot reuse
its old UID/RV. Initial resolved-input pinning remains active for the initial
revision; later revisions retain source/operation binding independently.

The existing executor, one-use dispatch, retirement observer, paired creator/
version publisher and manager cleanup now consume this authority for custodied
sources. No custody root or old receipt is rewritten. Native UUID/public-state
checks and all archived/current logical-field version floors remain mandatory.
Live and retained original-task retirement cannot fall through to unrelated
cleanup authority. Source-lost acknowledged retirement can finish without creating
its undelivered successor or claiming current-source InSync.

The bounded lifecycle suite covers inline/ConfigMap rotation, metadata changes,
new jobs, source prune and Retain omission, prune/recreate, removed/reintroduced
leaves, stale versions/projections, damaged archive/seal/scope, lost permit or task/
receipt acknowledgement, ambiguous deletion and original Unknown-task recovery.
Successful revisions also complete config deletion and independent manager release.
Controlled native responses and real isolated Kubernetes persistence remain
separate from native mutation/installed qualification.

At least one projected leaf must remain in the Delete-policy source. Final-leaf
removal, empty/mixed source migration, installed actors, native credential mutation
and wider pinned-model parity remain open.

See [source-bound revision qualification](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-18/discovery-credential-revisions.md).


## Delivered discovery owner with an empty source

A delivered pure credential-discovery owner may now revise its source to an
explicit empty discovery collection and remove all SecretRefs. Only existing
typed current-owner history admits this metadata shape; initial credential
enrollment remains unchanged. Full cohort/custody validation and the canonical
current source scope still control native execution.

The existing prune/Retain executor, one-use dispatch, atomic retirement receipts
and manager finalizer handle empty inline and ConfigMap sources. Twenty-eight
controlled/native-fixture and real Kubernetes API cases cover omission, last-job
pruning, recreation, known Unknown-task recovery, lost acknowledgements, source
loss and native reappearance. Successful cleanup continues through a subsequent
public owner lifecycle with archived receipts and delivered-version floors
preserved. The reused cleanup assertion now counts distinct archived owners,
including owners with multiple rotation/recreation deliveries.

This does not qualify removal of the last projected leaf from a retained job,
global-only/mixed source-family migration, unwitnessed empty successor ownership,
native credential delivery or installed actors. Wider pinned-model gaps remain
open. See [empty-source qualification](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-18/discovery-credential-empty-source.md).


## Native singleton repeated wireless tag lifecycle

The existing source now passes native singleton site/policy-tag repeated cycles
with stable tag UUIDs. Two delete/create cycles surround ordinary updates and
membership expansion/reduction; four complete predecessor cohorts survive.
Twenty-six original tasks recover through full trees/readback without replay,
including ordered tag/association pruning. Generated profile, disabled SSID and
empty-site inventories return to baseline. The native test passed in 1,626.75s.

Selected fixture/live source hashes still match the earlier local and real-API
gates; no implementation/foundation change was needed. Kubernetes actors/storage
are simulated. A separate bulk policy-cohort repeat run is in progress and is
not yet qualified. Installed workers, WLC/AP behavior, wider scopes and ownership/
parent/config lifecycle gaps remain open. See [native evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-18/wireless-tag-repeat-native.md).


## Existing-owner discovery metadata incarnations

Explicit v4 action-only incarnations now permit existing versioned owners to
replace jobs with global-reference/NoAuth metadata, preserving all delivered
floors and receipts. Older input formats still require versions; no empty
credential application or new store/schema is used. Typed ConfigMap scope
routing, mixed current-owner rows, reintroduction, pruning/recreation, source
loss and acknowledgement faults pass 131 overlay events, then the exact code
was applied. Full actual-worktree regression passed with 2,678 test events,
including the race detector and isolated Kubernetes API persistence. Native/installed and
initial metadata-only typed ownership remain unqualified. See [scope/evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-18/discovery-metadata-incarnations.md).

The bulk wireless repeated-cycle attempt observed both cycles and 28 original
task recoveries but expired before cleanup. Nine exact-ID supervised removals
restored its generated fixture baseline; the original gate remains failed. A
full retry with a larger explicit qualification deadline passed with 33 original
task recoveries, four predecessor cohorts, ordered tag/association pruning and
final native baseline restoration; assertions/default/production timeouts are
unchanged. Installed actors and physical WLC/AP remain open. See [native boundary](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-18/wireless-tag-repeat-native.md).


## Initial NoAuth discovery lifecycle

The applied implementation adds first-owner NoAuth discovery with manager-enrolled
Delete cleanup, first same-owner credential delivery, and version-1 projected
successors after metadata-only/cancelled ownership. Its corrected v4 refusal
retirement passed 423 targeted regression events, then the full 2,738-event overlay
matrix and 503 actual-worktree events including the public manifest. Five live
read-only cancellation cases using an isolated real Kubernetes API preserved
one discovery job and three devices with zero native mutation attempts. Native
discovery creation, installed workers, initial Retain/default NoAuth and
ordinary/typed adoption remain open. The current resource ledger records the
bounded delivered capability. See [implementation provenance and limits](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-18/discovery-initial-noauth-candidate.md).


## NoAuth Retain/default retention

Initial NoAuth Retain/default intent is implemented through the existing typed
source/compiler/journal path without a cleanup finalizer. Config deletion retains
the native job and reservation/audit, including unsubmitted work; a new UID cannot
inherit the claim. Fourteen controlled/real-API Retain scenarios and thirteen
Retain refusal cases per backend pass within 303 targeted events, including the
new default-policy manifest. Eleven live read-only versioned/Delete/Retain cases
preserved the one-job/three-device baseline with zero mutation attempts. Build,
foundation/ND/direct-upgrade/maintenance and SWIM/XFSU checks pass; full affected
regression remains running. Native job creation, installed actors and broad model
parity remain unqualified. See [source and limits](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-18/discovery-noauth-retain.md).


## Native NoAuth definition lifecycle and compatibility correction

The first Retain full run exposed accidental reclassification of an existing mixed
ordinary/credential owner after a versioned receipt appeared. Completed ordinary
receipts and pending ordinary operations now reserve that family. Corrective
composition/prune/lifecycle gates passed, and the final readback/family/example
matrix passed 377 events. Native testing then exposed a response version omission:
known v3 mode plus a nonempty SNMP user now derives v3, while explicit contradictory
versions and incomplete/unknown evidence remain unmatched. One generated native
NoAuth job passed Create, original Unknown recovery, manifest Delete and manager
release with restored baseline. The earlier failed job was causally bound and
supervised-cleaned separately. The exact passed live function is persisted;
corrected full regression is running. Device authentication, installed actors and
full 93-resource parity remain open. See [native and source-specific evidence](../evidence/catalyst-center-2026-10-18/discovery-noauth-retain.md).
